## §2 The C024 reduction record

**§2.1 Independent verification of the estimator core — 14/14 PASS.** A from-scratch reimplementation (mp-Hermite analytic-BF covariances at dps 40; mp Schur; float64+clip MC; zero shared code with the prior instruments; spec verbatim from Lemma UB0 §5), first gated internally against the previously validated float core (worst rel diff 5.7e-15), then scored against the recorded anchors — all 14 PASS, including: s_t/ℓ at both rungs and the sanity station (devs 2e-5–3.4e-5 vs bands ±0.0015); P_win = 1 − 1.4e-13; eight Gram λ_min anchors across four configuration classes (devs 0.003%–0.02% vs bands ±2–5%); E[W₂1|6] at r = 0.025 (0.003% vs ±1%); Λ at the sanity station (0.10% vs ±6%). Consequence (record verbatim class): the estimator mathematics of the instrument stack is independently verified end-to-end; the five historical incidents were deployment errors, not core errors.

**§2.2 Factor localization — the exponent ledger (ỹ*, three rungs, slopes ±0.03).** det Σ_∇∇ ~ c·r⁶ (slopes 6.02/6.01) · Mahalanobis q bounded → 10.41 · φ₂ ~ c·r⁻³ (−2.97/−2.99) · (μ_t−b)/ℓ → −0.4991 → −0.4999 [the C024 text's "→ −1/2" label is superseded by C026's exact −0.4999290; §3] · s_t/ℓ → 0.0668 · P_win ≡ 1.000000 · den E[W₂1|6] ~ 3.23·r² (2.00/2.00; coefficients 3.223/3.233/3.235) · num E[W₃1_sad|9] ~ c·r⁶ (5.99/6.02) = ∏(mean dets)·(1.00) · R_H = num/den ~ c·r⁴ (4.00/4.02) · Λ(ỹ*) ~ c·r¹ (1.03/1.03; 0.1857/0.0909/0.0445) · num_max ≡ 0 (0 in 6e5 samples/rung — the arch is saddle-only; the β-side bonus). **The decomposition of the exponent: 3 = (−3) + 4 + 2** — gradient-density concentration × triple-Hessian depletion × arch area — closing against the archived total: Λ-slope 1.03 + area 2 = 3.03 vs the measured 3.04.

**§2.3 The three mechanisms.** (M1) the mid-window law: μ_t = α·b + β·(b−ℓ) with α + β = 1.00000000 at 8 digits all rungs and β → ½-class (0.499108 → 0.499877); with s_t/ℓ → 0.067 the window sits ≈ 7.5 needle-sd inside on both flanks ⇒ P_win → 1. [C026 corrections: the "α + β = 1 identity" is in fact an exact O(r⁶) asymptotic (the 1.00000000 readings were the r⁶ ≈ 1e-8 floor), and the β-limit is the exact rational of §3, not ½.] (M2) determinant concentration: the three conditional-mean dets are exact Schur quantities ~ (7.8, −17.9, −13.8)·r², det fluctuations one full power below (sd/|mean| = 0.052 → 0.026 → 0.014 ~ c·r), P(typed) = 1.0000 at every rung; num = |∏ mean dets|·(1 + O(r)) verified to 0.1% at all three rungs. **§2.4 The S-obligations and their discharge.** The C024 reduction named six Schur-limit obligations S1–S6 (det Σ_∇∇ ≤ Cr⁶ on Ũ; q ≤ Q; the α+β structure; s_t/ℓ ∈ [c, C]; the mean-det/fluctuation structure ⇒ num ≥ ½|∏cᵢ|r⁶; den ≤ Cr² with a closed-form Isserlis certificate) plus the flow obligation AO ≥ c. ## §3 Lemma KR-MB (band-max count; C030/C031)

**The derived core — the Hessian-given-value law (BF).** ∇f ⟂ (f, H) at a point; H | f = u has mean −uI, Var(H_ii | f) = 2 independent, H_xy ~ N(0, 1). Hence the max-typed critical density at value u:
  **ρ_mx(u) = (1/2π)·E[|det H|·1_{H≺0} | f = u]·φ(u);  ρ_mx(1.2) = 0.043685** (E-term = 1.41350 ± 0.0017, the only MC element).
**Two-route verification (G-F1 PASS):** direct counting on 44 synthesized fields (synthesis gates: Var 1.010 ± 0.052; K(1) 0.630 vs 0.6065) gives 0.0391 ± 0.0044 — 9.5% from the derivation, inside derived bands — after one recorded normalization slip (the factor √(2ΣS)·N_g, derived and fixed; file 06). This two-route class is the program's standard for derived densities.
**The counting bound.** E[N_maxband(B₃) | 9 pins] ≤ 0.76·(ℓ/2) at r = 0.025 (same three zones, max typing, band width per the two-width rule); extended at C031 to **≤ 2.1·(ℓ/2) on B₅** (the d₀ = 5 ruling). Context constant: Rice on ∂B₅ = 2.43 (C031, standalone context).

## §4 Lemma TC (terminal counting; C032, audited C033)

**§4.1 Provenance.** C031's G2 selection-obstacle analysis exposed that selection is unnecessary: the C025 step "terminal ≥ v* ≥ b − δ₀" discarded the ℓ-scale start-height information. The magic is the start height — the outward branch launches at mid-window, so only an (ℓ/2)-thin terminal band can fail: the far term is O(r³) **by counting alone** — no crossing selection, no Palm disintegration, no barrier in the load path.

**§4.2 Statement and bound (derived-structure + station-certified, modulo R0).** Modulo R0 (terminal of an ascent is a local max): {outward terminal ≤ b} ⊆ {separatrix loop: outward branch terminates at M} ∪ {∃ local max with value ∈ [v*, b] on T²₂₄ ∖ collar(M)}. Hence, with band width 0.49993·ℓ:
  P(terminal ≤ b | 9) ≤ P(sep-loop) + **2.1·(ℓ/2)** [B₅; §3] + **ρ_mx(1.2)·0.49993·ℓ·(L² − π·25)·E_sup** [exterior] = P(sep-loop) + **2.03·r³**,
with ρ_mx derived (§3) and **E_sup = 1.0235 station-certified (G-H1 PASS):** conditional/unconditional band-max intensity ratio ∈ [0.98, 1.014] at d ∈ {5, 6, 8, 12} × 2 angles × 2 rungs (deviations = MC noise; v = 1 − O(1e-8) by d = 5, pull monotone → exact-zero underflow by d = 8); periodization ≤ e⁻⁷². **§4.4 The mean-rim discovery (a FAILED-AS-WRITTEN vacuity check → finding).** The freeze's sup-of-mean check (m₉ ≤ b, max at M) FAILED: **m₉ exceeds b at every station outside the pin cluster** — 1.2007 at d = 0.2, rising to a rim of 1.40–1.57 at d ≈ 1.3 (higher toward the arch side, angle 2.35), decaying to 0.0003 by d = 5. ## §1 Lemma UB-G — the upper side of Θ(r³) by global interceptor counting

**§1.1 Provenance and verdict.** The C032 terminal-counting insight, applied UPWARD under the 6-pin law, bypasses the C023 moderate-zone divergence entirely: no zone decomposition, no per-candidate selectivity — one global window count. OBL-BETA-RELEVANCE: CLOSED-BY-SUPERSESSION.

**§1.2 The Π/Γ decomposition (G-B0 taxonomy PASS; architecture matches Lemma UB0 §1 verbatim).** 1 − q = P(Π) + P(Γ) + err.
- **Π = window-saddle preemption:** "a window saddle adjacent to x_M with its other branch to a max above b forces D(x_M) ≠ x_S" (record verbatim). The summit window-disk INTERIOR carries pure loop saddles — bothM = 1.0000 measured, non-qualifying — while its rim merges with the arch filament: one ridge, one Π mechanism. **Conservativity note:** counting loop saddles too is conservative — the upper bound is unharmed.
- **Γ = direct gain coincidence:** x_S's second branch to a max with gain ∈ (0, ℓ) — already rigidity-killed at C020 (below).
- **Terminology collision registered (canon addendum):** C020's "rim" = the intensity ridge in ỹ-space; C032+'s "rim" = the mean-surface structure in x-space. Distinct objects; the lexicon (file 01 §5) carries the note.

**§1.3 The near mass and THE divergence refutation (G-B2).** 6-pin window-saddle mass on B₃∖collars = **0.657·r³ (r = 0.025) / 0.661·r³ (r = 0.05), rung ratio 1.01** — the r³-coefficient is r-FREE. **The historical divergence and its artifact explanation:** the C023 route's coefficient grew like r^{−1.88} (masses 2.07 → 7.31·r³; the E1 correction record) because that decomposition was PER-CANDIDATE — the moderate zone needed terminal selectivity only under that framing; the global count never sees it. The divergence was an artifact of the decomposition, not of the object.

**§1.4 The exterior count (G-B3).** Derived density ρ_sad(1.2) = 0.030449 (file 02b §3 class, two-route-verified) × window width ℓ (exact) × area (L² − π·9) × **E_sup6 = 1.014** — the 6-pin exterior transfer, station-certified: λ₆/λ_unc = 0.978–1.004 at d ∈ {5, 8} × 2 angles.

**§1.5 The typing floor (G-B1).** P(typed | 6 pins) = 0.7996 (r = 0.025) / 0.7935 (r = 0.05) — stable, 16× above the frozen floor; used as 0.80. **Limit annotation:** the r → 0 limit is the fluctuation-law constant (mean Hessians are O(r)); the limit formality is carried by the GRID class (§4 annotations).

**§1.6 The Γ-kill (G-B4 + the C020 cross-validation).** Exit-station exponent: the 6-pin eastward mean profile from S crosses b immediately; **E_ay = 91.6 at t = 0.1 (13.5σ)**, decaying as the horizon releases — the kill lives exactly at the exit ridge. Historical importance-sampling cross-validation (C020): exit ridge elevated 4.6–9.7σ above b; **zero typed events in 13,700 flows; Kac–Rice ceiling 2.6e-10.** The two validations agree at the same geometric locus. Γ contributes e⁻⁹² to the bound. [Pointer: the C020 protocol details live in Pinning_Module_C020.md, archive; the figures consumed here are as the C038 record states them.]

**§1.7 The assembly (station-certified + derived-structure, modulo the condition classes).**
  1 − q ≤ [E(N_ws(B₃∖collars) | 6, typed)] + [ρ_sad(1.2)·ℓ·(L² − π·9)·E_sup6]/P_typed + P(Γ) + [collar residue]
  ≤ (0.66 + 2.82)/0.80 · r³ + e⁻⁹² + [collar] = **4.3·r³ + e⁻⁹² + [collar class]**, both rungs, coefficient r-free by the G-B2/G-B3 structure.
**Deliberate-crudeness note (record verbatim class):** the exterior term dominates and is deliberately crude — it counts ALL exterior window saddles as interceptors, ignoring M-adjacency; tightening is available, not needed for the theorem shape. Scope note inherited from TC (canon ruling 9): the exterior constant is ∝ L²; the theorem is read at fixed L = 24 as r → 0.

---

## §2 Lemma KR-V (Kac–Rice validity under the pinned laws) — CLOSED

Three components (grade: Established-Math + derived + measured floors):
1. **Path regularity:** BF sample paths a.s. real-analytic [Established-Math].
2. **Nondegeneracy off the pins [Established-Math + two-line derived argument]:** for x ∉ {pins} and unit a: Var(a·∇f(x) | pins) = dist²_H(a·∇k_x, span{pin functionals}) > 0, because the Gaussian kernel is strictly positive definite and its point-derivative functionals at distinct points are linearly independent. **Compiled quantitative floors (measured, per zone):** 9-pin tube floors **6.9e-13 (r = 0.025) / 3.0e-11 (r = 0.05)**; exterior-crossing implied **1.4e-8** (from C033's q = 869 point); 6-pin analogs at the C038 stations. All > 0; every count in the program operates strictly inside a zone with a compiled floor.
3. **A.s. nondegeneracy of critical points:** Bulinskaya-class citations, the same hypothesis family as R0's finite verification (file 04).

---

## §3 Lemma COL (collar counting) — CLOSED, dual mechanism

**The rejected route (the recorded warning, in full).** Exclusion-radius arguments (λ_min(H_typed) vs D³) cost O(r): P(λ_min ≲ r) ~ r under the typed O(1) Hessian fluctuation — and would destroy the r³ statement. **Wrong tool** — recorded so no future cycle reaches for it.
**The operative mechanism (station-certified).** The conditional critical-point intensity at offset u from the pinned M under the 9-pin law is superexponentially killed: **λ₁ = 6.1e-241 / 5.8e-134 / 4.0e-77 / 1.6e-46 at u = 0.2r / 0.5r / 1r / 2r (r = 0.025; r = 0.05 analogous, ceiling 9.7e-14).** Mechanism: the O(r)-mean-Hessian generates a mean gradient H̄·u ≠ 0 at every u > 0, against horizon-suppressed gradient fluctuations — the C033 kill operating inside the collar. Collar count ≤ 1e-46-class: the O(r³) intent met by ~44 orders. **Registered model-misfit (preserved):** the freeze predicted the (ND′)-linear mechanism; the instrument shows rigidity-kill dominance; the power-fit α (196/62) is not a power law (exponential regime) and the rung ratio of two effective zeros is noise — both flagged, neither load-bearing.
**The theorem-grade backstop (derived, cited).** The (ND′)-chain near-diagonal law λ₂ ≤ C_nd|Δ| (one power from the degenerate-merger Jacobian; file 02a §1.4 with the Azaïs–Wschebor citation and the post-search Item-6 annotations) bounds the collar count by ∫₀^{2r} C_nd·t·2πt dt = O(r³) with no station input — the collar item is safe at derived grade even where stations are absent. The (ND′) register note records this scope extension.
Caveats (recorded): value-marginalized all-type integrand (correct for counting); 2 angles per separation (irrelevant at e⁻⁴⁶ ceilings).

---

## §4 Lemma GRID (the on-grid class, consolidated) — one lemma, one honest residue

**The single structure.** Every station-to-sup step in the program has one form: an analytic-in-x quantity (conditional means/variances/intensities — compositions of the analytic kernel through finite nonsingular linear algebra, nonsingularity by KR-V(ii)) evaluated on a δ-net; **sup ≤ net-max + δ·M**, M a measured local modulus.

Annotations carried: Λ-quadrature (E_hier, sharpened C043 to 0.0590); the UB-G near-zone WP-analog write-up; the typing-floor limit.

# 04_PART_IV_SARD_G.md
**Part of the q0 Rate Program Master Set; governed by the source-discipline rules of 00_INVENTORY_AND_TRACE.md. Program version frozen: Master v3.2 §8 + C041/C042/C043/C046 records, read at full fidelity; MorseSmale_R0_Reduction.md (C015) and MS_Shift_R0_Closure.md (project archive, 2026-07-09) read at full fidelity.**

## Table of contents
§1 Sublemma R0: statement, reduction, and the clearing-event register · §2 The prior shift-closure route (adjudicated) · §3 Lemma SARD-G, every step · §4 The verification record and the engineered testbed · §5 The independent write-up review (C046) · §6 Status and promotion semantics · Per-file completeness report

## §1 Sublemma R0

**§1.1 Statement (C015 record, verbatim class).** For a centered stationary C³ Gaussian field on T²_L under (H1+)(H2′), almost surely no gradient trajectory has its α- and ω-limits at two distinct index-1 saddles — no saddle–saddle heteroclinic connection; equivalently W^u(p) ⋔ W^s(q) for every ordered pair of index-1 saddles (the Morse–Smale property). **Why it is owed (verbatim):** "the elder-rule death-partner map, the persistence diagram, and hence Theorem A and Theorem B are only almost surely well-defined once R0 holds." Local nondegeneracy (a.s. Morse, a.s. distinct critical values) is already discharged by Bulinskaya; R0 is the GLOBAL gradient-flow constraint, and no off-the-shelf result covers it for Gaussian ensembles (statement as recorded; corroborated by the executed prior-art search, file 05 Item 1). Consequences consumed downstream: well-definedness of q; "terminal of an ascent is a local max" (Lemmas TC and MF-C′).

**§1.2 The C015 reduction (grade: reduction, honest — "this document does NOT prove R0").**
- *Geometry (established, standard):* under ẋ = ∇f an index-1 saddle in 2D has 1-dimensional W^u and W^s; a connection is a shared orbit — a codimension-1 (non-transverse) incidence, since two 1-manifolds sharing a 1-dimensional orbit inside a 2-manifold cannot cross transversally along it. Morse–Smale ⇔ all intersections transverse ⇔ no connections.
- *Defect and submersion (established, conditional):* for a candidate connection through an interior point x₀, fix a transversal Σ; D(f) = signed separation on Σ between the forward image of W^u(p) and the backward image of W^s(q); D = 0 iff a connection through x₀ exists. Perturb f ↦ f + h in the Cameron–Martin space H; the proposal: h ↦ dD is surjective onto ℝ provided ∇h(x₀) can be prescribed freely while holding the saddle data fixed — "free interior steering."
- *Finite nondegeneracy (VERIFIED, dps 40):* free steering reduces to nondegeneracy of the conditional law of ∇f(x₀) given the full 2-jets at p and q. P-M1: the 18×18 covariance of the three full 2-jets is nonsingular at every configuration tested; symmetric collinear-midpoint case certified — det₁₈ = 1.06e-36 > 0, conditional-gradient eigenvalues (4.817e-8, 1.607e-4), minimum strictly positive. P-M2: positive-definite across a separation/offset sweep, degenerating only as x₀ → p or q; smallest-but-positive transverse eigenvalue on the symmetry axis (the would-be axis-connection configuration). P-M3 subsumed: the conditioning holds all twelve endpoint jet functionals fixed, Hessians included.
- *The named crux (OPEN at C015):* **MS-Sard** — translating "a.e. Cameron–Martin shift" into "almost-sure f under the Gaussian law," uniformly over the continuum of candidate (p, q, orbit) configurations; recorded as having no directly citable reference for path-space transversality of a Gaussian gradient flow. A named acceptable alternative (an explicit justified Morse–Smale ASSUMPTION under the open-spectral-density hypothesis) was documented for deferred closure.

**§1.3 The clearing-event register (complete, chronological).** The pre-committed condition (set at the v3.0 build, C045): R0's condition-list status changes from "open crux" to "resolved at program grade, retained as external-review marker" if and only if [adversarial audit passed] ∧ [plumbing write-up issued] ∧ [prior-art executed with no prior proof found]. Events:
1. **C041 — closure candidate registered** (Lemma SARD-G derived + instrument-verified; R0 kept OPEN by pre-commitment; audit checklist pre-listed).
2. **C042 — adversarial audit:** skeleton AFFIRMED on every gate that tests the mathematics (G-A1 exact; G-A3′ 0.32%; AU-1 injectivity re-derivation PASS; AU-2 plumbing enumerated, all fixable-class, none structural); the explicit-G quadrature protocol FAILED at 10% precision, fully diagnosed as the instrument item (§3 Step 2), not a lemma defect.
3. **C043 — plumbing write-up issued** (all six items discharged at standard-technique grade; §3 Step 4-plumbing) and the instrument item CLOSED by adopting route-B as canonical (0.37%).

The SARD-G route replaces the finite basis with the Riesz representative and the kernel-injectivity argument — nonvanishing for every configuration with a nondegenerate connecting segment, with no per-configuration determinant — and was carried through audit, plumbing, and review to program grade. **The SARD-G chain governs the live text; the shift route is preserved at its recorded grade with OBL-R0-UNIF as its registered residue; no value conflict exists.** (Gap G-13 of file 00 resolves without a [CONFLICT] marker.)

## §3 Lemma SARD-G — every step

**Interface adjudication (G-X0; the free-steering history, record verbatim class).** The C015 "free interior steering" mechanism is adjudicated HEURISTIC for an analytic CM space: controlling finitely many jets leaves h uncontrolled along the rest of the orbit, and the full derivative could cancel — precisely why the step stayed open. SARD-G implies the named step by a different mechanism: nonvanishing of the derivative's Riesz representative, requiring no jet prescription. C015's verified finite nondegeneracy is retained as supporting input (the endpoint-jet structure). The two-sided defect and one-sided section-mismatch formulations are equivalent; SARD-G is stated in the latter.

**Step 1 — the mismatch functional [derived + instrument-verified formalization].** For an ordered saddle pair (p, q) and branch: the forward separatrix of p, evaluated at its first crossing of a section Σ placed in the O(1)-gradient interior near q, transverse to W^s(q); mismatch D = signed transverse offset; finite arclength; C¹ in CM perturbations by smooth ODE dependence — **per chart** (RF1: the C¹ statement is scoped to a chart on which the pair-tracking and section are fixed; global regularity is never used). **Section-placement necessity — both instrument-proven failure modes, preserved:** (i) the arc-length variational structure is singular at critical points (the 1/|∇f| factor) — the naive launch-integration runs blew up at 10⁵³–10¹⁴⁶ (the exhibit, preserved in c041_identity.json); (ii) the terminal funnel of a MAX is transversally contracting and degenerate for offsets — a section there collapsed the weights (route C ≈ 0); the section near the target SADDLE (expanding side) is not merely convenient but required. **Connection ⇔ D = 0, per chart** (RF5: within a chart, the first-crossing offset vanishes iff the separatrix lies on W^s(q) there; the chart family covers all connections by Step-4 item (i)).

**Step 2 — the Riesz representative [derived + verified].** D_h = ⟨h, G⟩_H with
  G = ∫ a(t)·∇₂k(·, γ(t)) dt + endpoint atoms,
the curve part running along the connecting segment γ with scalar weight a(t) = the transverse-adjoint solution composed through the interior propagator; the atoms: at p, the saddle-displacement term −H(p)⁻¹∇h(p) and the unstable-eigenvector rotation (standard eigenperturbation — the planar saddle's eigenvalues are simple, λ_s < 0 < λ_u, so the perturbation series is the textbook one: the eigenvalue-simplicity note); at the q end, the mirror atom set (saddle displacement −H(q)⁻¹∇h + stable-eigenvector rotation) composed through the short arc. **Why the scalar adjoint never vanishes (AU-1 sharpening):** the transverse adjoint is a SCALAR EXPONENTIAL — an exponential of a bounded integral along the compact segment — hence strictly positive throughout (numerically: all-positive weights in every run). **The endpoint tail law (audit discovery, added to the statement):** near each saddle a(s) ~ s^ν with ν = |λ_transverse|/λ_departure; the curve integrand behaves as s^{ν−1} — integrable but slow; **measured ν = 0.167 at BOTH ends = 1/6, exactly the theory's own prediction** from the scalar-exponential adjoint form. **H-convergence in the load-bearing time parametrization (RF2):** in time parametrization the weight a(t) decays exponentially (the approach to a hyperbolic saddle is exponential in t) while the kernel-gradient sections ∇₂k(·, γ(t)) have uniformly bounded H-norm; the defining integral therefore converges absolutely in H; the s^{ν−1} behavior is the arclength shadow of the same object, relevant only to quadrature, not to existence. **Route-B is canonical; explicit quadrature is not:** three explicit-G quadrature protocols FAILED-AS-WRITTEN — uniform nodes s₀ = 0.05 → 22%; s₀ = 0.01 → 33% (refinement WORSENED it — the tell); geometric ladder to 2e-3 + leading-order analytic tails → 36% — diagnosed by the tail law (any finite truncation misses an O(1) fraction: (2e-3)^{1/6} = 0.35; leading-order tail formulas a_min·(n·∇h)/|λ_t| recover only part; matched asymptotics beyond leading order would be needed). The pairing itself is computed assembly-free by route-B — the transverse variational ODE integrated section-to-section, seeded by the endpoint-atom compositions at s₀ = 0.01 — agreeing with full FD at **0.37%** (0.272278 vs 0.273289); adopted as the canonical evaluator; explicit-G kernel quadrature demoted to illustrative.

**Step 3 — G ≢ 0, always [Established-Math + derived + verified].** The BF spectral density e^{−|ξ|²/2} > 0 everywhere (Bochner) ⟹ the kernel embedding of compactly supported finite-order distributions into H is injective: ‖h_T‖²_H = ∫|T̂(ξ)|²K̂(ξ)dξ with K̂ > 0 and T̂ continuous (Paley–Wiener: compact support + finite order), so h_T = 0 ⟹ T̂ ≡ 0 ⟹ T = 0. G = 0 would therefore equate a curve measure with continuous, NONVANISHING density a(t)·n(t) (Step 2) with a finite atomic jet distribution at the endpoints — impossible by support: test functions supported at INTERIOR arc points (avoiding both endpoint atom sets) isolate the curve part, which cannot vanish. **Truncation-free note:** the injectivity/support argument uses no quadrature and is unaffected by the tail law — the tail is still a curve measure with nonvanishing density. **The nondegenerate-connecting-segment definition (RF3):** the hypothesis is nondegeneracy of the ENDPOINT saddles (Morse at p and q — a.s. by Bulinskaya); interior regularity of the segment is automatic (∇f ≠ 0 along a connecting orbit strictly between critical points). Hence: for every configuration with a nondegenerate connecting segment, some CM direction has dD ≠ 0. Numerical instantiation (G-X2): ‖G_curve‖² = 4e-4 > 0 on the test segment with non-collapsed weights (min|∇f| = 1.53 on the section-to-section segment; adjoint weights aw ∈ [0.17, 0.999]).

**Step 4 — countable-dense selection + 1-D Cameron–Martin Fubini [standard-technique write-up].** Take {h_j} dense in the CM unit ball. Every zero of the mismatch is j-regular for some j (Step 3: dD ≠ 0 in some direction; density supplies a witness). Along each h_j-line, j-regular zeros are isolated (nonvanishing derivative in the line coordinate). The CM coordinate's conditional law given the orthogonal complement is a nondegenerate 1-D Gaussian, so isolated zeros ⟹ per-(pair, branch, chart, j) connection probability 0; critical points are a.s. locally finite and Morse (Bulinskaya, cited); the countable union over pairs, branches, charts, and j gives **P(∃ saddle–saddle connection) = 0**.

**The six measurability plumbing items (C043 G-C3; each with argument and citation class):**
1. **Chart covering.** Nondegenerate saddle pairs persist on open ε-intervals (implicit function theorem on ∇f_ε at the saddle; Hessian nondegeneracy is open). Cover the ε-line by the countable family of maximal rational-endpoint subintervals on which a chosen pair-tracking (continuous Newton selection from rational seeds) stays nondegenerate, each chart equipped with a section from a countable family (lines with rational base points and directions; transversality is an open condition). Every connection between nondegenerate saddles lies in some chart. [RF4 expansion carried in the live text: the covering uses the rational section AND a rational tube around the tracked segment, with the first crossing tube-local, so the chart's mismatch is well-defined without global orbit knowledge.] [IFT; openness.]
2. **Degenerate-ε events.** Connections involving a degenerate saddle require (∇f_ε(x), det Hf_ε(x)) = (0, 0, 0): three analytic equations in (x, y, ε); for each ω the solution set is a countable union of points or analytic arcs; an arc's ε-projection is either null or contains an interval — the interval case is excluded a.s. by Bulinskaya applied at each rational ε plus continuity; the residual null ε-set is absorbed. [Analyticity; Bulinskaya.]
3. **Measurable section selection.** The chart construction selects sections by the FIRST rational index satisfying transversality — a measurable selection (countable infimum of measurable conditions). [Measurable selection, countable form.]
4. **Flow measurability.** The flow map of an a.s.-C² field is jointly measurable in (ω, x, t) (Carathéodory solutions with smooth dependence; standard); first-crossing times of fixed sections are measurable (hitting times of closed sets by continuous adapted paths). [ODE smooth dependence; hitting-time measurability.]
5. **Per-j regularity.** {⟨h_j, G(ω)⟩ ≠ 0} is measurable: the pairing with a fixed h_j equals the route-B functional — a composition of the flow map, Newton-selected saddle data, and integrals of measurable integrands. [Composition of measurable maps.]
6. **Union bookkeeping.** The connection event = ∪_pairs ∪_branches ∪_charts ∪_j {j-regular connection in chart}; each term has conditional probability 0 by the 1-D CM disintegration (nondegenerate Gaussian coordinate; isolated zeros ⟹ Lebesgue-null); countable union ⟹ 0. [CM disintegration: Bogachev.]

**Step 5.** Conclusion = Sublemma R0 as stated at C015, under (H1+)(H2′), BF satisfying both.

# CLAIM LANGUAGE ANNEX v1.0 (C047) — the calibrated novelty language for external distribution
**Companion to Master v3.1/v3.2 (verification lives there; claims live here). Every sentence below is constrained by the pre-committed rules CR1–CR7 (C047_Freeze). Ruling tags refer to Master §9.2. This Annex is the ONLY licensed source of novelty language for any external document derived from the program.**

## A0 — Global methodology block (for the paper's introduction; use verbatim or tighter)
"Prior-art status throughout reflects a documented literature search (July 2026; query log reproduced in the master document) across arXiv, journal databases, and general indices, with targeted follow-ups on the flagged residuals. All 'to our knowledge' statements are calibrated to that documented search and are not assertions of exhaustive absence; for the parity-law claim (Item 8) the search is explicitly incomplete and a zbMATH/INSPIRE pass is outstanding."

## A1 — The Morse–Smale theorem [Item 1: NO-CLOSE-MATCH-FOUND, follow-up-confirmed]
CLAIM (theorem-level): "We prove that a smooth Gaussian random field with Bargmann–Fock covariance is almost surely Morse–Smale: almost surely no gradient trajectory connects two saddle points. To our knowledge [Item 1: NO-CLOSE-MATCH-FOUND], no proof of this statement for any Gaussian ensemble has previously appeared: the literature establishes the almost-sure Morse property (Adler–Taylor 2007; Nicolaescu, arXiv:1209.0639) and an infinite-dimensional probabilistic Thom transversality theorem for JETS (Lerario–Stecconi, arXiv:1902.03805), which is local and does not by itself yield the global heteroclinic condition; deterministic genericity (Kupka 1963/64; Smale 1963; Peixoto 1962; Abraham–Robbin 1967) concerns residual sets rather than probability-one statements for a fixed Gaussian measure; and applied work constructs the Morse–Smale complex of Gaussian fields under an informal genericity assumption (Feldbrugge et al., arXiv:1908.01619)."
CLAIM (mechanism-level): "The proof mechanism — showing the Riesz representative of a heteroclinic-defect derivative is nonzero via injectivity of the Gaussian-kernel embedding of compactly supported finite-order distributions, then closing with a one-dimensional Cameron–Martin disintegration over a countable dense family — combines two established toolkits (characteristic-kernel injectivity: Sriperumbudur–Fukumizu–Lanckriet, JMLR 2011; Cameron–Martin disintegration: Bogachev 1998) in a way we have not found applied to transversality of random fields [Item 1c: NO-CLOSE-MATCH-FOUND]; the nearest Melnikov-type literature treats random TEMPORAL forcing of deterministic landscapes (stochastic-Melnikov escape criteria; Wiggins' modified method), not Cameron–Martin perturbations of a random landscape."
DISCLOSURE (CR7): "Key identities of the proof were additionally verified numerically — a three-route agreement (finite-difference vs variational vs adjoint pairing) at 0.00–1.96%, endpoint-atom formulas at 0.01–0.32%, and an engineered exact-heteroclinic testbed with route-B agreement at 0.37% — and the written argument passed an internal adversarial audit and an independent write-up review; all protocols are reproducible from the master document."
FORBIDDEN for this item: "settles a long-standing open problem"; "the first genericity result for random fields" (jet transversality is one); bare "novel"; any claim that the statement was previously POSED as open.

## A2 — The pairing-defect rate [Item 2: NO-CLOSE-MATCH-FOUND; confirmed by targeted follow-up, not exhaustive]
CLAIM: "Our main theorem gives, to our knowledge [Item 2: NO-CLOSE-MATCH-FOUND, follow-up-confirmed], the first explicit quantitative result on persistence-pairing defects for smooth Gaussian fields: the probability that a fold pair's elder-rule death partner differs from its geometric partner is Θ(r³) with two-sided r-free constants. The expected-persistence-diagram framework (Chazal–Divol, arXiv:1802.10457) and limit theorems for stationary-process persistence (Thomas, arXiv:2407.07326) address global diagram statistics; Betti/persistence statistics of planar Gaussian fields are fitted via the Morse–Smale complex in Feldbrugge et al. (arXiv:1908.01619); and the cosmological critical-events formalism (Cadiou–Pichon et al., arXiv:2309.11558) studies peak-saddle persistent pairs under scale filtration — none, per our documented and follow-up-confirmed but non-exhaustive search, computes a pairing-defect probability or its small-separation rate."
FORBIDDEN: bare "the first"; "solves the pairing problem"; omitting the non-exhaustive qualifier.

## A3 — Horizon and rim [Item 3: KNOWN-IN-PART]
CITE (the known part first, CR6): "The conditional-variance collapse near conditioning points is the classical screening effect of kriging (Stein, arXiv:1203.1801); conditional-mean profiles around a single conditioned peak go back to BBKS (ApJ 304, 1986); Palm-type conditioning at critical points of the Bargmann–Fock field appears in arXiv:2602.20434."
CLAIM: "The quantitative horizon profile under multi-point JET conditioning, and in particular the one-sided rim/valley angular anatomy of the conditional mean around a near-collinear critical triple, have to our knowledge [Item 3: unlocated part] not been described."
FORBIDDEN: claiming variance screening itself; "we discover conditional-variance suppression."

## A4 — The global counting device [Item 4: KNOWN-IN-PART]
CITE: "Value-window Kac–Rice counts are standard (Cheng–Schwartzman, Bernoulli 2018; Muirhead, SPL 2020; Estrade–Fournier, SPL 2016)."
CLAIM: "The reduction we employ — bounding gradient-flow OUTCOME probabilities by the expected number of band-valued critical points, replacing trajectory tracking entirely — is to our knowledge [Item 4: unlocated part] not in the literature as a device for persistence questions."
FORBIDDEN: claiming band counting itself.

## A5 — Shadowing and the launch cone [Item 5: KNOWN-IN-PART]
CITE: "Quantitative shadowing of deterministic flow under small random perturbation is classical Freidlin–Wentzell theory, and for gradient flows of Morse potentials, Hu–Li–Yang (arXiv:1706.00837) prove O(ln ε⁻¹) convergence."
CLAIM: "Conditional-MEAN-flow shadowing with superexponential failure bounds under jet conditioning, and the launch-direction concentration law at a pinned saddle (unstable-eigenvector scatter σ ≈ 0.023 rad with an r-stable composed exponent), are to our knowledge [Item 5: unlocated part] new in this setting."
FORBIDDEN: claiming Freidlin–Wentzell or Hu–Li–Yang content.

## A6 — Near-diagonal repulsion [Item 6: KNOWN — cite only, CR5]
CITE: "We use the near-diagonal two-point behavior of planar critical points as established: Beliaev–Cammarota–Wigman (ECP 2020, arXiv:1911.03455); Ladgham–Lachièze-Rey (SPA 2023; same-type hard repulsion); Azaïs–Delmas (SPA 2022; index-resolved attraction/neutrality/repulsion)."
NO CLAIM LANGUAGE IS LICENSED FOR THIS ITEM.

## A7 — Thermodynamic package [Item 7: KNOWN-IN-PART; preprint provisionality in-text]
CITE: "Persistence entropy is standard (Atienza–González-Díaz–Soriano-Trigueros, arXiv:1701.07857); partition-function framings appear in recent preprints (arXiv:2603.27903; arXiv:2602.09058) which are not yet peer-reviewed and whose specific values we treat as provisional."
CLAIM: "The topological-second-law formulation we propose is to our knowledge [Item 7: unlocated part] not in the literature."
FORBIDDEN: treating the 2026 preprints' values as established; bare "novel."

## A8 — The ΔJ parity law [Item 8: KNOWN-IN-PART; INCOMPLETE-SEARCH FLAG STANDS, in-text per CR4]
CITE: "Sensitivity of persistence statistics to local (f_NL) non-Gaussianity is established empirically: Cole–Shiu (JCAP 2018, arXiv:1712.08159) on CMB maps (Δf_NL = 35.8 at 68% CL versus 60.6 for Betti curves) and Biagetti–Cole–Shiu (JCAP 2021, arXiv:2009.04819) on large-scale structure — distinct settings not to be conflated; Minkowski-functional perturbation theory (Matsubara, arXiv:2011.04954; arXiv:1001.2321) is the closest analytic analogue, with first-order corrections governed by odd/skewness terms."
CLAIM: "The specific parity law — that only the odd part of log g′ contributes at first order to the persistence asymmetry functional ΔJ for f = g(F) — is to our knowledge not in the literature; we flag explicitly that our search on this item is incomplete [Item 8: flag stands; zbMATH/INSPIRE outstanding] and the priority claim is correspondingly provisional."
FORBIDDEN: unflagged parity-law priority claims; conflating the CMB and LSS results.

## §5 Rule R5 — rigor calibration, formalized as an annex rule
**R5 (extends CR7 across the master set).** Wherever a result rests on measured, station-certified, or on-grid inputs, the text says so AT THE POINT OF CLAIM, not only in the grade label. **Licensed pattern:** "a rate theorem whose structural argument is exact and whose two-sided constants are certified by the reproducible instrument protocols of the reproduction section" (and grade-accurate variants that name the instrument dependence in the claiming sentence). **Forbidden pattern:** bare "we prove Θ(r³)", or any phrasing presenting instrument-certified constants as proved in the classical unconditional sense. Numerical verification is disclosed as reproducible support for written arguments, never as a substitute for them. This rule binds every file of the set; files 01 §8, 02a §6, 02b §6, 03 §5, and 04 §6 carry its application sentences at their points of claim.

## §1 Reproduction protocols P1–P8 and failure semantics (verbatim extraction, Master v3.2 §11)

## §11 Reproduction protocols (what to run, in what environment, expected outputs)

**Environment:** Python 3 with mpmath (mp.dps = 40) and numpy; no network required. All protocols are self-contained given §1.2's covariance specification.
**P1 (covariance layer):** implement cov(P, a, Q, c) per §1.2; run the 13 closed-form checks; expected: all ≤ 1e-25.
**P2 (the tilt constant):** build the 6-pin Gram at rungs r = 0.025, 0.0125; Schur-reduce y's gradient block; compute (μ_t − b)/ℓ; expected: → −0.4999290 with O(r) approach.
**P3 (the integrand):** evaluate λ(ỹ*) per §4.1; expected 3.4755. Assemble the 730-station grid (or any refinement ladder h = 1/5 → 1/40 over the same domain); expected ∫ = 0.9091 with the §4.2 error budget reproducible from the same ladder's second differences.
**P4 (densities):** sample the §5.3 Hessian-given-value law at u = 1.2 (3 independent Gaussians: H₁₁, H₂₂ ~ N(−u, 2), H₁₂ ~ N(0, 1)); expected ρ_mx(1.2) = 0.043685, ρ_sad(1.2) = 0.030449 within MC tolerance.
**P5 (the horizon and rim):** Schur the 9-pin Gram on value functionals along rays; expected v(1/2/3) = 0.018/0.55/0.976; the arch-ray mean crest 1.40–1.57 at d ≈ 1.3; monotone west descent to −1.19 relative by d = 1.9; the sole exterior band crossing at d = 0.1133 with q_kill = 869.5.
**P6 (the collar kill):** the conditional critical intensity at u = 0.2r…2r from M under the 9-pin law (value-marginalized all-type Kac–Rice integrand); expected the superexponential ladder 6e-241 → 1.6e-46 at r = 0.025.
**P7 (SARD-G, complete on a laptop):** implement f₀ and the breaker per §8.3; verify D(0) = 0 exactly, D(±0.02) = ±0.01488, slope 0.7441; run route-B (transverse variational ODE + atom seeds at s₀ = 0.01) against FD at μ = 0.02 for a kernel-translate perturbation; expected agreement ≤ 0.5% (achieved: 0.37%); measure the endpoint exponent by the adjoint-weight ladder; expected ν = 1/6 at both ends.
**P8 (upper-side stations):** the 6-pin window count on B₃ ∖ collars at both rungs; expected 0.657–0.661·r³, rung ratio ≈ 1.01; typing floor 0.79–0.80; exterior ratios ≤ 1.014.
**Failure semantics:** any protocol missing its expected output at the stated tolerance falsifies the corresponding constant at its measured/station grade and must be logged, not reconciled silently.

# THE q0 RATE PROGRAM — MASTER DOCUMENT v3.2 (VERIFICATION-GRADE, FULLY SELF-CONTAINED; DISTRIBUTION-READY)
**Cycles C045–C047. Freezes b262bd0b… / 7629190f… / a3bea428…. Supersedes Master v3.0 (7b95b0c3…) and v2.0 (24ce2837…) as the citable spine; v2.0 and v1.0 remain archived. Precedence: this document governs over any conflicting archived text (supersede-never-overwrite). Design goal: every claim herein is verifiable at its declared grade FROM THIS DOCUMENT ALONE — derivations inline, instruments described with expected outputs, citations complete, ledgers total.**

---

# PART I — SETTING, CONVENTIONS, AND THE THEOREM

## §1 The field and its conventions (complete)

**§1.1 The field.** f: T²_L → ℝ, L = 24, a centered stationary Gaussian random field with Bargmann–Fock (BF) covariance
  K(u) = Cov(f(x), f(x+u)) = exp(−|u|²/2),  unit variance.
Sample paths are a.s. real-analytic (the spectral density e^{−|ξ|²/2} is entire-decaying; equivalently f is a Gaussian entire superposition). Torus periodization: the planar kernel is summed over the L·ℤ² lattice; every correction at program distances is bounded by e^{−L²/8} = e^{−72} and is ignored throughout (declared once, here).

**§1.2 Derivative conventions and the verification battery.** For multi-indices a = (a₁, a₂), Cov(∂ᵃf(P), ∂ᶜf(Q)) = (−1)^{|a|} ∂ᵃ⁺ᶜK(P−Q) with K as above; the sign convention is fixed by the following closed-form values, which any implementation MUST reproduce (this is the 78-check battery, all satisfied at ≤ 1e-25 by the program's mp implementation, mp.dps = 40):
- Var f = 1; Var ∂ᵢf = 1; Cov(f, ∂²ᵢᵢf) = −1; Var ∂²ᵢᵢf = 3; Cov(∂²ₓₓf, ∂²ᵧᵧf) = 1; Var ∂ₓᵧf = 1; all odd-total-order covariances at zero lag = 0.
- 36 stationarity/symmetry identities (exchange of arguments flips sign per |a|+|c| parity).
- 24 finite-difference vs raised-order consistencies at tolerance 1e-10.
- ∇ₓE[f(x)|pins] = E[∇f(x)|pins] verified to 7.6e-15; conditional variance by two routes (Schur complement vs residual projection) exact.
**Verification protocol:** implement cov(P, a, Q, c) by symbolic differentiation of K; run the 13 closed-form checks above; if all pass, the covariance layer is correct.

**§1.3 Scales, pins, and the estimand.** Level b = 6/5. Pair scale r ∈ {0.05, 0.025} (the two "rungs"); window depth ℓ = r³/6.
Pinned functionals (value + full gradient at three points; 9 scalar pins):
- M = (−r/2, 0) ↦ (f, ∇f) = (b, 0, 0)  [the maximum]
- S = (+r/2, 0) ↦ (b − ℓ, 0, 0)  [the fold saddle]
- y = M + r·(−0.76, 0.24) ↦ (v*, 0, 0)  [the arch companion]
where v* = clip_{[b−ℓ, b]}(μ_t), μ_t = the 6-pin (M, S only) conditional mean at y after Schur reduction on y's gradient block, and the EXACT limit
  **m := lim_{r→0} (μ_t − b)/ℓ = −0.4999290**
(NOT −½; the −½ conjecture is refuted — §4.1 gives the derivation route). The 6-pin configuration means (M, S) pins only; typed means (det H(M) > 0, tr H(M) < 0, det H(S) < 0) — M a maximum, S a saddle.
**The estimand.** q(r, b) = P(M's elder-rule death partner = S | 6-pin, typed). Sublevel filtration of −f (equivalently superlevel of f): as the level descends from +∞, M's component is born at b; it dies (merges into an older component) at the first saddle connecting it to a component born earlier; the elder rule assigns that saddle as M's death partner. q is the probability that this partner is the geometric fold partner S. **THE THEOREM: 1 − q = Θ(r³) with explicit two-sided constants (§2).**

**§1.4 The two-width rule (highest-confusion item — memorize).** The **window** = the value interval (b − ℓ, b), width ℓ: interceptor saddles must be valued here. The **band** = the value interval [v*, b], width |m|·ℓ = 0.4999290·ℓ: failing ascent terminals must be valued here (the outward branch launches at height v*). "(ℓ/2)" as a width symbol always means the band's exact width 0.4999290·ℓ; 0.5ℓ appears only as a conservative bound in upper estimates.

**§1.5 Zone lexicon (all quantitative claims in §§4–7 use these).**
- **collar(P)** = disk of radius 2r about pin P.
- **horizon** = the conditional-variance suppression: v(d) := Var(f(x) | 9 pins) at distance d from the cluster centroid = **0.018 / 0.55 / 0.976** at d = 1/2/3; 1 − O(1e-7) at d = 5. (Instrument: Schur complement of the 9-pin Gram on the value functional at x; expected outputs as stated; monotone in d.)
- **x-rim** = the 9-pin conditional MEAN surface m₉(x) exceeds b on the arch/east angular sector, with crest **1.40–1.57 above... (absolute heights; i.e. m₉ ∈ [b+0.20, b+0.37])** — precisely: m₉ reaches 1.40–1.57 (absolute) at d ≈ 1.3 on the arch side. **The rim is ONE-SIDED**: on the west sector m₉ descends monotonically, reaching b − 1.19·(1) i.e. −1.19 relative to b by d = 1.9 (the "west valley"). (Instrument: evaluate m₉ on rays; C033 audit data.)
- **ỹ-rim** = a DIFFERENT historical object (the intensity ridge in rescaled station coordinates from the C020-era analysis). Terminology collision registered; this document uses "x-rim" exclusively for the mean-surface object.
- **d₀ = 5** = the near/far split radius for exterior counting.
- **q_kill(x)** = ½·m_∇(x)ᵀ Σ_∇(x)⁻¹ m_∇(x), the mean-gradient kill exponent: P(∇f(x) = 0 near x | pins) carries the factor e^{−q_kill}.

**§1.6 Grade lexicon (every claim carries exactly one).** Established-Math (a cited standard result; full citation given at first use) · theorem (explicit self-contained construction herein) · derived (exact/closed-form herein) · derived-structure + measured constants (the argument is derived; specific constants are instrument outputs) · station-certified (a finite set of exact conditional-Gaussian evaluations with a stated coverage argument) · on-grid (station-exact + Lemma GRID §7.3) · measured (mp-verified instrument output) · named (a precise open obligation, listed §9) · standalone (correct, gate-passed, NOT load-bearing for the theorem) · superseded/retired (marked; non-load-bearing; retained in ledgers only).
Tiers for numeric bounds, always labeled: **rigorized** (measured moduli/station-certified with derived structure) / **Richardson** (extrapolation estimate) / **measured** (direct instrument value).

## §2 THE THEOREM

**Theorem A (two-sided pairing-defect rate).** For the BF field of §1.1 with the pinned typed configuration of §1.3, for all 0 < r ≤ 0.025, modulo the four-item condition set of §9.1 plus Sublemma R0 (§8):
  **0.8411·r³ ≤ 1 − q(r, b) ≤ 4.3·r³  (rigorized tier)**
with lower constant 0.8624 at the Richardson tier; the measured truth is 1 − q ≈ 0.946·r³ at r = 0.025, approaching the limit constant C*_∞ = 0.9091 from above with verified O(r) + O(r²) structure down to r = 0.003 (§4.3). Every constant is r-free; every constant traces to an inline derivation or a described instrument with expected output; nothing superseded is load-bearing (machine-checked on the 33-node dependency graph, §10.4).

**Architecture in one paragraph.** LOWER = [Λ-side: E[N_qual] = ∫Λ ≥ C*(r)·r³] × [AO-side: AO ≥ 1 − 2.24r³ − 2e⁻¹¹¹] composed through the Bonferroni reduction 1 − q ≥ E⁰[N_qual]·(1 − O(r³)) whose pair term is derived O(r⁶) (§4.4). UPPER = the decomposition 1 − q = P(Π) + P(Γ) + err, where Π (window-saddle preemption) is bounded by a GLOBAL Kac–Rice window count under the 6-pin law (Markov), Γ (gain coincidence) is rigidity-killed at e⁻⁹², and err is the closed collar class (§6). Four shared engines: the horizon, the one-sided x-rim/valley, the derived critical densities, and the exterior intensity transfer.

---

# PART II — THE LOWER SIDE

## §3 The Bonferroni reduction (derived)

**Lemma B (reduction).** Let N_qual = the number of typed arch configurations (y-points completing (M,S) to a qualifying 9-pin geometry, §4.1). Then 1 − q ≥ E⁰[N_qual]·(1 − ε_pair) with ε_pair = O(r³), because each qualifying configuration forces a pairing defect (the arch saddle at value in the window intercepts M's merge before S), and over-counting is controlled by the second factorial moment:
  E[N_qual(N_qual − 1)] ≤ [far pairs: decorrelation constant C_dec ≤ 2 at separations > d₀, station-certified ratios §5.4] + [near pairs: the near-diagonal law λ₂ ≤ C_nd|Δ| — Established-Math post-search, see §9.2 Item 6 (Beliaev–Cammarota–Wigman; Ladgham–Lachièze-Rey) — integrating to O(r⁶) over the pair domain of measure O(r³)·O(r³)].
Grade: derived, with the near-diagonal input now carrying full citations (§9.2).

## §4 The Λ-side: E[N_qual] = C*(r)·r³

**§4.1 The integrand (derived-exact).** By Kac–Rice under the 6-pin law, E[N_qual] = ∫ Λ(y) dy with

in the rescaled frame ỹ = (y − M)/r. Every factor has a removable-singularity rational expression in r (the "regularizing frame"); the r → 0 limits are EXACT rationals-and-Gaussians:

- the numerator |det| product collapses (the numerator product lemma: the three Hessian blocks decouple in the limit) so the limit integrand is FULLY closed-form, no Monte Carlo: λ(ỹ) = [e^{−q∞(ỹ)/2}/(2π√c₆)] · P_win∞ · |c_M c_S c_Y| · 1_typed∞ / den∞, with λ(ỹ*) = 3.4755 at ỹ* = (−0.76, 0.24).

AO = P(the y-saddle's M-side separatrix reaches M AND the outward terminal has value > b | 9-pin typed). **AO ≥ 1 − 0.213r³ − 2.03r³ − 2e⁻¹¹¹ = 1 − 2.24·r³ − 2e⁻¹¹¹**, modulo R0. Components:

**§5.1 (R1, monotone ascent; derived).** Gradient ascent is height-monotone; the outward branch launches at height v* = b − 0.4999290·ℓ, so every point of the trajectory has height ≥ v*; a terminal (a critical point, a maximum modulo R0) that fails the qualification has value in the band [v*, b].

Argument: zone decomposition of the disk of radius 3 — the rigidity zone (mean-gradient kill: contribution 3.6e-15), the transition annulus (station-certified intensity), the outer annulus (transfer ratios) — each zone's Kac–Rice integral bounded by stations + GRID; the ℓ-scaling verified across the octave: the count scales as 7.76/8.19 ≈ 8 = the ℓ-ratio (r³ ratio), confirming the window-width mechanism.

On B₅ the band-max count is ≤ 2.1·(band width).

**§5.4 (Lemma TC, terminal counting — the supersession; station-certified, audited).** {outward terminal ≤ b} ⊆ {separatrix loop} ∪ {∃ band-valued maximum on T² ∖ collar(M)} (terminals are maxima modulo R0; the loop case is closed by §5.5). Only the band can fail (§5.1), and band-maxima are counted GLOBALLY — no trajectory tracking:
  P(terminal ≤ b | 9) ≤ P(sep-loop) + 2.1·(0.4999290ℓ) [B₅] + ρ_mx·0.4999290ℓ·(L² − π·25)·E_sup [exterior] = P(sep-loop) + **2.03·r³**,
with E_sup = **1.0235** the station-certified sup of the conditional/unconditional intensity ratio outside d₀ (measured ratios 0.98–1.014 at d = 5–12, both rungs, monotone pull to underflow).

## §7 The formalities (all closed or one-lemma)

**§7.1 Lemma KR-V (Kac–Rice validity; CLOSED).** (i) a.s. analytic paths (§1.1). (ii) Nondegeneracy off the pins: the Gaussian kernel is strictly positive definite, hence its point-derivative functionals at distinct points are linearly independent, hence Var(a·∇f(x) | pins) = dist²_H(a·∇k_x, span{pin functionals}) > 0 for all x ∉ {pins}, |a| = 1. # PART IV — WELL-DEFINEDNESS: SUBLEMMA R0 AND LEMMA SARD-G

## §8 The Morse–Smale sublemma (post-search status: closure candidate, complete modulo write-up review)

**§8.1 R0 (statement).** A.s., the gradient flow of f has no saddle-to-saddle heteroclinic connection (equivalently: all stable/unstable manifold intersections are transverse; f is a.s. Morse–Smale). Consequences used: the elder-rule death partner is a.s. well-defined and stable under the flow decompositions of §5 ("terminals are maxima," Lemma TC/MF).

**§8.2 Post-search register status (per the pre-committed condition of C041–C043).** The pre-committed condition for status change was: adversarial audit passed (C042: skeleton affirmed) + plumbing issued (C043) + prior-art executed. All three cleared, and additionally (C046): the flagged companion arXiv:1906.04444 was read (orthogonal — polynomial singularity topology, not heteroclinics), the Melnikov and pairing residual searches were run (rulings confirmed; boundary and close-genre citations added, §9.2), and the INDEPENDENT WRITE-UP REVIEW of §8.3 was conducted against the pre-committed checklist RC1–RC4: verdict STRUCTURALLY SOUND, five precision-class findings RF1–RF5, all incorporated below, zero structural findings (C046_Review.md, full reasoning shown). The prior-art Item-1 ruling stands: NO-CLOSE-MATCH-FOUND — no published theorem proves a.s. Morse–Smale for smooth Gaussian fields (a.s. Morse: Adler–Taylor 2007, Nicolaescu arXiv:1209.0639; local jet transversality only: Lerario–Stecconi arXiv:1902.03805; deterministic residual/dense: Kupka–Smale, Peixoto, Abraham–Robbin; and the applied literature ASSUMES the property without proof — Feldbrugge et al. arXiv:1908.01619 use the Morse–Smale complex of 2D Gaussian fields with an informal genericity remark). Accordingly:
**R0 register status: RESOLVED AT PROGRAM GRADE via Lemma SARD-G — derived + verified + audited (C042) + independently write-up-reviewed (C046). External referee review remains for publication, as for every result in the program. The theorem's §9.1 entry reads accordingly; the theorem statement is unchanged.**

**§8.3 Lemma SARD-G (the candidate; full argument).**
**Step 1 (mismatch functional).** For an ordered saddle pair (p, q) and separatrix branch: the two-sided defect D = signed transverse separation, on a section Σ, between the forward flow-image of p's unstable branch and the backward flow-image of q's stable branch. Σ is placed in the O(1)-gradient interior transverse to W^s(q) — REQUIRED, not convenient: sections at flow termini are transversally contracting (offsets die) and the arc-length variational structure carries a 1/|∇f| singularity at critical points (both instrument-proven; the naive integrations blew up at 10⁵³–10¹⁴⁶ and the max-funnel weights collapsed to zero — preserved failure states). D is finite-arclength and, per chart (RF1), C¹ in Cameron–Martin (CM) perturbations: within a chart the first crossings are transversal by construction, so crossing time and point are C¹ by the implicit function theorem composed with smooth ODE dependence. Connection ⟺ D = 0 per chart (RF5): D = 0 forces both flow-images through the same point of the 1-D section, hence (trajectory uniqueness) the same trajectory — a connection; conversely a connection makes the first crossings coincide within the chart's tube, and connections realized through other crossing patterns are covered by other charts (plumbing (i)).
**Step 2 (Riesz representative).** For h in the CM space (the BF RKHS), D_h[D] = ⟨h, G⟩_H with
  G = ∫ a(t)·∇₂k(·, γ(t)) dt + [endpoint jet atoms at p and q],
where a(t) is the SCALAR transverse adjoint — the solution of a scalar linear ODE, hence an exponential, NEVER ZERO — and the atoms are: saddle displacement (−H(p)⁻¹∇h(p), similarly at q) and eigenvector rotation ((v_jᵀ D²h(p) v_i)/(λ_i − λ_j) · v_j), composed through the interior propagator. **Endpoint tail law:** a(s) ~ s^ν with ν = |λ_transverse|/λ_departure per end — measured ν = 0.167 = 1/6 at BOTH ends of the audit testbed, exactly the theory's own prediction — so G's curve density has integrable s^{ν−1} endpoint tails. **H-convergence (RF2, the load-bearing form):** in time parametrization a(t) decays exponentially (a ~ e^{−|λ_transverse|·Δt}) while ‖∇₂k(·, γ(t))‖_H = 1 uniformly, so ∫‖a∇₂k‖_H dt < ∞ absolutely — G is a well-defined H-element and D_h a bounded functional; the arclength s^{ν−1} law is this fact's reparametrized shadow and explains only the quadrature slowness. The eigenvalue-simplicity hypothesis for the rotation atoms is automatic in 2D (λ_u > 0 > λ_s). Because those tails converge slowly, explicit kernel-quadrature of G is NOT the evaluator; the **canonical evaluator is route-B**: the section-to-section transverse variational ODE seeded by the atom compositions.
**Verification record (all inline):** interior three-route identity (FD vs variational vs adjoint pairing): 0.00% / 1.96%; p-atoms 0.01%; q-atoms 0.32%; route-B on the full two-sided defect of the engineered heteroclinic: **0.37%** (0.272278 vs 0.273289); ‖G_curve‖² > 0 with non-collapsed weights on a certified-interior segment.
**The engineered testbed (reproduce it):** f₀ = −y²(1 − 2x)/2 + 3x² − 2x³ has an EXACT saddle-saddle connection (0,0) → (1,0) along the invariant axis y = 0 (check: ∂f/∂y = −y(1−2x) vanishes on the axis; the on-axis profile w = 3x² − 2x³ has w′ = 6x(1−x) > 0 between the endpoints; the transverse curvature −(1−2x) changes sign, making (0,0) unstable-along-x/stable-along-y and (1,0) the reverse — both genuine saddles). Break with μ·y·e^{−8(x−1/2)²}: the defect satisfies D(0) = 0 EXACTLY, D(±0.02) = ±0.01488 (antisymmetric), transversal slope dD/dμ = 0.7441.
**Step 3 (G ≢ 0, always).** The BF spectral density K̂(ξ) = e^{−|ξ|²/2} > 0 everywhere (Bochner). For a compactly supported distribution T of finite order, the H-embedding satisfies ‖h_T‖²_H = ∫|T̂|²K̂ with T̂ continuous (Paley–Wiener); positivity of K̂ makes the embedding INJECTIVE. G's distribution is [a curve measure with density a(t)·n(t), nonvanishing since a is an exponential] + [finite jet atoms at p, q]. G = 0 would force the curve measure to equal minus the atoms — impossible by support (test against functions supported at interior arc points, which see only the curve part; its pairing ∫a·(n·∇φ) can be made nonzero). TRUNCATION-FREE: the s^{ν−1} tails are irrelevant here. **Definition (RF3):** a nondegenerate connecting segment = a heteroclinic between two NONDEGENERATE saddles (the chart hypothesis); interior regularity is then automatic — a critical point interior to the trajectory would be a third limit point, impossible for a maximal trajectory between two saddles, so ∇f ≠ 0 on the interior and the arc is locally C¹ with nonvanishing density a·n. Hence for every configuration carrying a nondegenerate connecting segment, SOME CM direction has D_h ≠ 0.
**Historical note (why the step was open):** the earlier proposed mechanism — "free interior steering," prescribing h's jet at an interior point while holding saddle jets fixed — is heuristic for an ANALYTIC CM space: controlling finitely many jets leaves h uncontrolled along the rest of the orbit and the full derivative could cancel. The injectivity route replaces it; the kernel-injectivity mechanism itself is KNOWN in a different field (kernel embeddings of measures: Sriperumbudur–Fukumizu–Lanckriet, §9.2 Item 1c) but its application to saddle-connection breaking is not located (§9.2).
**Step 4 (countable-dense selection + 1-D CM Fubini).** Fix {h_j} dense in the CM unit ball. Every zero of D is j-regular for some j (Step 3). Along each h_j-line, j-regular zeros are isolated (C¹, nonzero derivative at the zero) hence Lebesgue-null; the h_j-coordinate's conditional law given the orthogonal complement is a nondegenerate 1-D Gaussian, so the per-(pair, branch, chart, j) connection probability is 0; critical points are a.s. locally finite and Morse (Bulinskaya; Adler–Taylor), so the union is countable, giving P(∃ saddle-saddle connection) = 0.
**The measurability plumbing (all six items, discharged):** (i) chart covering (expanded per RF4) — nondegenerate pairs persist on open ε-intervals (implicit function theorem); given a connection at (f₀, ε₀), choose a RATIONAL section Σ transverse to the trajectory near q and a RATIONAL tube T around the compact trajectory segment such that within T the forward separatrix's FIRST crossing of Σ is the connection crossing; transversality and tube-containment are open conditions, so both choices persist on an open ε-interval, and rational density supplies a countable family realizing every case — hence every connection between nondegenerate saddles lies in some chart, with 'first crossing' well-defined tube-locally. (ii) degenerate-ε — connections involving a degenerate saddle need (∇f_ε, det H) = 0: three analytic equations in (x, y, ε); solution sets are countable-or-arcs; the arc/interval case is excluded a.s. by Bulinskaya at rational ε plus continuity; residual null set absorbed. (iii) measurable section selection — first-rational-index satisfying transversality. (iv) flow measurability — flow maps of a.s.-C² fields are jointly measurable; first-crossing times of closed sections are hitting times of continuous adapted paths. (v) per-j regularity — {⟨h_j, G⟩ ≠ 0} is measurable: the route-B functional is a composition of the flow map, Newton-selected saddle data, and integrals of measurable integrands. (vi) union bookkeeping — over (pair, branch, chart, j), each term conditionally null. Citations class: implicit function theorem; Bulinskaya; Cameron–Martin disintegration (Bogachev, *Gaussian Measures*, AMS 1998); ODE smooth dependence.

Design goal: every claim herein is verifiable at its declared grade FROM THIS DOCUMENT ALONE — derivations inline, instruments described with expected outputs, citations complete, ledgers total.**

# PART I — SETTING, CONVENTIONS, AND THE THEOREM

## §1 The field and its conventions (complete)

**§1.1 The field.** f: T²_L → ℝ, L = 24, a centered stationary Gaussian random field with Bargmann–Fock (BF) covariance
  K(u) = Cov(f(x), f(x+u)) = exp(−|u|²/2),  unit variance.
Sample paths are a.s. real-analytic (the spectral density e^{−|ξ|²/2} is entire-decaying; equivalently f is a Gaussian entire superposition). Torus periodization: the planar kernel is summed over the L·ℤ² lattice; every correction at program distances is bounded by e^{−L²/8} = e^{−72} and is ignored throughout (declared once, here).

**§1.2 Derivative conventions and the verification battery.** For multi-indices a = (a₁, a₂), Cov(∂ᵃf(P), ∂ᶜf(Q)) = (−1)^{|a|} ∂ᵃ⁺ᶜK(P−Q) with K as above; the sign convention is fixed by the following closed-form values, which any implementation MUST reproduce (this is the 78-check battery, all satisfied at ≤ 1e-25 by the program's mp implementation, mp.dps = 40):
- Var f = 1; Var ∂ᵢf = 1; Cov(f, ∂²ᵢᵢf) = −1; Var ∂²ᵢᵢf = 3; Cov(∂²ₓₓf, ∂²ᵧᵧf) = 1; Var ∂ₓᵧf = 1; all odd-total-order covariances at zero lag = 0.
- 36 stationarity/symmetry identities (exchange of arguments flips sign per |a|+|c| parity).
- 24 finite-difference vs raised-order consistencies at tolerance 1e-10.
- ∇ₓE[f(x)|pins] = E[∇f(x)|pins] verified to 7.6e-15; conditional variance by two routes (Schur complement vs residual projection) exact.
**Verification protocol:** implement cov(P, a, Q, c) by symbolic differentiation of K; run the 13 closed-form checks above; if all pass, the covariance layer is correct.

**§1.3 Scales, pins, and the estimand.** Level b = 6/5. Pair scale r ∈ {0.05, 0.025} (the two "rungs"); window depth ℓ = r³/6.
Pinned functionals (value + full gradient at three points; 9 scalar pins):
- M = (−r/2, 0) ↦ (f, ∇f) = (b, 0, 0)  [the maximum]
- S = (+r/2, 0) ↦ (b − ℓ, 0, 0)  [the fold saddle]
- y = M + r·(−0.76, 0.24) ↦ (v*, 0, 0)  [the arch companion]
where v* = clip_{[b−ℓ, b]}(μ_t), μ_t = the 6-pin (M, S only) conditional mean at y after Schur reduction on y's gradient block, and the EXACT limit
  **m := lim_{r→0} (μ_t − b)/ℓ = −0.4999290**
(NOT −½; the −½ conjecture is refuted — §4.1 gives the derivation route). The 6-pin configuration means (M, S) pins only; typed means (det H(M) > 0, tr H(M) < 0, det H(S) < 0) — M a maximum, S a saddle.
**The estimand.** q(r, b) = P(M's elder-rule death partner = S | 6-pin, typed). Sublevel filtration of −f (equivalently superlevel of f): as the level descends from +∞, M's component is born at b; it dies (merges into an older component) at the first saddle connecting it to a component born earlier; the elder rule assigns that saddle as M's death partner. q is the probability that this partner is the geometric fold partner S. **THE THEOREM: 1 − q = Θ(r³) with explicit two-sided constants (§2).**

**§1.4 The two-width rule (highest-confusion item — memorize).** The **window** = the value interval (b − ℓ, b), width ℓ: interceptor saddles must be valued here. The **band** = the value interval [v*, b], width |m|·ℓ = 0.4999290·ℓ: failing ascent terminals must be valued here (the outward branch launches at height v*). "(ℓ/2)" as a width symbol always means the band's exact width 0.4999290·ℓ; 0.5ℓ appears only as a conservative bound in upper estimates.

**§1.5 Zone lexicon (all quantitative claims in §§4–7 use these).**
- **collar(P)** = disk of radius 2r about pin P.
- **horizon** = the conditional-variance suppression: v(d) := Var(f(x) | 9 pins) at distance d from the cluster centroid = **0.018 / 0.55 / 0.976** at d = 1/2/3; 1 − O(1e-7) at d = 5. (Instrument: Schur complement of the 9-pin Gram on the value functional at x; expected outputs as stated; monotone in d.)
- **x-rim** = the 9-pin conditional MEAN surface m₉(x) exceeds b on the arch/east angular sector, with crest **1.40–1.57 above... (absolute heights; i.e. m₉ ∈ [b+0.20, b+0.37])** — precisely: m₉ reaches 1.40–1.57 (absolute) at d ≈ 1.3 on the arch side. **The rim is ONE-SIDED**: on the west sector m₉ descends monotonically, reaching b − 1.19·(1) i.e. −1.19 relative to b by d = 1.9 (the "west valley"). (Instrument: evaluate m₉ on rays; C033 audit data.)
- **ỹ-rim** = a DIFFERENT historical object (the intensity ridge in rescaled station coordinates from the C020-era analysis). Terminology collision registered; this document uses "x-rim" exclusively for the mean-surface object.
- **d₀ = 5** = the near/far split radius for exterior counting.
- **q_kill(x)** = ½·m_∇(x)ᵀ Σ_∇(x)⁻¹ m_∇(x), the mean-gradient kill exponent: P(∇f(x) = 0 near x | pins) carries the factor e^{−q_kill}.

**§1.6 Grade lexicon (every claim carries exactly one).** Established-Math (a cited standard result; full citation given at first use) · theorem (explicit self-contained construction herein) · derived (exact/closed-form herein) · derived-structure + measured constants (the argument is derived; specific constants are instrument outputs) · station-certified (a finite set of exact conditional-Gaussian evaluations with a stated coverage argument) · on-grid (station-exact + Lemma GRID §7.3) · measured (mp-verified instrument output) · named (a precise open obligation, listed §9) · standalone (correct, gate-passed, NOT load-bearing for the theorem) · superseded/retired (marked; non-load-bearing; retained in ledgers only).
Tiers for numeric bounds, always labeled: **rigorized** (measured moduli/station-certified with derived structure) / **Richardson** (extrapolation estimate) / **measured** (direct instrument value).

## §2 THE THEOREM

**Theorem A (two-sided pairing-defect rate).** For the BF field of §1.1 with the pinned typed configuration of §1.3, for all 0 < r ≤ 0.025, modulo the four-item condition set of §9.1 plus Sublemma R0 (§8):
  **0.8411·r³ ≤ 1 − q(r, b) ≤ 4.3·r³  (rigorized tier)**
with lower constant 0.8624 at the Richardson tier; the measured truth is 1 − q ≈ 0.946·r³ at r = 0.025, approaching the limit constant C*_∞ = 0.9091 from above with verified O(r) + O(r²) structure down to r = 0.003 (§4.3). Every constant is r-free; every constant traces to an inline derivation or a described instrument with expected output; nothing superseded is load-bearing (machine-checked on the 33-node dependency graph, §10.4).

**Architecture in one paragraph.** LOWER = [Λ-side: E[N_qual] = ∫Λ ≥ C*(r)·r³] × [AO-side: AO ≥ 1 − 2.24r³ − 2e⁻¹¹¹] composed through the Bonferroni reduction 1 − q ≥ E⁰[N_qual]·(1 − O(r³)) whose pair term is derived O(r⁶) (§4.4). UPPER = the decomposition 1 − q = P(Π) + P(Γ) + err, where Π (window-saddle preemption) is bounded by a GLOBAL Kac–Rice window count under the 6-pin law (Markov), Γ (gain coincidence) is rigidity-killed at e⁻⁹², and err is the closed collar class (§6). Four shared engines: the horizon, the one-sided x-rim/valley, the derived critical densities, and the exterior intensity transfer.

# PART II — THE LOWER SIDE

## §3 The Bonferroni reduction (derived)

**Lemma B (reduction).** Let N_qual = the number of typed arch configurations (y-points completing (M,S) to a qualifying 9-pin geometry, §4.1). Then 1 − q ≥ E⁰[N_qual]·(1 − ε_pair) with ε_pair = O(r³), because each qualifying configuration forces a pairing defect (the arch saddle at value in the window intercepts M's merge before S), and over-counting is controlled by the second factorial moment:
  E[N_qual(N_qual − 1)] ≤ [far pairs: decorrelation constant C_dec ≤ 2 at separations > d₀, station-certified ratios §5.4] + [near pairs: the near-diagonal law λ₂ ≤ C_nd|Δ| — Established-Math post-search, see §9.2 Item 6 (Beliaev–Cammarota–Wigman; Ladgham–Lachièze-Rey) — integrating to O(r⁶) over the pair domain of measure O(r³)·O(r³)].
Grade: derived, with the near-diagonal input now carrying full citations (§9.2).

## §4 The Λ-side: E[N_qual] = C*(r)·r³

**§4.1 The integrand (derived-exact).** By Kac–Rice under the 6-pin law, E[N_qual] = ∫ Λ(y) dy with
  Λ(y) = φ₂(∇f(y) = 0 | 6-pin) · [Φ((b−μ_t)/s_t) − Φ((b−ℓ−μ_t)/s_t)] · E[|det H(y)| 1_typed | 9-pin @ v*] / normalizations,
in the rescaled frame ỹ = (y − M)/r. Every factor has a removable-singularity rational expression in r (the "regularizing frame"); the r → 0 limits are EXACT rationals-and-Gaussians:
- den∞ = 3.230979 (the limiting normalization determinant);
- m = −0.4999290 (the tilt constant; obtained as the limit of the Schur-reduced mean — the derivation route: expand the 6-pin Gram and cross-covariance at y in powers of r; the O(ℓ) term of μ_t − b has the stated coefficient; the deviation from −½ is genuine, produced by the gradient-block Schur correction);
- the numerator |det| product collapses (the numerator product lemma: the three Hessian blocks decouple in the limit) so the limit integrand is FULLY closed-form, no Monte Carlo: λ(ỹ) = [e^{−q∞(ỹ)/2}/(2π√c₆)] · P_win∞ · |c_M c_S c_Y| · 1_typed∞ / den∞, with λ(ỹ*) = 3.4755 at ỹ* = (−0.76, 0.24).
**Verification protocol:** implement the 6-/9-pin Schur machinery per §1.2; evaluate λ at ỹ*; expect 3.4755 ± grid tolerance; evaluate μ_t at r = 0.025 and 0.0125; the ratio (μ_t − b)/ℓ must approach −0.4999290 linearly.

**§4.2 The integral (derived-on-grid).** C*_∞ = ∫λ(ỹ) dỹ = **0.9091**, computed on a 730-station nested grid, h = 1/5 → 1/40, hierarchical refinement, zero degenerate-basis flags after the fallback basis repaired 18 stations. Error budget (post-C043): E_hier = 0.00533 (L40 regions) + 0.01748 (L20) + 0.02828 (L10 at h = 1/20, sup|D²λ| = 274) + 0.00793 (L5, sup|D²λ| = 1) = **0.0590**; the Λ-shell residual (|ỹ| < 0.15, excluded from the grid) is quantified at ±0.009. The integrand's ridge has large-but-finite curvature (sup|D²λ| ≈ 1500 at the core = a peak of 4.1 over width ~0.05): RESOLVED, not a cliff.
**Rigorized lower constant: C*(r) ≥ 0.9091 − 0.0590 − 0.009 = 0.8411.** Richardson tier: 0.8624.

# PART IV — WELL-DEFINEDNESS: SUBLEMMA R0 AND LEMMA SARD-G

## §8 The Morse–Smale sublemma (post-search status: closure candidate, complete modulo write-up review)

**§8.1 R0 (statement).** A.s., the gradient flow of f has no saddle-to-saddle heteroclinic connection (equivalently: all stable/unstable manifold intersections are transverse; f is a.s. Morse–Smale). Consequences used: the elder-rule death partner is a.s. well-defined and stable under the flow decompositions of §5 ("terminals are maxima," Lemma TC/MF).

**§8.2 Post-search register status (per the pre-committed condition of C041–C043).** The pre-committed condition for status change was: adversarial audit passed (C042: skeleton affirmed) + plumbing issued (C043) + prior-art executed. All three cleared, and additionally (C046): the flagged companion arXiv:1906.04444 was read (orthogonal — polynomial singularity topology, not heteroclinics), the Melnikov and pairing residual searches were run (rulings confirmed; boundary and close-genre citations added, §9.2), and the INDEPENDENT WRITE-UP REVIEW of §8.3 was conducted against the pre-committed checklist RC1–RC4: verdict STRUCTURALLY SOUND, five precision-class findings RF1–RF5, all incorporated below, zero structural findings (C046_Review.md, full reasoning shown). The prior-art Item-1 ruling stands: NO-CLOSE-MATCH-FOUND — no published theorem proves a.s. Morse–Smale for smooth Gaussian fields (a.s. Morse: Adler–Taylor 2007, Nicolaescu arXiv:1209.0639; local jet transversality only: Lerario–Stecconi arXiv:1902.03805; deterministic residual/dense: Kupka–Smale, Peixoto, Abraham–Robbin; and the applied literature ASSUMES the property without proof — Feldbrugge et al. arXiv:1908.01619 use the Morse–Smale complex of 2D Gaussian fields with an informal genericity remark). Accordingly:
**R0 register status: RESOLVED AT PROGRAM GRADE via Lemma SARD-G — derived + verified + audited (C042) + independently write-up-reviewed (C046). External referee review remains for publication, as for every result in the program. The theorem's §9.1 entry reads accordingly; the theorem statement is unchanged.**

**§8.3 Lemma SARD-G (the candidate; full argument).**
**Step 1 (mismatch functional).** For an ordered saddle pair (p, q) and separatrix branch: the two-sided defect D = signed transverse separation, on a section Σ, between the forward flow-image of p's unstable branch and the backward flow-image of q's stable branch. Σ is placed in the O(1)-gradient interior transverse to W^s(q) — REQUIRED, not convenient: sections at flow termini are transversally contracting (offsets die) and the arc-length variational structure carries a 1/|∇f| singularity at critical points (both instrument-proven; the naive integrations blew up at 10⁵³–10¹⁴⁶ and the max-funnel weights collapsed to zero — preserved failure states). D is finite-arclength and, per chart (RF1), C¹ in Cameron–Martin (CM) perturbations: within a chart the first crossings are transversal by construction, so crossing time and point are C¹ by the implicit function theorem composed with smooth ODE dependence. Connection ⟺ D = 0 per chart (RF5): D = 0 forces both flow-images through the same point of the 1-D section, hence (trajectory uniqueness) the same trajectory — a connection; conversely a connection makes the first crossings coincide within the chart's tube, and connections realized through other crossing patterns are covered by other charts (plumbing (i)).
**Step 2 (Riesz representative).** For h in the CM space (the BF RKHS), D_h[D] = ⟨h, G⟩_H with
  G = ∫ a(t)·∇₂k(·, γ(t)) dt + [endpoint jet atoms at p and q],
where a(t) is the SCALAR transverse adjoint — the solution of a scalar linear ODE, hence an exponential, NEVER ZERO — and the atoms are: saddle displacement (−H(p)⁻¹∇h(p), similarly at q) and eigenvector rotation ((v_jᵀ D²h(p) v_i)/(λ_i − λ_j) · v_j), composed through the interior propagator. **Endpoint tail law:** a(s) ~ s^ν with ν = |λ_transverse|/λ_departure per end — measured ν = 0.167 = 1/6 at BOTH ends of the audit testbed, exactly the theory's own prediction — so G's curve density has integrable s^{ν−1} endpoint tails. **H-convergence (RF2, the load-bearing form):** in time parametrization a(t) decays exponentially (a ~ e^{−|λ_transverse|·Δt}) while ‖∇₂k(·, γ(t))‖_H = 1 uniformly, so ∫‖a∇₂k‖_H dt < ∞ absolutely — G is a well-defined H-element and D_h a bounded functional; the arclength s^{ν−1} law is this fact's reparametrized shadow and explains only the quadrature slowness. The eigenvalue-simplicity hypothesis for the rotation atoms is automatic in 2D (λ_u > 0 > λ_s). Because those tails converge slowly, explicit kernel-quadrature of G is NOT the evaluator; the **canonical evaluator is route-B**: the section-to-section transverse variational ODE seeded by the atom compositions.
**Verification record (all inline):** interior three-route identity (FD vs variational vs adjoint pairing): 0.00% / 1.96%; p-atoms 0.01%; q-atoms 0.32%; route-B on the full two-sided defect of the engineered heteroclinic: **0.37%** (0.272278 vs 0.273289); ‖G_curve‖² > 0 with non-collapsed weights on a certified-interior segment.
**The engineered testbed (reproduce it):** f₀ = −y²(1 − 2x)/2 + 3x² − 2x³ has an EXACT saddle-saddle connection (0,0) → (1,0) along the invariant axis y = 0 (check: ∂f/∂y = −y(1−2x) vanishes on the axis; the on-axis profile w = 3x² − 2x³ has w′ = 6x(1−x) > 0 between the endpoints; the transverse curvature −(1−2x) changes sign, making (0,0) unstable-along-x/stable-along-y and (1,0) the reverse — both genuine saddles). Break with μ·y·e^{−8(x−1/2)²}: the defect satisfies D(0) = 0 EXACTLY, D(±0.02) = ±0.01488 (antisymmetric), transversal slope dD/dμ = 0.7441.
**Step 3 (G ≢ 0, always).** The BF spectral density K̂(ξ) = e^{−|ξ|²/2} > 0 everywhere (Bochner). For a compactly supported distribution T of finite order, the H-embedding satisfies ‖h_T‖²_H = ∫|T̂|²K̂ with T̂ continuous (Paley–Wiener); positivity of K̂ makes the embedding INJECTIVE. G's distribution is [a curve measure with density a(t)·n(t), nonvanishing since a is an exponential] + [finite jet atoms at p, q]. G = 0 would force the curve measure to equal minus the atoms — impossible by support (test against functions supported at interior arc points, which see only the curve part; its pairing ∫a·(n·∇φ) can be made nonzero). TRUNCATION-FREE: the s^{ν−1} tails are irrelevant here. **Definition (RF3):** a nondegenerate connecting segment = a heteroclinic between two NONDEGENERATE saddles (the chart hypothesis); interior regularity is then automatic — a critical point interior to the trajectory would be a third limit point, impossible for a maximal trajectory between two saddles, so ∇f ≠ 0 on the interior and the arc is locally C¹ with nonvanishing density a·n. Hence for every configuration carrying a nondegenerate connecting segment, SOME CM direction has D_h ≠ 0.
**Historical note (why the step was open):** the earlier proposed mechanism — "free interior steering," prescribing h's jet at an interior point while holding saddle jets fixed — is heuristic for an ANALYTIC CM space: controlling finitely many jets leaves h uncontrolled along the rest of the orbit and the full derivative could cancel. The injectivity route replaces it; the kernel-injectivity mechanism itself is KNOWN in a different field (kernel embeddings of measures: Sriperumbudur–Fukumizu–Lanckriet, §9.2 Item 1c) but its application to saddle-connection breaking is not located (§9.2).
**Step 4 (countable-dense selection + 1-D CM Fubini).** Fix {h_j} dense in the CM unit ball. Every zero of D is j-regular for some j (Step 3). Along each h_j-line, j-regular zeros are isolated (C¹, nonzero derivative at the zero) hence Lebesgue-null; the h_j-coordinate's conditional law given the orthogonal complement is a nondegenerate 1-D Gaussian, so the per-(pair, branch, chart, j) connection probability is 0; critical points are a.s. locally finite and Morse (Bulinskaya; Adler–Taylor), so the union is countable, giving P(∃ saddle-saddle connection) = 0.
**The measurability plumbing (all six items, discharged):** (i) chart covering (expanded per RF4) — nondegenerate pairs persist on open ε-intervals (implicit function theorem); given a connection at (f₀, ε₀), choose a RATIONAL section Σ transverse to the trajectory near q and a RATIONAL tube T around the compact trajectory segment such that within T the forward separatrix's FIRST crossing of Σ is the connection crossing; transversality and tube-containment are open conditions, so both choices persist on an open ε-interval, and rational density supplies a countable family realizing every case — hence every connection between nondegenerate saddles lies in some chart, with 'first crossing' well-defined tube-locally. (ii) degenerate-ε — connections involving a degenerate saddle need (∇f_ε, det H) = 0: three analytic equations in (x, y, ε); solution sets are countable-or-arcs; the arc/interval case is excluded a.s. by Bulinskaya at rational ε plus continuity; residual null set absorbed. (iii) measurable section selection — first-rational-index satisfying transversality. (iv) flow measurability — flow maps of a.s.-C² fields are jointly measurable; first-crossing times of closed sections are hitting times of continuous adapted paths. (v) per-j regularity — {⟨h_j, G⟩ ≠ 0} is measurable: the route-B functional is a composition of the flow map, Newton-selected saddle data, and integrals of measurable integrands. (vi) union bookkeeping — over (pair, branch, chart, j), each term conditionally null. Citations class: implicit function theorem; Bulinskaya; Cameron–Martin disintegration (Bogachev, *Gaussian Measures*, AMS 1998); ODE smooth dependence.
