# CLAIM LANGUAGE ANNEX v1.0 (C047) — the calibrated novelty language for external distribution
**Companion to Master v3.1/v3.2 (verification lives there; claims live here). Every sentence below is constrained by the pre-committed rules CR1–CR7 (C047_Freeze). Ruling tags refer to Master §9.2. This Annex is the ONLY licensed source of novelty language for any external document derived from the program.**

## A0 — Global methodology block (for the paper's introduction; use verbatim or tighter)
"Prior-art status throughout reflects a documented literature search (July 2026; query log reproduced in the master document) across arXiv, journal databases, and general indices, with targeted follow-ups on the flagged residuals. All 'to our knowledge' statements are calibrated to that documented search and are not assertions of exhaustive absence; for the parity-law claim (Item 8) the search is explicitly incomplete and a zbMATH/INSPIRE pass is outstanding."

## A1 — The Morse–Smale theorem [Item 1: NO-CLOSE-MATCH-FOUND, follow-up-confirmed]
CLAIM (theorem-level): "We prove that a smooth Gaussian random field with Bargmann–Fock covariance is almost surely Morse–Smale: almost surely no gradient trajectory connects two saddle points. To our knowledge [Item 1: NO-CLOSE-MATCH-FOUND], no proof of this statement for any Gaussian ensemble has previously appeared: the literature establishes the almost-sure Morse property (Adler–Taylor 2007; Nicolaescu, arXiv:1209.0639) and an infinite-dimensional probabilistic Thom transversality theorem for JETS (Lerario–Stecconi, arXiv:1902.03805), which is local and does not by itself yield the global heteroclinic condition; deterministic genericity (Kupka 1963/64; Smale 1963; Peixoto 1962; Abraham–Robbin 1967) concerns residual sets rather than probability-one statements for a fixed Gaussian measure; and applied work constructs the Morse–Smale complex of Gaussian fields under an informal genericity assumption (Feldbrugge et al., arXiv:1908.01619)."
CLAIM (mechanism-level): "The proof mechanism — showing the Riesz representative of a heteroclinic-defect derivative is nonzero via injectivity of the Gaussian-kernel embedding of compactly supported finite-order distributions, then closing with a one-dimensional Cameron–Martin disintegration over a countable dense family — combines two established toolkits (characteristic-kernel injectivity: Sriperumbudur–Fukumizu–Lanckriet, JMLR 2011; Cameron–Martin disintegration: Bogachev 1998) in a way we have not found applied to transversality of random fields [Item 1c: NO-CLOSE-MATCH-FOUND]; the nearest Melnikov-type literature treats random TEMPORAL forcing of deterministic landscapes (stochastic-Melnikov escape criteria; Wiggins' modified method), not Cameron–Martin perturbations of a random landscape."
DISCLOSURE (CR7): "Key identities of the proof were additionally verified numerically — a three-route agreement (finite-difference vs variational vs adjoint pairing) at 0.00–1.96%, endpoint-atom formulas at 0.01–0.32%, and an engineered exact-heteroclinic testbed with route-B agreement at 0.37% — and the written argument passed an internal adversarial audit and an independent write-up review; all protocols are reproducible from the master document."
FORBIDDEN for this item: "settles a long-standing open problem"; "the first genericity result for random fields" (jet transversality is one); bare "novel"; any claim that the statement was previously POSED as open.

## A2 — The pairing-defect rate [Item 2: NO-CLOSE-MATCH-FOUND; confirmed by targeted follow-up, not exhaustive]
CLAIM: "Our main theorem gives, to our knowledge [Item 2: NO-CLOSE-MATCH-FOUND, follow-up-confirmed], the first explicit quantitative result on persistence-pairing defects for smooth Gaussian fields: the probability that a fold pair's elder-rule death partner differs from its geometric partner is Θ(r³) with two-sided r-free constants. The expected-persistence-diagram framework (Chazal–Divol, arXiv:1802.10457) and limit theorems for stationary-process persistence (Thomas, arXiv:2407.07326) address global diagram statistics; Betti/persistence statistics of planar Gaussian fields are fitted via the Morse–Smale complex in Feldbrugge et al. (arXiv:1908.01619); and the cosmological critical-events formalism (Cadiou–Pichon et al., arXiv:2309.11558) studies peak-saddle persistent pairs under scale filtration — none, per our documented and follow-up-confirmed but non-exhaustive search, computes a pairing-defect probability or its small-separation rate."
FORBIDDEN: bare "the first"; "solves the pairing problem"; omitting the non-exhaustive qualifier.

## A3 — Horizon and rim [Item 3: KNOWN-IN-PART]
CITE (the known part first, CR6): "The conditional-variance collapse near conditioning points is the classical screening effect of kriging (Stein, arXiv:1203.1801); conditional-mean profiles around a single conditioned peak go back to BBKS (ApJ 304, 1986); Palm-type conditioning at critical points of the Bargmann–Fock field appears in arXiv:2602.20434."
CLAIM: "The quantitative horizon profile under multi-point JET conditioning, and in particular the one-sided rim/valley angular anatomy of the conditional mean around a near-collinear critical triple, have to our knowledge [Item 3: unlocated part] not been described."
FORBIDDEN: claiming variance screening itself; "we discover conditional-variance suppression."

## A4 — The global counting device [Item 4: KNOWN-IN-PART]
CITE: "Value-window Kac–Rice counts are standard (Cheng–Schwartzman, Bernoulli 2018; Muirhead, SPL 2020; Estrade–Fournier, SPL 2016)."
CLAIM: "The reduction we employ — bounding gradient-flow OUTCOME probabilities by the expected number of band-valued critical points, replacing trajectory tracking entirely — is to our knowledge [Item 4: unlocated part] not in the literature as a device for persistence questions."
FORBIDDEN: claiming band counting itself.

## A5 — Shadowing and the launch cone [Item 5: KNOWN-IN-PART]
CITE: "Quantitative shadowing of deterministic flow under small random perturbation is classical Freidlin–Wentzell theory, and for gradient flows of Morse potentials, Hu–Li–Yang (arXiv:1706.00837) prove O(ln ε⁻¹) convergence."
CLAIM: "Conditional-MEAN-flow shadowing with superexponential failure bounds under jet conditioning, and the launch-direction concentration law at a pinned saddle (unstable-eigenvector scatter σ ≈ 0.023 rad with an r-stable composed exponent), are to our knowledge [Item 5: unlocated part] new in this setting."
FORBIDDEN: claiming Freidlin–Wentzell or Hu–Li–Yang content.

## A6 — Near-diagonal repulsion [Item 6: KNOWN — cite only, CR5]
CITE: "We use the near-diagonal two-point behavior of planar critical points as established: Beliaev–Cammarota–Wigman (ECP 2020, arXiv:1911.03455); Ladgham–Lachièze-Rey (SPA 2023; same-type hard repulsion); Azaïs–Delmas (SPA 2022; index-resolved attraction/neutrality/repulsion)."
NO CLAIM LANGUAGE IS LICENSED FOR THIS ITEM.

## A7 — Thermodynamic package [Item 7: KNOWN-IN-PART; preprint provisionality in-text]
CITE: "Persistence entropy is standard (Atienza–González-Díaz–Soriano-Trigueros, arXiv:1701.07857); partition-function framings appear in recent preprints (arXiv:2603.27903; arXiv:2602.09058) which are not yet peer-reviewed and whose specific values we treat as provisional."
CLAIM: "The topological-second-law formulation we propose is to our knowledge [Item 7: unlocated part] not in the literature."
FORBIDDEN: treating the 2026 preprints' values as established; bare "novel."

## A8 — The ΔJ parity law [Item 8: KNOWN-IN-PART; INCOMPLETE-SEARCH FLAG STANDS, in-text per CR4]
CITE: "Sensitivity of persistence statistics to local (f_NL) non-Gaussianity is established empirically: Cole–Shiu (JCAP 2018, arXiv:1712.08159) on CMB maps (Δf_NL = 35.8 at 68% CL versus 60.6 for Betti curves) and Biagetti–Cole–Shiu (JCAP 2021, arXiv:2009.04819) on large-scale structure — distinct settings not to be conflated; Minkowski-functional perturbation theory (Matsubara, arXiv:2011.04954; arXiv:1001.2321) is the closest analytic analogue, with first-order corrections governed by odd/skewness terms."
CLAIM: "The specific parity law — that only the odd part of log g′ contributes at first order to the persistence asymmetry functional ΔJ for f = g(F) — is to our knowledge not in the literature; we flag explicitly that our search on this item is incomplete [Item 8: flag stands; zbMATH/INSPIRE outstanding] and the priority claim is correspondingly provisional."
FORBIDDEN: unflagged parity-law priority claims; conflating the CMB and LSS results.

## A9 — Global forbidden list (all items)
Bare tokens never licensed anywhere: "novel" (unqualified), "the first" (without "to our knowledge"), "unprecedented", "breakthrough", "settles", "long-standing open problem". The Annex's claim sentences are the ceiling: external documents may weaken them, never strengthen them.

# B2 Positivity by Composition — Ghost-Debt Closure Note (C015 companion)
**Artifact class:** obligation-closure note. **Object:** the File-5 designated Phase-2 obligation "k₂(0;b) > 0" — positivity of the pair intensity at the fold configuration — carried since the Theorem-B derivation under the label PROVEN-MODULO and never discharged in any single document. **Naming caution:** this is the *old* File-5 "Proposition B2" (pair-intensity neutrality/positivity), one of four objects sharing the name "B2" across eras (see the supersession-map task, manuscript item (a)); it is not C010's P-B2 nor the modern adjacency program.

## Statement
For the testbed class (and, with the stated general-moment inputs, under (H1+)–(H2′)): the pair-Palm intensity k₂ of near-fold max–saddle pairs at separation r is strictly positive for all sufficiently small r, with k₂ bounded below by an explicit product of verified constants.

## Composition
The positivity follows by composing four already-certified ingredients; none is new, which is exactly why this note is owed rather than a cycle.

**(1) Frame nondegeneracy of the limiting conditional law.** The six-pin conditional covariance of the target block is positive-definite with exact diagonal (2, 2, 6, 6, 6, 24) and determinant 13824 (C012, two-route, exact; principal minors 2, 4, 24, 96, 576, 13824). In general moments: positive-definiteness holds for every (H2′) sequence by the projection-Gram argument — the conditional covariance is the Gram matrix of the projections of six monomial-derivative functionals onto the orthocomplement of the span of six others in L²(ρ); (H2′) at jet order ≤ 4 says all twelve are linearly independent, hence the projections are linearly independent, hence the Gram is PD. Verified beyond the reflection-symmetric class on five randomized fully-general atom spectra, exact arithmetic (C015 arm B, P-G4).

**(2) The fold event is open and charged.** In the limiting conditional Gaussian, the fold configuration is the event {c₃₀ near 2κ, μ_S in a compact positive interval, μ_M in a compact positive interval, ν-block in a bounded box} — a nonempty open set in the six-dimensional target space (explicit witness: center the box at the conditional mean, which realizes c₃₀ = 2κ exactly by the pinning identity, and take edges inside one conditional standard deviation per coordinate; the C012 variances make every edge positive). A nondegenerate Gaussian charges every nonempty open set; by (1) the mass is strictly positive, and it is an explicit error-function product if a numerical floor is wanted.

**(3) The index indicators cost a bounded factor.** The max/saddle typing at ±r/2 is implied on a sub-box of (2) by continuity of the Hessian entries in the jet (the box in (2) can be taken inside the typing region: det H_S < 0, det H_M > 0, tr H_M < 0 hold at the conditional mean with strict inequalities at scale r, and persist on a shrunken box). Measured typed fractions on the untilted six-pin law: 0.766–0.786 across the rungs — the indicator is not merely positive but order-one.

**(4) The adjacency indicator, where the pair event carries it.** Where k₂ is defined with the separatrix-adjacency mark, C013's result applies: det-weighted adjacency = 1 − O(r) on the pair event (measured 1.0000 at every rung within resolution), so the mark costs a factor 1 − O(r), not a positivity risk. (The *tail-conditioned* adjacency is a different object — currently 0.36 ± 0.05 at the authoritative rung per C015 — and does not enter the plain positivity statement.)

Composing (1)–(4): k₂(0;b) ≥ [Gaussian mass of the witness box] × [typing sub-box factor] × (1 − O(r)) > 0 for small r. ∎ (composition grade)

## Labels and scope
- Grade: **composition of certified parts** — (1) exact/two-route (C012) plus proof-note-general (this note + P-G4); (2) elementary Gaussian; (3) elementary continuity plus measurement; (4) C013 measured with its stated scope. Nothing here is at raw architecture grade.
- The File-5 ledger entry "PROVEN-MODULO (positivity)" may be advanced to **DISCHARGED-BY-COMPOSITION** with this note as the record; the manuscript's File-5 patch should cite C012 §P5, C013 Lemma ADJ, C015 arm B, and this note.
- What this note does **not** claim: any sharp constant for k₂ (that is the constants program), and any statement about the tail-conditioned adjacency (superseded chain lives in C015).

## The general-stationary Lemma P statement (recorded here for the manuscript)
Under (H1+)–(H2′), the cubic-pinning limiting conditional law of {f_ss, f_tss, f_sss, f_ttss, f_ttts, f_tttt} given {f, f_t, f_tt, f_ttt, f_s, f_ts} exists, is Gaussian with positive-definite covariance (projection-Gram argument above), and under frame-reflection symmetry is block-diagonal by joint parity with the closed forms of C015 arm B; the Bargmann–Fock instance carries the exact constants (2, 2, 6, 6, 6, 24; 13824) used throughout the constants program. This is the form in which Lemma P should be stated in the unified manuscript, with BF as the constants-bearing example rather than the load-bearing case.

# C015 Package — Joint Analysis Part 2: Tilt Integration, Deep Rung, Branch Audit
**Artifact class:** cycle package (observed side; companion to the frozen snapshot).
**Chain:** C012 (pinned laws, exact) → C013 (Lemma ADJ, weighted adjacency) → C014 part 1 (germ/joint at r=1/5) → **C015** (this cycle) → part 3 (registered).
**Snapshot:** `C015_Joint2_snapshot.json`, sha256 `e082b6f6f492e18e442259d0866bdb987189ec8c444a4c9946538badece97a4f`, frozen 2026-07-06T22:13:04Z, **before** any engine run. Hand derivations H1–H6 recorded there; this package reports the observed side and the adjudications. Testbed: Bargmann–Fock, b = 6/5, κ = 1, ℓ = r³/6.

## 1. What this cycle was for
Part 1 measured the tilted germ mechanics at two tilt values and one rung and left three registered items: the pair-Palm-weighted integration over the tilt (toward the exact inner-law constant), the deeper rung, and the branch-labeling audit. This cycle executed all three, plus two companion arms: the general-moment limiting Lemma P pass (arm B) and the B2-positivity-by-composition note (separate artifact).

The snapshot's centerpiece was an honest adversarial fork (P-J6). The hand assembly H1–H3 produced, before any run, a **Θ(r⁴)** exponent for the Palm mass of the μ-tilt failure channel

> T_w(r) := r² · Σ_m [trapezoid] ρ₆(mr²) · E_tilt[1_fail · W₂] / E_unt[W₂],  W₂ = |det H_M||det H_S|,

in direct conflict with the FlatSaddle r⁵ law and the C007-C measurement (4.959). The conflict could not be resolved by hand at freeze time. Per protocol it was committed as a fork with all three outcomes pre-interpreted, rather than silently repaired.

## 2. Instrument
`joint_sim2.py` — vectorized rebuild of the part-1 instrument. Exact-rational 7-row (tilted) / 6-row (untilted) conditioning with nullspace projection; D-A1′ physical gate inherited verbatim (all ten runs passed at machine epsilon, 4.4–6.7e−16, against thresholds ℓ/100 = 1.3e−5 and 1.7e−6). Batched 24-start Newton partner sweep (annulus r²/50 < d ≤ 10r², nearest). Two-branch germ flows from S with capture radius r²/20 checked through **both** phases — fixing the part-1 capture gap; the fix turned out immaterial (≤ 0.003 shift at every rung, now measured rather than suspected). Per-sample Palm weights W₂ from the exact jets at ±r/2. Branch outcomes recorded per branch under both the part-1 eigen-sign labels and the geometric y-ward labels. Runtime: 5–10 s per rung at Ns = 6000 (the part-1 scalar loops replaced by batched numpy; exact-rational conditioning retained — design lesson #4 held at cond(G) ~ r⁻⁶).

**Validation (D-V1, gate):** fresh-seed reproduction of part 1 at r=1/5, m=±1/2, Ns=3000, PASSED within 3σ on every gated quantity; adjM reproduced to 0.001 without being gated. The instrument is like-for-like where it claims to be.

## 3. Results
Per-rung table (Ns = 6000 new rungs, 3000 validation rungs; full JSONs shipped alongside):

| r | m | partner | pmax | psad | pmin | fail(fixed) | J_w | adj† | E[W₂] | E[1_f·W₂] |

| 1/5 | −3/2 | 0.999 | 0.318 | 0.328 | 0.354 | 0.306 | 0.258 | 0.215 | 1.95e−3 | 5.03e−4 |
| 1/5 | −1/2 | 1.000 | 0.211 | 0.305 | 0.484 | 0.205 | 0.163 | 0.231 | 1.67e−3 | 2.71e−4 |
| 1/5 | +1/2 | 0.999 | 0.097 | 0.546 | 0.357 | 0.094 | 0.099 | 0.281 | 1.29e−3 | 1.27e−4 |
| 1/5 | +3/2 | 0.999 | 0.047 | 0.703 | 0.250 | 0.044 | 0.058 | 0.263 | 1.32e−3 | 7.74e−5 |

| 1/10 | −1/2 | 0.584 | 0.020 | 0.058 | 0.922 | 0.002 | 0.0030 | 0.372 | 1.00e−4 | 3.01e−7 |
| 1/10 | +1/2 | 0.688 | 0.012 | 0.380 | 0.608 | 0.003 | 0.0072 | 0.341 | 9.25e−5 | 6.70e−7 |

Untilted companions (N = 20000): E[W₂|pins] = 0.13296 (r=1/5), 0.034069 (r=1/10); exact six-pin law of F_ss(S): mean −1.1983484 / −1.1997926, variance 2.0001500 / 2.0000094 (exact rationals in the artifacts), density at 0: 0.197004 / 0.196835 against the hand value e^{−b²/4}/(2√π) = 0.196817 — **P-K1 PASS** at 0.09% and 0.009%. Refinement: the mean's leading correction is the ℓ-injection, mean = −b + c·ℓ with c = 1.239, 1.244 across the octave; c → 5/4 is recorded as a conjecture only.

**Gate scorecard:** D-A1′ PASS (all runs) · D-V1 PASS · P-K1 PASS · P-W1 PASS (W-ratio slope 1.974 against hand 2) · **P-J6 → branch 3** (below) · P-J7 PASS decisively (y-ward = 1.000, both-branch = 0 everywhere) · **P-J9 FAILED-AS-WRITTEN** at r=1/10 (0.758, 0.496 vs ≥ 0.85; no rescue; root cause in the observed update) · P-J10 PASS both rungs · P-G1, P-G2, P-G4 PASS (arm B).

## 4. The fork's adjudication and the mechanism
T_w(1/5) = 4.136e−5; T_w(1/10) = 8.614e−8 (resting on 55 failure events — a near-zero upper bound). Two-rung log₂ slope **8.91**, outside both committed bands: **branch 3, moderate-r transient.** The r=1/5 joint constants are demoted to moderate-r phenomenology; r=1/10 is authoritative.

The mechanism, identified post-hoc and stated as the cycle's structural finding: **the fixed search ball of radius 10r² is 2r at r = 1/5 — it contains M itself (at distance r) and the pair's entire r-scale fold structure.** The part-1 "max partners" were dominantly ball-edge r-scale interlopers (window points of the near-field class), not r²-scale splitting partners. At r = 1/10 the ball (radius r) barely reaches that structure; the genuine splitting partner dominates and is **asymptotically never a maximum**: f_tt(y) = κr + O(r²) > 0 forces saddle or minimum type, so pmax → 0 with r (0.318 → 0.030 at m = −3/2 across one octave). The partner is min-dominated at m < 0 (0.91–0.92), matching the sign prediction f_ss(y) ≈ −mr² > 0.

Consequences, in order of importance:
1. **The H3 hand hypothesis (a genuine Θ(r⁴) inner failure channel) is killed by the engine.** Its error is located exactly: H3 assumed J(m) = Θ(1); in fact J(m) → 0 with r because the max-type factor vanishes. The W-ratio ingredient (H2) was simultaneously *confirmed* (P-W1, slope 1.974 vs hand 2) — the fork decomposed cleanly into a right ingredient and a wrong one.
2. **FlatSaddle r⁵ and the C007-C 4.959 measurement stand unthreatened**; min partners are H₀-inert under the elder bookkeeping committed at the part-1 freeze. The tension the snapshot refused to paper over is resolved in FlatSaddle's favor, by measurement.
3. The preliminary constant T_w(1/10)/r⁵ = 0.0086 is recorded **only** as an upper-bound-class number: with pmax → 0 the channel vanishes faster than any fixed power fit from two rungs, and part 3 should treat the inner failure channel as asymptotically negligible relative to the r³ assembly unless the ball-radius scan revives a component of it.

**Design lesson (candidate #5 for the registry):** fixed-physical-radius search domains conflate scales across rungs when the radius crosses another structural scale. 10r² crossed r exactly where the part-1 value-gate warning (2.2ℓ) fired. Scale search domains in the invariant variable; check rung-crossing overlaps at design time.

## 5. Branch audit (registered item, closed)
At every rung, in 42,000 flowed samples: the away branch **never** terminates at M; adj† (either branch reaches M) equals the part-1 eigen-labeled adjM identically, and every capture is on the y-ward branch (P-J7: 1.000, both-branch 0.0000). Part 1's labeling convention is therefore vindicated for the adjacency measurement — no label-swap contamination existed — and the geometric restatement is now the recorded one: capture happens on, and only on, the branch pointing into the partner's half-plane. The deep-tail adjacency **supersede-in-scope chain**: 0.92 (C013, flat-set window |μ_S| ≤ r) → 0.25 (C014, r=1/5 μ-tilt) → **0.36 ± 0.05** (C015, r=1/10 μ-tilt, authoritative; per-rung 0.326–0.415, rising as r falls). Each value belongs to its stated conditioning window; part 3 extends the trend one octave.

## 6. Arm B — general-moment Lemma P (manuscript de-risking)
The limiting Lemma P computation was rerun symbolically in general spectral moments λ_jk. Results: **(P-G2)** under frame-reflection symmetry the conditional 6×6 is block-diagonal by joint parity, blocks {f_ss, f_ttss, f_tttt | f, f_tt}, {f_tss | f_t, f_ttt}, {f_sss | f_s}, {f_ttts | f_ts}, off-block entries identically zero, closed forms shipped (e.g. Var(f_sss|f_s) = (λ₀₂λ₀₆ − λ₀₄²)/λ₀₂). **(P-G1)** BF specialization reproduces diag (2,2,6,6,6,24), det 13824, all minors positive, exactly. **(P-G4)** for five randomized fully-general stationary spectra (14-atom reflection-completed measures, odd–odd moments present, exact rational arithmetic) the conditional 6×6 is positive-definite in every trial. Together with the projection-Gram argument (stated in the B2 note): **the manuscript may state Lemma P under (H1+)–(H2′) in general, with BF as the constants-bearing instance** — the structural decision item (g) of the remaining-work register is closed on the Lemma P front.

## 7. Part 3 — registered
(i) Ball-radius scan at fixed r in the invariant variable, separating interloper exclusion from genuine-partner loss (also resolves the P-J9 failure's anatomy). (ii) One octave deeper (r = 1/20, Ns ≥ 20000) if the collapse is to be bounded rather than observed. (iii) Per-sample window-membership checks (the value envelope scales ~r^3.5 and sits at 1.7–2.5ℓ — the in-window property holds in bulk, not at the max). (iv) The c → 5/4 mean-correction conjecture. (v) Propagation done this cycle: Constants_Table013.md.

# C031 — Lemma LB-RATE: the Integration Document of Record
**Freeze:** e165821b1479f619af8ebdb1438460edfebe88f44c189553ca86f73f8fe1afbe. **Scope:** Bargmann–Fock kernel K = exp(−|u|²/2), b = 6/5, ℓ = r³/6, arch station ỹ* = (−0.76, 0.24); rungs r ∈ {0.05, 0.025} unless stated. This document assembles the lower half of Theorem A's rate from the cycle artifacts C022–C030, states every term at its exact grade, registers two composition findings discovered during assembly (one repaired this cycle, one named), and lists the complete named-formality set. Nothing here re-derives a registered result; every grade cites its cycle.

## 1. Target and reduction chain
**Target (lower half of Θ(r³)):** 1 − q(r, b) ≥ c·r³ for small r, with c explicit or measured-with-derived-structure.

**Reduction (C024, freeze 0df10fa6…139, 14/14-verified instrument):** 1 − q ≥ E[N_qual]·(1 − O(r³)) by Bonferroni (pair term O(r⁶) registered at C022), with E[N_qual] = ∫ Λ(y)·AO(y) dA over the arch region. The estimand, verbatim as frozen at C024: Λ(y) = φ₂(∇f(y)=0 | 𝒥₆, with mean) · [Φ((b−μ_t)/s_t) − Φ((b−ℓ−μ_t)/s_t)] · E[W₃1_typed | 9 pins @ v* = clip(μ_t)] / E[W₂1_typed | 𝒥₆]; typing (detM>0, trM<0, detS<0, detY<0); window (b−ℓ, b); pin values ((b,0,0), (b−ℓ,0,0), (v*,0,0)). So LB-RATE = [Λ-side rate: ∫Λ dA ≥ c_Λ·r³] × [AO-side floor: inf AO ≥ c_AO > 0], composed through the C024 reduction.

## 2. The Λ-side: status of the factor limits (S1–S6)
C024 reduced the Λ-side to six factor-limit statements S1–S6 plus the AO floor. Their disposition (C026 freeze 6ac9a33c…7df; C027 freeze f0833443…dc2, package c9d1466a…3b4):

- **Exact (rational, regularizing frame, C026):** the S-limits including den∞ = 3.230979 (closed form) and the numerator product lemma num∞ = |∏c|. **S3 FAILED-AS-WRITTEN and was superseded by the exact value:** m = lim (μ_t − b)/ℓ = −0.4999290, *not* −1/2; the −1/2 conjecture is dead, the exact constant lives (kill registered at C026).
- **Derived-on-grid (C027):** the assembled station integrand λ(ỹ) and its integral **C*_∞ = ∫λ(ỹ) dỹ = 0.9091 ± 0.038 (quad) ± 0.009 (shell)** over a 730-station grid; λ(ỹ*) = 3.4755. Radius certificates: 6-pin r₀ = 0.1011 (proved); 9-pin r₀ = 0.0165 (proved), extended empirically to r = 0.05 via a 1e-13 function identity (named: 9-pin certificate tightening).
- **Measured, with derived structure:** C*(0.05) = 0.9728, C*(0.025) = 0.946 — approach to the limit is clean O(r) (successive-difference ratio 1.73 ≈ 2); all 9-pin mean-Hessian entries are O(r) with tr M coefficient −13.5327 (C027).

**Λ-side grade:** ∫Λ dA = C*·r³ with C* measured at rungs and its r→0 limit derived-on-grid (0.9091). The r³ scaling itself is measured (two-rung ratio 8.23 ≈ 8, C021) with the factor localization derived at C024–C026 (the ℓ window factor carries the rate; the remaining factors have exact limits). The fully rigorous r-uniform lower rate on ∫Λ remains the named residue of this side (grid → continuum: quadrature + shell errors are quantified; the formality is the station-density argument, same class as C027's grade).

## 3. The AO-side: the C025 architecture and per-term grades
**Registered verbatim (C025, freeze 0f8cb3dc…60b):** AO-failure ⊆ {non-adjacency} ∪ {terminal ≤ b}; (R1) the ascent from the arch saddle's outward branch is monotone with height ≥ v*; (R2) P(terminal ≤ b) ≤ E[N_maxband(B_d₀) | 9 pins] + far band-termination; (R3) Lemma FD: conditional-vs-unconditional TV ≤ 2.2% at d ≥ 3, ≤ 1e-4 at d = 5; (R4) OBL-FAR-ASCENT(δ₀), r-free. Assembly as registered: AO ≥ 1 − P(non-adj) − E[N_maxband] − p̄(δ₀) − TV(d₀).

**Per-term grade table (d₀ = 5 per §4's finding G1):**

## 4. The two composition findings (the integration cycle's own contribution)
**G1 — additive-TV vacuity at theorem grade: FOUND AND REPAIRED (R3′).** As registered, the assembly subtracts TV additively: AO ≥ c − TV − O(r³) with c the C028 theorem constant. Since c = 0.0896·P₀ with P₀ plausibly 1e-4–1e-6-class, c ≪ TV(d₀=3) = 0.022 and the theorem-grade assembly as written is vacuous (negative). **Repair (closed this cycle):** route the barrier *through* the conditioning. The support-theorem positivity argument is conditioning-robust for nondegenerate Gaussians: the conditional law given the 9 pins is Gaussian with CM space {h ∈ H : pins(h) = 0}; the shift ũ₀′ = ũ₀ − Proj_pins(ũ₀) satisfies the pin constraints with ‖ũ₀′‖ ≤ ‖ũ₀‖ (CM factor no worse), and the barrier's C¹ ramp property survives because the two induced perturbations — the conditional mean m₉ and the projection field — have C¹ size on the d₀ = 5 slab bounded by max(|m₉|, |∇m₉|) + ‖ũ₀‖·√(1−v_grad) = 0.0016 + 0.0020 = **0.0036, a 36× underrun of the 0.1307 unallocated margin** (exact mp station table, c031_verify.json). The horizon phenomenon (C030) is precisely what made d₀ = 3 dangerous and d₀ = 5 safe: the pull scales as ‖·‖_H·√(1−v), and v = 1 − O(1e-7) at d = 5. Consequence: theorem-grade far-term positivity needs **no TV subtraction**; Lemma FD is repositioned as the quantitative channel only. Moving d₀ from 3 to 5 raises the R2 constant by the area factor to ≈ 2.1·(ℓ/2) — still O(r³), immaterial.

**G2 — entry-point selection/multiplicity: FOUND AND REGISTERED (OBL-FAR-COMPOSE).** The far term concerns the trajectory's crossing of ∂B_{d₀}. Entries with f(ξ) > b win outright; only band entries f(ξ) ∈ [v*, b] can be bad. Because BF sample paths are a.s. analytic (the same fact behind the C030 horizon), conditioning on the trajectory's past region determines the far field — naive "restart at the crossing point" Palm arguments are therefore delicate and are NOT used. Two rigorous routes, both registered:
(i) *Union bound over band components:* E[#components of the band on ∂B₅] ≤ Rice up-crossings of v* ≈ b: (1/2π)√(λ₂/λ₀)·e^{−b²/2}·2π·5 = **2.43** (+1 wrap) — derived this cycle (V1). Measured-grade composition: far ≤ 2.43·p̄(0.05)·(1 + 1e-4) = 2.43·0.0334 ≈ **0.081**. Theorem-grade via this route requires c > 1 − 1/2.43 ≈ 0.59 — far beyond the C028 barrier class; route (i) is measured-grade only.
(ii) *Selection/disintegration lemma:* make the single-crossing Palm bound rigorous (the crossing point is field-selected; a disintegration over the crossing location with a local-conditioning Palm kernel would give far ≤ sup-Palm p̄ with no multiplicity factor). This is the theorem-grade route and is OPEN. **OBL-FAR-COMPOSE registered with both routes; the theorem-grade AO assembly below is conditional on it.**

## 5. Assembled bounds
**Measured grade (r = 0.025, d₀ = 5):** AO ≥ 1 − [non-adj: 0 measured, channels ≤ 0.21·r³ + named] − [2.1·(ℓ/2) = 3.4e-6] − [far ≤ 0.081] − [TV 1e-4] ≥ **0.918**. Composed with the Λ-side: **1 − q ≥ 0.918 · 0.946 · r³ · (1 − O(r³)) ≈ 0.87·r³** — the measured-grade LB-RATE, consistent with the direct two-sided measurement C* ≈ 0.96 ± 0.06 (C021) since AO there is measured ≈ 1 rather than bounded by the assembly's conservative far term.

**Theorem grade (conditional):** AO ≥ c_cond − 2.1·(ℓ/2) − [named non-adjacency channels] with c_cond > 0 the R3′ conditional-barrier constant — **non-vacuous and positive for small r**, conditional on: OBL-FAR-COMPOSE route (ii); the sup-over-zone step (above-b saddle); mean-ridge connectivity; KR validity + collar exclusion; and the R0/γ-LOC architecture inherited by every AO statement. Composed with the Λ-side: 1 − q ≥ c_cond·c_Λ·r³ conditional on the same set plus the Λ-side grid formality. **The lower half of Θ(r³) is therefore: measured at 0.87·r³ with derived structure throughout; theorem-grade modulo the named set below, with the analytic skeleton now complete** (positivity constants explicit at every node; no term is bare measurement without a derived-structure bound).

## 6. The complete named-formality register (as of C031)

# C033 — AUDIT-TC: Foundation Enforcement of the Terminal-Counting Supersession
**Freeze:** 0269521474943ee563610c78dd8f5b37a167e289bc10b060f13738d97aea515c. **Verdict: ALL GATES PASS — Lemma TC AFFIRMED at its stated grade (derived-structure + station-certified, modulo R0 and the named set), with one new structural finding registered.** Scope: BF, b = 6/5, r = 0.025, L = 24, arch station.

## AU-0 — chain integrity: PASS
All eight archived C028–C032 freeze/package hashes recomputed and matched exactly (4a343a18…, ddd8596f…, ae20f4e3…, aed6683e…, e165821b…, e7998ef0…, 1487c20c…, 8a76c558…). The provenance layer is intact.

## AU-1 + supplement + resolution — the mean-gradient kill: PASS (complete, 6 rays)
The audit's target was the sparse-station failure class: the mean surface crosses the terminal band [v*, b] on thin structures the C030 near stations could have straddled. Bracket-bisection hunting across rays 0, 2.35, 4.2, π over d ∈ [0.05, 1.9]:
- **Exactly one collar-exterior band crossing exists** (arch side, ang = 2.35, d = 0.1133, m = 1.199995). At it: **q_kill = ½ mᵍᵀΣ_∇⁻¹mᵍ = 869.5**, i.e. φ_∇ ≤ e⁻⁸⁶⁹ — the mean-gradient kill verified AT the dangerous point, not near it. Critical points of the field cannot form there.
- Rays 0 (past S): crossing collar-interior (m already above guard at d = 0.05 = collar edge).
- **Rays 4.2 and π: NO crossing anywhere — the mean descends monotonically below b** (see the finding below). Supplementary window [0.575, 0.95] and full-zone resolution sweep: 0 crossings, min q_kill vacuously ∞.

## AU-2 — band-valued mean-critical points: PASS (with caveat)
8 angles × 9 distances over d ∈ [0.7, 2.1]: **zero** small-gradient loci (|∇m₉| < 0.02) and zero band-valued points outside collars. Caveat recorded: rim-crest points (where the radial derivative vanishes) were not captured at this grid resolution; the protection is double — crest values 1.40–1.57 sit far above the band, and the kill holds everywhere else profiled.

## AU-3 — intra-collar dip: PASS

The dip is real; on these sides the band re-entry (if any) is collar-interior or absent — carried by the existing collar-exclusion named item, exactly as the TC package stated.

## AU-4 — B₅-extension margin: PASS decisively
Band-max intensity ratios at d ∈ {3.5, 4, 4.5} × 2 angles: **0.68–0.99** — all under the 2.0 margin, and actually SUPPRESSED below unconditional at 3.5–4 (the rim's elevated mean pushes band values down-weight). The 2.1·(ℓ/2) B₅ constant is conservative.

## FINDING (registered): the rim is one-sided — an anisotropic rim/valley structure
C032 recorded the rim as "anisotropic, higher toward the arch side." The audit sharpens this to a qualitative dichotomy: **the mean bump/rim exists only on the arch/east sector (angles ≈ 0–2.4; crest 1.40–1.57 at d ≈ 1.3); on the west sector (angles ≈ 3–4.5) the mean has NO rim — it descends monotonically below b, reaching −1.19 relative to b by d = 1.9 (a below-b valley).** Consequences: (i) TC unaffected — the valley floor is below the band (value-factor kill; AU-4 confirms conditional ≤ unconditional there) and its edges have no band crossings on the audited rays; (ii) for Lemma MF the anisotropy is load-bearing: mean-uphill shadowing is available only on the rim side, so the ±20° launch-fan certificates (C025) become the mechanism confining the outward branch to the rim sector — the MF architecture must couple fan-geometry to the mean-flow argument rather than assume radial mean-uphill; (iii) the C032 package's rim description is SUPERSEDED-IN-PART by this sharper geometry (no number changes).

## MF-seed facts (for C034, recorded, ungraded)
∇m₉ radial structure mapped on 6 rays; rim crest ≈ 1.4–1.6 at d ≈ 1.3 arch-side; west valley monotone-descending; the unique below-b mean structure near the cluster is the M-dip (collar-scale); kill map: the only exterior band crossing (0.1133, ang 2.35) is e⁻⁸⁶⁹-dead; outward launch direction sits near the rim's western shoulder — fan confinement is the bridge.

## Gate ledger
AU-0 PASS · G-K1 PASS complete (1 exterior crossing, killed; 6 rays, bisection-refined) · G-K2 PASS (0/72, crest caveat) · G-K3 PASS (dip collar-interior) · G-K4 PASS (0.68–0.99 ≤ 2.0). No corrections to TC required; the finding is additive.

# C034 — The Definitions & Derivatives Canon (DEF-AUDIT)
**Freeze:** b665c84b343ae485cf8249f93996c73151c5caee9ab524e96807138a8eaa15ee. **Battery:** G-D1 PASS, 78/78 (c034_battery.json). **Rule of precedence:** where any archived document conflicts with this canon, the canon's precedence rulings (§10) govern; superseded text remains in the archive untouched, per supersede-never-overwrite.

## 1. The field and its hypotheses
**Field.** f: T²_L → ℝ, centered stationary Gaussian, C³, with the Bargmann–Fock (BF) covariance kernel K(u) = exp(−|u|²/2), unit variance. Torus side **L = 24** throughout the current chain; the plane kernel is used directly since periodization corrections are ≤ e^{−L²/8} = e^{−72} at all program distances (recorded C032). BF sample paths are a.s. real-analytic; consequence in use: the field on any open set determines it globally a.s. (the analytic-determinism fact behind both the C030 horizon and the C031 G2 obstacle).
**Hypotheses (H1+), (H2′).** The standing regularity/nondegeneracy hypotheses under which R0 and the architecture are stated (verbatim statements live in the founding module; BF satisfies both). POINTER — not re-quoted here; no current computation depends on their fine print beyond BF membership.
**Level.** b = 6/5 = 1.2, fixed.

## 2. Derivative conventions — verified by battery
**Multi-indices.** a = (a₁, a₂) means ∂^{a₁}_x ∂^{a₂}_y. J01 := [(0,0), (1,0), (0,1)] (the 1-jet: value, gradient). HESS := [(2,0), (1,1), (0,2)]. The 6-jet = J01 ∪ HESS in that order: (f, f_x, f_y, f_xx, f_xy, f_yy).
**Covariance operator.** cov_mp(P, a, Q, c) = Cov(∂^a f(P), ∂^c f(Q)). Verified conventions (battery, mp.dps = 40): **B1** stationarity symmetry Cov(∂^a f(P), ∂^c f(Q)) = (−1)^{|a|+|c|} Cov(∂^a f(Q), ∂^c f(P)) — 36/36 exact; **B2** raising an output order equals differentiating in the point argument — 24/24 at 1e-10 with h = 1e-8, covering every order in program use (outputs |a| ≤ 2, totals |a|+|c| ≤ 4 — the Hessian–Hessian covariances need K's 4th derivatives and no computation needs more); **B3** BF coincidence values Var f = Var f_x = Var f_y = 1, Cov(f, f_xx) = Cov(f, f_yy) = −1, Var f_xx = Var f_yy = 3, Cov(f_xx, f_yy) = 1, Var f_xy = 1, all odd-total covariances 0 — 13/13 at 1e-25. **Completeness statement:** the derivative objects the program uses are exactly {jet and Hessian covariances at arbitrary point pairs; conditional means/covariances thereof; the gradient of the conditional mean}. B1–B3 cover the first; B5 the second; B4 the third. Nothing in the current chain requires derivatives beyond total order 4.
**Conditioning operator.** schur(PIN, vals, OUT) returns (m_o, S_o, ·): the conditional mean vector and covariance of the OUT functionals given the PIN functionals equal vals, via Schur complement on the joint Gram. **B5:** Var(f(x) | pins) from schur equals 1 − kᵀG⁻¹k computed independently — exactly (0.0 difference), two points. **B4:** the gradient of the conditional mean field equals the conditional mean of the gradient — ∂ᵢ m₉(x) = E[∂ᵢ f(x) | pins] — verified to 7.6e-15 at a rim point, a valley point, and a near point. This identity underlies every kill exponent, every rim/valley gradient, and the R3′ margin; it is now battery-verified, not assumed.
**Numerical regime.** The 9-pin Gram is divided-difference ill-conditioned (λ_min ~ r⁶-scale); mp.dps = 40 exists precisely so that G⁻¹ quadratic forms remain exact-grade. No float-precision Gram inversion is permitted anywhere in the chain (the C029 G-E1 float failure and its mp-exact repair, negmass 2e-15, is the precedent).

## 3. Geometry, scales, and the pin configuration (exact)
r = the pair scale (current rungs 0.05, 0.025); **ℓ = r³/6** (the window depth); the two-scale structure r vs ℓ is the source of the r³ rate.
**Pins (9 functionals = 3 points × J01):** M = (−r/2, 0) with (f, ∇f) = (b, 0, 0) — the max-typed partner; S = (+r/2, 0) with (b − ℓ, 0, 0) — the window-bottom saddle-typed point; y = M + r·(−0.76, 0.24) with (v*, 0, 0) — the arch saddle at the canonical station ỹ* = (−0.76, 0.24) in r-units from M.
**v\* (exact definition):** v* = clip_{[b−ℓ, b]}(μ_t), where μ_t is the 6-pin conditional mean of f(y) after Schur-removing the gradient block (the tilted mean). Exact limit: m := lim_{r→0} (μ_t − b)/ℓ = **−0.4999290** (C026; the −1/2 conjecture is dead). Hence v* = b − 0.4999290·ℓ·(1 + o(1)).

## 4. The estimand chain (top to bottom, with verbatim anchors)
**q(r, b) and Theorem A.** q is the elder-rule death-partner probability for the pinned fold pair at level b (the persistence-diagram pairing object; the map is a.s. well-defined **modulo R0** — verbatim from the R0 document: "the elder-rule death-partner map, the persistence diagram, and hence Theorem A and Theorem B are only almost surely well-defined once R0 holds"). **Theorem A (target):** 1 − q(r, b) = Θ(r³). The current program is the LOWER half; the upper half is OBL-BETA-RELEVANCE.
**The reduction (C024, verbatim anchor from the Pinning Module):** "1 − q ≥ P⁰(N_qual ≥ 1) ≥ E⁰[N_qual](1 − O(r³))" — Bonferroni with the pair term derived O(r⁶) (I_far via decorrelation C_dec ≲ 2; I_near via the near-diagonal Kac–Rice bound λ₂ ≤ C_nd|Δ|, one power from the degenerate-merger Jacobian).
**The estimand Λ (C024 freeze, verbatim):** Λ(y) = φ₂(∇f(y)=0 | 𝒥₆, with mean) · [Φ((b−μ_t)/s_t) − Φ((b−ℓ−μ_t)/s_t)] · E[W₃1_typed | 9 pins @ v* = clip(μ_t)] / E[W₂1_typed | 𝒥₆]; **typing tuple:** (det M > 0, tr M < 0, det S < 0, det Y < 0); window (b−ℓ, b); pin values ((b,0,0), (b−ℓ,0,0), (v*,0,0)). This frozen estimand IS the operative definition of the typed/qualified configuration (14/14-verified instrument); the C020-era prose definition is superseded by it as the working reference.
**AO (adjacency-and-outcome qualification).** AO(y) = P(the M-side separatrix of y reaches M AND the outward-branch terminal exceeds b | the 9-pin typed law). E[N_qual] = ∫ Λ·AO dA. **Current AO bound (C032, audited C033):** AO ≥ 1 − 0.213·r³ (WP) − 2.03·r³ (TC) − [flow-topology named] − [KR formalities], modulo R0 = 1 − 2.24·r³ − named.
**Assembled LB-RATE:** 1 − q ≥ C*(r)·r³·(1 − 2.24r³)(1 − O(r³)); measured 0.946·r³ at r = 0.025; limit constant C*_∞ = 0.9091 ± 0.038 ± 0.009 (C027, 730 stations); consistent with the direct two-sided C* = 0.96 ± 0.06.

λ_type(x) = φ_∇(0 | conditioning at x) · [value factor] · E[|det H| · 1_type | conditioning, ∇ = 0, value], where the value factor is: the window/band Gaussian mass for counting lemmas (saturating at width/√(2πv) when the mean sits inside), or the tail Φ̄((b − m_c)/√v) for above-threshold counts (with u-quadrature when the |det|-term varies over the tail, per C032 G-H2: 7 nodes × 6k draws standard). Typing: max ⇔ det H > 0 ∧ tr H < 0 (code: det > 0 ∧ H_xx < 0, equivalent for 2×2 with det > 0); saddle ⇔ det H < 0. # C035 — Lemma MF: Mean-Flow Shadowing Closes the Flow-Topology Family
**Freeze:** 89fad14eb8c92eb584343b63ef9c6f67c3b74561b4ad2aa5c5dab64b7cec28bb. **Two registered corrections this cycle:** (E-class, mine) the branch labels in the gate code were swapped by a sign convention — run(+1) is the M-side branch (launch direction has positive inner product with M−y), run(−1) the outward; caught by G-M1's failure-as-coded; physics unchanged, adjudicated on the corrected labels. (Freeze-premise) the freeze stated "mean-shadowing fails intra-cluster" from the estimate |∇m₉| ~ ℓ/r; the instruments show |∇m₉| ~ (O(r)-Hessian)·dist ≫ ℓ/r, and q_shadow ≥ 2.2e4 at every cluster station — **the flow is mean-dominated at all scales; the positivity/support route (MF-1 as frozen) is NOT NEEDED and is retired to standalone-optional.**

## The skeleton (G-M1 PASS, corrected labels)
Arc-length RK4 on ∇m₉/|∇m₉| from y ± 0.2r·e₊, r = 0.025:
- **M-side branch → captured by M** (enters the r/2 collar in 4 steps; path entirely intra-cluster; q_shadow ≥ 4.1e5 along it).
- **Outward branch → crosses height b** at d ≈ 0.35, end (−0.291, 0.198), angle ≈ 146° (the northwest rim sector), never entering any pin collar; 22 steps.
The mean-flow separatrix skeleton of y is exactly the qualifying topology: one branch to M, one over the rim to height > b.

## Shadowing certificates (G-M2 PASS)
q_shadow(x) := |∇m₉(x)|²/(2·var_g(x)) along the paths: outward path minimum **39.0**, attained at the launch vicinity (where the launch-cone argument governs instead — below), rising to ≥ 1.3e7 within the cluster and astronomically beyond (the C033 kill map's regime); M-side path minimum 4.1e5. Cluster stations independently: 2.2e4–1.5e10. **G-M3 finding:** sd(f | 9)/ℓ ≤ 0.27 at all cluster stations (0.001–0.268) — the field is pinned to the mean to a fraction of ℓ even at cluster scale.

## Launch confinement (G-M4, station-grade, r-stable)
Mean Hessian at y: eigenvalues (−0.370, +0.0234), gap 0.393; unstable eigenvector **5.6° from the y→M axis** — inside the ±20° C025 fan with 14.4° to spare. Hessian conditional sd 9.2e-3 ⟹ angular scatter σ_ang ≈ 0.023 rad ⟹ the ±20° tail exponent ≈ **111** (e⁻¹¹¹). Both σ_H and the eigen-gap scale as O(r), so σ_ang is r-free: the confinement is rung-stable.

## Lemma MF (established at station-certified grade; write-up named)
Modulo R0, the collar exclusion, and the on-grid class: **P(flow-topology failure | 9 pins) ≤ P(launch outside the ±20° cone) + P(shadow-tube exit along the two paths) + [collar residue] ≤ C·(e⁻¹¹¹ + e⁻³⁹) + named.** Consequences:
- **Separatrix loop: CLOSED** at this grade — the shadowed outward branch exceeds b at d ≈ 0.35; monotone ascent then forbids terminal = M (value b). 
- **M-side escape (ridge split): CLOSED** at this grade — the shadowed M-side branch enters M's collar; escape requires tube exit (e⁻³⁹-class) or a collar violation (named).
- **Above-b-saddle diversion: CLOSED** at this grade — any diversion is a tube exit; the O(1) saddle population (C032 AB) is irrelevant to a trajectory confined to the tube.
**The named flow-topology family (register item 5) is REPLACED by one item: the MF shadowing inequality write-up** — the chaining/discretization lemma converting station q-values on a tube around the computed paths into P(sup-deviation > θ) ≤ Σ e^{−q}-class (rigidity/standard-technique class), plus the existing collar and on-grid items it composes with. Retired-to-standalone: the positivity/CM witness route (architecture recorded in the freeze; may serve the eventual write-up as an alternative).

## Updated AO and LB-RATE
AO ≥ 1 − 0.213·r³ (WP) − 2.03·r³ (TC) − C·e⁻³⁹ − [MF write-up + collar + KR + on-grid], modulo R0. **Every O(1)-uncertainty channel in AO now carries a superexponential station-certified bound; the quantitative ledger is complete.** LB-RATE unchanged numerically: 1 − q ≥ 0.946·r³ measured; 0.9091·r³·(1 − o(1)) limit — now with the flow-topology family quantitatively closed rather than named-open.

**Freeze:** 4278a6eb63327b73bb23059c21caf8787898f488483beb70b5ba0645fd9450aa. **This document is the write-up that closes the C035 named item.** Two corrections registered up front: (i) C035's composed statement "≤ C·(e⁻¹¹¹ + e⁻³⁹)" used pointwise stall exponents as composed exponents — corrected here; (ii) C035's "min q = 39 at the launch vicinity" was an artifact of that cycle's label-swap sampling — the true outward profile has q = 1.8e4 AT launch, decaying to 29–34 in the horizon-RELEASE zone near the deep b-crossing. Let γ be the computed mean-flow separatrix of y (outward branch), T the tube of radius ρ = 0.3·d_y around γ from the launch shell d_y = 0.2r to the **securing point x\*** := the first path point with E_h(x) := (m₉(x) − b)²/(2v(x)) ≥ 40. P(outward-branch flow-topology failure | 9 pins) ≤ e^{−E_cone} + N(T, δ)·e^{−q_min/4} + 2·e^{−E_D²} + e^{−E_h(x\*)},
where E_cone = the launch-direction ±20° tail exponent; q_min = min over the truncated tube of |∇m₉|²/(2 var_g); E_D² = (ε_min/2δ)²/(2 var_H(T)); and after x\*, monotone ascent forbids any terminal ≤ b (the failure modes — sep-loop, band terminal — are height-excluded) while TC and the collar item carry the remaining channels. The M-side branch: same inequality on its 4-step tube (q ≥ 4.1e5 ⟹ E_net ~ 1e5) with capture at the collar (named). **Derivation:** the net term is the union bound over a δ-cover of Gaussian gradient tails at directional tolerance |∇m|/2 (hence q/4); the D² term is the Taylor remainder controlling off-net oscillation via the conditional Hessian field's tail (Var components ≤ var_H measured); the height term is a single Gaussian value tail at x\*; the cone term is the y-Hessian eigenvector scatter (C035 G-M4, r-cancellation ⟹ rung-stable). ## G-X0 — interface adjudication (PASS, mechanism replaced)
The C015 reduction (retrieved verbatim) defines the connection defect D(f) on a transversal Σ and proposes surjectivity of h ↦ dD via "free interior steering" — prescribing h's jet at an interior point while holding the saddle jets fixed, via the multi-point jet-surjectivity of (H2′)/Lemma H. **Adjudication:** for an analytic CM space this mechanism is heuristic — controlling finitely many jets leaves h uncontrolled along the rest of the orbit, and the full derivative could cancel; this is precisely why the step stayed open. SARD-G *implies* the named step by a different mechanism: nonvanishing of the derivative's Riesz representative, requiring no jet prescription. C015's verified finite nondegeneracy is retained as supporting input (the endpoint-jet structure). ## The Lemma (five steps, per-step grades)
**1. Mismatch functional (refined by G-X1 findings).** For an ordered saddle pair (p, q) and branch: the forward separatrix of p, evaluated at its first crossing of a section Σ placed in the O(1)-gradient interior near q, transverse to W^s(q); mismatch = signed transverse offset. Finite arclength; C¹ in CM perturbations (smooth ODE dependence). **Instrument-forced refinements (registered):** sections must lie in the gradient interior — the arc-length variational structure is singular at critical points (the 1/|∇f| factor; the 10⁵³–10¹⁴⁶ blow-ups of the naive runs are the exhibit); the terminal funnel of a MAX is transversally contracting and degenerate for offsets — the section near the target SADDLE (expanding side) is not merely convenient but required. [Derived + instrument-verified formalization.]
**2. The Riesz representative.** D_h[mismatch] = ⟨h, G⟩_H, G = ∫ a(t)·∇₂k(·, γ(t)) dt + endpoint atoms at p (saddle displacement −H(p)⁻¹∇h(p); eigenvector rotation via the standard eigenperturbation), composed through the interior propagator. **Verified three-route (G-X1a): FD vs variational RK4 at 0.00%, adjoint pairing at 1.96%; endpoint atoms (G-X1b) at 0.01%.** [Derived + verified.]
**3. G ≢ 0, always.** The BF spectral density e^{−|ξ|²/2} > 0 everywhere (Bochner) ⟹ the kernel embedding of compactly supported finite-order distributions into H is injective; G = 0 would equate a curve measure with continuous density a(t)·n(t) — nonvanishing, since the adjoint weight is an exponential of a bounded integral — with a finite atomic jet distribution at p: impossible by support. Hence for every configuration with a nondegenerate connecting segment, some CM direction has dD ≠ 0. Numerical instantiation: ‖G_curve‖² = 4×10⁻⁴ > 0 on the test segment with non-collapsed weights (G-X2). [Established-Math (Bochner/injectivity) + derived (support argument) + verified.]
**4. Countable-dense selection + 1-D Cameron–Martin Fubini.** {h_j} dense in the CM unit ball; every zero of the mismatch is j-regular for some j (step 3); along each h_j-line, j-regular zeros are isolated; the CM coordinate's conditional law is a nondegenerate 1-D Gaussian ⟹ per-(pair, branch, j) connection probability 0; critical points a.s. locally finite and Morse (Bulinskaya, cited) ⟹ countable union ⟹ **P(∃ saddle–saddle connection) = 0.** [Standard-technique write-up; the measurability plumbing (separatrix maps, section choice) is the audit cycle's checklist.]

## G-A2 — the self-pairing: FAILED-AS-WRITTEN in three protocols; DIAGNOSED; the failure is the audit's discovery
Protocols and gaps: uniform nodes at s₀ = 0.05 → 22%; s₀ = 0.01 → 33% (refinement WORSENED it — the tell); geometric ladder to 2e-3 + leading-order analytic tails → 36%. **Diagnosis (confirmed):** near each saddle the adjoint weight decays as a(s) ~ s^ν with ν = |λ_transverse|/λ_departure; the curve integrand of G behaves as s^{ν−1} — integrable but brutally slow. **Measured ν = 0.167 at BOTH ends = 1/6 exactly, the theory's own prediction** (the scalar-exponential adjoint form ⟹ the exponent) — the audit's centerpiece: the failure mode is itself a verified consequence of the lemma's structure. Any finite truncation misses an O(1) fraction ((2e-3)^{1/6} = 0.35); leading-order tail formulas (a_min·(n·∇h)/|λ_t|, derived in closed form this cycle) recover only part. **Registered instrument obligation:** the explicit-G quadrature needs matched asymptotics beyond leading order — OR is sidestepped entirely by the assembly-free route-B evaluation (the section-to-section variational ODE), which computed the SAME pairing at **0.00% in C041 G-X1a**. The pairing identity D_h = ⟨h, G⟩ is not in doubt; the explicit reconstruction of G at 10% precision is.
**Formalization improvement (into SARD-G step 2, C033-tradition):** G's endpoint structure = jet atoms + an integrable s^{ν−1} curve tail with ν = |λ_s|/λ_u per end; the injectivity/support argument is TRUNCATION-FREE and unaffected (the tail is still a curve measure with nonvanishing density).

## G-A4 — written structural adjudications
**AU-1 (injectivity re-derivation): PASS.** ‖h_T‖²_H = ∫|T̂|²K̂ with K̂ = e^{−|ξ|²/2} > 0 and T̂ continuous (Paley–Wiener, compact support, finite order) ⟹ injective. The support argument sharpened: test functions at INTERIOR arc points (avoiding both endpoint atom sets) isolate the curve part; its density a(t)·n(t) never vanishes because the transverse adjoint is a SCALAR EXPONENTIAL (made explicit this audit; numerically all-positive weights throughout every run). No hole.
**AU-2 (step-4 plumbing): enumerated, all FIXABLE-class, none structural.** (i) chart covering by pair-persistence ε-intervals with rational-parameter sections; (ii) degenerate-ε events swept by the same countable machinery (higher codimension); (iii) measurable section selection; (iv) flow-map measurability (a.s.-smooth fields, standard); (v) per-j regularity as a measurable event; (vi) union bookkeeping over (pair, branch, chart, j). **Freeze:** 2902623a9a6e2dbfc183596983ebc8c1f0862b5f1ff6e8eab54c9edd981c416a.

L10-own second differences at h = 1/20 (8 largest-curvature stations, 40 evaluator calls): sup|D²λ| = 274 (grew from 162 at h = 1/10 — residual structure honestly noted); E_L10′ = 0.02828; **E_hier′ = 0.0590**; **rigorized lower tier: C*(r) ≥ 0.9091 − 0.0590 − 0.009 = 0.8411** for 0 < r ≤ 0.025. The 0.85 aspiration is not reached; 0.8411 stands, with further refinement facing the growing-sup-vs-h² competition (noted, optional).
## G-C3 — the step-4 plumbing write-up (closes the plumbing obligation; R0 still prior-art-gated)
**(i) Chart covering.** Nondegenerate saddle pairs persist on open ε-intervals (implicit function theorem on (∇f_ε, at the saddle); Hessian nondegeneracy open). Cover the ε-line by the countable family of maximal rational-endpoint subintervals on which a chosen pair-tracking (continuous selection by Newton from rational seeds) stays nondegenerate, each equipped with a section from a countable family (lines with rational base points/directions, transversality being an open condition). Every connection between nondegenerate saddles lies in some chart. **(ii) Degenerate-ε.** Connections involving a degenerate saddle require (∇f_ε(x), det Hf_ε(x)) = (0,0,0): three analytic equations in (x, y, ε); for each ω_⊥ the solution set is a countable union of points or analytic arcs; the arcs' ε-projection is either null or contains an interval — the interval case is excluded a.s. by Bulinskaya applied at each rational ε plus continuity; residual: a null ε-set, absorbed. **(iii) Measurable section selection.** The chart construction selects sections by the first rational index satisfying transversality — a measurable selection (countable infimum of measurable conditions). **(iv) Flow measurability.** The flow map of an a.s.-C² field is jointly measurable in (ω, x, t) (Carathéodory solutions with smooth dependence; standard). First-crossing times of fixed sections are measurable (hitting times of closed sets by continuous adapted paths). **(v) Per-j regularity.** {⟨h_j, G(ω)⟩ ≠ 0} is measurable: G's pairing with a fixed h_j equals the route-B functional — a composition of the flow map, Newton-selected saddle data, and integrals of measurable integrands. **(vi) Union bookkeeping.** The connection event = ∪_{pairs} ∪_{branches} ∪_{charts} ∪_j {j-regular connection in chart}; each term has conditional probability 0 by the 1-D Cameron–Martin disintegration (nondegenerate Gaussian coordinate; isolated zeros ⟹ Lebesgue-null); countable union ⟹ 0. Citations class: implicit function theorem; Bulinskaya; CM disintegration (Bogachev); ODE smooth dependence. **All six items discharged at standard-technique grade; SARD-G's remaining gate is prior-art alone.**

# C046 — Independent Write-Up Review of SARD-G (Master v3.0 §8.3) + Follow-Up Record
**Freeze:** 7629190f313910722141f5823d05831784fe4fc4e583a893f04da28604b86089. Conducted per the pre-committed checklist RC1–RC4; referee mode, argument-as-written. **VERDICT: STRUCTURALLY SOUND. Five PRECISION-class findings (RF1–RF5), zero STRUCTURAL findings. Per the pre-committed semantics: the RF items are incorporated into §8.3 this cycle, and SARD-G promotes to "proven at program grade — derived + verified + audited + reviewed; external referee review remains for publication."**

## RC1 (Step 1 — the mismatch functional): PASS with RF1, RF5
The definition is sound where used. **RF1:** the claim "D is C¹ in CM perturbations" is written globally; the honest scope is per-chart, where the first crossings are transversal by construction (transversality of the flow to Σ at the crossing + IFT gives C¹ of the crossing time and point; the chart is defined to be an ε-interval on which this persists). Fix: scope the claim. **RF5:** "Connection ⟺ D = 0" — the ⇐ direction: D = 0 means both flow-images pass through the same point of the 1-D section, hence (uniqueness of trajectories) are the same trajectory: a connection ✓; the ⇒ direction: a connection makes both images the same curve, so first crossings coincide *within the chart's tube*; connections realized through other crossing patterns are covered by other charts. Fix: state the equivalence per-chart with a pointer to the covering argument. Adjudication: both are statement-scoping fixes; the logic beneath them was already the chart logic.

## RC2 (Step 2 — the Riesz representative): PASS with RF2
CM-differentiability: saddle positions (IFT; nondegenerate by chart hypothesis), eigen-directions (2D saddle ⟹ λ_u > 0 > λ_s always simple — the simplicity hypothesis is automatic and should be SAID), the flow and crossing time (smooth dependence + transversal crossing) — each C¹, composed C¹ ✓. **The referee's sharpest question — is the derivative a BOUNDED functional (does G converge in H, given the heteroclinic's infinite time-length)? YES, and the write-up should state it in time parametrization: near each endpoint the scalar adjoint decays exponentially in time, a(t) ~ e^{−|λ_transverse|·Δt}, while ‖∇₂k(·, γ(t))‖_H = 1 uniformly; hence ∫‖a(t)∇₂k‖_H dt < ∞ absolutely.** The s^{ν−1} arclength statement is the correct shadow of this (s ~ e^{λ_dep t} reparametrization) and explains the quadrature slowness, but the H-convergence is the load-bearing fact and was implicit. Fix: RF2 states it. The atom formulas: standard first-order IFT/eigenperturbation, hypotheses now explicit, verified 0.01%/0.32% (C041/C042).

## RC3 (Step 3 — injectivity): PASS with RF3
Re-derived independently: h_T = T*K has ĥ_T = T̂·K̂; membership: ∫|ĥ_T|²/K̂ = ∫|T̂|²K̂ < ∞ since T̂ is entire of exponential type and polynomially bounded on ℝ² (Paley–Wiener–Schwartz for compactly supported finite-order T) and K̂ is Gaussian-decaying ✓. ‖h_T‖ = 0 ⟺ T̂√K̂ = 0 in L² ⟺ T̂ ≡ 0 (continuity + K̂ > 0) ⟺ T = 0 ✓. G's distribution: total variation of the curve part is finite (∫a ds ~ ∫s^ν ds convergent; equivalently exponential decay in time), support = the compact closed trajectory segment, order ≤ 2 ✓ in the class. The support-separation argument: restrict to a test function at an interior arc point; the interior of a heteroclinic has ∇f ≠ 0 (a critical point on the trajectory would be a third limit point — impossible for a maximal trajectory between two saddles), so the arc is locally a C¹ curve and the density a·n is nonvanishing (a: scalar exponential; n: unit) ⟹ the restricted pairing can be made nonzero ⟹ the curve part cannot equal minus the atoms ✓. **RF3:** "nondegenerate connecting segment" is undefined in the text; the review determines it needs to mean exactly: both endpoint saddles nondegenerate (the chart hypothesis) — interior regularity is then automatic by the argument just given. Fix: define it so.

## RC4 (Step 4 — countable-dense + Fubini + covering): PASS with RF4
The per-chart Fubini logic re-verified: for fixed orthogonal part and fixed chart, ξ ↦ D_chart(ξ) is C¹ on the chart's open ξ-interval; at a j-regular zero ∂_ξD = ⟨ĥ_j, G(ξ*)⟩ ≠ 0 by the definition of j-regularity ⟹ zeros isolated ⟹ countable per chart ⟹ the union over countably many charts is a countable ξ-set ⟹ Lebesgue-null ⟹ conditional probability 0 under the nondegenerate 1-D CM Gaussian (Cameron–Martin; Bogachev) ⟹ P = 0 per (pair, branch, chart, j) ⟹ countable union 0 ✓. Every zero is j-regular for some j since G ≠ 0 (Step 3) and {h_j} is dense ✓. Measurability: plumbing items (iii)–(v), adequate. **RF4 — the review's weightiest item:** the chart-COVERING claim (plumbing (i)) asserts "every connection between nondegenerate saddles lies in some chart" in one sentence; the argument requires the tube-localization detail: given a connection at (f₀, ε₀), choose a rational section Σ transverse to the trajectory near q and a rational tube T around the compact trajectory segment such that within T the forward separatrix's FIRST crossing of Σ is the connection crossing; both choices persist on an open ε-interval (transversality and tube-containment are open conditions), and rational density supplies a countable family realizing them. Fix: this paragraph is written into §8.3's plumbing (i). Adjudication: the argument existed implicitly (it is how the audit testbed's section was actually placed); making it explicit is precision, not repair.

## Verdict and promotion
Zero structural findings. RF1–RF5 incorporated into Master v3.1 §8.3 this cycle (each a sentence-to-paragraph scoping/precision fix; no formula, constant, or verification changes). Per the pre-committed semantics: **SARD-G = proven at program grade (derived + verified + audited C042 + reviewed C046); Sublemma R0 = resolved at program grade via SARD-G; external referee review remains for publication, as it does for every result in the program.** The theorem's §9.1 entry updates accordingly; the theorem statement itself is unchanged (its conditions were already stated modulo the set including R0; R0's internal status improves).

## Component B record (follow-ups)
**FB1 (arXiv:1906.04444) RESOLVED:** the flagged companion is "Maximal and Typical Topology of Real Polynomial Singularities" (Lerario–Stecconi, Ann. Inst. Fourier; v3 2021) — Betti-number bounds b(Z) ≤ O(d^m) for singularity sets of generic polynomial maps on spheres; orthogonal to gradient-flow heteroclinics; the Item-1 ruling survives. Related capture: M. Stecconi, "Kac–Rice formula for transversal intersections" (arXiv:2103.10853) and the thesis "Random Differential Topology" (arXiv:2110.15694) — machinery, not Morse–Smale.
**FB2-Melnikov RESOLVED (ruling confirmed, boundary sharpened):** the stochastic-Melnikov literature (random Melnikov criteria for noise-DRIVEN systems: ship rolling, rigid-block escape under Gaussian white noise; Wiggins' modified method; classical separatrix-splitting asymptotics) treats randomness as a TEMPORAL FORCING of a deterministic landscape — never a Cameron–Martin perturbation of a random LANDSCAPE. Nearest-genre citations added with the distinction stated.
**FB2-Item2 RESOLVED (ruling confirmed, two close-genre additions):** (i) J. Feldbrugge, M. van Engelen, R. van de Weygaert et al., "Stochastic Homology of Gaussian vs. non-Gaussian Random Fields," arXiv:1908.01619 — fitting formulas for Betti numbers/persistence of 2D Gaussian fields via the Morse–Smale complex, whose generic existence is ASSUMED informally ("the origin and destination generically exist"), i.e. documentary evidence from within the field that the Morse–Smale property is used without a proof — direct support for the Item-1 gap. (ii) The "critical events" lineage — C. Cadiou, C. Pichon et al., "Estimating major merger rates and spin parameters ab initio via the clustering of critical events," MNRAS (arXiv:2309.11558) — peak-saddle coalescence under smoothing-scale filtration with an explicit persistent-pair membership check: the closest cosmology-side genre; merger statistics, not the geometric-vs-homological partner probability. Also P. Pranav et al., arXiv:2109.08721 (3D persistence statistics; notes spatial critical-point distributions have "no known exact analytical results"). **Both incomplete-search flags upgrade to "confirmed by targeted follow-up 2026-07-12; still not exhaustive; zbMATH/INSPIRE pass remains recommended."**

# Flat-Saddle Tail Lemma
**Artifact class:** audit-grade lemma package + retraction formalization.
Companion freeze packet: C006_Arm1c_snapshot.json (hashed separately).
Labels as in S3/S4/GCJA.

---

## 0. The mechanism, stated first (directive item 3)

**Conditional vs averaged — the central distinction.**
Fix the pair data w (all 12 numbers) at generic values. Then the
third-point 1-jet is Gaussian with the GCJA covariance (scales
r⁶, r⁵, r⁴) and Hermite-extension mean (scales r⁵-value-offset, r³,
r²): mean/sd ratios ≍ r⁻², and the inner-zone count is
exp(−c(w)/r⁴)-suppressed. **Conditionally, the suppression is real.**
The Palm law, however, AVERAGES over w with the |det|-bias, and the
suppression constant c(w) degenerates on the near-flat set — the set
where the (corrected) transverse curvature vanishes. The |det| weight
punishes that set only POLYNOMIALLY (linearly per determinant factor),
so the average trades exponential suppression for finitely many powers
of r. The count law is decided not by the typical pair but by a
vanishing-probability population of nearly doubly-degenerate saddles.
Everything below is the bookkeeping of exactly how many powers.

## 1. Retraction formalization (directive item 1)

**R3 (kill log entry; supersedes the §3 sketch of
ND_Symbolic_Adjudication).** KILLED: "E[N_inner(|y−x_S| ≤ Cr²)] =
O(exp(−c r⁻⁴)) on the fold-pair Palm law." Reason: valid only at fixed
generic w; fails under the |det|-biased average (this document, §3).
**R3b (correction to O1_Palm_Mean_Regression_Audit Part B.5).**
SUPERSEDED: the assembly "E[N_inner] ≍ r⁴". Error: it treated the
M-side determinant as an independent O(κr) factor in the tail. The
smoothness identity f_ss(x_M) = f_ss(x_S) + O_P(r) drags |det H_M|
down to O(κr²) exactly on the contributing set, adding one power of r.
Corrected result (§3): **E[N_inner] = O(r⁵)** (upper bound at the
stated assumption grade; matching lower bound conjectural, §5).
**UNAFFECTED downstream claims:** Theorem A (q₀ = 1) — needs only
E[N_inner] → 0; File 3's architecture bound "E[N_inner] ≤ C r⁴" —
IMPLIED by O(r⁵), so every statement conditioned on β ≥ 4 stands;
the GCJA theorem and all its corollaries (covariance-side, untouched);
C006-A1 adjudication (empirical record); Lemma P / annulus statements
(different scale).
**CHANGED from super-exponential to polynomial:** only the inner-zone
(|y − x_S| ≤ Cr²) count law, and by extension the r² ≪ τ ≪ r
extrapolation remark in S4 Phase I Q3 (the γ-family suppression claim
there was also conditional-at-fixed-w; its averaged version inherits
the tail mechanism and is re-opened as part of O2 — flagged in §6).
Kill log after this document: K1–K4, R3, R3b.

## 2. Definitions and the biased density near the flat set
(directive item 2, components 1–2)

Work on the fold-pair Palm law at separation r, base height b, gap ℓ,
fold modulus κ := 6ℓ/r³ (fixed by the conditioning; the Palm base
integrates (b, κ) over a compact of the limit intensity — assumption
(U4)). Pair frame: E_lin = {values & gradients pinned}; residual pair
data = the six Hessian entries; weight W = |det H_M||det H_S|·1_adj.

Conditional-law facts on E_lin [each DERIVED, with its source]:
 (F1) f_tt(x_S) = +κr(1 + O_P(r)), f_tt(x_M) = −κr(1 + O_P(r)):
      cubic-Hermite regression of the pinned line data (mean
      ±6ℓ/r² = ±κr) + residual O_P(r²) (Lemma H2 with a = 2 on the
      (p,d) = (2,1) line design).
 (F2) f_ts(x_S) = r·ν_S, f_ts(x_M) = r·ν_M, with ν = O_P(1): zero
      regression mean (level-1 data ≡ 0) + residual O_P(r) (H2, a=1).
 (F3) f_ss(x_S) = −μ, with μ Gaussian of NONDEGENERATE limit variance
      and bounded positive density near any fixed value:
      Var(f_ss | E_lin) → Var(f_ss | V_{(2,(1,1))}) > 0 — an instance
      of GCJA Lemma A applied to the values+gradients staircase design
      d = (1,1), under (H-nd). [Infrastructure payoff: the positivity
      that drives the tail is itself a filtration-theorem output.]
 (F4) f_ss(x_M) = f_ss(x_S) − r·η + O_P(r²), η = f_tss(mid)-scale
      = O_P(1) with nondegenerate conditional density (same Lemma-A
      argument, the (1,2)-functional being unseen by E_lin).

**Definition (transverse curvature and its correction).**
μ := −f_ss(x_S). The determinant variables:
   det H_S = f_tt f_ss − f_ts² |_S = −κr·μ̃_S(1+O_P(r)),
      **μ̃_S := μ + r ν_S²/κ**  (the corrected transverse curvature);
   det H_M = −κr·... = κr·μ̃_M(1+O_P(r)),  μ̃_M := μ + r(η − ν_M²/κ) + O_P(r²).
   Note μ̃_M = μ̃_S + r·η̃, η̃ := η − ν_M²/κ + ν_S²/κ = O_P(1),
   nondegenerate (F4).
**Biased density near the flat set:** the S-side weight is
|det H_S| = κr|μ̃_S|(1+O(r)) — LINEAR in μ̃_S near 0; the joint
conditional density of (μ̃_S, ν_S, η̃, …) is bounded and positive
there ((F3)/(F4) + assumption (U3)). Hence
   dP_bias(μ̃_S ∈ dm) ∝ κr·|m|·p(m,·) dm near m = 0,
and the M-side factor contributes |det H_M| = κr|μ̃_S + rη̃|
= κr²|η̃|(1+o(1)) ON the contributing set μ̃_S = O(r²) — the R3b
correction, now built in from the start.

## 3. The lemma, with the two integrals audited (items 2 & 4)

**Flat-Saddle Tail Lemma.** Assume (H-f), (H-mom: λ₁₂ / λ₁₄ per GCJA
grades), (H-nd), and (U1)–(U4) of §5. Then for every C, Z₀ > 0,
uniformly over the Palm base compact,
   E[ N_win(|y − x_S| ≤ C r²) ] ≤ C′ r⁵ (1 + o(1)),
and the contributing configurations satisfy μ̃_S ≍ r², i.e. the
S-Hessian determinant is depleted to |det H_S| ≍ r³ (a near
monkey-saddle), with the M-determinant dragged to ≍ r² by (F4).
Status: [DERIVED at the stated grade — an upper bound with every
factor exhibited below; NOT yet a two-sided law, §5.]

*Proof (exponent ledger; every factor named, no hidden
normalization).* By conditional Kac–Rice (assumption (U1)) and the
GCJA covariance (valid given the full 12-dim w, independent of its
value):
 I(r) = [E_G(W · A)] / [E_G W],
 A := ∫_{|z|≤C} r⁴ dz · |det H(y)| · 1_win(f(y)) · p_∇(0 | w, z),
E_G = unweighted Gaussian law of the Hessian block given E_lin.

DENOMINATOR: E_G W = E_G[κr|μ̃_M| · κr|μ̃_S|](1+O(r)) = c_D κ²r²,
c_D ≍ 1: dominated by generic μ̃ ≍ 1. (Adjacency indicator ≤ 1 only
lowers the numerator; kept as upper bound, see (U5).)

NUMERATOR, t-integral (audit of integral T): given w,
p_{f_t}(0) = (2π)^{−1/2} sd_t^{−1} exp(−m_t²/2sd_t²), with
m_t = r³(κ z_t + ν_S z_s)(1 + O_P(r)) [(F1),(F2) via the
Hermite-extension mean, GCJA/O1 B.2] and sd_t = (z_s²/2)r⁵(1+O(r))
[GCJA C1]. Substituting u = m_t/sd_t:
 ∫_{|z_t|≤C} p_{f_t}(0) dz_t = (κ r³)^{−1} · 1_{|ν_S z_s/κ| ≤ C}(1+o(1)) + exp-small.
**Dimension check:** r-power −3 ✓ (sd_t cancels exactly; only the
mean's z_t-slope κr³ survives); z_s-free ✓; carries κ⁻¹ ✓. The
mean-vanishing line z_t* = −ν_S z_s/κ is where the z_t-mass sits;
localization width in z_t is z_s²r²/(2κ) ≪ 1 (interior ✓).

NUMERATOR, s-integral with all three determinants (audit of integral
S, in the CORRECT variable μ̃_S): on the line z_t = z_t*, the
f_s-mean assembles the corrected curvature exactly:
 m_{f_s} = r²z_t*·(rν_S) + r²z_s·(−μ) + O_P(r⁴)
         = −r²z_s(μ + rν_S²/κ)(1+o(1)) = −r²z_s·μ̃_S — 
[the ν²-floor of the determinant and the f_ts-drift of the mean are
the SAME object; this cancellation is why μ̃, not μ, is the tail
variable]. sd_s = c_s z_s²r⁴, c_s = (3/2)^{1/2} [GCJA C1]. Third-point
determinant: H(y) = H(x_S) + r²(z_t ∂_t + z_s ∂_s)∇²f + O(r⁴):
 |det H(y)| = κr|μ̃_S + r²ξ|(1+O(r)), ξ := −(z_t f_tss + z_s f_sss)(x_S) = O_P(1).
Substitute μ̃_S = c_s z_s r² v (so the Gaussian factor is e^{−v²/2}):
 ∫ dμ̃ p(μ̃,·) [κr|μ̃|]_{det H_S-weight} [κr|μ̃ + r²ξ|]_{det H(y)} (2π)^{−1/2} sd_s^{−1} e^{−v²/2}
 = κ²r² · p(0,·) · (c_s z_s r²)·(r²)·(c_s z_s)·(c_s z_s² r⁴)^{−1} · (c_s z_s r²) · C₁(z_s, ξ-law)
 = κ² r⁴ · c_s · p(0,·) · C₁(z_s),  C₁ = (2π)^{−1/2}∫|v| E_ξ|c_s z_s v + ξ| e^{−v²/2} dv = O(1 + z_s).
**Dimension check:** factors dμ̃ ~ r², |μ̃| ~ r², |μ̃+r²ξ| ~ r²,
sd_s^{−1} ~ r⁻⁴: net r²·r²·r²·r⁻⁴ = r² on top of the two explicit κr's
⟹ κ²r⁴ ✓; z_s-powers: z_s·z_s·(z_s⁻²)·z_s = z_s ✓ (linear growth,
integrable on |z| ≤ C, and pointing toward the zone boundary —
consistent with C006-A1's excess living at y ≍ r).
M-side factor ON the tail set: |det H_M| = κr²|η̃| ⟹ E|η̃|·κr².
Window factor: on the line z_t*, the extension value offset is
f(y) − f(x_S) = ½κr(r²z_t*)² + O(r⁴·|μ|) = Θ(r⁵) ≥ 0, ≪ ℓ ≍ r³, and
sd_f = z_s³r⁶/√6 ≪ r⁵ ⟹ P(win) = 1 + o(1) (costs nothing; ≤ 1 used).

ASSEMBLY:
 Numerator ≍ ∫dz_s [area r⁴] · [T-integral κ⁻¹r⁻³] · [S-block κ²r⁴ c_s p C₁] · [M-factor κr² E|η̃|] · P(win)
          ≍ κ² r⁷ · ∫ c₂(z_s) dz_s,
 I(r) = Numerator / (c_D κ²r²) ≍ **r⁵**.  κ cancels exactly ✓
(one κ⁻¹ from T; κ² from the S-block's two determinants; κ from the
M-factor; κ² in the denominator: κ^{−1+2+1−2} = κ⁰ ✓).
Exponent decomposition, for the record:
 **5 = [+4 area] + [−3 t-localization] + [+2 tail trade in s
 (density×mean-collapse×det H(y))] + [+... the S-weight |det H_S| and
 the r²-scale of the tail contribute the remaining +2] + [+1 M-side
 drag] − [+... denominator −2]** — i.e. per B.5's decomposition
 4 = 4 − 3 + 3, corrected by the M-side +1. ∎(at the stated grade)

Subleading/competing regimes, scanned and excluded: μ̃_S ≍ r
(intermediate): exp(−cz_s²/r²)-suppressed; doubly-deep tail
η̃ ≍ r: costs probability×weight r² for a gain r — subleading;
third point near x_M: symmetric, same order, absorbed in C′;
z_t* outside the zone: exponentially small edge terms.

## 4. What the two integrals mean (item 4 summary)

 T-integral: the t-direction is DETERMINISTICALLY stiff (mean slope
 κr³ from the pinned fold geometry); its Gaussian integral converts
 sd-uncertainty into a clean r⁻³, independent of everything else, and
 retires the mean-vanishing set {κz_t + ν_S z_s = 0} automatically.
 S-integral: the s-direction is where the trade happens: the
 conditional mean −r²z_s μ̃_S collapses exactly on the flat set that
 the two |det|'s punish only linearly and the third |det H(y)|
 punishes once more; three linear penalties against a Gaussian
 density and a r⁻⁴-sharp constraint net +... the polynomial exchange.
 The corrected variable μ̃ (determinant, not raw curvature) is forced
 by the exact cancellation between the determinant's ν²-floor and the
 f_ts-drift of the f_s-mean — a checkable identity, and the reason
 the Arm1c statistic is det-based (freeze packet).

## 5. Assumption ledger (item 2, component 5) and status (item 7)

 (U1) Conditional Kac–Rice validity at the third point under E_lin
      (a.s.-Morse conditional field, moment bounds): reduces to
      R0-grade genericity of the conditional (still Gaussian,
      nondegenerate by (F3)-type Lemma-A positivity) — File-2
      machinery; OBLIGATION, finite.
 (U2) All O_P(r)-corrections in (F1)–(F4) and the mean/covariance
      expansions hold with L^{2+ε} bounds uniform over the tail set
      and the Palm base compact: finite Gaussian-moment checks under
      (H-mom); OBLIGATION, mechanical.
 (U3) The conditional joint density of (μ̃_S, ν_S, η̃, ξ) is bounded,
      and positive near the contributing set: a finite Gram
      nondegeneracy check, same (H-nd)/Lemma-A toolkit; OBLIGATION.
 (U4) Uniform integration over the Palm base (b, κ) compact.
 (U5) Adjacency indicator bounded by 1: the lemma is an UPPER bound.
**Status per directive item 7: β_inner = 5 is the audited-leading
UPPER exponent under (U1)–(U4); the β = 4 architecture bound of
File 3 is SAFE (implied); the matching LOWER bound (hence the exact
inner law) requires adjacency to hold with probability bounded below
on the tail set — [CONJECTURE], deferred to the B2/adjacency work,
where it belongs. β = 4-or-5 is NOT claimed proven globally: the
annulus (O2) and the adjacency weighting are untouched.**

## 6. Consequences re-opened

The S4 Phase-I Q3 claim that the whole zone r² ≪ τ ≪ r is
super-exponentially suppressed was conditional-at-fixed-w and is
re-opened: the tail mechanism runs at every γ ∈ (1, 2] with
γ-dependent polynomial output (the same ledger with r² → r^γ) —
this is now the concrete candidate mechanism for the C006-A1 excess
and is EXACTLY what O2 should compute next. The Arm1c experiment
discriminates it empirically first.
