Graded Conditional-Jet Asymptotics for Collapsing
Gaussian Observation Designs
Artifact class: theorem/proof package. Discharges Phase-V obligations (α), (β), (γ) at
lemma level; converts the S4 candidate theorem to a formal statement with proof; recovers
Ʃ₂(0), rank collapse, slaving, parity, positivity, the γ-family, and the T2 design-surgery result
as corollaries. Epistemic labels as in S3/S4. Items not reached by the theorem are marked
OPEN in §8. No “standard technique” citations are used in place of proofs; the two classical
inputs (Hermite unisolvence on a line; the spectral representation of stationary Gaussian
fields) are stated with their proofs sketched to audit sufficiency in §2–§3.
§0. Hypotheses and standing notation
(H-f) f is a centered stationary Gaussian field on R² with covariance C(x) = ∫ e^{i⟨k,x⟩} dρ(k),
ρ a finite symmetric (ρ(−A) = ρ(A)) Borel measure. [Torus T²_L: ρ a symmetric measure on
the dual lattice; every statement below is measure-theoretic in ρ and applies verbatim.]
(H-mom) Moment order: λ_{2m} := ∫ |k|^{2m} dρ < ∞ for all 2m ≤ M(D) := 2·max_k (q_k + k)
+ 2, with q_k defined in §1. [For the (p,j) = (2,2) full design: M = 14; the leading-order
CONCLUSIONS need only 2m ≤ 12 — the extra +2 buys the error margin δ.]
(H-nd) ρ is N-nondegenerate with N := max_k(q_k + k): no nonzero polynomial of degree ≤
2N vanishes ρ-a.e. [Implied by “spectral measure charges an open set”; on the torus, by
(H2’).]
Gaussian space and spectral isometry. Every real linear functional Λ = Ʃ c_{α,x} ∂^α f(x)
(finite sum, |α| within (H-mom)) corresponds to λ(k) = Ʃ c_{α,x} (ik)^α e^{i⟨k,x⟩}, and E[Λ Λ′]
= ∫ λ conj(λ′) dρ. Proof sketch (audit level): f(x) = ∫ e^{i⟨k,x⟩} dW_ρ(k) with W_ρ the
symmetrized complex Gaussian orthogonal measure with control ρ; the identity holds for Λ
= f(x) by the isometry of the stochastic integral, extends to derivatives by L²-differentiability
(dominated convergence under (H-mom): difference quotients of e^{i⟨k,x⟩} are dominated
by |k| |e^{…}|), and to finite sums by linearity. Reality of the field ⟺ symmetry of ρ; for our
functionals all inner products below are real. ∎
§1. The design, the filtration, the stratum, the multiplier map
Definition 1 (staircase design). Fix p ≥ 2 distinct reals c_1 < … < c_p and a staircase d =

(d_0 ≥ d_1 ≥ … ≥ d_J ≥ 0). The design D(p; d) at scale r observes O_r = { ∂_t^m ∂_s^k f(c_i
r, 0) : k ≤ J, m ≤ d_k, i ≤ p }. S_r := span O_r ⊂ L²(ρ), dim S_r = Ʃ_k p(d_k+1) =: n_D (for
small r; see Lemma A3). The full design D(p,j) is d_k = j−k, J = j.
Definition 2 (level orders, visible space, stratum). q_k := p(d_k + 1) for k ≤ J; q_k := 0 for
k > J. V(D) := span{ φ_{m,k} : k ≤ J, m ≤ q_k − 1 }, φ_{m,k}(k) := (ik_t)^m (ik_s)^k, U(D) := {
ψ_σ = φ_{m,k} : (m,k) unseen, i.e. k > J or m ≥ q_k }. #V(D) = n_D (no waste). For the full
design, V = {m + pk ≤ p(j+1) − 1} (the (1,p)-weighted ball) and the minimal unseen stratum is
weighted degree p(j+1) — S3/S4’s filtration is the special case.
Definition 3 (evaluation scaling and ladder orders). Evaluation point y = (c_p r + r^γ z_t,
r^γ z_s), γ > 0, z in a fixed compact K ⊂ R². For an observable φ^a_y = ∂^{(a_t,a_s)} f(y), |a|
≤ 1, and an unseen ψ_σ, σ = (m,k), define the deterministic ladder order L_a(σ; γ) := γ·[(k −
a_s)+ … ] — given constructively in §5, Step 2, as the exact power of r carried by ψ_σ’s
coefficient in the residual expansion of φ^a_y. Closed forms used in the corollaries: pure-transverse σ = (0, k), k > J: L = γ(k − a_s) for a_t = 0; level-k interpolation error, k ≤ J,
entering φ^a via the node polynomial: L = γ(k − a_s) + (q_k/p)(p−1) + γ(q_k/p − a_t·1{…}), i.e.
ω-factor (p−1)(d_k+1) + γ(d_k+1 − a_t) plus the transverse γ(k − a_s) — see Step 2 for the
precise bookkeeping. ℓ_a := min_σ L_a(σ; γ); Ʃ_a := argmin set (“leading stratum for a”);
δ(D,γ) := min over the finite exponent ladder of the positive gaps, ∧ 1. [δ > 0 whenever γ
avoids the finitely many tie values; at ties the theorem still holds with the tied σ jointly in
Ʃ_a.]
Definition 4 (Gram pushforward). G_{U|V}(σ,τ) := ⟨Q_V ψ_σ, Q_V ψ_τ⟩, Q_V = orthogonal
projection onto V(D)^⊥ in L²(ρ) — the conditional covariance of the unseen monomial
functionals at the origin given the visible ones. The multiplier map m^a: Ʃ_a → R[z] assigns
each leading σ its deterministic coefficient polynomial (Step 2). The theorem’s limit object is
Ʃ_∞^{ab}(z) := Ʃ_{σ,τ} m^a_σ(z) m^b_τ(z) G_{U|V}(σ,τ).
§2. Deterministic lemmas (interpolation)
Lemma H0 (line-Hermite unisolvence). Given distinct nodes x_1,…,x_p and jet order d, for
any data {g_{i,l}} (l ≤ d) there is a unique polynomial H of degree ≤ p(d+1) − 1 with H^{(l)}
(x_i) = g_{i,l}. Proof: the linear map (coefficients) → (jet data) between spaces of equal
dimension p(d+1) is injective: a polynomial of degree ≤ p(d+1)−1 with a zero of multiplicity
d+1 at each of p points has p(d+1) roots with multiplicity, hence is 0. ∎
Lemma H1 (confluent divided differences with rate; obligation (α), deterministic half).
Nodes c_i r, jet order d, q = p(d+1). For each m ≤ q−1 there are weights w_{i,l}(r) = r^{m−l}
ŵ_{i,l} (ŵ from the unit-spacing problem) with: for all g ∈ C^q on I_r := [c_1 r, c_p r]∪{0}, |
Ʃ_{i,l} w_{i,l}(r) g^{(l)}(c_i r) − g^{(m)}(0) | ≤ C_D r^{q−m} sup_{I_r}|g^{(q)}|. Proof. Define
the functional as (H[g])^{(m)}(0), H the Lemma-H0 interpolant; exact on polynomials of

degree ≤ q−1. Weights: expand H in the Hermite basis; homogeneity by the substitution x = r
x̂(jets scale as r^l, the m-th derivative at 0 as r^{−m}·unit-problem). Error: e := g − H has a
zero of multiplicity d+1 at each node (p(d+1) = q zeros with multiplicity in conv(I_r)). By
Rolle applied q−m times with multiplicity bookkeeping (each differentiation loses exactly
one zero counted with multiplicity, interior zeros produced by Rolle between consecutive
distinct zeros), e^{(m)} has ≥ q−m zeros ζ_1 ≤ … ≤ ζ_{q−m} in conv(I_r). Fix x ∈ conv(I_r ∪
{0}); if x is a ζ we are done; otherwise set F(u) := e^{(m)}(u) − K Π_i (u − ζ_i) with K chosen
so F(x) = 0. F has ≥ q−m+1 zeros with multiplicity, so by Rolle F^{(q−m)} has a zero ξ: 0 =
e^{(q)}(ξ) − K (q−m)!; since H^{(q)} ≡ 0, K = g^{(q)}(ξ)/(q−m)!. Hence e^{(m)}(x) = g^{(q)}
(ξ)/(q−m)! · Π(x − ζ_i), and |x − ζ_i| ≤ C r for x ∈ I_r-hull (which contains 0 when 0 ∈
conv{c_i} — otherwise enlarge I_r to the convex hull with {0}; C_D adjusts). ∎
Lemma H2 (interpolation error at a collapsing evaluation point; node-proximity
factorization — the suppression engine). Same setting; evaluation x* with |x* − c_p r| ≤ Z
r^γ and x* ∈ conv(I_r)
O(r^γ). Then for 0 ≤ a ≤ d, |e^{(a)}(x*)| ≤ C_{D,Z} · r^{(q−a) − (d+1−a)} · |x* − c_p
r|^{d+1−a} · sup|g^{(q)}| = C · r^{(p−1)(d+1)} · r^{γ(d+1−a)} (up to the sup factor). Proof.
As in H1, e^{(a)} has ≥ q−a zeros in conv(I_r) with, at the node c_p r, a zero of
multiplicity ≥ d+1−a (differentiating a multiplicity-(d+1) zero a times). Run the auxiliary-function argument of H1 at x = x*: e^{(a)}(x*) = g^{(q)}(ξ)/(q−a)! Π_{i=1}^{q−a}(x* − ζ_i),
where at least d+1−a of the ζ_i equal c_p r (giving factors |x* − c_p r| = O(r^γ) each) and
the remaining (q−a) − (d+1−a) = (p−1)(d+1) factors are ≤ C r. ∎
Lemma T (exponential Taylor remainder). For real x, N ≥ 1: |e^{ix} − Ʃ_{n<N} (ix)^n/n!| ≤
|x|^N/N!. Proof: induction on N via e^{ix} − Ʃ_{n<N} = i∫_0^x (e^{iu} − Ʃ_{n<N−1}(iu)^n/n!)
du. ∎
§3. Hilbert-space lemmas
Lemma P (projection perturbation, explicit). Let e_1(r),…,e_n(r) ∈ H with e_i(r) → e_i(0)
and Gram G(r) → G(0) ≻ 0. Let P_r project onto span{e_i(r)}. Then for every ψ ∈ H, ‖P_r ψ −
P_0 ψ‖ ≤ C(G(0), max‖e_i‖, ‖ψ‖) · ( ‖G(r)−G(0)‖ + Ʃ_i ‖e_i(r)−e_i(0)‖ ). Proof. P_r ψ = Ʃ_{i,l}
(G(r)^{−1})_{il} ⟨ψ, e_l(r)⟩ e_i(r); G ↦ G^{−1} is Lipschitz near the nondegenerate G(0)
(‖G(r)^{−1} − G(0)^{−1}‖ ≤ ‖G(r)^{−1}‖‖G(0)^{−1}‖‖G(r)−G(0)‖ with ‖G(r)^{−1}‖ bounded for
small perturbations); expand the difference term by term. ∎
Lemma A (gap convergence with rate; obligation (α)). Under (H-f),(H-mom),(H-nd): (A1)
For each visible (m,k) there is Λ_r^{(m,k)} ∈ S_r with ‖Λ_r^{(m,k)} − φ_{m,k}‖{L²(ρ)} ≤ C
r^{q_k − m}. (A2) The limit Gram G_V of {φ{m,k}} is ≻ 0, and the Gram of {Λ_r^{(m,k)}}
converges to it at rate O(r). (A3) For small r, {Λ_r^{(m,k)}} is a basis of S_r; consequently,
for EVERY Ψ ∈ L²(ρ) with the required moments, dist(Ψ, S_r)² = dist(Ψ, V)² + O(r)·(1 + ‖Ψ‖²),

uniformly over ‖Ψ‖-bounded sets. In particular liminf dist(ψ_σ, S_r) = dist(ψ_σ, V) > 0 for
unseen σ. Proof. (A1): fix level k; apply Lemma H1 in the physical variable to g_u(x) :=
e^{iuk…}: precisely, define Λ_r := Ʃ_{i,l} w_{i,l}(r) ∂_t^l ∂_s^k f(c_i r, 0), whose spectral
function is (ik_s)^k Ʃ w_{i,l}(r) (ik_t)^l e^{i c_i r k_t} = (ik_s)^k [ h^{(m)}(0) + R(k_t) ] for
h(x) := e^{i k_t x}, i.e. = (ik_s)^k (ik_t)^m + (ik_s)^k R(k_t) with |R| ≤ C r^{q_k−m}
|k_t|^{q_k} by H1 (sup|h^{(q_k)}| = |k_t|^{q_k}). Square-integrate against ρ: ‖·‖² ≤ C²
r^{2(q_k−m)} ∫ k_s^{2k} k_t^{2q_k} dρ, finite by (H-mom). ∎ (A2): G_V ≻ 0 ⟺ the visible
monomials are linearly independent in L²(ρ) ⟺ no nonzero polynomial of degree ≤
2·max(q_k−1+k) vanishes ρ-a.e. — (H-nd). Rate: bilinearity plus (A1) and (H-mom). ∎ (A3):
the n_D elements Λ_r^{(m,k)} lie in the n_D-dimensional S_r and have Gram → G_V ≻ 0,
hence are independent for small r, hence span S_r. Then dist(Ψ, S_r) = ‖Ψ − P_r Ψ‖ with P_r
as in Lemma P (e_i(r) = Λ_r, e_i(0) = φ), and Lemma P gives the O(r) comparison to dist(Ψ,
V). Positivity for unseen σ: dist(ψ_σ, V) > 0 again by (H-nd) (ψ_σ ∉ V as an L²(ρ) function). ∎
§4. Theorem
Theorem (Graded Conditional-Jet Asymptotics). Assume (H-f), (H-mom), (H-nd); fix a
staircase design D(p; d), γ > p − 1, and a compact K ∋ z. Let Ʃ_r(z) be the conditional
covariance matrix of the 1-jet (f, ∂_t f, ∂_s f)(y), y = (c_p r + r^γ z_t, r^γ z_s), given S_r.
Then, uniformly for z ∈ K (INCLUDING points where the limit form degenerates), Ʃ_r^{ab}(z)
= r^{ℓ_a + ℓ_b} [ Ʃ_∞^{ab}(z) + O(r^{δ(D,γ)}) ], with ℓ_a, Ʃ_∞ = m^a G_{U|V} (m^b)ᵀ, δ > 0
as in Definitions 3–4. The same holds for γ ∈ (0, p−1] for the (f, ∂_s f) sub-block (the value
block never uses the γ > p−1 condition). Label: [PROVEN under (H-f),(H-mom),(H-nd),
modulo the two explicitly flagged verifications V1–V2 in §5, which are finite bookkeeping.]
§5. Proof
Throughout, “≲” carries constants depending on D, γ, K, and the moments in (H-mom) only.
Step 1 (approximant ladder; obligation (β)). Set N := J + 2 ∨ (max leading transverse
degree + 1). Spectrally, e_y(k) = e^{i y_t k_t} e^{i y_s k_s}. Apply Lemma T to the s-factor:
e_y = Ʃ_{n<N} (iy_s k_s)^n/n! · e^{iy_t k_t} + T_N, ‖T_N‖² ≤ (|y_s|^N/N!)² ∫ k_s^{2N} dρ ≲
r^{2γN} — below every leading order by the choice of N (this is (β): the remainder is
controlled at one full transverse level past the deepest leading stratum, using exactly the
top moment in (H-mom)). For n ≤ J: approximate k_s^n e^{iy_t k_t} within the level-n
observation span by the Lemma-H0 interpolant EVALUATED at y_t: A^{(n)} := Ʃ_{i,l} B^{(n)}
{i,l}(y_t) ∂_t^l ∂_s^n f(c_i r, 0) ∈ S_r, whose spectral error is (ik_s)^n E_n(k_t) with, by Lemma
H2 (a = 0), |E_n| ≤ C r^{(p−1)(d_n+1)} r^{γ(d_n+1)} |k_t|^{q_n}. Moreover H2’s error
REPRESENTATION (the Π(x*−ζ_i) form) splits E_n into its leading coefficient times the
monomial k_t^{q_n} plus lower terms: expanding Π(y_t − ζ_i) and the mean-value point to
first order costs a relative O(r^{min(1,γ)}), absorbed in δ. [Flagged verification V1: the

expansion of the H2 representation into leading-monomial + O(r^δ) remainder, per level —
finite one-page bookkeeping per design; executed implicitly by the exact BF series for the
corollary cases.] For J < n < N: no approximation; write k_s^n e^{iy_t k_t} = k_s^n e^{i c_p r
k_t}(1 + (e^{i r^γ z_t k_t} − 1)) and Taylor the second factor to the needed depth: leading
term = the stratum functional ψ{(0,n)} translated to the node, plus O(r^γ |k_t|)-terms.
Step 2 (residual decomposition and the multiplier map). Summing Step 1: for each
observable φ^a_y (a = value, ∂_t, ∂_s — the latter two obtained by differentiating the ladder
in y, which by H2 with a = 1 costs one node-proximity factor exactly as in the ω′-
mechanism): φ^a_y = A^a_r + Ʃ_{σ ∈ Ʃ̂} M^a_σ(r,z) ψ̃_σ(r) + E^a, where A^a_r ∈ S_r; Ʃ̂ =
the finite set of candidate strata (unseen monomials entering the ladder up to depth N);
ψ̃_σ(r) = the stratum functional at the node c_p r (‖ψ̃_σ(r) − ψ_σ‖ ≲ r by one extra moment);
M^a_σ = r^{L_a(σ;γ)} m^a_σ(z)(1 + O(r^δ)) with m^a_σ polynomial in z (explicitly:
transverse Taylor coefficients y_s^{k−a_s}/(k−a_s)! and H2 node-polynomial leading
coefficients — this constructive list IS Definition 3’s multiplier map); and ‖E^a‖ ≲ r^{ℓ_a + δ}.
[Flagged verification V2: for each design instance, the finite table of L_a(σ;γ) values and the
identification of the argmin set Ʃ_a — mechanical; done exactly for the corollary designs
below.]
Step 3 (assembly; obligation (γ)). With Q_r = I − P_r (projection onto S_r^⊥): Q_r A^a_r =
0, so Ʃ_r^{ab} = ⟨Q_r φ^a, Q_r φ^b⟩ = Ʃ_{σ,τ} M^a_σ M^b_τ ⟨Q_r ψ̃_σ, Q_r ψ̃_τ⟩ + cross(E)
terms. By Lemma A3 + Lemma P + ‖ψ̃_σ(r) − ψ_σ‖ ≲ r: ⟨Q_r ψ̃_σ, Q_r ψ̃_τ⟩ = G_{U|V}(σ,τ) +
O(r). Non-leading σ contribute r-powers ≥ ℓ_a + δ by definition of δ; the E-cross terms are ≲
r^{ℓ_a+δ} r^{ℓ_b} by Cauchy–Schwarz. Every constant is an explicit polynomial in |z| times
moment constants, so all bounds are uniform on K — including on the degeneracy locus of
Ʃ_∞, where the THEOREM’s error bound is unaffected (only the leading form is small there).
Divide by r^{ℓ_a+ℓ_b}. ∎
§6. Corollaries (each recovers a previously certified fact; the
certified computations now serve as independent confirmations)
C1 (Ʃ₂(0), BF). D(2,2) full, γ = 2, BF kernel: Ʃ_a-selection gives value & ∂_s: σ = (0,3); ∂_t:
σ = (2,2) via H2(a=1). G_{U|V} entries: Var(f_sss|V) = 6, Var(f_ttss|V) = 4, cross 0. Theorem
output = the six certified leading entries. [Matches nd_symbolic exactly.]
C2 (rank-one collapse + Euler slaving). Whenever Ʃ_a = Ʃ_b = {single pure-transverse σ
= (0,k*)} for two observables a = value, b = ∂_s, the leading 2×2 block is the rank-1 form
(m^a, m^b)ᵀ Var(ψ_σ|V)(m^a, m^b), and m^a/m^b = (y_s^{k*}/k*!)/(y_s^{k−1}/(k−1)!) =
y_s/k* — the slaving identity IS this ratio; Euler’s identity for s^{k*}. K4’s degeneracy is thus
a THEOREM output, not an anomaly.
C3 (parity). If the design is reflection-symmetric (c_i = −c_{p+1−i}, equal staircase) and ρ

is invariant under k_s → −k_s and k_t → −k_t, then G_V and G_{U|V} block-diagonalize over
(t,s)-parity classes (the isometry intertwines the reflections with the functional parities);
Cov(Ξ,T) = 0 is the (eo)/(ee) instance.
C4 ((ND′), general kernels). Under (H-nd), G_{U|V} ≻ 0 on the span of any finite unseen
set (Lemma A3’s positivity). For D(2,2), γ = 2: the gradient-block Ʃ_∞ is diag-modulo-parity
with strictly positive diagonal off {z_s = 0}: (ND′) holds for EVERY kernel satisfying (H-f),(H-mom),(H-nd) — the compression theorem, now a corollary of a proven theorem rather than
a sketch.
C5 (γ-family = test T1). Same design, γ = 3/2: the L_a table shifts as in Definition 3;
predicted exponents (18,16,15,12 in ρ) and constants unchanged as Gram entries. [Matches
the executed T1 run exactly.]
C6 (design surgery = test T2, the stress test). Staircase d = (2,1), J = 1 (f_ss deleted).
Leading strata: value & ∂_s & ∂_t all select level-2 pure/near-pure functionals: value: (0,2)
with multiplier y_s²/2; ∂_s: (0,2) with y_s; ∂_t: (1,2) with y_s²/2. Theorem output: Var f =
(y_s²/2)² Var(f_ss|V₁₀), Var f_s = y_s²·same, Cov = (y_s³/2)·same — rank-1 with slaving y_s/2
(C2 with k* = 2); Var f_t = (y_s²/2)² Var(f_tss|V₁₀); cross-parities 0 (C3). With Var(f_ss|V₁₀) =
2, Var(f_tss|V₁₀) = 2: exactly the executed T2 output. The theorem reproduces T2 as a
corollary — the stress test is passed at statement level, which required (and drove)
the staircase generalization.
C7 (Matérn wall). For Matérn ν, (H-mom) at level k requires 2(q_k + k) + 2 ≤ … with λ_{2m}
< ∞ ⟺ m < ν: ν = 3.5 violates (H-mom) for D(2,2) already at the level-0 requirement (needs
λ₁₂ at full strength; even the frame’s f_tttt needs λ₈, and λ₈ = ∞). The theorem’s hypotheses
FAIL — the wall is a hypothesis boundary, with the fractional replacement OPEN (§8).

§8. OPEN items and residual obligations (honest ledger)
O1 (was O-ND1): conditional means under Palm |det|-biased pinning. O2 (was O-ND2): γ =
p−1 boundary; tied strata; the annulus regime. O3: fractional filtration for kernels violating
(H-mom) (Matérn); conjectured to yield the τ^{ν−·} laws behind F2/P5. O4: verifications V1–
V2 of §5 written out as the finite per-design tables (mechanical; the corollary instances are
already covered by the exact computations, so V1–V2 gate only the GENERAL statement’s
audit stamp). O5: torus lattice version of (H-nd) restated against (H2’) and checked for the
program’s L-fixed setting (expected verbatim). O6: registered targeted literature pass

circulation of this document, on: confluent Hermite interpolation; collapsing/coalescing
kriging designs; RKHS power functions under node coalescence; Gaussian conditioning of
jet bundles; graded/weighted interpolation filtrations. Session-level searches (S4 Phase VII)
found the pair-frame precedent (arXiv:2209.04150) and differentiated Stein screening; the

restatement (O5) standing between the general theorem and an unqualified audit stamp —

A.2 Moment hypothesis: sharp vs safe (item 2)
Ledger of exactly which moment each step consumes (D(2,2)): Lemma A1, level 0: ∫k_t¹² dρ

A.3 Circularity check (item 3)

[Lemma H1 + moments] and (i) + Lemma P. Consumes NOTHING about unseen functionals.

B.1 Exact statement of the conditioning used
The fold-pair Palm law at separation r, heights (b, b−ℓ): the law of the field conditioned on
the SIX linear constraints f(x_M) = b, f(x_S) = b−ℓ, ∇f(x_M) = ∇f(x_S) = 0, REWEIGHTED by
the Kac–Rice density |det∇²f(x_M)|·|det∇²f(x_S)| and the index/adjacency indicators.
Decomposition [PROVEN — Gaussian conditioning + change of measure]: (i) GAUSSIAN-LINEAR PART: conditioning on the 6 linear values. The conditional field is Gaussian; its mean
is linear regression on the 6 numbers; its covariance is a Schur complement independent of
the numbers. (ii) |det|-BIASED PART: the residual pair data (the 6 Hessian entries) keeps its
conditional Gaussian law RE-WEIGHTED by the two |det| factors and indicators — a change
of measure on 6 variables only. (iii) KEY STRUCTURAL FACT: given ALL 12 pair numbers, the
law of the rest of the field is unweighted Gaussian regression — the |det| weight is a function
of the conditioning variables. Hence the third-point conditional mean given the pair data w
is the SAME linear regression map in both the biased and unbiased worlds; the bias only
changes the DISTRIBUTION of w.
B.2 The mean obeys the Hermite-extension law [DERIVED from
the

GCJA theorem]
With φ^a = A^a_r(·) + (residual) as in GCJA §5: E[φ^a_y | w] = A^a_r(w) + E[resid | w],
|E[resid | w]| ≤ ‖Q_rφ^a‖·‖w‖_{G^{-1}} i.e. conditional mean = the ladder (Hermite-extension) value at the observed pair jets + an error of the SAME ORDER as the
conditional sd (r^{ℓ_a}), with all frame coordinates O_P(1) on the Palm event (verified: the
corrected frame is exactly the normalization in which the pinned data is O(1); e.g. c5 = −ℓ/r³
= −κ/6, and c4 = −f_tttt/12 because the gradient pinning forces (f_tt⁺+f_tt⁻)/2 = r²f_tttt/12 —
derived below). Answer to the directive’s first question: YES, the regression means obey
the Hermite-extension law; the |det| bias adds NO new drift term to the regression
map. The bias acts only through the law of w. That is where the story changes.
B.3 What the gradient pinning forces on the pair jets (Rolle
identities) [DERIVED; deterministic given a.s.-C³]
On the pair event, along the axis: f_t(±r/2) = 0 ⟹ f_tt has a zero on the segment ⟹ f_tt(x_S)
= (r/2) f_ttt(mid) + O(r²) = ±κ r (1+o(1)), κ = |f_ttt|/2 — the soft eigenvalue law, RE-DERIVED
as a Rolle consequence of the linear constraints alone. Similarly f_s(±r/2) = 0 ⟹ ∫ f_ts dt = 0
over the segment ⟹ f_ts(x_S) = O_P(r) — the axis/soft-direction misalignment is O(r);
the off-diagonal Hessian entry is small automatically. The transverse curvature µ :=
−f_ss(x_S) is UNCONSTRAINED (O_P(1) generic) — and is precisely the variable the |det|
weight acts on: |det∇²f(x_S)| = |f_tt f_ss − f_ts²| = κ r µ (1 + O(r)) — the weight is LINEAR in µ
near µ = 0.
B.4 Leading-order means of the third-point 1-jet (γ = 2)
From B.2’s extension law with B.3’s inputs (y = x_S + (r²z_t, r²z_s)): m_f − (b−ℓ) = ½(r²z_t)²
f_tt + (r²z_t)(r²z_s) f_ts + ½(r²z_s)² f_ss + … = O_P(r⁵ z_t²) − ½ µ r⁴ z_s² + … [O(r⁴) ≪ ℓ ≍ r³]
m_{f_t} = (r²z_t) f_tt(x_S) + (r²z_s) f_ts(x_S) + O_P(r⁴) = (κ z_t + ν z_s) r³ (1+o_P(1)), ν :=
f_tts-scale O_P(1)·r/r m_{f_s} = (r²z_t) f_ts + (r²z_s) f_ss + O_P(r⁴) = −µ r² z_s (1+o_P(1)).
Comparison to the GCJA covariance scales: sd_f = (z_s³/√6) r⁶, sd_{f_t} = (z_s²/2) r⁵,
sd_{f_s} = √(3/2) z_s² r⁴. Mean/sd ratios: value O(r⁻²) but INSIDE the window (bounded by
the indicator ≤ 1, and the mean offset r⁴ ≪ window ℓ ≍ r³ keeps P(window) = Θ(1)); gradient
ratios (κz_t+νz_s)/z_s² · r⁻² and µ/(√(3/2) z_s) · r⁻².
B.5 Does the suppression story survive? — the |det| tail, and R3
At FIXED generic pair data (κ, ν, µ bounded away from 0) the ratios r⁻² give exp(−c/r⁴)-
suppression: the retracted sketch was correct CONDITIONALLY. The audit question is the
AVERAGE over the biased law of w — and the biased density of the transverse curvature

near µ = 0 is ∝ µ (the pair weight is linear in µ, B.3). Two exact integrals: (1) t-direction: ∫
dz_t p_{f_t}(0) = √(2π)/(κ r³) — the z_t Gaussian integral cancels sd_{f_t} entirely and
retires the (κz_t + νz_s) mean-vanishing set. Contributes r⁻³ per pair, one factor κ⁻¹. (2) s-direction with the third-point determinant weight |det∇²f(y)| = κ µ r (1+O(r)): with biased
density ∝ µ dµ, E_µ[ κµr · p_{f_s}(0) ] = κ r · (1/sd_s)∫ µ² e^{−µ²X²/2}dµ /Z ≍ κ r ·
sd_s²/(r²z_s)³ ≍ κ r · z_s r², X := r²z_s/sd_s. The suppression is traded for TWO powers of r:
the contributing configurations have µ ≍ X⁻¹ ≍ z_s r² — anomalously FLAT transverse
curvature. Assembly (area element r⁴ dz, window factor ≤ 1, κ’s cancel): E[N_inner(|z| ≤ C)]
≍ ∫ r⁴ dz_s · r⁻³ · z_s r³ · P(win) ≍ r⁴. [Label: DERIVED, leading order; listed obligation O1-a:
the uniform- integrability enumeration over the remaining pair variables and the O(r)-
correction terms — finite, same toolkit.] Verdict: the suppression story is KILLED in its
super-exponential form (R3) and REPLACED by a polynomial law that lands exactly on
the original β = 4 target. Mechanism, named: flat-saddle tail — the third critical point
materializes when x_S is close to a transverse degeneracy (monkey-saddle/cusp proximity),
an event the |det| weight suppresses only linearly. β = 4 is now: 4 = [2γ area] + [−3 t-direction] + [+3 s-direction-with-tail]. Theorem A unaffected; File 3’s Lemma-I target is
restored WITH mechanism and WITH the identity of the dominant configurations.

The mechanism makes a sharp, pre-registrable prediction about the EXISTING near-zone
excess (C006-A1, OBJ-C006-1): window events should be hosted by pairs with anomalously
small transverse curvature. Registered falsification test (C006-Arm1c, to be frozen
before running): recompute, from the stored seeds, µ = |f_ss(x_S)| in the fold chart for (i)
pairs hosting a window point at d ≤ 3r and (ii) matched control pairs (same r-bin, no window
point). Predictions: (P-1c-1) median µ_window / median µ_control < 1, with the ratio
DECREASING in decreasing r (approaching the r²-scaling regime); (P-1c-2) the window-event rate, reweighted by µ (i.e. E[N_w·µ]/E[µ]), loses its small-r excess: the reweighted
slope moves TOWARD 3 by a pre-committed margin (to be fixed at freeze). Explicit
falsification condition: if µ_window is NOT stochastically smaller than µ_control (ratio
≥ 1 within the bootstrap CI), the flat-saddle-tail explanation of the finite-u excess is
FALSE, and the excess must be sought in the γ = 1 annulus mechanism instead (O-ND2) —
a clean fork, cheap to run, using data already on disk.

S3 — Proof Architecture of Ʃ₂(0): the Weighted-Jet
Filtration
Artifact class: structural analysis (operator-directed protocol: proof-architecture mode).
Companion to ND_Symbolic_Adjudication.md and nd_symbolic.py. Epistemic labels used
throughout: [PROVEN] / [DERIVED: assumptions listed] / [COMPUTATIONAL IDENTITY:
exact, this session] / [EMPIRICAL] / [CONJECTURE] / [OPEN].
Executive finding: Ʃ₂(0) is not an accident of the 15×15 algebra. Its entire leading structure
is forced by one organizing principle — a weighted jet filtration induced by the pair data —
and its two nontrivial constants are one-point conditional spectral-moment invariants. An
independent derivation through that principle reproduces every certified entry exactly, and
the principle yields a one-paragraph theorem that replaces the symbolic computation for
general kernels.
1. The organizing principle
Filtration Lemma. [PROVEN — counting + Hermite interpolation; assumptions: smoothness
only (jets exist); NO Gaussianity, NO stationarity, NO isotropy needed for the counting itself]
The pair data (2-jets at two points ±r/2 on the t-axis) constitutes, on the axis, exactly
Hermite interpolation data of order 5 for f(·,0), order 3 for f_s(·,0), order 1 for f_ss(·,0), and
nothing for ∂_s^k f(·,0), k ≥ 3. Hence the visible axis-monomial set is V₅ = { t^m s^k : m + 2k
≤ 5 }, #V₅ = 12, i.e. the pair σ-algebra sees precisely the monomials of (1,2)-weighted
degree ≤ 5 — and the 12-dimensionality of the frame is this count, not a coordinate choice.
The first unseen stratum is weighted degree 6: { f_6t, f_tttts, f_ttss, f_sss } — exactly the
four “new functionals” identified in the by-hand analysis, now understood as a graded piece
of a filtration.
Suppression mechanism (the hidden cancellation engine). [DERIVED: smoothness +
interpolation theory; deterministic] For the third point y = x_S + (r²z_t, r²z_s), each unseen
monomial (m,k) enters the conditional fluctuation of the 1-jet at y through the Hermite error
factor ω_{5−2k}(t_y) (or its t-derivative) times y_s^k/k!, where ω_j(t) = (t−a)^⌈·⌉(t−b)^⌈·⌉
is the node polynomial. Because y is r²-CLOSE TO THE NODE x_S, every ω vanishes to its
node order there: ω₅(t_y) ≍ r³·(r²z_t)³, ω₃ ≍ r²·(r²z_t)², ω₁ ≍ r·(r²z_t). Node-vanishing kills
every unseen direction that has ANY t-visibility. Survivors at leading order:
f(y), f_s(y): the pure-transverse functional Ξ := resid(f_sss | V₅), entering through y_s³/6

and y_s²/2 respectively;
f_t(y): the independent functional T := resid(f_ttss | V₅), entering through ω₁′(t_y)·y_s²/4
= r·y_s²/4. This explains, as mechanism rather than observation: (i) the z_t-invisibility of
the limit (z_t lives only inside the ω’s, which are subleading); (ii) the scales (r⁶, r⁵, r⁴) —
they are the weighted degrees; (iii) the rank-1 collapse (V3): f and f_s read the SAME
scalar Ξ, and the slaving identity f_res = (y_s/3)·∂_s f_res is nothing but Euler’s identity
for the degree-3 homogeneous monomial s³/6. The cancellation det₂ ≡ 0 is therefore
classified: **not parity, not isotropy, not Palm structure — shared-first-unseen-functional
transverse Euler homogeneity.** It is structural and exact, which is why it is z-uniform.
Constants Lemma. [COMPUTATIONAL IDENTITY: exact, verified this session by direct one-point linear algebra, independent of the series route] Var(Ξ) = Var(f_sss | V₅) = 6 and Var(T)
= Var(f_ttss | V₅) = 4 for Bargmann–Fock, with Cov(Ξ, T | V₅) = 0 by parity (Ξ is (even-t,
odd-s); T is (even-t, even-s)). The full predicted leading matrix, entry by entry INCLUDING
the mixed z_t terms: Var f = z_s⁶/6·r¹² Cov(f,f_t) = z_s⁴z_t/4·r¹² Cov(f,f_s) = z_s⁵/2·r¹⁰ Var f_t
= z_s⁴/4·r¹⁰ Cov(f_t,f_s) = z_s³z_t/2·r¹⁰ Var f_s = 3z_s⁴/2·r⁸ reproduces the certified Schur
output EXACTLY (the z_t cross terms arise from the ω₁-suppressed T-content of f and f_s
beating against f_t’s leading T-content — the mechanism predicts even the “subleading”
entries). Two mathematically distinct derivations now agree on all six entries
(independent-validation requirement: satisfied).
2. Answers to the architecture questionnaire, per step
Step A — frame choice (the T-matrix, corrected coordinates). Structural necessity: the
INVARIANT content is the filtration V₅ (a property of the pair σ-algebra, frame-free). Any
frame whose limit spans V₅ gives a congruent Ʃ₂(0) (Ʃ → JƩJᵀ): positivity, rank structure,
strata, and the slaving identity are frame-invariant; the numbers −1/12, 1/60, and det G₁₂ =
1/6480 are frame artifacts (Hermite-basis normalizations; det scales by Jacobian²).
Coordinate dependence enters EXACTLY here and nowhere else. Assumptions: smoothness
(λ-moments for the divided-difference limits); scaling convention (t-axis alignment of the
pair — provided by the fold chart, i.e. by Morse geometry upstream).
Step B — series inversion of the 12×12 pair block. Compression test: FAILED in the
productive sense — a theorem replaces it. The one-point route (Filtration + Constants
Lemmas) obtains the leading Ʃ₂(0) with no series and no inversion; the series computation
is thereby demoted from load-bearing derivation to independent confirmation and finite-r
correction generator. This answers “is there a theorem that would replace this derivation”:
yes, and it has been executed.

Step C — Schur complement. Forced by Gaussian conditioning (Gaussian-only
assumption; this is the single genuinely Gaussian step: conditional law = linear projection).
Ordering-invariant by the Schur quotient property; the alternative ordering IS the validated
one-point route.
Step D — parity. The covariance factorizes over the four (t,s)-parity classes BEFORE any
conditioning (stationarity + the reflection symmetries of the configuration; for BF also
separability C = c(u)c(v), which is BF-specific and gives the Hankel structure below, but
parity alone needs only the symmetric placement of the pair). det G₁₂ =
(2/3)·(2)·(1/360)·(1/24) = 1/6480 over classes (ee, eo, oe, oo). [COMPUTATIONAL IDENTITY]
Assumption ledger for the final leading Ʃ₂(0) (question 3):
Gaussian only: conditioning = projection (Step C).
Stationarity: jet covariances depend on differences (Steps A, D).
Smoothness: spectral moments λ_{2m} < ∞ for 2m ≤ 12 (frame limits through f_5t and
residual variances through the degree-6 stratum; a safe sufficient order, not
sharpened).
Isotropy: NOT USED anywhere. θ enters only through which axis the fold chart selects;
the filtration argument is direction-covariant.
BF-specific: ONLY the numerical values 6, 4, 1/6480 (and the Hankel/separability
remark). Everything structural is kernel-general.
Scaling convention: the (1,2)-weighting is FORCED by the pair separation r vs blow-up
r²; it explains a posteriori why r² is the canonical inner scale — it is the scale at which the
transverse first-unseen contribution and the node-suppressed axial contributions
balance in weighted degree.
3. The compression theorem (general kernels)
Theorem (ND′, general form). [DERIVED: assumptions as listed] Let f be a stationary
Gaussian field on R² (or T_L², L fixed) with spectral measure ρ satisfying: (a) λ_{2m}(ρ) < ∞
for 2m ≤ 12; (b) ρ is not supported on a proper algebraic subvariety of the plane (implied by
(H2’)’s open-set positivity). Then in the two-scale limit the gradient-block Ʃ₂(0) is
diag(Var_ρ(T)·z_s⁴/4-normalized, …) ≻ 0 for z_s ≠ 0, with sole stratum the axis, and the
value/s-derivative block is rank-1 with the slaving identity. Proof mechanism: conditional
variances such as Var(f_sss | V₅) equal the squared L²(ρ)-distance from the polynomial k_s³
to span{k_t^m k_s^k : m + 2k ≤ 5}. Distinct monomials are linearly independent in L²(ρ)
whenever ρ charges no proper algebraic subvariety, so the distance is strictly positive;
likewise for f_ttss; Gram nondegeneracy of V₅ (the G₁₂ ≻ 0 input) is the same statement for

the visible monomials. Everything else is the deterministic Filtration/Suppression
mechanism. ∎ (One paragraph, replacing the kernel-by-kernel symbolic route. The BF
computation’s role is re-classified: discovery instrument + constants + confirmation.)
Positivity is thus a MOMENT-PROBLEM invariant: the constants 6 and 4 are (squared)
distances in L²(ρ) from degree-6 monomials to the visible span — Hankel-type spectral-moment determinant ratios. For separable kernels (BF) they reduce to products of 1-D
Gaussian-moment Hankel data; this is the “broader Gaussian invariant” answer (question
10): Ʃ₂(0) belongs to the class of graded Gram/Schur forms of the weighted-jet filtration
of the spectral measure — objects defined for any kernel and any node configuration, of
which our 15×15 is the (2-node 2-jet, weight-(1,2), degree-6 stratum) instance.
[Documented here as directed, separately from the primary proof.]
4. A discovered constraint with program-wide consequences
[DERIVED, with a conjecture attached] The r²-scale machinery requires λ_{2m} < ∞ up to
2m ≈ 12 (C⁶-class fields). Matérn ν has λ_{2m} < ∞ iff m < ν: ν = 3.5 fails at m = 4 (f_tttt
does not exist); the quintic Hermite frame itself degenerates, the filtration truncates at a
lower weighted degree, and the inner-zone conditional variances acquire kernel-roughness
exponents. [CONJECTURE, flagged for O-ND2 / F2:] this truncation is the structural origin
of Prop P5’s τ^{ν−3} degradation and of the kernel-ordered finite-u corrections measured in
C005/C006-A1 (P3’s Matérn > BF window-count ratio). If confirmed, F2 (“kernel
dependence of the q deficit”) stops being a measured mystery and becomes a computable
filtration invariant of ρ.
5. Failure-protocol retrospective (question: positivity failed —
what happened?)
Positivity of the FULL 15-frame did fail (V3), and the protocol was followed: algebra stopped
at the first contradiction; the smallest responsible block (the 2×2 value/s-derivative minor)
was isolated; the failure was classified GEOMETRIC/STRUCTURAL (shared first-unseen
functional; Euler identity), not computational and not an assumption failure; the statement
was downgraded (K4) and replaced by the correct invariant statement (ND′) which the
count actually needs. The failure was the discovery.
6. Status ledger after this pass
[PROVEN] Filtration Lemma; Suppression mechanism; parity factorization; Schur ordering-invariance. [COMPUTATIONAL IDENTITY] Var(Ξ)=6, Var(T)=4, Cov(Ξ,T)=0; all six leading
Ʃ₂(0) entries by two routes; det G₁₂ = 1/6480 = (2/3)(2)(1/360)(1/24). [DERIVED] Theorem

ND′ general form (assumptions (a),(b)); frame-invariance of positivity/rank/strata.
[EMPIRICAL] C006-A1 P2/P3 support; near-zone excess at y~r. [CONJECTURE] Matérn
truncation 㱺 P5/F2 mechanism identity. [OPEN] O-ND1 (conditional MEANS under Palm
pinning — note the architecture now predicts their form: regression = Hermite extension, so
the means are the interpolants’ values; verification remains); O-ND2 (intermediate scales
r²≪τ≲3r: the filtration weight interpolates from (1,2) toward (1,1) as τ grows —
[CONJECTURE] the exponent table is the weight flow); sharp constants beyond BF.

S4 — The Filtration on Trial: Falsification, Universality,
Hierarchy
Artifact class: structural adjudication (operator-directed seven-phase program).
Companion: S3, ND_Symbolic_Adjudication.md, nd_symbolic.py, and the falsification test log
(this session). Epistemic labels as in S3. Burden of proof accepted: the weighted-jet filtration
is treated below as the hypothesis under attack, not the organizing principle. Verdict at end.
PHASE I — Internal falsification (five attacks, two executed as
exact computations)
Q1. Different frame, same Ʃ₂(0), different filtration? Attack outcome: NO — but the attack
forced the correct intrinsic definition, which is a strengthening. The conditional law of the
third-point block depends only on the SPAN of the pair observables (Gaussian conditioning is
projection onto the span), so Ʃ₂(0) is frame-free by construction. The filtration itself must
therefore be defined without frames, and it can be: with S_r ⊂ L² the 12-dim span at
separation r, define V := { jet functionals φ : dist_{L²}(φ, S_r) → 0 as r → 0 }. This references
no frame. Proof obligation created and dischargeable: V = span{∂^{(m,k)}f(0) : m+2k ≤ 5}
requires (i) explicit approximating sequences for each visible monomial [the corrected-frame
constructions ARE these sequences — done], and (ii) liminf dist(ψ, S_r) > 0 for unseen ψ
[follows from S_r → V in the Grassmannian gap metric, which the certified frame convergence
+ G₁₂ ≻ 0 provide]. STATUS: the filtration survives as an intrinsic invariant of the observation
σ-algebra flow; frames demoted to computational devices. Note the map {filtration} → Ʃ₂(0)
is many-to-one; the filtration is the finer invariant — non-injectivity is expected, not
threatening.
Q2. Different interpolation scheme, same asymptotics, different grading? The grading is
intrinsic per Q1 (decay rates of distances); interpolation schemes are proof devices and
cannot alter it. What CAN alter the grading is a different OBSERVATION DESIGN — and it
does, in exactly the way the theory predicts (see T2 below). Attack fails; scope sharpened:
the filtration is an invariant of the design, not of the field alone.
Q3. Is the (1,2)-weighting forced? Attack outcome: the weighting is NOT unique — it is one
member of a γ-family, and discovering this is a GENERALIZATION, not a weakening. For blow-up y − x_S ~ r^γ the suppression exponents are: transverse level k contribution to the value =
(3−k)(1+γ) + γk = 3(1+γ) − k… giving pure-transverse dominance for the value/f_s block at

EVERY γ > 0, and the ω′-mechanism for f_t whenever γ > 1. [COMPUTATIONAL IDENTITY —

≤ 2, the whole intermediate zone r² ≪ τ ≪ r is super-exponentially suppressed, and the C006-
A1 count excess must live at τ ≍ r exactly — consistent with the measurement (excess at d ≤
3r). [DERIVED, pending O-ND1 mean audit.]
Q4. Infinitesimal perturbation of the pair geometry? Node asymmetry and O(r²)
placement errors: Hermite orders unchanged, ω’s perturbed at lower order — filtration stable.
What breaks: the PARITY decomposition (a convenience: constants and Cov(Ξ,T) ≠ 0,

nodes: filtration persists with a ragged unseen boundary and possibly ≥ 2 functionals tied at

boundary mapped.
Q5. Hidden analyticity? Located and quarantined: the SERIES route uses analyticity of BF
(expansion to depth 13); the one-point route needs only Taylor-with-remainder at weighted
order 6 + L² moment finiteness (λ_{2m}, 2m ≤ 12) + gap convergence of spans. Consequence
for labels: the certified identities are [COMPUTATIONAL IDENTITY] on an analytic kernel; the
smoothness-only general statement is [DERIVED] with the remainder-control obligation
explicit. No step of the GENERAL argument secretly needs analyticity. Attack fails; label
hygiene enforced.

observations at both nodes (10 observations). The theory, computed BEFORE the run from

Var(f_tss|V₁₀) = 2; scales jump to Var f = z_s⁴/2·r⁸, Var f_s = 2z_s²·r⁴, Cov = z_s³·r⁶, Var f_t =
z_s⁴/2·r⁸; rank-1 persists; slaving coefficient changes from y_s/3 to y_s/2 (Euler identity for
the new degree-2 stratum). Pipeline output (symbolic z, exact): ALL SIX predictions exact,
det₂ ≡ 0 confirmed. The mechanism predicted the behavior of a design it was never derived
from, including a changed rational constant in a structural identity. This is the strongest
single piece of evidence that the filtration is intrinsic rather than an artifact.
Phase I verdict: the hypothesis survived five attacks and two exact out-of-domain tests; two
attacks produced strengthenings (intrinsic definition; γ-family with located phase transition).

PHASE III — The invariant hierarchy [CONJECTURE, with the

degree-count proven]
For the design D(p, j): j-jets at p collinear nodes with spacing r, Hermite unisolvence on the
line gives, at transverse level k ≤ j, p(j+1−k) axis conditions, hence visible degree p(j+1−k) − 1,
hence
V(p,j) = { t^m s^k : m + p·k ≤ p(j+1) − 1 }, #V = p(j+1)(j+2)/2
— the s-weight is the NUMBER OF NODES (for us p = 2: weight (1,2)), and the count equals
the number of observations with no waste [PROVEN: line-Hermite unisolvence]. First unseen
stratum U(p,j) = weighted degree p(j+1), of dimension j+2. Suppression: pure-transverse
dominance for the value block at all γ > 0; gradient-block ω′-mechanism for γ > p − 1 (phase
transition at γ = p−1) [DERIVED at p = 2; the general-p exponent count is the same
arithmetic]. Conditional invariants: the Gram form of U(p,j) modulo V(p,j) in L²(ρ) — a (j+2)-
dimensional graded object per design. Positivity: L²(ρ) monomial independence, uniformly in
the design. Higher strata (weighted degree > p(j+1)) [CONJECTURE]: govern the subleading
terms of the conditional covariance — testable against the banked series data (the r¹¹/r¹³
coefficients should be second-stratum Gram forms; REGISTERED as a future exact test, not
run). Our theory is the (p, j, γ) = (2, 2, 2) member. The C006 numerical pinning constant lives
at the (2,2,1) boundary member. Fold TRIPLES would be (3, ·, ·) with transition at γ = 2 —
qualitatively different inner analysis [flagged for any future chain-preemption work].
PHASE IV — Independent reconstruction from first principles
Given only: Gaussian conditioning, Hermite interpolation, jet spaces, Kac–Rice, pair
geometry. Reconstruction (third derivation, distinct from both the series route and the one-point route): in the RKHS H(C), observations are the kernel elements C^{(α)}_{x_i}; the
conditional variance of any functional φ is the squared H-distance from φ to the observation
span — the POWER FUNCTION of the design. The power function of line-Hermite data,
evaluated at a point collapsing onto a node at rate r^γ, expands over the interpolation-error
ladder: node polynomials ω × unseen divided differences. Transplanting the classical error
ladder through the RKHS isometry yields the filtration, the suppression, and the Gram
constants — no step fails, no hidden assumption surfaced beyond those already in the ledger
(moments; gap convergence). CONCLUSION: rediscoverable; the strongest theorem is the
intersection of the three derivations, which is precisely the Phase V candidate below.
[DERIVED at sketch level; uniformity of the remainder control is the one obligation shared
with Phase I Q5.]
PHASE V — Compression challenge: the one theorem

Candidate Theorem (Graded Conditional-Jet Asymptotics). [DERIVED — proof obligations
listed] Let C be a stationary kernel on R² with spectral measure ρ, λ_{2m}(ρ) < ∞ for 2m ≤
2·p(j+1), ρ not supported on a proper algebraic subvariety. Let the observation design be
D(p,j) on a line with spacing r, and let the evaluation point approach a node at rate r^γ, p−1 <
γ. Then, uniformly on compact z-sets, the conditional covariance of the 1-jet at the evaluation
point is, at leading order in r, the pushforward of the Gram form of the first unseen stratum
U(p,j) mod V(p,j) under the deterministic multiplier map (node polynomials ω^{(·)} ×
transverse Taylor coefficients). All of the following are corollaries: Ʃ₂(0) and its exact entries;
the suppression scales; the rank-one collapse whenever a single stratum member dominates
two observables (with slaving = Euler identity of its transverse degree); the parity block
structure when the design and ρ are reflection-symmetric; positivity (ND′) via monomial
independence in L²(ρ); the γ- and design-covariance verified in T1/T2. Proof obligations (the
honest residue): (α) gap convergence S_r → V with rate, uniform on compacts; (β) Taylor
remainder control at weighted order p(j+1)+1 under the moment hypothesis; (γ) uniformity in
z including the strata approach. Each is standard-technique (Gaussian L² + interpolation
theory); none is discharged yet at audit grade. Verdict: the seven-step flow in the
operator’s diagram does compress to this single statement; the current lemmas
become corollaries once (α)–(γ) are written.

PHASE VII — External novelty audit (searches executed this
session)
Findings, with verified content boundaries:
1. Divided-difference conditioning at critical-point collision: KNOWN. Azaïs–Wschebor
(Level Sets and Extrema, Wiley 2009) is the school; and the symmetrized pair frame with
expansions of exactly our c/d type appears explicitly in <cite>arXiv:2209.04150 (local
repulsion of planar Gaussian critical points), whose proof section introduces symmetrized
sum/difference coordinates Δ_i, Δ_{i1} with the expansions ∂_iψ(0) + (r²/2)∂_{i11}ψ(0) and
(r²/6)∂_{i111}ψ(0), and notes that at collision the determinant is dominated by third-order
derivatives with sign constraints forcing fourth-order differentiability</cite>. Our PAIR
frame is this technique; no novelty claimed there. That work treats the two-point function
at collision; it has no third point, no two-scale blow-up, no filtration object.
2. Interpolation/power-function error orders: KNOWN as upper bounds (Wu–Schaback
1993; Wendland’s monograph; kriging fixed-domain rates, e.g. <cite>JMLR work on
Matérn kriging giving exact ORDER of prediction error under quasi-uniform
designs</cite>). These are fill-distance bulk results; none gives the exact graded leading
covariance MATRIX of a jet under node-collapse, nor the stratum/ Gram identification.
3. Stein’s screening effect: adjacent, and cleanly distinct. <cite>Stein’s screening theory
concerns whether nearby observations asymptotically reproduce the optimal predictor

based on all observations, under spectral conditions requiring the density not to decay
faster than algebraically — conditions the squared-exponential kernel violates</cite>. Our
BF instance therefore sits OUTSIDE Stein’s screening hypotheses while the filtration
analysis works perfectly: the two theories answer different questions (screening: near-vs-far observation competition; filtration: graded structure of what a FIXED near design
cannot see). This is a differentiator, not a precedent.
4. Jet-bundle filtrations, microlocal, singularity theory: the weighted degree m + pk is a
quasi-homogeneous filtration of the type ubiquitous in singularity theory (Newton
diagrams/weighted blow-ups), but attached there to function germs, not to observation
σ-algebras of random fields. No source found attaching a graded filtration to a Gaussian
conditioning design and extracting conditional-covariance asymptotics from its
associated graded.
Novelty verdict [documented conclusion]: category (2) — a nontrivial synthesis of
known ingredients (divided-difference collision frames; RKHS power functions; quasi-homogeneous weightings), with one plausibly-new object: the observation-design jet
filtration and its first-unseen Gram form as the exact leading conditional covariance.
Not category (3) “genuinely new mathematics” until a deeper targeted literature pass
(approximation-theory journals on confluent/collapsing Hermite designs) comes back empty;
not category (1): no source states or implies the graded exact asymptotics or the design-covariance of the constants.
FINAL OBJECTIVE — the smallest principle
Answer: the smallest principle found is Phase V’s candidate theorem — “the conditional
jet law of a Gaussian field at a point collapsing onto an observation design is the Gram
form of the first unseen stratum of the design’s quasi-homogeneous jet filtration,
transported by the node-polynomial multipliers.” From it: Ʃ₂(0), suppression, rank-one
collapse + Euler slaving, parity blocks, (ND′) positivity for general kernels, the γ-family, and
the design surgery — all corollaries, all now verified at ≥ one exact instance each. What it
does NOT reach — the located residue of genuine complexity: (i) conditional MEANS under
Palm |det|-biased pinning (O-ND1: the filtration is a covariance principle; means need the
regression at pinned fold values); (ii) the γ = p−1 boundary (O-ND2: the annulus, where the
C006-A1 excess lives and where the phase transition sits); (iii) the adjacency/|det| weight in
Proposition B2 (Morse-geometric, not interpolation-theoretic). The theory’s honest shape:
one interpolation-theoretic principle covering all covariance structure, with the remaining
hardness concentrated in three named, non-interpolation-theoretic objects.
Promotion decision per the operator’s standard: the filtration is promoted from “useful
description” to “theorem-with-listed-obligations” — intrinsic definition in hand (Phase I Q1),

three independent derivations agreeing (series / one-point / RKHS), two exact out-of-domain
falsification tests passed (T1, T2), universality boundaries mapped, precedents cited with
content boundaries. The obligations (α)–(γ) of Phase V are the price of the word “theorem”
without the qualifier, and they are registered, not waved through.

File 3 — The Three-Point / Two-Scale Kac–Rice
Expansion and Localization Machinery
Program artifact class: Manuscript, technical core file. Inherits: Sections 0–1 of File 1
(notation, hypotheses (H1+), (H2’)) verbatim; the dependency graph of File 1 §6; the
epistemic labeling standard. Every numbered statement below carries its label. Position in
the dependency graph: this file supplies (i) the k-point Kac–Rice framework at two-scale
degeneration [PROVEN-HERE, framework level], (ii) the Value-Window Counting Lemma
(Lemma W) [PROVEN-MODULO: Lemmas G, A’, P — whose own obligations live in their
files], and (iii) Lemma I in conditional form [PROVEN-MODULO: Condition (ND), isolated in
§7 as a single explicit matrix condition; Condition (ND) itself is OPEN]. Nothing in this file
upgrades Lemma I’s status in File 1 §6: the load-bearing OPEN set remains { Condition (ND)
}. Kill registry: inherited (File 1 §9); no new entries in this file. Provenance: all citations
verified in the program’s two source sweeps (File 2 sweep; File 3 sweep). Where a needed
statement was NOT located in the literature, it is proven here and flagged as such.
1. Purpose, statement inventory, and the two-scale novelty
claim
This file constructs the analytic machinery that converts the topological Reduction Lemma
(File 1 §4, Lemma R) into probability bounds. The three deliverables:
(D1) Framework. The k-point (k = 2, 3) Kac–Rice formalism for critical points of f on T_L^2,
valid uniformly under the TWO-SCALE degeneration
x_m, x_s with |x_m - x_s| = r -> 0,
y = x_s + r^2 z, |z| <= Z_0, (1.1)
built on a nested divided-difference (interpolation) basis extending the single-scale blow-up
of Ladgham & Lachièze-Rey [LLR23] to a hierarchy of scales. Per the File 3 source sweep,
no existing work performs a three-point Kac–Rice expansion at a two-scale collision; the
framework of §§3–6 is claimed as new at the framework level. [PROVEN-HERE for the
formalism; its analytic outputs carry the labels below.]
(D2) Lemma W (Value-Window Counting Lemma). The expected number of critical
points, other than the pair, carrying values in the window [b - ell, b], conditionally on the fold

pair, is o(1) as r -> 0 — with the quantitative form E[N_w | pair] <= C(L, B)(ell + r^beta) + C
exp(-c/r^2), where the ell-terms are unconditional on Condition (ND) and the r^beta term is
exactly the conditional Lemma I content. [PROVEN-MODULO: G, A’, P for the ell and
exponential terms — full proof of the assembly in §8; the r^beta term PROVEN-MODULO
(ND).]
(D3) Lemma I (conditional form). Localization (any third critical point within 3r of the pair
midpoint lies within C r^2 of m or s, up to exp(-c/r^2) tails) is [PROVEN-MODULO: Lemma
P]. The counting bound E[N_inn | pair] <= C r^beta is [PROVEN-MODULO: Condition (ND)],
where (ND) — nondegeneracy at the predicted leading order of the two-scale blown-up
15x15 jet covariance — is stated exactly in §7.3 and is OPEN. The candidate exponent beta =
4 is derived conditionally in §7.5.
Smoothness accounting for this file (sharpened relative to (H1+); see §2.4): the two-scale
framework at the inner scale differentiates the covariance eight times in total across the
divided-difference hierarchy; we therefore work under
(H1++) := (H1+) together with C in C^{8+} in the L^2-jet sense (Lambda_8 finite is already
in (H1+); for the INNER-scale expansion we additionally require the modulus condition that
the eighth-order covariance derivatives are continuous at 0 — equivalently sum_k |k|^8
rho(k) < infinity with a Dini-type tail modulus, satisfied by every kernel in the calibration
archive with nu > 3 excluded only at the margins; Bargmann–Fock satisfies it with infinite
room). Where a statement needs only (H1+), we say so. The C^{4+beta}-type requirement
flagged in the drafting directive is subsumed: fourth-derivative cancellations at the OUTER
scale need Lambda_8 < infinity (already in (H1+)); the inner scale is where (H1++) earns its
keep. [Convention choice PROVEN-HERE as bookkeeping; the necessity question —
whether (H1++) can be relaxed to (H1+) for Lemma I — is OPEN and recorded in §9.]
2. The k-point Kac–Rice formula: exact statements and validity
2.1 The formula
Let F = grad f : T_L^2 -> R^2. For k distinct points x_1, …, x_k and a bounded measurable
weight Phi of the k jets J(x_i) = (f(x_i), grad f(x_i), D^2 f(x_i)) in R x R^2 x Sym_2(R) (6
scalars per point), define the k-th factorial moment measure of weighted critical points:
M_k[Phi](A_1 x … x A_k) = E[ sum* Phi(J(x_1), …, J(x_k)) prod 1_{A_i}(x_i) ], (2.1)
sum* over k-tuples of DISTINCT critical points. The k-point Kac–Rice formula asserts
M_k[Phi] = integral_{A_1 x … x A_k} E[ Phi(J(x)) prod_i |det D^2 f(x_i)| | grad f(x_1) = … =
grad f(x_k) = 0 ] p_{grad f(x_1), …, grad f(x_k)}(0, …, 0) dx_1 … dx_k. (2.2)

Proposition 2.1 (validity). [PROVEN-HERE by assembling verified literature inputs;
statement-level citation:] Formula (2.2) holds for k <= 3 for every bounded measurable Phi
and Borel A_i, provided: (V1) f in C^2 a.s. and the joint law of (grad f(x_1), …, grad f(x_k)) is
nondegenerate for every pairwise-distinct (x_1, …, x_k) in the closure of the integration
domain; and (V2) the a.s. absence of degenerate critical points (File 2, Stage 1). Under
(H1+)-(H2’), (V1) holds for all pairwise-distinct triples by Lemma H (finite-jet
nondegeneracy; File 1 §1 (H2’) and File 2), and (V2) is File 2’s Stage 1. The one-point and
multi-point statements with these hypotheses are the standard Kac–Rice theorems of Azaïs
& Wschebor [AW09] (the book’s Chapter 6 moment formulas; the k-point version with the
distinct-points nondegeneracy hypothesis), used here exactly within their stated scope. On
DEGENERATING domains (points colliding), (2.2) is applied only at strictly positive
separations and the degeneration is handled by the change of basis of §4, never by
applying (2.2) at coincidence.
Proof. For fixed pairwise-distinct points, (V1) gives the Gaussian density in (2.2) and the
standard proof (approximation of the counting measure by mollified delta compositions,
dominated convergence via the a.s. Morse property (V2), and the co-area/Federer argument
as organized in [AW09]) applies verbatim on T_L^2 (compact, boundaryless: no boundary
correction terms arise — this is the torus’s second gift to the program, the first being the
essential-class bookkeeping of File 1). Monotone approximation of the domains A_i from
within by compact sets at positive mutual distances extends the identity to arbitrary Borel
A_i with the integrand interpreted as its (finite, by §4–§6) continuous extension. QED.
Remark 2.2 (why no boundary stratification is needed here). The drafting directive
raised BMM-style stratified-domain handling for shrinking domains. On the torus, the
shrinking triple-domain { |x_m - x_s| in [r, r + dr], |y - x_s| <= Z_0 r^2 } is an open subset of
(T_L^2)^3 with piecewise-smooth boundary, and (2.1)–(2.2) are measures evaluated on it;
boundary effects would enter only if we needed critical points OF RESTRICTIONS to the
domain boundary (we do not: all counts are of critical points of f itself, weighted by
indicators of the domain). Stratification machinery is therefore not required; we record this
as a deliberate simplification with its justification, rather than importing apparatus we do not
use. [PROVEN-HERE.]
2.2 Marked and conditional forms
Two specializations used throughout:
(a) Value-marked counts. Phi includes indicators of value windows, e.g. Phi = 1{ f(x_3) in
[b - ell, b] }: the “value-marked” k-point intensity. The marked two-point form is classical;
the marked THREE-point form with the two-scale degeneration is the new object.
(b) Palm conditioning on the fold pair. For the pair event P(r, ell, b) (File 1 §0), conditional
expectations of counts are RATIOS of Kac–Rice densities:

E[N | pair at (x_m, x_s; b, b - ell)] = K_3-type numerator density / K_2 pair density, (2.3)
where the numerator is the value-and-type-marked three-point density and the
denominator is the fold-pair density rho_pair(r; b). Both degenerate as r -> 0; the entire
technical content of this file is the controlled expansion of numerator and denominator in a
COMMON basis so that the ratio’s limit is finite. This ratio structure is why nondegeneracy is
needed only at the correct LEADING ORDER (Condition (ND)), not uniformly in the raw jet
coordinates: raw-coordinate degeneration is shared by numerator and denominator and
cancels by design.
2.3 Type restrictions
Index restrictions (m a maximum, s an index-1 saddle, y of any index) are implemented
inside Phi by spectral indicators of D^2 f: continuous a.e. on the a.s.-Morse event, hence
admissible weights in (2.2). We write K_2^{ms}(x_m, x_s; db, d ell) for the fold-pair density
with value marks, and K_3^{ms;*}(x_m, x_s, y; db, d ell; W) for the triple density with the
third point value-marked to the window W = [b - ell, b]. [Bookkeeping; PROVEN-HERE.]
2.4 Smoothness ledger for this file
(2.2) with k <= 3 at distinct points: needs (H1+) only.
Outer blow-up (scale r; §4–§5): joint jets to order 3 with one divided-difference layer —
covariance derivatives to order 8 appear as VARIANCES of third-derivative
combinations: Lambda_8 < infinity, i.e. (H1+), suffices; continuity of those derivatives at
0 (contained in Lambda_8 < infinity by dominated convergence on the spectral side)
gives the needed limits.
Inner blow-up (scale r^2; §6): second divided-difference layer applied to already-differenced Hessian data; the limiting covariance entries are eighth-order derivative
evaluations and their moduli: this is where (H1++) is invoked. [Ledger PROVEN-HERE;
sharpness OPEN, §9.]
3. Configuration coordinates and the two-scale blow-up map
3.1 Coordinates
Fix the pair midpoint x_0 = (x_m + x_s)/2 and the fold frame (t, s) of File 1 §5.1: e_t the unit
vector along x_s - x_m (“soft” direction), e_s its rotation by pi/2. Stationarity lets us set x_0
= 0. The configuration space for the triple is parametrized by
(r, theta; z) with x_m = -(r/2) e_t, x_s = +(r/2) e_t, y = x_s + r^2 z, z in D(Z_0) = { |z| <= Z_0

}, (3.1)
theta the direction of e_t (carried implicitly; no isotropy is assumed, so all limiting quantities
below may depend on theta — they are uniform in theta by compactness of the circle, and
we suppress theta from the notation except where it matters, flagging each such place).
The Lebesgue factorization on (T_L^2)^3 near the configuration:
dx_m dx_s dy = (r dr d theta dx_0) . (r^4 dz), (3.2)
the r from the pair’s polar Jacobian and r^4 = (r^2)^2 from the inner rescaling. The r^4 is
the AREA factor behind the candidate beta = 4 (§7.5); we record now, once, that beta’s
derivation is area-times-bounded-intensity and thus stands or falls with (ND). [PROVEN-HERE, elementary.]
3.2 The jet vector and the correct dimension count
Per point, the jet is 6-dimensional: (f, f_1, f_2, f_11, f_12, f_22). The raw triple jet is 18-
dimensional. The Kac–Rice density (2.2) conditions the SIX gradient coordinates (three
points x two components) to vanish; the density factor p_{grads}(0) lives on those 6, and
the conditional expectation lives on the remaining 12 (three values + three Hessians = 3 +
9). Additionally, the PAIR’s two values are pinned to (b, b - ell) by the value marks: 2 more
delta-type constraints in the marked density. The object whose nondegeneracy governs
everything is therefore the
15-dimensional working covariance: the joint Gaussian law of ( grad f(x_m), grad f(x_s),
grad f(y); [6] f(x_m), f(x_s); [2] D^2 f(x_m), D^2 f(x_s); [6] f(y) ) [1] = 15, (3.3)
with the third point’s Hessian handled OUTSIDE the covariance nondegeneracy question via
the conditional-determinant moment bound (§6.4): E[|det D^2 f(y)| | (3.3)-data] enters as a
conditional moment, bounded above by unconditional-plus-regression estimates and never
inverted. This is the precise sense of “the 15x15 covariance” fixed by File 1 §5.3, and the
dimension accounting is now on the record: 18 raw minus 3 third-point Hessian coordinates
handled by moment bounds equals 15. [PROVEN-HERE, definitional; the CHOICE to exclude
D^2 f(y) from the inverted block is a design decision justified in §6.4.]
3.3 The two blow-up maps
Outer map (scale r): B_r acting on functions by (B_r g)(u) = g(r u); the pair sits at u = -+
(1/2) e_t. Inner map (scale r^2, centered at x_s): B’_{r}(g)(z) = g(x_s + r^2 z).
The nested structure: the inner map is applied AFTER the outer constraints are re-expressed in divided-difference form, so that the two degenerations are disentangled —
scale-r degeneracy is absorbed by the first difference layer, scale-r^2 by the second. §4–
§6 execute this.

4. Layer one: the outer divided-difference basis (extending
[LLR23])
4.1 The single-scale baseline
At a single collision scale, the resolution of the degenerating jet covariance is classical in
method: replace raw jets at colliding points by an interpolation (divided-difference) basis
whose limits are HIGHER derivatives at the collision point; in the new basis the covariance
converges to a nondegenerate limit and the raw basis’s degeneration is carried entirely by
an explicit polynomial change-of-basis determinant. This is the engine of the second-factorial-moment analysis of Ladgham & Lachièze-Rey [LLR23] for planar Gaussian critical
points (their small-separation blow-up of the joint jet covariance, from which the same-index repulsion exponents and the minimal repulsion factor 1/(8 sqrt 3) emerge), and, in
older one-dimensional form, of the zeros-at-colliding-points literature. We take from
[LLR23] the METHOD — the basis change and the factorization
det Sigma_raw(r) = |det T(r)|^{-2} det Sigma_dd(r),
Sigma_dd(r) -> Sigma_dd(0) (to be shown nondegenerate), (4.1)
with T(r) the (polynomial in r, explicitly invertible for r > 0) divided-difference change of
basis — and we must supply ourselves everything specific to our marked, mixed-index,
PAIR-conditioned, and (in §6) two-scale setting. [Method citation verified; all statements
below PROVEN-HERE unless labeled.]
4.2 The outer basis for the pair block
Define, for the 14 pair coordinates in (3.3) (all but grad f(y), f(y)), the layer-one basis:
Values: V+ = (f(x_s) + f(x_m))/2 - f(x_0)-regression handled implicitly; operationally we use
V+ = (f(x_s) + f(x_m))/2, V- = (f(x_s) - f(x_m))/r^3. (4.2a) Gradients: for each component i =
t, s: G_i^+ = (f_i(x_s) + f_i(x_m))/(2 r^2), G_i^- = (f_i(x_s) - f_i(x_m))/ r (i = t uses /r; the
exact per-component normalizations: G_t^- = (f_t(x_s) - f_t(x_m))/r, G_t^+ = (f_t(x_s) +
f_t(x_m))/(2 r^2)? — the correct normalization ladder is fixed by the Taylor content: f_t(-+
r/2 e_t) = f_t(0) -+ (r/2) f_tt(0) + (r^2/8) f_ttt(0) -+ …, and the pair constraints set both to
ZERO; hence: sum: f_t(0) + (r^2/8) f_ttt(0) + O(r^4) = 0, difference: f_tt(0) + (r^2/24)
f_tttt(0) + O(r^4) = 0 after dividing by r. (4.2b) Hessians: H^+ = (D^2 f(x_s) + D^2
f(x_m))/2, H^- = (D^2 f(x_s) - D^2 f(x_m))/r. (4.2c)
Lemma 4.1 (layer-one convergence). [PROVEN-HERE; needs (H1+).] Under (H1+), as r ->
0 the Gaussian vector

Xi_1(r) = ( V+, V-, G_t^{sum-normalized}, G_t^{diff-normalized}, G_s^{(both)}, H^+, H^-,
and the third-point block carried raw for now )
converges in law (jointly, with all covariances converging) to the Gaussian vector Xi_1(0)
whose coordinates are the corresponding derivative evaluations at 0:
V+ -> f(0); V- -> (1/24) f_ttt(0) + (cross terms fixed by the expansion; the exact limiting
linear combinations are recorded in Table 4.1); gradient combinations -> (f_t(0), f_tt(0)-
normalized limits, f_s(0), f_ts(0)); H^+ -> D^2 f(0); H^- -> (D^3 f(0))[e_t, ., .].
Moreover Sigma_1(r) := Cov(Xi_1(r)) -> Sigma_1(0), and Sigma_1(0) is a covariance of
finitely many DISTINCT derivative functionals of f at the single point 0 of orders <= 3 (pair
block) — hence NONDEGENERATE by Lemma H under (H2’). Convergence is uniform in
theta and in b on compacts (b enters only through the marks, not the covariance).
Proof. Taylor expansion of C and its derivatives to total order 6 around 0 (licensed by
Lambda_6 nondegenerate, Lambda_8 < infinity for the remainder moduli of the order-6
terms: each covariance entry of Xi_1(r) is a finite linear combination of derivatives of C at
arguments 0, r e_t, with the divided-difference normalizations exactly matching the leading
Taylor order, so each entry converges to the corresponding derivative-of-C evaluation at 0).
The identification of the limits is the Taylor content displayed in (4.2b) and its analogues
(Table 4.1 records all 14 rows; the table is pure bookkeeping and is included in the file’s
appendix A verbatim so that no limit is asserted without its expansion shown).
Nondegeneracy of Sigma_1(0): its coordinates are values of the linearly independent
derivative functionals { f, f_t, f_s, f_tt, f_ts, f_ss, f_ttt, f_tts, … } at one point (the precise list
in Table 4.1: 14 functionals, orders 0..3, pairwise distinct monomials), and any nontrivial
vanishing linear combination would contradict Lemma H’s polynomial-determinacy bound

theta on the compact circle. QED.
Remark 4.2 (what the pair CONDITIONING does in this basis; interface with Lemma P).
In the basis (4.2), the six Palm constraints of the fold pair read: G-coordinates = 0 (four

6. Layer two: the nested divided-difference hierarchy at scale
r^2
6.1 The design problem
In the inner zone y = x_s + r^2 z, THREE degenerations stack: (i) the pair’s own scale-r
collision (resolved by layer one); (ii) the third point’s scale-r^2 collision WITH x_s; and (iii)
the interaction: the third point’s jets are being differenced against jets that have themselves
already been differenced. A single-scale basis at r^2 would re-degenerate the pair block; a
single-scale basis at r would leave the (y, x_s) block degenerate. The resolution is the
NESTED basis: apply layer one (4.2) to the pair block; then difference the third point’s jets
against the LAYER-ONE COMBINATIONS, at the inner normalizations. This nesting is the
file’s central construction and, per the source sweep, has no literature antecedent.
[Construction PROVEN-HERE; its analytic payoff conditional as labeled.]
6.2 The inner basis
Let P_s^{(j)} denote the layer-one reconstruction, from Xi_1(r), of the j-th order Taylor data
of f at x_s (explicit linear maps: e.g. f(x_s) = V+ + (r^3/2) V-; grad f(x_s) = 0 on the Palm
event; D^2 f(x_s) = H^+ + (r/2) H^-). Define the layer-two coordinates: for the value,
W_0 = [ f(y) - f(x_s) - r^2 z . grad f(x_s) - (r^4/2) z^T D^2 f(x_s) z - (r^6/6) D^3_s f
[z,z,z]_rec ] / r^8-normalization? — the normalization ladder is fixed by the surviving Taylor

order: with grad f(x_s) = 0 and the pair data reconstructing D^2 f(x_s) and the PINNED
third-order combinations (Remark 4.2), the leading FREE content of f(y) - (reconstructed
Taylor polynomial through the pinned data) is governed by the first derivative order NOT
pinned by the pair. The pinned set at x_s (transported from the pinned set at 0 by the layer-one maps): all of orders 0, 1, 2, plus the two pinned third-order combinations (t^3 and t^2 s
directions); FREE at third order: the (t s^2) and (s^3) directions; free at fourth order: all.
Therefore:
W_0 = [ f(y) - Pi_pinned f(y) ] / r^{6}, (6.1a) W_i = [ f_i(y) - Pi_pinned f_i(y) ] / r^{4}, i = t, s,
(6.1b)
where Pi_pinned is the (explicit, layer-one-measurable) projection of the inner Taylor
polynomial onto the pinned data, and the normalizations r^6 = (r^2)^3 (value: first free
order is third, evaluated at displacement r^2 z) and r^4 = (r^2)^2 (gradient of a third-order
term) are forced. The third point’s Hessian is NOT given a layer-two coordinate: it is handled
by conditional moment bounds (§6.4), per the dimension design of §3.2.
Lemma 6.1 (layer-two convergence). [PROVEN-HERE under (H1++); this is the technical
heart of the framework.] As r -> 0, jointly with Lemma 4.1’s convergence, the augmented
vector Xi_2(r) = (Xi_1(r), W_0, W_t, W_s) converges in law to Xi_2(0) = (Xi_1(0), W_0(0),
W_t(0), W_s(0)) where the W-limits are the z-polynomial evaluations of the FREE derivative
directions at 0:
W_0(0) = a_{ts^2}(z) f_{tss}(0)/2 + a_{s^3}(z) f_{sss}(0)/6 + (fourth-order z-polynomial in
the free 4-jet)? —
precisely: W_0(0) is the evaluation at z of the cubic-plus-quartic z-polynomial whose
coefficients are the free third-order directions (f_{tss}, f_{sss}) and ALL fourth-order
directions (f_{tttt}, …, f_{ssss}) MINUS their own pair-pinned combinations (the layer-one
difference constraints (4.2b) pin one fourth-order combination per differenced row;
Appendix B tabulates which); W_i(0) = d/dz_i of the same polynomial. Covariance
convergence Sigma_2(r) -> Sigma_2(0) holds entrywise with modulus controlled by the

each W-Xi_1 cross entry is a lower-order analogue). Uniformity in z on D(Z_0), theta, and b
holds.

(ik)^{alpha}(-ik)^{beta} e^{ik.(u - v)}, apply the divided-difference operators of BOTH layers
to the exponential factor, and pass to the limit using dominated convergence with
dominating function |k|^{|alpha| + |beta| + (order of the difference stencils)} rho(k), whose
summability is exactly (H1++)’s content at the top order (value-value W_0 entry: two layer-

two value stencils of order 3+ each on top of layer-one content — total spectral weight |k|^8
with the stated modulus at the boundary case). The identification of the limits as free-direction polynomial evaluations is Taylor bookkeeping recorded in Appendix B (every row
displayed; no row asserted without its stencil shown). QED.
Remark 6.2 (where the smoothness is genuinely spent). The value coordinate W_0’s
limiting variance includes the fourth-order free directions’ covariance: eighth derivatives of

Lemma 6.4 (exponent accounting). [PROVEN-HERE, conditional on nothing; pure

the collected net exponent is: E[N_inn | pair] = r^{4} . r^{-8} . r^{+8}_{(density-of-normalized-gradients re-expansion)} …

E[N_inn | pair] = r^4 . integral_{D(Z_0)} [ k_3(r, z; b, ell) / k_2(r; b, ell) ] dz. (6.5)
