6.4 The determinant weights: why D^2 f(y) is a moment, not a
coordinate
Lemma 6.5. [PROVEN-HERE under (H1+).] Uniformly in r <= r_0, z in D(Z_0), b in B, and
uniformly over the pinned data in compacts:
E[ |det D^2 f(y)| . prod_{pair} |det D^2 f| . 1{indices} | Xi_2(r) = pinned ] <= C, (6.6)
and the pair determinants are moreover BOUNDED BELOW on the fold event in the sense

needed for k_2’s positivity: |det D^2 f(x_s)| = |f_tt(x_s)| . mu-part with f_tt(x_s) = kappa r/1 .
(1 + o(1)) — the soft eigenvalue — so the pair weights contribute the explicit factor
Theta(r^2) (one soft eigenvalue per pair member: |det D^2 f(x_m)| . |det D^2 f(x_s)| =
Theta(r) . Theta(r) = Theta(r^2)) TO BOTH numerator and denominator, cancelling in the
ratio (6.5) up to constants.
Proof. Upper bound (6.6): each Hessian entry is a Gaussian variable whose conditional law
given Xi_2(r) has mean linear in the pinned data (bounded on compacts, uniformly in r since
the regression is onto the CONVERGENT frame — Lemma 6.1 — with nondegenerate limit by
Lemma H for the Xi_1 block and, for the cross-terms onto the W block, bounded regression
coefficients whenever Sigma_2(r) is invertible; for the UNIFORMITY of those coefficients as
r -> 0 we do NOT need (ND): we need only that the W-block variance not degenerate to
zero, which is Lemma H’s LOWER bound applied to the free-direction polynomial — the free
directions (f_{tss}, f_{sss}, free 4-jet) are honest derivative functionals with positive-definite
joint covariance, and the evaluation polynomial W_0(0)(z) vanishes identically in z only if all
free coefficients vanish: for each fixed z != 0 outside the common zero set of the evaluation
forms — a finite union of curves in D(Z_0), tabulated in Appendix B — Var(W_0(0)) > 0; on
the exceptional curves the value coordinate is dropped from the conditioning frame and the
argument proceeds with the 14-frame; this stratified handling is spelled out in Appendix B
and is where care, not new mathematics, is spent). Gaussian conditional moments of |det| (a
degree-2 polynomial in jointly Gaussian entries) are then bounded by unconditional
moments plus polynomial functions of the bounded conditional means. Lower/order
statement for the pair: the fold normal form gives the soft eigenvalue f_tt(x_pm) = -+ kappa
r (1 + o(1)) and stiff eigenvalue -mu + o(1) on the Palm event, whence the Theta(r^2)
product; its appearance in BOTH k_3 and k_2 with the same order is manifest from
(4.3)/(6.2) sharing the pair block. QED.
Design justification (the §3.2 decision). Inverting a covariance containing D^2 f(y) would
force nondegeneracy questions about SECOND derivatives at the inner scale, raising the
spectral order needed beyond 8 and — decisively — coupling (ND) to data the counting
bound never needs pinned. Moment-bounding |det D^2 f(y)| instead costs only (6.6). This is
why the working covariance is 15-dimensional and why (ND) is stated on exactly that block.
[PROVEN-HERE at the level of design coherence; not a mathematical claim beyond 6.5.]
7. Lemma I: conditional formulation, the isolated condition
(ND),
and the conditional proof
7.1 Localization (unconditional given Lemma P)

Proposition 7.1 (inner localization). [PROVEN-MODULO: Lemma P.] Conditionally on the
fold pair, on the event { exists a critical point y’, y’ not in {m, s}, d(y’, x_0) <= 3r }, we have,
with probability 1 - C exp(-c / r^2): d(y’, m) <= C_* r^2 or d(y’, s) <= C_* r^2. Equivalently:
the annulus-side gradient analysis of Lemma A’ (mean kappa(t^2 - a) against sd tau^3 from
the pinned residual) forbids critical points at 3r >= tau >= C_* r^2-neighborhood boundaries
except on Gaussian tails. This is File 1 §4’s localization restated; its proof lives with Lemma
A’/P and is not re-proven here. The constant C_* is explicit in Lemma P’s file.
The inner count is therefore reduced, up to exp(-c/r^2), to the two balls B(m, C_* r^2), B(s,
C_* r^2); by symmetry of the argument (the roles of the two soft-direction endpoints are
exchanged by t -> -t with kappa -> -kappa) we treat B(s, C_* r^2) and write Z_0 = C_*.
7.2 Statement
Lemma I (inner counting; conditional form). [PROVEN-MODULO: Condition (ND) of §7.3.
Without (ND): OPEN. The label of record for the unconditional statement remains OPEN,
exactly as in File 1 §6.]
Under (H1++), (H2’), there exist beta > 0 and C < infinity, uniform for b in compacts, with
E[ #{ critical y in B(s, Z_0 r^2), y != s } | fold pair ] <= C r^{beta}. (7.1)
Conditionally on (ND) with its predicted leading order, the proof below gives (7.1) with beta
= 4, and in fact the sharper statement that the integrand ratio in (6.5) stays bounded:
sup_{r <= r_0} sup_{z in D(Z_0)} k_3(r, z; b, ell) / k_2(r; b, ell) <= C(Z_0, B). (7.2)
7.3 Condition (ND): the exact matrix condition
Let Sigma_2(r) be the covariance of the 15-coordinate vector of §3.2 written in the nested
basis: Xi_2(r) restricted to the (gradients-normalized [6: the pair’s four G’s and the third
point’s W_t, W_s], marked values [3: V+, V-, W_0], pair Hessians [6: H^+, H^-]) — fifteen
coordinates. By Lemmas 4.1 and 6.1, Sigma_2(r) -> Sigma_2(0) entrywise, uniformly in (z,
theta) on compacts.
Condition (ND). For every z in D(Z_0) off the exceptional curves of Appendix B (and with
the stratified 14-frame replacement on them), and every theta:
det Sigma_2(0)(z, theta) > 0, (7.3)
with a positive lower bound uniform on the stated compact strata.
Equivalently, in the language of File 1 §5.3: the leading order of det Sigma_raw(r) under the
two-scale degeneration equals EXACTLY the order dictated by the divided-difference ladder
— the order 2 . (sum of all normalization exponents in T_3) — with a nonvanishing

coefficient; any EXCESS vanishing (a “hidden constraint”: some linear combination of the
fifteen limiting functionals degenerating despite the ladder) falsifies (ND).
Status of (ND): OPEN. What is and is not known: (i) Each individual limiting coordinate of
Sigma_2(0) is a bona fide derivative functional or free-direction polynomial evaluation with
POSITIVE variance (Lemma H) — so no single row degenerates. (ii) The Xi_1(0) block alone
is nondegenerate (Lemma 4.1). (iii) The danger is a CROSS-BLOCK collapse: the third
point’s limiting coordinates (W_0, W_t, W_s)(0) are z-polynomial evaluations in the free
directions, and free directions are CORRELATED with the Xi_1(0) block (fourth-order
directions appear in both layer-one difference remainders and layer-two limits — the
Appendix B tabulation identifies the shared functionals). Whether the shared content
produces an exact rank drop at some (z, theta) is exactly what no hand argument in this file
settles and what the literature (File 3 sweep verdict) does not address. (iv) The designated
resolution path, per File 1 §5.3 and the program plan: symbolic assembly of Sigma_2(0) for
the Bargmann–Fock kernel and evaluation of (7.3) on a certified grid in (z, theta) with
interval arithmetic on the determinant — a FINITE computation, deliberately excluded from
this generation. A degenerate finding falsifies the beta = 4 route and forces a re-blow-up (a
different inner ladder); this is the program’s designated failure fork.
7.4 The window mark in the inner zone (why the value window is free
here)
In B(s, Z_0 r^2), any critical y automatically satisfies |f(y) - f(s)| <= C r^{6} + fluctuation (the
pinned Taylor content plus r^6 W_0), which is o(ell) = o(r^3): the window mark 1{f(y) in W}
is IDENTICALLY 1 on the inner event up to exp(-c/r^2) tails. The window therefore imposes
NO additional smallness in the inner zone — the inner count must be killed by (ND)-
governed intensity boundedness plus the area factor, NOT by the window. This is why beta
and the window exponent (the ell = kappa r^3/6 of the outer zones) are INDEPENDENT
parameters in (2.2), and it is recorded here to prevent a reader (or a future instance of this
program) from double-counting the window. [PROVEN-HERE, elementary given Lemmas
P/6.1.]
7.5 Conditional proof of Lemma I and of beta = 4
Proof of Lemma I assuming (ND). By (6.5) it suffices to prove (7.2). Fix z off the exceptional
strata (the strata contribute zero area and are handled by the 14-frame variant verbatim).
The ratio k_3/k_2 is, by (6.3) and its k = 2 analogue: [Gaussian density of the 15-frame at
the pinned values] / [Gaussian density of the 8-coordinate pair frame at its pinned values] x
[ratio of conditional determinant-weight expectations]. The second ratio is bounded above
by Lemma 6.5’s upper bound divided by k_2’s positive determinant-weight content
(Proposition 4.3 / B2’s positivity; the shared pair soft factors Theta(r^2) cancel exactly per
Lemma 6.5). The first ratio is a conditional Gaussian density: the density of (W_t, W_s, W_0-

window) at their pinned values GIVEN the pair frame — bounded above by (2 pi)^{-3/2} (det
Cov(W | pair frame))^{-1/2}, and (ND) is PRECISELY the statement that this conditional
covariance has determinant bounded below, uniformly on the compact strata, in the r -> 0
limit; uniformity for r <= r_0 then follows from the entrywise convergence of Lemma 6.1 plus
continuity of determinants on the compact parameter set. Hence (7.2); integrating over
D(Z_0) (finite area) in (6.5) gives E[N_inn | pair] <= C r^4: beta = 4. The exp(-c/r^2) additive
terms come from Proposition 7.1’s localization tails. QED (conditional).
What (ND) buys and what it does not. (ND) with ANY positive lower bound gives beta = 4
through the area factor; a WEAKER version of (ND) — det Sigma_2(0) vanishing on a
positive-codimension set with polynomial rate — would still give some beta > 0 by
integrating the inverse-square-root singularity, PROVIDED the singularity is integrable over
D(Z_0); this fallback is stated as Remark 7.2 and means the program survives some
degenerate findings, but not a full-rank collapse on an open set. [Remark PROVEN-HERE
conditional on its own hypothesis; recorded so the falsification fork of §7.3(iv) is three-pronged: clean (beta = 4), integrable-degenerate (some beta > 0), open-set collapse (route
falsified).]
8. Lemma W: statement and full proof of the assembly
Lemma W (Value-Window Counting Lemma). [PROVEN-MODULO: Lemmas G, A’, P (their
files’ executed obligations) for the displayed ell and exponential terms; the r^beta term
PROVEN-MODULO (ND). This is the honest composite label; the ASSEMBLY below is
PROVEN-HERE in full.]
Under (H1++), (H2’), uniformly for b in a compact B:
E[ N_w | fold pair ] := E[ #{ critical y not in {m, s} : f(y) in [b - ell, b] } | pair ] <= C(L, B) ell +
C(delta, B) ell + C r^{beta} + C exp(-c/r^2). (8.1)
Consequently, by File 1’s Reduction Lemma R and Markov’s inequality applied to the
nonnegative integer count N_w (P(A_w) = P(N_w >= 1) <= E[N_w]; no second-moment input
is needed — recorded explicitly since the k = 3 machinery above might suggest otherwise:
the THIRD moment machinery of this file is used to bound a FIRST conditional moment, the
third factorial structure arising from the two conditioning points plus the one counted point),
1 - q(r, b) <= E[N_w | pair] + P(A_loop | pair) <= (8.1) + [B0-B1 band terms, exp(-c/r^2)],
(8.2)
which is File 1’s (2.2).
Proof. Partition T_L^2 = FAR (d(y, x_0) >= delta) UNION ANNULUS (3r <= d <= delta) UNION

INNER (d <= 3r); N_w = N_far + N_ann + N_inn accordingly (the pair points themselves
excluded by definition). Far: Proposition 5.1 gives <= C(L, delta, B) ell — here the count over
the FIXED-VOLUME far zone is finite because the conditional one-point intensity of window-marked critical points is bounded (Lemma G frame) and the window mark contributes the
factor ell through the bounded conditional value density integrated over a width-ell interval;
the integration over the far zone contributes area <= L^2: assembling, E[N_far | pair] <= L^2
. C(delta, B) . ell. Annulus: Proposition 5.2. Inner: Proposition 7.1 localizes to the two r^2-
balls up to exp(-c/r^2); on the balls the window mark is void (§7.4) and Lemma I
(conditional) gives <= C r^beta. Summation gives (8.1). For (8.2): Lemma R gives {D(m) != s}
subset A_w UNION A_loop UNION A_0; P(A_0) = 0 (File 2, Stage 1.5); P(A_w | pair) <=
E[N_w | pair] by Markov on the integer count; A_loop’s bound is Lemmas B0-B1’s content
(their file), quoted, not re-proven. QED.
Remark 8.1 (sharpness ledger). (8.1) is an upper-bound architecture (File 1 §7.2). The
far/annulus ell-terms are expected sharp up to constants (the heuristic lower bound: a
window-valued far maximum adjacent to the growing component preempts with positive

(Remark 7.2) the inner term can become leading; the calibration cycle C006 (File 1 §8.3) is

BEFORE the symbolic computation does. [Ledger PROVEN-HERE at the level of its

File 4 — The Pinning Lemma and Critical-Pair Palm
Conditioning
Program artifact class: Manuscript, technical core file. Inherits: File 1 Sections 0–1
(notation; hypotheses (H1+), (H2’)) verbatim; File 3’s nested divided-difference conventions
(its §4, §6 and the normalization ladder), the 15-coordinate working frame (File 3 §3.2), and
the epistemic labeling standard. Every numbered statement carries its label. Position in the
dependency graph (File 1 §6): this file discharges the executed-obligation node “Lemma P
[finite-dimensional; to execute]” and supplies the conditional-density machinery quoted by
Lemma G, Lemma A’, Lemma B1, and File 3’s Lemmas 6.1/6.5. It does NOT touch the load-bearing OPEN set: Condition (ND) (File 3 §7.3) remains OPEN, and nothing below
strengthens Lemma I. Smoothness ledger: the pair-Palm representation and the cubic
pinning need (H1+) only. The tau^4 residual upper bound needs Lambda_8 < infinity (inside
(H1+)). The general-nu variant (spectral tail exponent nu in (3,4), Lambda_8 = infinity) is
carried as Proposition P5 with degraded exponents. Kill-registry interface: the results
below are precisely what retire the K2 entry of File 1 §9 (the O(K^-3) annulus floor): K2’s
supersession is DISCHARGED by Theorem P3 + Corollary P4, and this file is its proof of
record.
1. Purpose and statement inventory
Three deliverables, matching the drafting directive:
(D1) The pair-Palm representation (§3). An explicit, from-the- ground-up construction of
the field conditioned on an r-fold critical pair: f = m_r(.; pinned data) + g_r, with m_r an
explicit random polynomial-plus-regression mean and g_r a centered Gaussian residual
independent of the pinned data, together with the identification of the representation as the
Kac–Rice Palm kernel (so that “conditioning on the pair” has one meaning across the
manuscript). Single-point precedents: the Slepian-model conditioning of Lindgren and the
Kac–Rice conditional laws as organized in Azaïs–Wschebor [AW09]; the Gaussian-regression-plus-independence mechanism is classical. The PAIR version — two critical
points with a degenerating separation, six simultaneous constraints, and uniformity
demands as r -> 0 — was not located in the literature (File 2 and File 3 sweeps) and is
claimed as new at the level of its uniform statements. [Construction PROVEN-HERE.]
(D2) Uniform conditional-density bounds under degenerating conditioning (§4). The

static theory (fixed distinct points) gives nondegenerate conditional laws immediately from
(H2’) via Lemma H. The new content is UNIFORMITY along the degeneration r -> 0:
Theorem P2 (uniform interpolation determinacy) proves two-sided bounds on conditional
variances of the field and its derivatives at a third location, given the six pair constraints,
with constants uniform in r <= r_0 — by transporting the problem to the convergent divided-difference frame of File 3 §4 and proving a uniform invertibility statement there. The
contrast with the standard references is made explicit in Remark 4.4: fixed-frame
nondegeneracy is [AW09]/Lemma-H territory; DEGENERATING-frame uniformity is not, and
is the file’s second novel claim. [PROVEN-HERE.]
(D3) The cubic-pinning proof (§5). Theorem P3: the Palm conditioning on the pair
determines the on-axis cubic coefficient c_{t^3} (and the mixed coefficient c_{t^2 s}) of the
local expansion at the midpoint, exactly, as measurable functions of the pinned data, and
the conditioned residual vanishes to the stated orders with the stated free directions.
Corollary P4 packages the working consequences quoted everywhere (the tau^4 / tau^3 /
tau^3 scalings and the Theta(1/tau) mean-to-sd ratios). [PROVEN-HERE under (H1+).]
Throughout, x_0 = 0, e_t along x_s - x_m, x_m = -(r/2) e_t, x_s = +(r/2) e_t, coordinates (t,
s), pair values (b, b - ell).
2. The static layer: regression calculus and Lemma H quantified
We first fix, in one place, the Gaussian regression identities used by every construction
below, and the quantitative form of Lemma H this file needs. Everything in this section is
classical in mechanism and is written out to keep the file self-contained.
2.1 Regression identities. Let (X, Y) be jointly Gaussian, X in R^n the conditioning block
with covariance Sigma_X invertible, Y in R^m. Then conditionally on X = x:
Y | X = x ~ N( C_{YX} Sigma_X^{-1} x , Sigma_Y - C_{YX} Sigma_X^{-1} C_{XY} ), (2.1)
and the conditional covariance (the Schur complement) satisfies the variational
characterization used repeatedly below:
Var(v.Y | X) = min_{a in R^n} Var( v.Y - a.X ), (2.2)
i.e. conditional variance = squared L^2(P)-distance from v.Y to span(X). Identity (2.2) is the
entire engine of the uniformity theory: lower bounds on conditional variances are DISTANCE
bounds, and distance bounds survive limits of the conditioning frame whenever the limit
frame’s span does not swallow the target. [Classical; PROVEN-HERE by one-line orthogonal
projection.]
2.2 Lemma H, quantitative form. [PROVEN-HERE from (H2’); this is the File 1/File 2

Lemma H restated with the two-sided rates this file consumes.] Under (H2’), for every
integer J <= 4 there exist 0 < c_J <= C_J such that:
(a) (single-point jets) the covariance of the full J-jet of f at a point has all eigenvalues in
[c_J, C_J]; (b) (polynomial determinacy with rate) for every polynomial Q of degree <= J
with coefficient vector on the unit sphere, Var( Q(D) f(0) ) = sum_k |Q(i k)|^2 rho(k) in [c_J,
C_J]; (c) (Taylor-order two-sided bounds) for |y| <= delta_0, writing Pi_J f(y) for the J-th
Taylor polynomial at 0, c |y|^{2(J+1)} <= Var( f(y) - Pi_J-regression at 0 ) <= C |y|^{2(J+1)},
the upper bound requiring Lambda_{2(J+1)} < infinity and the lower bound only (H2’) — for
J = 3 the upper bound is exactly where Lambda_8 enters. Analogous two-sided bounds
hold for first derivatives with exponents 2J.
Proof. (a), (b): the displayed spectral identity plus compactness of the coefficient sphere
and continuity of the (finite by Lambda_{2J}) sum; positivity at each point of the sphere
because a.e.-vanishing of the polynomial |Q(ik)|^2 on the open positivity set of rho forces Q
= 0. (c): expand f(y) - (regression of f(y) on the J-jet at 0) via (2.2): its variance is the
distance from the functional e_y := f(y) to the span of the jet functionals; spectrally,
distance^2 = min over polynomials P of degree <= J of sum_k |e^{i k.y} - P(ik)|^2 rho(k).
Upper bound: take P = the Taylor polynomial of the exponential, |e^{iky} - Taylor_J| <=
|k|^{J+1} |y|^{J+1} / (J+1)!, summable against rho when Lambda_{2(J+1)} < infinity. Lower
bound: restrict the sum to the open set U where rho has positive density; on U the function
k -> e^{ik.y} - P(ik) cannot be small simultaneously for all k in U below the stated rate unless
it vanishes identically to order J+1 in y — quantitatively: expand in y; the coefficient of the
(J+1)-st order y- monomials is (ik)^{alpha}/alpha! - 0 (P has no such order), and (b) applied
at degree J+1 on U gives the |y|^{2(J+1)} lower rate with c > 0 uniform for |y| <= delta_0 by a
compactness argument in the direction of y. QED.
Remark 2.1 (what is standard and what is not). Everything in §2 is static: fixed
conditioning frames, fixed or single points. The references supply exactly this layer ([AW09]
for the regression organization; the BMM-type nondegeneracy conditions for planar fields
verified in the File 2 sweep are of this static kind). None of it survives, as stated,
conditioning on a frame whose covariance matrix DEGENERATES with a parameter — which
is what the pair constraints do as r -> 0. Sections 3–4 build that extension.
3. The pair-Palm representation
3.1 The conditioning functionals
Define the six-vector of raw pair functionals
Phi_r(f) = ( f(x_m), f(x_s), f_t(x_m), f_s(x_m), f_t(x_s), f_s(x_s) ) in R^6. (3.1)

For every r > 0, Cov(Phi_r) is invertible (Lemma H(a)–(b) at two distinct points; File 2’s static
two-point nondegeneracy), but Cov(Phi_r) degenerates as r -> 0: its determinant is
Theta(r^{2 p_2}) with the integer p_2 fixed by the divided-difference ladder (File 3 §4.2 and
its Appendix A; the exact integer is never load-bearing).
3.2 The normalized pair frame
Following File 3 (4.2), define the invertible-for-r>0 linear map T_2(r): R^6 -> R^6 sending
Phi_r to the NORMALIZED frame
Psi_r = ( V^+, V^-, G_t^+, G_t^-, G_s^+, G_s^- ), V^+ = (f(x_s) + f(x_m))/2, V^- = (f(x_s) -
f(x_m))/r^3, G_t^- = (f_t(x_s) - f_t(x_m))/r, G_t^+ = (f_t(x_s) + f_t(x_m))/2, G_s^- =
(f_s(x_s) - f_s(x_m))/r, G_s^+ = (f_s(x_s) + f_s(x_m))/2. (3.2)
(The gradient SUMS carry no r-normalization: their Taylor content f_t(0) + O(r^2) already
converges; only the differences and the value difference need rescaling. This differs from a
draft normalization in File 3 (4.2b)’s parenthetical and is the definitive convention; File 3’s
Appendix A adopts it. The choice affects explicit determinants only, never the ratios in
which they cancel.)
Lemma P1 (frame convergence and uniform invertibility). [PROVEN-HERE under (H1+).]
As r -> 0, Sigma_Psi(r) := Cov(Psi_r) converges entrywise to Sigma_Psi(0) = Cov( f(0),
(1/24) f_{ttt}(0), f_t(0), f_{tt}(0), f_s(0), f_{ts}(0) ) — six DISTINCT derivative functionals at
one point (orders 0..3, pairwise distinct monomials) — wait: the limit identifications, with the
(3.2) normalizations and the Taylor expansions f(x_pm) = f(0) -+ (r/2) f_t(0) + (r^2/8) f_{tt}
(0) -+ (r^3/48) f_{ttt}(0) + O(r^4), f_t(x_pm) = f_t(0) -+ (r/2) f_{tt}(0) + (r^2/8) f_{ttt}(0) +
O(r^3), f_s(x_pm) = f_s(0) -+ (r/2) f_{ts}(0) + (r^2/8) f_{tts}(0) + O(r^3), are:
V^+ -> f(0); V^- -> -(1/24) f_{ttt}(0) - (1/ r^2) f_t(0)? — NO: the raw V^- contains the term -
(1/r^2) f_t(0), which does NOT converge.
The frame (3.2) is therefore NOT the right convergent frame in isolation: value differences
mix with gradient content at lower Taylor order. The correct convergent frame — and this is
precisely the kind of silent trap the file exists to close — takes GRADIENT-CORRECTED
divided differences:
V^-_corr = [ f(x_s) - f(x_m) - r . (f_t(x_s) + f_t(x_m))/2 ] / r^3. (3.3)
With (3.3): Taylor gives f(x_s) - f(x_m) = r f_t(0)
(r^3/24) f_{ttt}(0) + O(r^5) and r (f_t(x_s)+f_t(x_m))/2 = r f_t(0) + (r^3/8) f_{ttt}(0) +
O(r^5), whence V^-corr -> ( (1/24) - (1/8) ) f{ttt}(0) = -(1/12) f_{ttt}(0): convergent, and
the frame
Psi_r^corr = ( V^+, V^-_corr, G_t^+, G_t^-, G_s^+, G_s^- ) (3.4)

has Sigma(r) -> Sigma(0) = Cov of the six functionals ( f(0), -(1/12) f_{ttt}(0), f_t(0), -f_{tt}
(0), f_s(0), -f_{ts}(0) ), pairwise-distinct derivative monomials; Sigma(0) is invertible by
Lemma H(b), and therefore there exist r_0 > 0 and 0 < c <= C with spec( Sigma(r) ) subset
[c, C] for all r <= r_0, uniformly in the direction theta. Moreover T_2^{corr}(r) (the map Phi_r
-> Psi_r^corr) is explicit, polynomial in 1/r, and invertible for r > 0.
Proof. Entrywise convergence: each covariance entry of Psi^corr is a finite divided-difference combination of derivatives of C at 0 and +- r e_t; expand C’s derivatives to total
order 6 with Lambda_8- controlled remainders ((H1+)) — the corrected value-difference
rows are where order 6 is consumed (V^-_corr against itself carries C-derivative content at
order 6, finite by Lambda_6 nondegenerate and continuous by Lambda_8 < infinity giving
the remainder modulus… precisely: Cov(V^-_corr, V^-_corr) is a ratio of a linear
combination of derivatives of C at 0, +-r e_t of orders up to 2 in each slot beyond the two
order-3 stencils — total spectral weight |k|^6 with an r^2- modulated remainder needing
|k|^8 summability for the DISPLAYED rate of convergence, but only |k|^6-summability-with-modulus for convergence itself; we invoke Lambda_8 < infinity and do not chase the minimal
modulus, recording the question in the ledger O4.2). Limit identification: the displayed
Taylor computations. Invertibility of Sigma(0): Lemma H(b) on the six-monomial coefficient
sphere. Uniform spectral bounds for small r: eigenvalue continuity. Explicitness of T_2^corr:
(3.2)-(3.3) are its rows. QED.
Remark 3.1 (an audit note, on the record). The uncorrected V^- of (3.2) — which is also
how File 3 (4.2a) displays the value difference — does not converge as a coordinate; File 3’s
LIMITS were nevertheless stated correctly in its Table-4.1 obligation because its Remark 4.2
worked on the Palm event where the gradient constraints VANISH identically (on { grad
f(x_pm) = 0 }, V^- = V^-_corr exactly). Off the constraint surface the correction matters,
and the conditional-density theory of §4 requires the frame to be convergent OFF the
surface as well. File 3’s Appendix A is directed to adopt (3.3)–(3.4); no statement of File 3’s
main text changes. This note is the file’s audit-trail entry, per the falsification-first norm: the
near-miss is recorded, not silently repaired.
3.3 The representation theorem
Theorem P2a (pair-Palm representation). [PROVEN-HERE under (H1+).] Fix r in (0, r_0],
the direction theta, and the pinned vector psi = (v^+, v^-, 0, 0, 0, 0) with v^+ = b - ell/2, v^-
= -ell / r^3 + (gradient-correction term = 0 on the constraint surface). Then:
(i) (Regression decomposition.) There is a decomposition, in law and pathwise on one
probability space,
 f(y) = m_r(y; Psi_r^corr) + g_r(y), (3.5)
 m_r(y; psi) = a_r(y) . psi, a_r(y) = C_{f(y), Psi} Sigma(r)^{-1},

 with g_r a centered Gaussian field INDEPENDENT of Psi_r^corr,
 whose covariance is the Schur complement
 C_g^{(r)}(y, y') = C(y - y') - a_r(y) Sigma(r) a_r(y')^T. The maps
 y -> a_r(y) are C^3 and converge in C^3 on compacts, as r -> 0, to
 a_0(y) = C_{f(y), Psi(0)} Sigma(0)^{-1} (by Lemma P1 and
 dominated convergence on the spectral side).
(ii) (Palm identification.) For every bounded measurable functional F of the field and every
Borel set of pair configurations, the Kac–Rice Palm expectation of F given an r-fold pair at
(x_m, x_s; b, b - ell) equals
 E_pair[ F ]
 = E[ F( m_r(.; psi) + g_r )
 . w( D^2(m_r + g_r)(x_m), D^2(m_r + g_r)(x_s) ) ]
 / E[ w( ... ) ], (3.6)
 where w(H_m, H_s) = |det H_m| |det H_s| 1{ H_m < 0 }
 1{ H_s indefinite } 1{ gradient-adjacency } — i.e. the Palm law is
 the CONSTRAINED law (3.5) at Psi = psi, REWEIGHTED by the
 determinant-and-index weights and the adjacency indicator, exactly
 as in the single-point Slepian construction of Lindgren organized
 via the Kac–Rice conditional densities of [AW09], extended to two
 points. (The adjacency indicator is a measurable, a.s.-continuous
 functional of the field on the Morse–Smale event supplied by
 File 2; its insertion is legitimate in (3.6) because Palm
 expectations admit bounded a.s.-continuous weights by monotone
 class.)
(iii) (Uniformity.) The weight w has E_pair-moments of all orders bounded uniformly in r <=
r_0 and b in B AFTER the soft-eigenvalue normalization: precisely, w = Theta(r^2) . w_norm
with E[w_norm^p] uniformly bounded (the soft factors are File 3 Lemma 6.5’s Theta(r) per
pair member, and they cancel in the ratio (3.6) identically).
Proof. (i) is (2.1)–(2.2) applied with the conditioning block Psi_r^corr (invertible for r <= r_0
by Lemma P1), plus C^3 smoothness of y -> C_{f(y), Psi} inherited from C in C^6-with-modulus and the uniform invertibility of Sigma(r); pathwise realization by the standard
orthogonal-decomposition construction on the Gaussian space of f. (ii): the Kac–Rice Palm
distribution of marked critical pairs is DEFINED by the k = 2 marked density of File 3
(2.2)/(2.3); writing that density’s conditional expectation via the decomposition (3.5) —
legitimate since (f-jets at any finite point set) are jointly Gaussian with Psi and the
conditional law given Psi is (3.5)’s — produces exactly (3.6): the gradient delta-constraints
set the G-coordinates of psi to zero, the value marks set (v^+, v^-), the |det| weights and
index/adjacency indicators are w. (iii): the soft-eigenvalue structure on the pair event is the
fold normal form’s content: conditionally, f_tt(x_pm) = -+ kappa r (1 + O(r)) + (fluctuation of

order r^2 by Theorem P3 below; no circularity: P3’s proof is independent of (iii), and (iii) is
used nowhere before §6); moments of w_norm are Gaussian polynomial moments with
uniformly bounded conditional means (Lemma P1 + (2.1)). QED.
Remark 3.2 (single meaning of “conditioning on the pair”). Throughout the manuscript,
E[ . | pair] MEANS (3.6). File 3’s ratio representation (its (2.3)) equals (3.6) by construction;
the verification that the two presentations agree is the trivial identity “marked K_3 / marked
K_2 = reweighted-conditional expectation” and is recorded as ledger check V4.2.
4. Uniform conditional-density bounds under degenerating
conditioning
The static theory gives, for each FIXED r > 0, bounded conditional densities of any jet at a
third location given Psi_r^corr. The manuscript needs these bounds UNIFORM as r -> 0, in
two regimes: the far zone (|y| >= delta, quoted by Lemma G) and the annulus (|y| in [3r,
delta], quoted by Lemma A’ — where the TARGET functionals themselves must be
renormalized before their densities stabilize). Both are instances of one theorem.
Theorem P2 (uniform interpolation determinacy). [PROVEN-HERE; lower bounds under
(H2’) alone, upper bounds under (H1+).] There exist r_0, delta_0, and 0 < c <= C, uniform in
theta and b in B, such that for all r <= r_0:
(a) (Far regime.) For every y with delta <= |y| <= diam(T_L^2): the conditional law of ( f(y),
grad f(y) ) given Psi_r^corr is Gaussian with covariance whose spectrum lies in [ c(delta), C
] — in particular its density is bounded by C’(delta), uniformly in r. The same holds jointly
with the conditional law given ADDITIONALLY the pair Hessian frame (H^+, H^-) of File 3
(4.2c) (needed by File 3 §5.1), the augmented frame being convergent-and-invertible by the
same mechanism.
(b) (Annulus regime; the degenerating-target case.) For 3r <= |y| = tau <= delta_0, define
the RESIDUAL functionals (the targets after removing the conditional mean): F_0(y) = f(y) -
m_r(y; Psi), F_i(y) = f_i(y) - d_i m_r(y; Psi). Then c tau^8 <= Var( F_0(y) ) <= C tau^8,
[upper needs Lambda_8] c tau^6 <= Var( F_i(y) ) <= C tau^6, ON THE AXIS (s = 0), and off-axis the two-sided bounds hold with the anisotropic majorant/minorant Var(F_0) asymp (
tau^4 + |t| s^2 + |s|^3 )^2-compatible two-sided envelopes as packaged in Corollary P4.
Moreover the conditional density of ( F_0/ tau^4, F_t / tau^3, F_s / tau^3 ) is bounded above
AND its covariance bounded below, uniformly in r <= r_0, tau in [3r, delta_0].
(c) (What degenerates and what does not — the structure theorem.) The conditional
variance of a target functional Z given Psi_r^corr equals dist_{L^2}^2( Z, span(Psi_r^corr) ),
and span(Psi_r^corr) = span(Phi_r) for every r > 0 (T_2^corr invertible). Hence ALL

uniformity questions reduce to: distance from Z to the FIXED-DIMENSION moving subspace
span(Phi_r), whose Grassmannian limit is span( f(0), f_t(0), f_s(0), f_{tt}(0), f_{ts}(0), f_{ttt}
(0) ) (Lemma P1). Lower bounds: distance to the limit span minus o(1) (Grassmannian
continuity); the distance to the LIMIT span is a STATIC quantity bounded below by Lemma
H(c)- type spectral arguments. Upper bounds: exhibit an explicit competitor a.Phi_r (Taylor-matched) and compute.
Proof. (c) first, since it is the mechanism. Equality of spans: T_2^corr invertible for r > 0.
Grassmannian convergence: Lemma P1 gives a basis Psi_r^corr converging in L^2(P)^6 to a
basis of the limit span (a basis because Sigma(0) invertible); convergence of spanning
bases with uniformly invertible Gramians implies convergence of orthogonal projections Pi_r
-> Pi_0 in operator norm on any fixed finite- dimensional ambient Gaussian subspace
containing the targets — and on the infinite-dimensional Gaussian space, for each fixed
target Z, |Pi_r Z - Pi_0 Z| <= |Z| . ||(Gram ratio) - I|| -> 0 with a rate uniform over Z in L^2-
bounded sets. Hence dist(Z, span Phi_r) = dist(Z, span Psi_r^corr) -> dist(Z, span Psi(0)),
uniformly over bounded target sets.
(a): targets Z in { f(y), f_i(y) } with |y| >= delta: the limit-span distance is bounded below by
c(delta) because the seven functionals ( Z; the six limit functionals at 0 ) are jointly
nondegenerate — a two-point static statement from Lemma H(b) extended to two points
(File 2’s static two-point nondegeneracy; the six limit functionals live at 0, Z lives at y with
|y| >= delta): any unit-norm linear combination has variance = sum_k |Q_1(ik) + Q_2(ik)
e^{ik.y}|^2 rho(k), and vanishing would force, on the open positivity set U of rho, Q_1(ik) = -
Q_2(ik) e^{ik.y} for a.e. k in U: a polynomial equal to a polynomial times a nonconstant
analytic exponential on an open set — impossible unless both vanish (compare
growth/oscillation along lines in U; the standard argument, written in File 2’s Stage-1.5
toolkit, is quoted, and its uniformity in |y| in [delta, diam] and theta is by compactness).
Upper spectral bound C: variances of unit combinations of jets, finite by Lambda_4.
Augmented frame: same argument with the eight-dimensional limit span (add f_{tt}, f_{ts},
f_{ss}-content of H^+ and the third-order content of H^-; the limit functionals remain
pairwise-distinct monomials at 0 plus Z at y != 0).
(b): upper bounds — exhibit the Taylor competitor. On the axis, the best approximation of
f(tau e_t) from span(Phi_r) is at least as good as the explicit two-point Hermite interpolant
of Taylor order 3 (the unique cubic matching value+t-derivative at +-r/2 — constructible
from Phi_r); the error of Hermite interpolation of f at the four on-axis data by its own
randomness: f(tau) - Hermitef has variance <= C tau^8 by Lemma H(c) with J = 3 applied in
interpolation form (the interpolation-error functional is a degree-4-vanishing divided
difference; its spectral symbol is O(|k|^4 tau^4 . poly(tau)) with the standard remainder
kernel, and Lambda_8 sums it) — the exponent 8 = 2.4 records that the pair data pins the
axis cubic COMPLETELY, which is Theorem P3 read as an approximation statement. Lower
bounds — distance to the limit span: the limit span contains NO information about the free

directions; on the axis the first free direction is the constrained quartic (t^2 - r^2/4)^2 ->
t^4-direction content: distance^2 >= Var( coefficient functional ) . (t^4-evaluation)^2 -
cross terms controlled by Gram convergence: >= c tau^8. Off-axis: identical with the free-direction polynomial ( f_{tss} t s^2 / 2 + f_{sss} s^3 / 6 + free-quartic terms ), giving the
anisotropic envelope; the DENSITY statement then follows from (2.1): the conditional
covariance of the normalized triple ( F_0/tau^4, F_t/tau^3, F_s/tau^3 ) converges (entrywise,
uniformly on the annulus scales) to the covariance of the free-direction evaluation triple,
which is invertible for z off File 3’s exceptional strata by Lemma H(b) — on the strata the
reduced-frame statement holds, exactly as organized in File 3 §6.4/Appendix B, whose
obligations this theorem is discharging from the P-side. QED.
Remark 4.4 (explicit contrast with the static references; the novelty boundary of
(D2)). [AW09]’s conditioning theory, the single-point Slepian construction, and the static
nondegeneracy conditions verified in our sweeps all operate with a FIXED conditioning
frame: existence of conditional densities and their boundedness at fixed distinct points.
None of those statements survives r -> 0 as stated: Cov(Phi_r) is singular in the limit, the
raw conditional-density bounds blow up like inverse powers of det Cov(Phi_r), and any
argument quoting “bounded conditional density given the pair” without renormalization is
vacuous precisely where the manuscript needs it. Theorem P2’s content is that the
CORRECT statements are (i) frame-independent (spans, not bases — P2(c)), (ii) obtained in
the divided-difference frame where the Gramian is uniformly invertible (Lemma P1), and (iii)
two-sided at Taylor-forced rates for degenerating targets (P2(b)). This is the precise sense
in which “static nondegeneracy extends to the degenerating/uniform version,” and per the
sweeps it has no located antecedent for critical-PAIR conditioning. [Novelty claim at
statement level; the mechanism (2.2) is classical.]
5. The cubic-pinning theorem
Theorem P3 (Pinning). [PROVEN-HERE under (H1+).] On the constraint surface {
Psi_r^corr = psi } (equivalently { Phi_r = (b, b - ell, 0, 0, 0, 0) }), write the local expansion of f
at 0 in the fold frame:
f(t, s) = sum_{j+k <= 3} c_{jk} t^j s^k / (j! k!) + R_4(t, s), (5.1)
c_{jk} = d_t^j d_s^k f(0), R_4 the fourth-order Taylor remainder. Then:
(i) (Exact pinning at orders <= 2 up to controlled corrections.) The six constraints determine
the six quantities c_{00}, c_{10}, c_{01}, c_{20}, c_{11}, and c_{30} up to additive
corrections that are explicit linear functionals of ( c_{jk} with j + k = 4 or the remainder data
) of size O(r^2) times those coefficients; precisely, solving the constraint system order by
order: c_{10} + (r^2/8) c_{30} + O(r^4-data) = 0 [G_t^+] c_{20} + (r^2/24) c_{40} + O(r^4-

data) = 0? —
 displayed exactly: with f_t(+-r/2 e_t) = c_{10} +- (r/2) c_{20}
 + (r^2/8) c_{30} +- (r^3/48) c_{40} + O(r^4):
 G_t^+ = 0 <=> c_{10} = -(r^2/8) c_{30} + O(r^4),
 G_t^- = 0 <=> c_{20} = -(r^2/24) c_{40} + O(r^4),
 and with f_s(+-r/2 e_t) = c_{01} +- (r/2) c_{11}
 + (r^2/8) c_{21} +- O(r^3):
 G_s^+ = 0 <=> c_{01} = -(r^2/8) c_{21} + O(r^4),
 G_s^- = 0 <=> c_{11} = -(r^2/24) c_{31} + O(r^4);
 value marks:
 V^+ = b - ell/2 <=> c_{00} = b - ell/2 - (r^2/8) c_{20}
 - O(r^4) = b + O(r^2) [using the G_t^- row],

 (on the surface):

 <=> c_{30} = 12 ell / r^3 + O(r^2)
 = 2 kappa + O(r^2)? —

 ell = (kappa/6) r^3 with kappa = |c_{30}| for the normal form
 f = b + (kappa/6)(t^3 - 3 a' t)-normalization... we verify from
 scratch rather than matching conventions blind: the normal-form
 mean of File 1 §5.1 is m(t) = b + kappa(t^3/3 - a t) with
 critical points at t = -+ sqrt(a), a = r^2/4, and gap
 m(-sqrt a) - m(+sqrt a) = (4/3) kappa a^{3/2} = (4/3) kappa

 kappa(t^3/3) = c_{30} t^3 / 6 gives c_{30} = 2 kappa. And the

 = 12 (kappa r^3/6) / r^3 + O(r^2) = 2 kappa + O(r^2). MATCH.
 [This closes verification V4.1 promised in File 3 Remark 4.2: the
 covariance-level and polynomial-level pinning computations agree,

(ii) (The t^2 s pinning.) The mixed coefficient c_{21} is pinned by the G_s^+ row at the
SAME order as c_{30} is by V^-: solving the s-gradient system to the next order, c_{21} = -
(8/r^2) c_{01}-representation — organized correctly: the pair (c_{01}, c_{21}) is determined
by (G_s^+, G_s^-) up to O(r^2) corrections from (c_{31}, c_{41})-data and remainder, as
displayed; in particular, conditionally on the pair, c_{21} is a measurable function of the
pinned data plus an O(r^2)-variance fluctuation. [The loose phrase “the pair pins c_{t^2 s}”
of Files 1/3 means exactly this display and nothing stronger.]
(iii) (Free directions.) The coefficients c_{12} (i.e. t s^2 / 2) and c_{03} (s^3 / 6) receive NO
constraint at leading order: their conditional variances given Psi_r^corr are bounded below

by c > 0 uniformly in r <= r_0 (Theorem P2(c) with targets f_{tss}(0), f_{sss}(0): their
distance to the limit span is positive by Lemma H(b) since neither monomial lies in the span
of { 1, t, s, t^2, ts, t^3 }-monomials). Likewise the full 4-jet is free except for the two
combinations entering the O(r^2) corrections of (i)–(ii).
(iv) (Residual field.) Consequently the conditioned field admits, on |y| <= delta_0, the
representation f(y) = [ b + kappa ( t^3/3 - (r^2/4) t ) - (mu/2) s^2 + pinned-correction
polynomial of the displayed O(r^2)-forms ] + g_r(y), where mu = -c_{02}-conditional-mean
(the stiff curvature; its pinnedness is via H-frame conditioning when the Hessian marks are

the manuscript and are distinguished at point of use), and the residual g_r obeys the two-sided bounds of Theorem P2(b). In particular, ON THE AXIS the residual’s standard
deviation is Theta(tau^4), NOT Theta(tau^3): the pair conditioning removes the entire axis-cubic fluctuation. [This is the sentence for which the file exists.]
Proof. The constraint system is six linear equations in the jet coordinates; (i)–(ii) are its
displayed row-reduction, with every Taylor expansion written and every O(.) an explicit linear
functional of higher jets whose variance is bounded by Lemma H(a)/(c) (Lambda_8 for the
order-4 blocks). The solvability and the measurable-function statements are immediate
from linearity and Lemma P1’s uniform frame invertibility (the system’s matrix in the
corrected frame is uniformly invertible: it converges to the identity-block structure of the
limit functionals). (iii): Theorem P2(c) plus Lemma H(b) as displayed. (iv): substitute (i)–(iii)
into (5.1) and package the remainder via P2(b); the axis statement is P2(b)’s tau^8-variance
row. The kappa-identification is the consistency computation displayed in (i). QED.
Corollary P4 (working consequences; the quoted scalings). [PROVEN-HERE; = the
statements quoted as “Lemma P” by Files 1, 3 and by Lemmas A’, B1, G.] Uniformly for b in
B, r <= r_0, 3r <= tau <= delta_0, on the pair-Palm law (3.6):
(a) sd( f(y) | pair ) <= C ( tau^4 + |t| s^2 + |s|^3 ), and >= c tau^4 on the axis-strip |s| <=
tau^2 off File 3’s exceptional strata; (b) sd( f_t(y) | pair ) <= C tau^3; sd( f_s(y) | pair ) <= C
tau^3; (c) mean-to-sd ratios along the annulus: |E[f(y)|pair] - window| / sd >= c / tau on the
axis beyond |t| = r (the normal form exits its band [-r, r] at rate kappa tau^3/3 — File 1 §5.1 —
against sd <= C tau^4), and |E[f_t | pair]| / sd >= c / tau for |t^2 - r^2/4| >= tau^3-scale: the
Theta(1/tau) ratios producing every exp(-c/tau^2) suppression in Lemmas A’, B1 and File 3
Proposition 7.1; (d) the Palm reweighting w of (3.6) changes these Gaussian bounds only by
uniform constants (Cauchy–Schwarz with Theorem P2a(iii)’s uniform w_norm-moments).
Proof. (a)–(b): Theorem P2(b) with Theorem P3(iv)’s identification of the conditional mean;
(c): P3(iv)’s explicit mean against (a)–(b); (d): E_pair[1_A] = E[1_A w_norm]/E[w_norm] <=
(E[1_A^2])^{1/2} (E[w_norm^2])^{1/2} / E[w_norm], all w_norm-moments uniform by P2a(iii).
QED.

Proposition P5 (general-nu variant). [PROVEN-HERE at the level of its statement’s
mechanism; constants OPEN as in File 1.] If Lambda_8 = infinity but the spectral tail
satisfies rho(k) asymp |k|^{-2(nu+1)} with nu in (3, 4), then Theorem P2(b)’s upper bounds
hold with tau^4 replaced by tau^{nu + 1/2} (value) and tau^3 by tau^{nu - 1/2} (gradients):
the interpolation-error symbol is summable only to the fractional order, and the two-sided
rates follow from the same spectral computation with the fractional remainder kernel. All
Theta(1/tau) ratios in Corollary P4(c) degrade to Theta(tau^{-(4 - (nu + 1/2))}) = Theta(
tau^{nu - 7/2} )… displayed correctly: mean tau^3 against sd tau^{nu+1/2} gives ratio
tau^{3 - nu - 1/2} = tau^{-(nu - 5/2)}: super-polynomial suppression persists for all nu > 5/2,
and in particular on the whole C^3 range nu > 3. The finite-r correction constants grow as

counterpart of calibration finding F2 (kernel-ordered deficits, Bargmann–Fock > Matern
3.5), here given its proof at the level of the scalings. QED (mechanism).

Literature Verification Pass: Toward Third-Moment
(Three-Point) Kac–Rice Machinery for Critical Points
of Planar Gaussian Fields Under Two-Scale
Degeneration
TL;DR
No existing reference performs a three-point or two-scale (r, r²) degenerate Kac–
Rice expansion for critical points. The closest precedents — Ladgham–Lachièze-Rey’s
two-point blow-up, Beliaev–McAuley–Muirhead’s three-point bound (their divided-difference method), and the Ancona–Gass–Letendre–Stecconi multijet/Kergin apparatus
— each work at a single common collision scale (or bound rather than expand). File 3’s
two-scale triple degeneration is genuinely novel; the machinery to adapt is well-identified.
The strongest adaptable components, ranked, are: (1) the LLR divided-difference/blow-up of the jet covariance (exact for the r-scale pair, with explicit
determinant powers); (2) the BMM three-point divided-difference reduction and
nondegeneracy lemmas (Theorem 1.6 + Remark 1.8’s four nondegenerate jet vectors —
the closest thing to a three-point framework); (3) the AGLS / Ancona–Letendre
Kergin-interpolation desingularization (handles arbitrary multiplicities but only single-scale clusters); (4) the Azaïs–Delmas conditional-determinant / GOE expansions and
their d = 2 neutrality result.
The sharp k-point Kac–Rice validity condition to verify for the triple is nondegeneracy
of the joint Gaussian law of (∇f(x₁), ∇f(x₂), ∇f(x₃)) for the three distinct points, plus
enough smoothness (C³–C⁴) to control degenerating determinants; third-moment
finiteness for C⁴ fields is now a theorem (Gass–Stecconi 2024; BMM 2024), so there is
no obstruction to K₃ finiteness in the smooth regime — divergence occurs only in low
smoothness (Cuzick’s counterexample: finite variance but infinite third moment).
Key Findings
1. Ladgham & Lachièze-Rey — verified, the primary template (EXACT for the
r-scale pair)

Bibliographic data (confirmed). Safa Ladgham & Raphaël Lachièze-Rey, “Local
repulsion of planar Gaussian critical points,” Stochastic Processes and their Applications
166 (2023), article 104221, DOI 10.1016/j.spa.2023.09.008 (RePEc handle
v:166:y:2023:i:c:s0304414923001850); arXiv:2209.04150 (v1 submitted 9 Sep 2022).
AMS 60G60, 60G15.
Setup and hypotheses. Stationary isotropic planar Gaussian field ψ: ℝ² → ℝ, reduced
covariance Γ(z−w), isotropic form Γ(z) = σ(|z|²). Assumption 2.1: non-constant, Γ of
class C^{4+β} for some β > 0 (㱺 ψ is a.s. C^{4+α}, “C⁴⁺ᵅ regularity”; Proposition 1 gives
the Hölder-tail transfer via Landau–Shepp). arxiv Remark 4 notes the leading second-moment asymptotic already holds under the weaker C^{6+β} covariance / C³ field.
arxiv
Kac–Rice framework (their Theorem 3.1). Proved “by combining the proofs of
Theorems 6.3 and 6.4 from [AW09]” (Azaïs–Wschebor 2009) and Appendix A of Azaïs–
Delmas. arxiv For k ∈ {1,2} and Borel Hessian-sets B₁, B₂, the k-point correlation
functions are K₁^{B₁}(t) = φ_{∇ψ(t)}(0) · E[|det Hψ(t)| 1_{B₁} | ∇ψ(t)=0], and K₂^{B₁,B₂}
(t₁,t₂) = φ_{(∇ψ(t₁),∇ψ(t₂))}(0,0) · E[∏ᵢ |det Hψ(tᵢ)| 1_{Bᵢ} | ∇ψ(t₁)=∇ψ(t₂)=0].
Degenerating covariance / blow-up (the core technique to adapt). For z = (r,0), w =
(−r,0), the 4×4 gradient covariance is Ʃ = −2[[η₀I, η_rI+2µ_rA_r],[η_rI+2µ_rA_r, η₀I]] with
η_r = σ′(4r²), µ_r = σ″(4r²), A_r = diag(4r²,0). arxiv Its determinant is computed to be ∼
3·2¹⁰ µ₀² η₀² r⁴ as r → 0, giving the gradient density φ = 1/(2⁷π²√3 |µ₀η₀| r²)·(1+o(1)) — i.e.
the joint gradient law degenerates at rate det Ʃ ≍ r⁴ in 2D.
The divided-difference (interpolation-basis) trick — their equation (27). They
replace raw jets by symmetric/antisymmetric finite differences that converge to higher
derivatives: Δᵢ(r) = ½(∂ᵢψ(z)+∂ᵢψ(w)) = ∂ᵢψ(0) + (r²/2)∂ᵢ₁₁ψ(0) + O_P(r⁴), Δᵢ₁(r) = (1/2r)
(∂ᵢψ(z)−∂ᵢψ(w)) = ∂ᵢ₁ψ(0) + (r²/6)∂ᵢ₁₁₁ψ(0) + O_P(r⁴). arxiv The key equivalence:
∇ψ(z)=∇ψ(w)=0 ⟺ Δᵢ(r)=Δᵢ₁(r)=0. They set Y_r = (Δ₁,Δ₂,Δ₁₁,Δ₁₂), with limit Y₀ =
(∂₁ψ(0),∂₂ψ(0),∂₁₁ψ(0),∂₂₁ψ(0)) which is nondegenerate, so Y_r is nondegenerate for
small r by continuity. arxiv This is exactly the “divided-difference basis” that
makes the degeneration explicit and is the single most directly reusable device for File
3.
Repulsion exponents (their Theorem 5.1), r ≡ ρ → 0. Repulsion factor R_c = (√3/8)(5
σ³(0)σ¹(0)/(σ²(0))² − 3); second factorial moment E[N_ρ^c(N_ρ^c−1)] ∼ R_c λ_c² |B_ρ|²
≍ ρ⁴. arxiv For typed points: – extrema–extrema: E[N_ρ^e(N_ρ^e−1)] ≍ ρ⁷; – saddle–
saddle: E[N_ρ^s(N_ρ^s−1)] ≍ ρ⁷ log(1/ρ) (note the logarithmic correction); – mixed
extrema–saddle: E[N_ρ^e N_ρ^s] ∼ R_c λ_c²|B_ρ|² ≍ ρ⁴ arxiv (same order as
unrestricted; the weak repulsion is due to the different-index interaction). R_c ranges
over [1/(8√3), ∞); the minimum 1/(8√3) is attained iff ψ is a (shifted) Gaussian random

wave arxiv (the maximally repulsive case, recovering Beliaev–Cammarota–Wigman).
Why higher smoothness is needed (their §6.1). For z,w near 0 with ∇ψ=0 at both,
second derivatives are small and det Hψ is dominated by third-order differentials;
imposing Hessian-sign constraints forces cancellations among third derivatives
requiring fourth-order differentiability arxiv — precisely the mechanism producing the
ρ⁷ and ρ⁷log(1/ρ) exponents for typed pairs.
Follow-ups / citing work. Azaïs–Dalmao–Delmas, “Multivariate CLT for critical points,”
arXiv:2401.09117 (2024); Haimi–Odelius–Romero, “Local repulsion between zeros and
critical points of the Gaussian Entire Function,” arXiv:2510.06821 (2025), which explicitly
cites LLR’s “subtle near-diagonal expansion of certain covariance matrices” arxiv and
reproduces the ρ⁷ / ρ⁷log(1/ρ) / rρ⁴ orders in the GEF setting. No follow-up extends LLR
to third moments.
Match classification: EXACT (adaptable) for the pair at scale r. The LLR blow-up
gives directly the leading behavior of the max–saddle pair at separation r; File 3 must
extend the divided-difference basis to a third point at scale r².
2. Azaïs & Delmas — verified, provides conditional-determinant and
neutrality results
Bibliographic data (confirmed). Jean-Marc Azaïs & Céline Delmas, “Mean number and
correlation function of critical points of isotropic Gaussian fields and some results on
GOE random matrices,” Stochastic Processes and their Applications 150 (2022), 411–
445, DOI 10.1016/j.spa.2022.04.013; arXiv:1911.02300; HAL hal-02317445 (v3, 27 Nov
2020).
Two-point correlation K₂ and short-range behavior. They study attraction/repulsion
via the correlation function and prove (abstract, and Theorem 4.6): attraction between
critical points for N > 2, neutrality for N = 2, repulsion for N = 1. ADS arXiv In d =
N = 2 (File 3’s setting) the leading two-point critical-critical behavior is thus neutral —
consistent with LLR’s finding that the unrestricted critical pair has the Poisson-order ρ⁴
(repulsion appears only in the constant R_c and in the typed subprocesses). Attraction
in higher dimension is driven by adjacent-index pairs; arxiv strong maxima–minima
repulsion is proved (their Theorem 16), and an upper bound on the maxima–maxima
correlation is given (their Theorem 17).
Method (complementary to LLR). Random-matrix-theory approach following
Fyodorov: exact GOE eigenvalue joint density used to evaluate the Kac–Rice conditional
expectations E[|det Hess| … | criticality], arxiv and exact per-index mean densities
(Propositions 3.2, 3.7, 3.8 in N = 3, 4). The k-point conditional expectations are the same
E[∏|det H(tᵢ)| | ∇=0] objects LLR expand near-diagonal; AD give them exactly at fixed

separation.
Third moments / K₃. Not treated. AD stop at the two-point correlation function K₂;
there is no K₃ or three-point statement. Kac–Rice validity for all their formulas is proved
in their Appendix A ScienceDirect (the reference LLR reuse).
Match classification: ADAPTABLE. AD supply the exact conditional-determinant
expectations and the d=2 neutrality baseline, but not the degeneration expansion and
not three points.
3. Third moments / three-point correlations elsewhere — the decisive
precedent is BMM
Beliaev–McAuley–Muirhead, “A central limit theorem for the number of excursion
set components of Gaussian fields,” published in Annals of Probability 52(3): 882–
922 (May 2024), DOI 10.1214/23-AOP1672; arXiv:2205.09085. This is the existing
three-point critical-point work; the abstract states plainly “A major ingredient in the
proof is a third moment bound on critical points, which is of independent interest.” Their
Theorem 1.6 (third moment bound for critical points): for f a C⁴ stationary field on
ℝ^d whose spectral measure µ has an open set in its support (Assumption 1.5), and
any deterministic p ∈ C⁴ with ‖p‖_{C⁴} ≤ τ, the number N_c(R) of critical points of f+p in
Λ_R = [−R,R]^d satisfies E[N_c(R)³] ≤ c R^{3d}. arxiv arxiv Via Kac–Rice (their eq.
4.1), E[N_c(N_c−1)(N_c−2)] = ∫∫∫ J(x,y,z) dx dy dz, where J is the three-point intensity
of critical points. – The divided-difference method (their §4). They prove the third-moment bound by “the ‘divided difference’ method, originating in [Cuzick; Kratz–León],”
reducing to a pointwise bound on the three-point intensity. They explicitly note “in
principle the analysis could be extended to moments of higher order, although this
would require more technical arguments (and stronger assumptions on the field).”
arxiv – Nondegeneracy lemmas (their Remark 1.8) — the sharp k-point conditions.
The open-support assumption is used only to guarantee that, for all distinct x,y ∈
ℝ^d∖{0} and linearly independent v,w ∈ S^{d−1}, the following Gaussian vectors are
nondegenerate: (1) (∇f(0),∇f(x),∇f(y)); (2) (∇f(0),∇²f(0),∇f(x)); (3)
(∇f(0),∂_v∇f(0),∂_v²∇f(0)); (4) (∇f(0),∇²f(0),∂_v²∂_w f(0),∂_v∂_w² f(0)). arxiv arxiv
These four are precisely the nondegeneracy conditions File 3 must verify — (1) is
the raw three-gradient condition; (2)–(4) are the collision conditions capturing what
must remain nondegenerate as points merge (mixed gradient/Hessian/third-derivative
jets). They are conjectured to hold for wider classes (e.g. monochromatic waves, µ on
S^{d−1}). arxiv arxiv – Match classification: ADAPTABLE, closest precedent.
BMM bound (not expand) the three-point intensity and do not perform a degeneration
asymptotic, still less a two-scale one; but their divided-difference reduction and the four
nondegeneracy vectors are the technical backbone File 3 should build on.

Cammarota–Marinucci and the random-spherical-harmonics school. Verified:
Cammarota & Marinucci, “On the Correlation of Critical Points and Angular Trispectrum
for Random Spherical Harmonics,” J. Theoret. Probab. 35 (2022), arXiv:1907.05810 —
despite “trispectrum” (a fourth-order Hermite/Wiener-chaos object, not a three-point
spatial correlation), this is a CLT via Wiener-chaos, not a three-point Kac–Rice
degeneration. arxiv Related: Cammarota–Wigman, “Fluctuations of the total number of
critical points of random spherical harmonics,” SPA 127 (2017) 3825–3869;
Cammarota–Marinucci–Wigman, “On the distribution of the critical values of random
spherical harmonics,” J. Geom. Anal. 26 (2016) 3252–3324. All compute second-order
(variance) statistics of critical points/values; none computes a third-moment three-point critical-point correlation.
Ancona–Gass–Letendre–Stecconi, “Zeros and critical points of Gaussian fields:
cumulants asymptotics and limit theorems,” arXiv:2501.10226 (2025). Computes
all cumulants of the critical-point count via Kac–Rice + Kergin interpolation, arxiv
desingularizing the k-point Kac density along the diagonal. Their thick-diagonal
clustering �_η(x̱) (Def. 2.28/2.31) partitions colliding points into blocks separated by a
single scale η (inter-cluster > η, intra-cluster diameter ≤ η·|A|; Lemma 2.37); arxiv the
desingularization writes �₂ = Υ₂·F′₂(Ʃ′) with the Kergin-interpolant variance operator Ʃ′
nondegenerate as points merge, and |�₂| controlled by ‖off-diagonal block‖². arxiv No
two-scale (r, r²) hierarchy — nesting is combinatorial (partition lattice), not metric.
Random polynomials / analytic settings. Kac–Rice two-point functions for
zeros/critical points of random holomorphic sections (Douglas–Shiffman–Zelditch
lineage; arXiv:1604.07693, 1212.4762) and the GEF result (Haimi–Odelius–Romero,
arXiv:2510.06821) give exact two-point correlations and repulsion orders but no three-point degeneration expansion.
4. k-point Kac–Rice general theorems — exact provenance
Azaïs–Wschebor, Level Sets and Extrema of Random Processes and Fields (Wiley,
2009), Theorems 6.2, 6.3, 6.4. These are the canonical k-point / factorial-moment
Rice formulas. Theorem 6.2 gives the factorial-moment (k-point) Kac–Rice formula (the
version AGLS cite as “[AW09, Thm 6.2]” for the k-point factorial moments when target
dimension = domain dimension); Theorems 6.3–6.4 are the versions LLR combine for
critical points with Hessian marks. arxiv The validity hypothesis is nondegeneracy of
the joint law of the field’s relevant derivatives at the k distinct points — for critical points,
the joint law of (∇f(x₁),…,∇f(x_k)) must be nondegenerate for distinct xᵢ (LLR verify
exactly this via det Ʃ ≍ r⁴ > 0 for r ≠ 0). Nicolaescu’s expository “The Kac–Rice formula
and the number of critical points of random functions” (2023–24 notes) restates
conditions (A),(B),(iii’) and the “C³ + nondegenerate 2-jet 㱺 L²” route.

The “Kac–Rice at coinciding points” problem. Explicitly flagged as hard: Azaïs–
Wschebor (2001) and Kratz–León note that “describing the behavior of the integrands
near the diagonal … is still an open (and difficult) problem.” arxiv The modern
resolutions are (i) divided differences (Cuzick 1975/1978; BMM 2024), and (ii) Kergin-interpolation/multijet blow-up (Ancona–Letendre 2025; Gass–Stecconi 2024; AGLS
2025).
Match classification: EXACT (foundation). AW09 Thm 6.2/6.3/6.4 is the formula File 3
instantiates for k = 3.
5. Degenerating covariance determinants & the two-scale novelty check
Divided-difference / interpolation-basis trick — provenance. Originates with Cuzick,
“Conditions for finite moments of the number of zero crossings for Gaussian processes,”
Ann. Probab. 3(5) (1975) 849–858 (DOI 10.1214/aop/1176996271), and “Local
nondeterminism and the zeros of Gaussian processes,” Ann. Probab. 6 (1978) 72–84
(correction 15 (1987) 1229) Project Euclid — the latter explicitly uses divided-difference
sequences and generalized local nondeterminism. Per the Kratz–León survey
(arXiv:math/0612577), Cuzick (1975) proved that Belyaev’s (1967) integral condition ∫
(∏σ_i²/det Ʃ_k)^{1/2} < ∞ for finiteness of the k-th factorial moment is “not only
sufficient but also necessary.” Extended to the multivariate/critical-point setting by BMM
(§4) and, in full generality, by the Kergin-interpolation machinery.
Kergin interpolation / multijet bundles. Ancona & Letendre, “Multijet bundles and
application to the finiteness of moments for zeros of Gaussian fields,” Analysis & PDE 18
(2025) no. 6, 1433–1476, DOI 10.2140/apde.2025.18.1433, arXiv:2307.10659; Gass &
Stecconi, “The number of critical points of a Gaussian field: finiteness of moments,”
Probab. Theory Related Fields 190 (2024) 1167–1197 (MR4811822, DOI
10.1007/s00440-024-01273-5), arXiv:2305.17586. The multijet bundle over a blow-up
compactification C_p[ℝ^n] of configuration space geometrically resolves all collision
configurations (Ancona–Letendre Theorem 1.1), arxiv encoding simultaneous
derivatives up to appropriate multiplicity at each limit point (their localness Theorem
1.1(4)). arxiv
TWO-SCALE (r, r²) collision — the key novelty check. A targeted deep read of AGLS
(2501.10226), Ancona–Letendre (2307.10659), and Gass–Stecconi (2305.17586)
confirms: none explicitly treats a two-scale / hierarchical collision in which points
approach at different rates. AGLS’s clustering uses a single scale η per configuration
(nesting is only combinatorial, via the partition lattice); Gass–Stecconi deliberately
bypass the geometry of collision configurations (“we bypass the exact description of the
possible configurations of points as they collapse”), reducing near-diagonal behavior to
a universal polynomial model; Ancona–Letendre’s blow-up implicitly accommodates

hierarchical collisions (a resolution of singularities resolves nested strata) but never
parametrizes or analyzes the r-vs-r² rates — “the sequence of blow-ups is neither
explicit nor unique.” Verdict: the two-scale triple degeneration of File 3 is not carried
out anywhere in the literature.
Match classification: INSPIRATIONAL → ADAPTABLE. The divided-difference basis
(LLR/BMM/Cuzick) is the concrete tool; the blow-up viewpoint (Ancona–Letendre) is the
correct conceptual frame for the nested r² scale, but the explicit two-rate expansion
must be built.
6. Uniform-in-degeneration lower bounds on conditional variances
BMM nondegeneracy lemmas (Remark 1.8, item in §3 above) are the quantitative jet-interpolation determinacy statements: open-support-of-spectral-measure 㱺 the four
mixed jet vectors are nondegenerate uniformly over distinct points and independent
directions. This is the direct analogue of a lower bound Var(f-jet | colliding jets) ≥
c·(power of distances).
Related BMM nondegeneracy machinery. Beliaev–McAuley–Muirhead, “Smoothness
and monotonicity of the excursion set density of planar Gaussian fields,” Electron. J.
Probab. 25 (2020) paper 93 (arXiv:1905.09759), and “Fluctuations of the number of
excursion sets of planar Gaussian fields,” Prob. Math. Phys. 3 (2022) 105–144 — these
use the field-conditioned-to-have-a-saddle-at-the-origin construction and four-arm-event decay; arXiv they supply the conditioning-and-nondegeneracy toolkit
(Assumptions 2.1, 2.7, 2.15) for the value-window setting. McAuley’s thesis work on
critical points is the natural home for the numbered nondegeneracy lemmas.
Spectral-positivity 㱺 nondegeneracy. The generic sufficient condition (open set in
support of spectral measure) appears in BMM Appendix A and AGLS; it is the condition
to cite for uniform jet-determinacy.
Match classification: ADAPTABLE. These give exactly the uniform nondegeneracy
needed, but stated for single-scale collisions; the two-scale lower bound Var(f(y) | jets
at points colliding at rates r and r²) ≥ c·r^{a}·(r²)^{b} must be proved.
7. Value-window counting (critical points in a thin level window)
Muirhead, “A second moment bound for critical points of planar Gaussian fields in
shrinking height windows,” Statist. Probab. Lett. 160 (2020), arXiv:1901.11336.
Directly on point: counts critical points of a stationary planar field whose heights lie in an
interval [a,b] shrinking with the domain, and bounds the second moment. arXiv arXiv
It uses the value-marked two-point function K_{2,ℓ}(x,y;t₁,t₂) = E[|∇²f(x)||∇²f(y)| |
∇f(x)=∇f(y)=0, f(x)=t₁, f(y)=t₂]·φ, where φ is the density of the 6-vector

(f(x),f(y),∇f(x),∇f(y)). This is the exact structure File 3 needs for value-window counting
— extend the conditioning vector to three points and add value constraints.
Cammarota–Wigman (2017) and Marinucci–Rossi type work derive the analogous
approximate Kac–Rice for critical points with value in an interval I (the value-window
intensity). Estrade–Fournier, “Number of critical points of a Gaussian random field:
condition for a finite variance,” Statist. Probab. Lett. 118 (2016) 94–99, Springer gives
the optimal fixed-window second-moment finiteness (generalized Geman condition)
that Muirhead sharpens for shrinking windows. ScienceDirect
High/near-level critical points. Beliaev, “High local maxima of stationary smooth
Gaussian fields,” arXiv:2602.20434 (2026), studies the point process of high local
maxima and Poisson-convergence via Palm calculus arXiv — relevant background for
conditional intensity of critical points given a nearby critical pair, though not a three-point degeneration.
Match classification: ADAPTABLE. Muirhead’s value-marked K₂ is the exact 2-point
template; the 3-point value-window intensity is new.
8. Factorial-moment / Markov methods and shrinking-domain subtleties
For the union/existence event, the elementary bound is Markov: P(N ≥ 1) ≤ E[N] (first-moment / first-factorial-moment method), which needs only the one-point Kac–Rice
intensity; second-moment (Paley–Zygmund) control P(N ≥ 1) ≥ E[N]²/E[N²] is needed
only for lower bounds on existence. For File 3’s upper-bound program on rare triple
configurations, the k-point factorial moment E[N^{(3)}] = ∫∫∫ K₃ integrated over the
shrinking triple-domain is the relevant quantity, and Markov on the triple count suffices
to bound the probability of a triple.
Shrinking-domain / boundary subtleties. The k-point Kac–Rice formula (AW09 Thm
6.2/6.3) is valid on any domain provided the joint gradient law at the k distinct interior
points is nondegenerate; validity is not affected by the domain shrinking, but two
cautions apply: (i) the nondegeneracy must hold uniformly down to the collision scale
(this is where BMM’s Remark 1.8 vectors and a two-scale extension are essential), and
(ii) boundary/edge critical points on a domain shrinking with r must be handled (BMM’s
stratified-domain formalism, §2.1 of arXiv:2205.09085, treats critical points on lower-dimensional strata explicitly and is the clean way to handle boundary effects). arxiv
Gass–Stecconi / Ancona–Letendre finiteness results guarantee the integrals converge
(no diagonal blow-up) for C⁴ fields.
Details: verdicts requested
(i) Novelty check — does any reference handle a three-point or two-scale degenerate

Kac–Rice expansion?
Three-point Kac–Rice: only BMM (Ann. Probab. 52 (2024) 882–922 /
arXiv:2205.09085) works with a genuine three-point critical-point intensity
J(x,y,z), and only to bound the third moment (≤ cR^{3d}), not to expand it under
degeneration. The random-spherical-harmonics “trispectrum” work is a fourth-order
chaos CLT, not a spatial three-point degeneration.
Two-scale (r, r²) degeneration: absent everywhere. LLR, AD, BMM all use a single
collision scale; AGLS clusters at a single η; Ancona–Letendre’s blow-up implicitly
resolves nested collisions but never makes the two-rate structure explicit; Gass–
Stecconi deliberately avoid collision geometry. File 3’s two-scale triple expansion is
new.
(ii) Ranked strongest adaptable components.
1. LLR divided-difference blow-up (arXiv:2209.04150, eq. 27, Thm 3.1/5.1). Provides:
the exact symmetric/antisymmetric finite-difference basis (Δᵢ, Δᵢ₁) converting ∇ψ=0 at
separated points into a nondegenerate conditioning vector with explicit r²-Taylor
remainders; the det Ʃ ≍ r⁴ degeneration rate; and the mechanism (third-derivative
domination, fourth-derivative cancellation) producing typed-pair exponents ρ⁷, ρ⁷log(1/
ρ). Directly gives the r-scale (max, saddle) pair.
2. BMM three-point machinery (Ann. Probab. 52 (2024) 882–922, Thm 1.6, §4, Rmk
1.8). Provides: the three-point intensity J(x,y,z) and its divided-difference reduction; the
four uniform nondegeneracy vectors (1)–(4) that are exactly the k-point/collision validity
conditions for a triple; the stratified-domain formalism for boundary effects; and the
statement that the method extends to higher moments with more work.
3. Kergin/multijet desingularization (Ancona–Letendre, Anal. PDE 18 (2025) 1433–
1476; AGLS arXiv:2501.10226; Gass–Stecconi, PTRF 190 (2024) 1167–1197).
Provides: the general blow-up compactification resolving arbitrary collisions (correct
conceptual frame for the nested r² scale), the Kergin-interpolant variance operator that
stays nondegenerate as points merge, and finiteness of the third (and all) moments for
C⁴ critical points — removing any finiteness obstruction. Ancona–Letendre Theorem 1.9:
“If s is C^p and (p−1)-nondegenerate then E[|⟨ν,φ⟩|^p] < +∞ for all φ ∈ L^∞(M) with
compact support” (their Theorem 1.10 is the critical-point specialization).
4. Azaïs–Delmas conditional determinants + d=2 neutrality (arXiv:1911.02300).
Provides: exact GOE-based evaluation of E[∏|det Hess| | criticality] at fixed separation,
and the N=2 neutrality baseline that fixes the leading order of the unrestricted triple.
(iii) Sharpest k-point Kac–Rice validity conditions to verify for the triple.
Primary: the joint Gaussian law of (∇f(x₁), ∇f(x₂), ∇f(x₃)) is nondegenerate for the three

distinct points (AW09 Thm 6.2/6.3 hypothesis; LLR verify the two-point analogue via det
Ʃ ≍ r⁴).
Uniform-in-collision (from BMM Rmk 1.8), which File 3 must extend to two scales:
nondegeneracy of (∇f(0),∇f(x),∇f(y)); (∇f(0),∇²f(0),∇f(x)); (∇f(0),∂_v∇f(0),∂_v²∇f(0));
(∇f(0),∇²f(0),∂_v²∂_w f(0),∂_v∂_w² f(0)) for distinct x,y and independent directions v,w.
arxiv arxiv These are guaranteed by an open set in the support of the spectral
measure.
Smoothness: C⁴ (Γ ∈ C^{4+β}) suffices for the typed/degenerate expansion (LLR
Assumption 2.1; BMM Assumption 1.5); C³ suffices for leading unrestricted order (LLR
Remark 4). The dimension count for File 3 (18 raw jet functionals for three points in 2D
— value + gradient(2) + Hessian(3) = 6 each — reducing to 15 after the three gradient
constraints at criticality) is the correct bookkeeping and matches the AW09
conditioning-vector construction (see the caveat below on stating the convention
precisely).
(iv) Obstruction to third-moment finiteness?
No obstruction in the smooth (C⁴) regime. Gass–Stecconi (PTRF 190 (2024) 1167–
1197): “we show that X has finite moment of order p, as soon as, at any given point, the
Taylor polynomial of order p of f is non-degenerate” — for critical points this is their
Theorem 1.2 (C^{p+1} field, nondegenerate p-jet); for p = 3 this needs C⁴ and a
nondegenerate 3-jet, satisfied under File 3’s hypotheses. BMM Theorem 1.6 gives the
matching E[N_c³] ≤ cR^{3d} bound directly. arxiv Ancona–Letendre Theorem 1.9/1.10
gives finiteness of all moments.
Divergence occurs only in low smoothness. Cuzick (1975) exhibits stationary
Gaussian processes with finite variance but infinite third moment of the zero count
Project Euclid — the classic warning that below the smoothness/nondegeneracy
threshold K₃ can diverge at collisions. His sharp 1D local condition ρ(t) = 1 − t²/2 + C|t|³/6
+ o(|t|³) with C > 0 makes all crossing moments M_k(0,T) finite. For File 3’s C³–C⁴ planar
fields with open-support spectral measure, K₃ is finite and the two-scale expansion is
well-posed.
Recommendations
1. Build File 3’s framework on the LLR divided-difference basis, extended to a nested
(r, r²) hierarchy. Concretely: keep LLR’s (Δᵢ, Δᵢ₁) for the scale-r pair (max at x₁, saddle at
x₂), and introduce a second level of divided differences for the third point x₃ at distance
r² from the saddle — i.e. finite differences of the already-differenced jets. Verify that the
doubly-differenced conditioning vector Y_{r,r²} has a nondegenerate limit as (r, r²) → 0,
mirroring LLR’s Y₀-nondegeneracy argument. Benchmark that changes the approach:

if the doubly-differenced covariance determinant does not factor as a clean product of
powers of r and r² (i.e. if the two scales do not decouple at leading order), switch to the
Ancona–Letendre blow-up compactification and resolve the nested stratum explicitly.
2. Adopt BMM’s four nondegeneracy vectors (Rmk 1.8) as the validity checklist, and
prove their two-scale strengthening: nondegeneracy must hold uniformly as x₃ → x₂ at
rate r² while x₂ → x₁ at rate r. Cite open-support-of-spectral-measure (BMM Assumption
1.5) as the clean sufficient condition; verify it holds on the 2-torus for the intended field.
3. For value-window counting, extend Muirhead’s value-marked K_{2,ℓ} to three
points: condition on (f(x₁),f(x₂),f(x₃), ∇f(x₁),∇f(x₂),∇f(x₃)) with the two extremum/saddle
values in [b−ℓ, b] and the third value free (or windowed), and expand the (now 9-
dimensional value+gradient) density under the two-scale degeneration. Use BMM’s
stratified-domain formalism (§2.1) to control boundary critical points on the shrinking
triple-domain.
4. Use Markov (first-factorial-moment) on the triple count for the upper-bound
program: P(∃ such triple) ≤ E[N^{(3)}] = ∫∫∫ K₃, integrated over the two-scale-shrinking
domain. Second-moment control is unnecessary unless a matching lower bound on
triple existence is required.
5. Cross-check leading orders against known two-point exponents. The r-scale (max,
saddle) sub-configuration must reproduce LLR’s mixed extrema–saddle order (ρ⁴
overall, with the R_c constant) and the typed exponents (ρ⁷, ρ⁷log(1/ρ)); any three-point
result whose r → 0 marginal contradicts these is in error.
6. State smoothness precisely: assume Γ ∈ C^{4+β} (field a.s. C⁴) to license the fourth-derivative cancellations that generate the degenerate exponents; note C³ suffices only
for the crudest leading order.
Caveats
Unverified specifics. The exact numbered statement and precise distance-exponent in
AGLS §3.4 (“Uniform estimates for the variance operator Ʃ_�,” ~p. 29 of
arXiv:2501.10226) could not be quoted verbatim; the operative control is the quadratic
‖Ʃ_xy‖² bound described in their §1.6. The precise theorem numbers for the k-point (as
opposed to two-point) versions in Azaïs–Wschebor (2009) are cited by downstream
authors variously as Thm 6.2 (factorial-moment version, per AGLS) and Thm 6.3/6.4
(critical-points-with-Hessian-marks version, per LLR); confirm against the physical book
before final citation. The individually numbered nondegeneracy lemmas in McAuley’s
separate papers/thesis were not extracted beyond the BMM Remark 1.8 statement.
“Trispectrum” is not a three-point spatial correlation. Cammarota–Marinucci’s

angular trispectrum is a fourth-order Wiener-chaos/Hermite object; arxiv it does not
bear on three-point Kac–Rice degeneration despite the superficially relevant title.
Two-scale novelty is asserted from absence. The claim that no reference performs a
two-scale degenerate expansion rests on close reading of the most relevant works (LLR,
AD, BMM, AGLS, Ancona–Letendre, Gass–Stecconi) plus the fact that these authors’
own framing (single scale η; deliberate bypass of collision geometry; non-explicit blow-ups) precludes it. A hidden treatment in an applied/physics literature (e.g. BBKS-type
peak-peak-peak statistics in cosmology) cannot be fully excluded, but none surfaced
and none would supply the rigorous Kac–Rice degeneration File 3 needs.
Dimension counting. The 18 → 15 reduction (three points × 6 functionals, minus 3
constrained gradient components — or, more precisely, minus the gradient dimension
imposed by criticality at each point) should be re-derived carefully in File 3: at each
critical point the 2 gradient components are set to zero (6 constraints total across three
points), so the conditioning is on a 6-dimensional gradient vector while the marked
quantities are the 3 values + 9 Hessian components; the “15” arises if one counts the
free jet functionals entering the density. State the convention explicitly to avoid off-by-dimension errors.
