File 1 — Architectural Overview and Core Theorems
The Elder-Rule Selection Constant and the Near-Diagonal Law
for H0 Persistence of Smooth Gaussian Fields on the Two-Torus
Program artifact class: Manuscript, flagship file (nomenclature-setting). Epistemic status
header (binding on all files): every numbered statement in this manuscript carries exactly
one of the labels [PROVEN-HERE], [PROVEN-MODULO: <named lemmas>], [OPEN],
[CONJECTURE], [RETRACTED-SUPERSEDED]. A statement’s label is part of the statement.
The kill registry (Section 9) travels with the manuscript. Calibration archive: cycles C001–
C005 plus the C005R re-adjudication, with hashed prediction snapshots and observed
updates; hash chain referenced in Section 8.4.
0. Notation and global conventions
Fixed throughout the entire manuscript sequence; subsequent files inherit this section
verbatim.
T_L^2 = R^2 / (L Z)^2, the flat two-torus of side L >= 1, with L FIXED. Points x = (x_1,
x_2); d(x, y) the quotient (flat) metric; Lebesgue measure dx with |T_L^2| = L^2.
f : T_L^2 -> R, a centered Gaussian random field, law P, expectation E. Covariance C(x) =
E[f(y) f(y + x)] (stationarity), C(0) = 1 (unit variance). We do NOT assume isotropy: C(x)
need not depend on |x| alone. See Scope Remark 3.4.
Spectral measure rho on the dual lattice (2 pi / L) Z^2, with C(x) = sum_k rho(k)
e^{i<k,x>}. “Spectral density positive on an open set” refers to the continuum
idealization; the operative torus form is the finite-jet nondegeneracy it implies,
hypothesis (H2’) below.
Spectral moment tensors: Lambda_2 = Cov(grad f) (2x2); Lambda_4, Lambda_6,
Lambda_8 the covariance tensors of the second-, third-, and fourth- derivative
Gaussian vectors at a point. Nondegeneracy of Lambda_{2j} means the full order-j
derivative vector has nondegenerate covariance.
Derivatives: grad f = (f_1, f_2); D^2 f the Hessian with entries f_{ij}; D^3 f the symmetric

third-derivative tensor; for a unit vector v, f_{vvv} = D^3 f[v, v, v].
Crit(f) = { x : grad f(x) = 0 }. Under (H1+)-(H2’), f is a.s. Morse with pairwise distinct
critical values (File 2). Index 0 = local minimum, 1 = saddle, 2 = local maximum.
Superlevel sets: E_t = { x : f(x) >= t }, filtration DESCENDING in t. H0(E_t) = components;
all H0 statements are coefficient-independent.
Elder rule. As t decreases, a component is born at t = f(m) for each local maximum m;
components merge at index-1 critical values. At a merge, the component with the
SMALLER birth value (the younger) dies; its H0 bar is [f(s), f(m)] where s is the merging
saddle. D(m) denotes the death saddle of m; on the torus exactly one component per
realization is essential. Lifetime: ell(m) = f(m) - f(D(m)). dgm(f) = { (f(m), f(D(m))) : m
non-essential local maximum }.
Fold pairs. (m, s) with m a local maximum, s an index-1 saddle, is an r-FOLD PAIR at
height b when d(m, s) = r, f(m) = b, f(s) = b - ell, ell > 0, and s is GRADIENT-ADJACENT
to m: one ascending separatrix of s (maximal integral curve of grad f emanating from s)
terminates at m. The fold normal form (Section 5.1) locks gap to separation: ell = (kappa
/ 6) r^3 (1 + o(1)), r -> 0, (0.1) kappa = |f_{vvv}(x_0)| along the soft direction at the
midpoint x_0 = (m + s)/2. (0.1) is elementary singularity theory, [PROVEN-HERE] (fold-coordinates file); it is link L1 of the program and is verified in-distribution (log-log slope
3.01 in the session-1 archive; 2.883 [2.388, 3.347] under the C005 protocol).
Selection probability. For r > 0 small and b in a compact B, with respect to the Palm
distribution of r-fold pairs at height b (Kac-Rice Palm formalism for critical pairs, File 5
series): q(r, b) = P( D(m) = s | (m, s) an r-fold pair at height b ). (0.2)
Near-diagonal bar density. N(ell_1, ell_2; B) = expected number of H0 bars with lifetime
in [ell_1, ell_2] and birth in B; nu(ell) is the expected bar count density per unit lifetime
as ell -> 0 (birth marginalized over compact B), when it exists.
Asymptotics: a ~ b means a/b -> 1; O, o, Theta standard; constants C, c > 0 may change
line to line and are uniform in b on compacts and in r <= r_0 unless stated otherwise.
u-variable (dimensionless separation, for contact with the calibration archive): u = r
sqrt(lambda_4 / lambda_2) with scalar isotropic moments; in the anisotropic setting the
microscale normalization is direction- dependent and appears only in numerical scope
remarks.
1. Hypotheses
(H1+) f is a centered stationary Gaussian field on T_L^2 with unit variance and C^3 sample

paths; Lambda_2, Lambda_4, Lambda_6 are nondegenerate; and Lambda_8 is finite (sum_k
|k|^8 rho(k) < infinity).
Role of Lambda_8 < infinity: used ONLY for the sharp tau^4 residual scaling in the annulus
estimate (Lemma A’) and hence for the sharp remainder rate in (2.2). If Lambda_8 = infinity
but the field has effective spectral smoothness nu in (3, 4) (spectral tail |k|^{-2(nu+1)}), the
pinned residual scales as tau^{nu + 1/2}, all suppression factors remain super-polynomial,
and Theorems A and B survive with degraded, nu-dependent correction constants. That
degradation is the theoretical counterpart of the kernel-ordered finite-u deficits measured
in calibration cycle C005 (finding F2): mechanism [PROVEN-MODULO: Lemma P general-nu
variant]; the constants themselves [OPEN].
(H2’) The spectral measure has, in the continuum idealization, a density positive on an
open set; operatively we assume the finite-jet nondegeneracy consequence: for every finite
family of derivative functionals { D^{alpha_i} f(y_i) }, |alpha_i| <= 4, at finitely many distinct
points, the joint Gaussian law is nondegenerate, with two-sided quantitative rates at
collision governed by Taylor order (Lemma H, quantitative jet nondegeneracy, [PROVEN-HERE] in File 2 via polynomial determinacy: Var(linear functional minus regression) =
integral |Q(k)|^2 d rho(k) > 0 for nonzero polynomials Q).
Remark 1.1 (economy of hypotheses). Earlier drafts carried a separate hypothesis (H3)
(sixth-order regression nondegeneracy). (H3) is REDUNDANT given (H2’) via Lemma H; it is
demoted to a lemma. The hypothesis set of the entire manuscript is (H1+) and (H2’) only.
[PROVEN-HERE, File 2.]
Remark 1.2 (what is NOT assumed). No isotropy. No covariance positivity (no FKG input;
percolation machinery is unused at fixed L, Section 7.1). No sign or threshold condition on
the height b beyond compactness of its range. The b-uniformity of Theorem A —
contradicting the b-threshold refinement proposed in the program’s ancestral document —
was predicted by the present architecture and confirmed across cycles C001-C005 (q flat in
b across quartiles; pre-registered rule 3 null).
2. The main theorems
Theorem A (elder-rule selection constant; q0 = 1). [PROVEN-MODULO: Lemma P
(Pinning), Lemma I (inner two-scale blow-up nondegeneracy), Sublemma R0 (Morse-Smale
genericity). All remaining ingredients — Reduction Lemma R with Sublemmas R1-R3, far-field Lemma G, annulus Lemma A’, band Lemmas B0-B1 — are proven in this manuscript
sequence, G and A’ carrying finite-dimensional Gaussian-regression obligations executed in
their own files.]

Let f satisfy (H1+) and (H2’) on T_L^2, L fixed, and let B subset R be compact. With q(r, b)
as in (0.2):
 lim_{r -> 0} q(r, b) = 1, uniformly for b in B. (2.1)
The proof yields the quantitative remainder
 1 - q(r, b) <= C(L, B) [ r^3 + r^beta ] + C exp(-c / r^2), (2.2)
where beta > 0 is the exponent of Lemma I (candidate value beta = 4, [CONJECTURE] at the
level of the exact exponent; any beta > 0 suffices for (2.1); beta >= 3 preserves the r^3
remainder). The matching lower bound 1 - q >= c r^3 is [OPEN] (Section 7.2).
Interpretation. The geometric fold partner of a maximum is, asymptotically almost surely,
its homological death partner: geometry determines homology at the diagonal, with
selection constant exactly one. No height threshold, covariance sign condition, or isotropy
enters.
Theorem B (near-diagonal H0 bar-density law). [PROVEN-MODULO: Theorem A’s lemma
set, plus Proposition B2 (pair-intensity nondegeneration, the program’s link L2).]
Under (H1+)-(H2’) on T_L^2, the expected H0 persistence diagram of the superlevel
filtration satisfies
 nu(ell) = C_* ell^{-1/3} (1 + o(1)), ell -> 0, (2.3)
with
 C_* = (1/3) integral_B h(b) J(b) db in (0, infinity), (2.4)
where h is the height density of the participating maxima and J(b) packages the fold-pair
intensity: writing rho_pair(r; b) for the Palm intensity of r-fold pairs at height b, Proposition
B2 asserts rho_pair(r; b) -> rho_0(b) in (0, infinity) as r -> 0 (neutrality at contact of the
adjacent-index channel in dimension 2); the change of variables ell = (kappa/6) r^3 (so that
r dr is proportional to ell^{-1/3} d ell) then yields (2.3)-(2.4) with the kappa-law folded into
J(b). The selection factor in (2.3) is EXACTLY 1 by Theorem A: no selection constant
appears in C_*.
Proposition B2’s two-point input is verified literature: Azais & Delmas, Stochastic Process.
Appl. 150 (2022) 411-445 (attraction for N > 2, NEUTRALITY for N = 2, repulsion for N = 1),
corroborated by Beliaev, Cammarota & Wigman, Electron. Commun. Probab. 25 (2020),
paper 82. The uniform-in-r conditional version required here (convergence of the fold-pair

Palm intensity, not merely the two-point limit) is [PROVEN-MODULO: the L2 degeneration
computation, executed in its own file; its Bargmann-Fock instance is a finite symbolic
computation].
Remark 2.1 (empirical status). In the calibration archive: q measured at 1.000 [0.957,
1.000] in the smallest resolvable separation bin, monotone in r, b-uniform, covariance-sign-indifferent, and dimension-free at matched microscale for u < 1.7 (cluster-robust, Holm-corrected, re-adjudication C005R); the r^3 lock (0.1) verified in-distribution. These are
Reported trend measurements at r/xi >= 0.3. The r -> 0 statements (2.1) and (2.3) are
strictly the theorems’ content, not the measurements’.
3. Novelty statement and prior art
[All citations below were located and setting-classified in the program’s primary-source
verification sweep; zero-tolerance provenance applies.]
3.1 The headline claims are, to the best of a systematic search, new. No published or
preprint result was located that proves a persistence- pairing SELECTION law — identifying
WHICH saddle is the elder-rule death partner of a given maximum, with probability — for
random fields in dimension >= 2. Both claims,
(i) q0 = 1: the geometric fold partner is asymptotically a.s. the homological death partner
(Theorem A), and (ii) the ell^{-1/3} near-diagonal law with unit selection factor (Theorem B),
have no located antecedent for smooth fields in dimension two or higher.
3.2 The 1D contrast (sharpening, not eroding, the novelty). Exact pairing laws DO exist
in one dimension:
Rychlik, I., “A new definition of the rainflow cycle counting method,” Int. J. Fatigue 9
(1987) 119-121: the exact min-max (rainflow) pairing law for 1D processes. Setting: 1D,
exact, non-asymptotic. Classification: morally related; non-overlapping.
Baryshnikov, Y., “Brownian motions, persistent homology and chirality,” J. Appl. Comput.
Topology 9(4), Article 28, 2025; DOI: 10.1007/s41468-025-00224-w (preprint
arXiv:1909.09846): elder-rule persistence laws for Brownian motion. Setting: 1D,
Brownian (non-smooth) regularity. Classification: adjacent — the same homological
pairing object, one dimension down, where the death partner is combinatorially forced
by the total order of the path.
In dimension two the merge structure is mediated by saddle geometry and nothing is
combinatorially forced; the content of Theorem A is precisely that fold geometry forces the
homology asymptotically. This dimensional dichotomy — exact 1D laws versus a newly

proven 2D asymptotic selection law — is the core of the novelty claim.
3.3 What adjacent literature supplies, and what it does not.
Critical-pair correlations at collision: Azais & Delmas (SPA 150, 2022; neutrality in d = 2)
and Ladgham & Lachieze-Rey (SPA 166 (2023) 104221; arXiv:2209.04150; same-index
hard repulsion, minimal repulsion factor 1/(8 sqrt 3)) furnish the two-point inputs used in
Proposition B2 and in Lemma I’s zone analysis. NO located work performs the THREE-point Kac-Rice expansion under two-scale degeneration (pair separation ~ r, third point
at ~ r^2) that Lemma I requires: per the sweep this is a genuine literature gap and the
program’s central open technical object (Section 5.3).
Small bars and universality: the Bobrowski-Skraba universality line (arXiv:2406.05553)
concerns geometric filtrations over point processes, not superlevel filtrations of smooth
fields: morally related only. Persistence-measure frameworks (Chazal-Divol line) provide
the measure-theoretic frame for nu(ell), not a law.
Morse-Smale genericity (our Sublemma R0): an explicit almost-sure no-saddle-connection statement for stationary Gaussian fields was NOT located in the required
form (folklore-gap flag from the sweep). R0 is therefore proven here rather than cited;
the risk is bibliographic, not mathematical.
Palm/Slepian conditioning at critical points: single-point Slepian models are classical
(Lindgren; Azais & Wschebor, Level Sets and Extrema of Random Processes and Fields,
Wiley, 2009). The critical- PAIR version with degenerating-constraint uniformity — and
the observation that pair conditioning PINS the on-axis cubic coefficient (Lemma P) —
was not located anywhere and is claimed as new. Lemma P is simultaneously the
program’s most consequential and most elementary novel ingredient.
3.4 Scope Remark (isotropy and the calibration archive). Theorems A and B are stated
and proved in anisotropic-capable form: hypotheses (H1+) and (H2’) only; the fold chart,
Pinning Lemma, and window machinery are direction-covariant and never invoke isotropy.
However, EVERY numerical artifact in the calibration archive (C001-C005, C005R:
Bargmann-Fock in d = 2, 3; Matern nu = 3.5, 2.5) is isotropic. The anisotropic sector is
analytically CLOSED modulo the same Phase-2 positivity computation as the isotropic
sector (Proposition A6, File 6: the theta-uniform order-one contact limit is proven from
(H1+)-(H2’) alone, with positivity reduced to the identical finite-dimensional check, now
theta-parametrized with a continuity reduction) — but remains numerically untested; an
anisotropic calibration arm is queued (Section 8.3). Inherited stress-table expectation,
consistent with the present proof and now with Prop. A6(iv): anisotropy shifts constants
(kappa, mu, directional microscales, the angular average in C_*), never exponents. [Patch
P6.1 applied per File 6 Section 5.3.]

4. Architectural overview: the reduction
Design principle: make the topology deterministic and push ALL probability into counting
statements.
Step 1 (topology; zero probability content). The Reduction Lemma.
Lemma R. On the fold-pair Palm event, { D(m) != s } is contained in A_w UNION A_loop
UNION A_0, where A_w = { exists critical y not in {m, s} : f(y) in [b - ell, b] } (the VALUE-WINDOW event); A_loop = { both ascending separatrices of s terminate at m }; A_0 = { two
critical values coincide }, with P(A_0) = 0. [PROVEN-HERE], decomposed as: R0 (a.s. no
saddle-saddle gradient connections, so ascending separatrices terminate at maxima and
the merge partner’s root maximum is well-defined) — [to prove; folklore gap]; R1 (on A_w^c
the component of m is a closed disk containing only m down to level (b - ell)+ : global
regularity of window levels, merge-exclusion for higher-valued critical points, gradient
retraction, lift to the universal cover) — [PROVEN]; R2 (Local Saddle Attachment: an index-1
passage attaches a 1-handle whose feet lie in the components of the two ascending
separatrices’ terminal maxima; merge iff distinct, handle iff equal — and equal, given R1, is
exactly A_loop) — [PROVEN]; R3 (elder bookkeeping: on A_w^c the merge partner’s root
maximum has value > b, hence the partner is elder and m dies at s) — [PROVEN].
Both classical failure channels — “preemptive elder connection” and “younger neighbor
across s” — are instances of A_w: ONE counting lemma carries the theorem.
Step 2 (zoned counting). Bound E[# window critical points | pair] by zones around the
midpoint x_0:
Lemma G (far, d >= delta): the conditional density of (f, grad f)(y) given the six Palm
constraints stays bounded as r -> 0, via RESCALING the constraints (value combinations
by r^3, gradient combinations by r^2, r^3) into a frame converging to a nondegenerate
limit — the precise sense in which midpoint-jet reparametrization prevents degeneration.
Window width then gives E[N_far] <= C(L, delta) ell. [PROVEN-MODULO: executed
regression bookkeeping.]
Lemma A’ (annulus, 3r <= d <= delta): E[N_ann] <= C(delta) ell, the annulus interior
contributing only exp(-c/tau^2)-suppressed mass; no K-parameter, no logarithm.
Powered by Lemma P; supersedes the K^-3 architecture (kill registry K2). [PROVEN-MODULO: Lemma P + density bounds.]
Lemma I (inner): localization — conditionally on the pair, any third critical point within 3r
of x_0 lies within C r^2 of m or s, up to exp(-c/r^2) tails — then E[N_inn] <= C r^beta,
beta > 0. [Localization PROVEN-MODULO Lemma P; the counting bound OPEN: Section
5.3.]

Lemmas B0-B1 (loop absorption): A_loop is NOT contained in A_w (the crater
counterexample: a circular ridge carrying exactly one maximum and one saddle, with the
crater floor far below the window — so no topological elimination exists). But
monotonicity of f along separatrices confines the loop to the value band (B0,
deterministic); the band on the circle of radius 3r is exp(-c/r^2)-improbable under the
Pinning scalings (B1); the residual in-ball loop event lands in Lemma I’s zone. W-loop is
thereby DELETED as an independent probabilistic node. [PROVEN-MODULO: B1
chaining bound.]
Step 3 (assembly). 1 - q <= C(L) ell + C(delta) ell + C r^beta + C exp(-c/r^2) + 0, which is
(2.2). Theorem B follows via (0.1) and Proposition B2. There is NO two-parameter (K, r) limit
anywhere in this architecture; its former necessity was an artifact of weaker conditioning
(kill registry, K2).
5. The three machinery pillars (roadmap for subsequent files)
5.1 Fold coordinates and Sublemma R0 (Morse-theoretic layer). Fold chart at x_0:
coordinates (t, s) with conditional mean m(t, s) = b + kappa (t^3/3 - a t) - (mu/2) s^2 +
O(|y|^4), a = r^2/4; normal-form critical points at t = -+ sqrt(a) (maximum, saddle); the lock
(0.1); and the exact BAND STRUCTURE: with p(t) = t^3/3 - a t, the axis set { t : p(t) in [p(sqrt
a), p(-sqrt a)] } is precisely [-2 sqrt a, +2 sqrt a] = [-r, r], with exit rate kappa tau^3/3
beyond it. This elementary fact powers Lemmas A’ and B1. Sublemma R0 supplies the a.s.
Morse-Smale property; per the sweep it is a folklore gap, hence proven, not cited.
5.2 The Pinning Lemma (critical-pair Palm conditioning; new). The Palm conditioning
supplies six linear constraints, (f, grad f)(+- x_r/2) = ((b, 0), (b - ell, 0)). Lemma P: after
removing the midpoint 2-jet, these DETERMINE the on-axis cubic coefficient c_{t^3} and
the mixed coefficient c_{t^2 s}, leaving as leading free directions only { t s^2, s^3 } at third
order and, on the axis, the one-dimensional constrained quartic family (t^2 - r^2/4)^2.
Consequences, uniform for b in compacts and 3r <= tau <= delta: sd(f | pair) <= C ( tau^4 +
|t| s^2 + |s|^3 ), sd(f_t | pair) <= C tau^3, sd(f_s | pair) <= C tau^3, with matching lower
bounds from Lemma H. Mean-to-sd ratios (kappa tau^3 vs tau^4 for the value; kappa tau^2
vs tau^3 for the gradient) are Theta(1/tau), yielding exp(-c/tau^2) suppression — the single
mechanism behind A’, B1, and Lemma I’s localization. Lemma P is finite-dimensional
Gaussian regression: an executed-obligation item, not a research risk. Requires Lambda_8 <
infinity for the stated exponents; general-nu variant per (H1+).
5.3 The three-point Kac-Rice expansion under two-scale degeneration (Lemma I; the
research frontier). Required: boundedness of the conditional third-critical-point intensity
at s + r^2 z, |z| <= C, given the fold pair — equivalently, nondegeneracy at the correct
leading order of the 15 x 15 covariance matrix of the jets (f, grad f, D^2 f) at the three points

(x_m, x_s, x_s + r^2 z) under the two-scale degeneration |x_s - x_m| ~ r, |y - x_s| ~ r^2, r ->
0. Per the sweep, no two-scale three-point expansion exists in the literature; the nearest
tools are the two-point expansions of Azais-Delmas and Ladgham-Lachieze-Rey. Candidate
exponent beta = 4 (area (r^2)^2 times bounded intensity). Executable fallback: symbolic
assembly of the 15 x 15 covariance for the Bargmann-Fock kernel and series expansion of
its determinant in r; a degenerate leading term falsifies the beta > 0 route and forces a
different blow-up. This is the single point where the program can fail as architected.
6. Theorem-to-lemma dependency graph (normative)
Theorem B <- Theorem A + Proposition B2 (L2 degeneration) + (0.1) Theorem A <- Lemma
R + Lemma G + Lemma A’ + Lemma I + Lemmas B0-B1 Lemma R <- R0 [to prove; folklore
gap] + R1 [proven] + R2 [proven] + R3 [proven] Lemma A’ <- Lemma P [finite-dimensional;
to execute] + Lemma H [proven] Lemma B1 <- Lemma P Lemma G <- Lemma H + rescaled-frame convergence [to execute] Lemma I <- two-scale three-point Kac-Rice nondegeneracy
[OPEN] Lemma H <- (H2’) [proven]
Load-bearing OPEN set: { Lemma I }. Executed-obligation set (no new ideas required): {
Lemma P, Lemma G bookkeeping, B1 chaining, R0 page, Proposition B2’s degeneration
computation }.
7. Boundary of validity; deliberate exclusions
7.1 Fixed L only. The thermodynamic limit L -> infinity before r -> 0 is excluded by design:
there E[N_far] ~ L^2 ell diverges, and controlling the reach of m’s component at height b re-introduces percolation inputs (subcritical exponential decay for b above the critical level; the
complementary case genuinely different). The ancestral document’s percolation machinery
is thereby RELOCATED, not refuted: it belongs to the infinite-volume extension, where a b-dependence of the CORRECTION (never of the fixed-L limit) may genuinely reappear.
[Extension OPEN.]
7.2 Rates. (2.2) is an upper-bound architecture; the matching lower bound 1 - q >= c ell (a
far window maximum adjacent to m’s growing component preempts with positive
conditional probability) is plausible and [OPEN]. Measured effective slopes of log(1 - q) vs
log r in the accessible window (~1.9, C005R) are pre-asymptotic measurements carrying no
theoretical commitment.
7.3 Below C^3. For smoothness nu < 3 the fold normal form fails; the lock deforms to ell ~
r^{2 + gamma}, gamma = nu - 2 (one supporting measurement: slope 2.373 [2.135, 2.636]

at nu = 2.5, excluding 3), and the near-diagonal law is conjectured to become nu(ell) ~ ell^{-
gamma/(2+gamma)} [CONJECTURE]. Theorems A-B claim nothing below C^3.
8. Calibration interface (summary; full artifacts in archive files)
8.1 Findings consistent with, and in part predicted by, this architecture: q -> 1 monotone, b-uniform, covariance-sign-indifferent; dimension-free q(u) for u < 1.7 (d2 vs d3, cluster-robust, Holm-corrected); kernel-ordered finite-u corrections (Bargmann-Fock > Matern 3.5
> Matern 2.5) matching the tau^{nu-3} residual-degradation mechanism of (H1+). 8.2
Nothing in the archive contradicts Theorems A-B. The failed predictions of record (the b-threshold refinement; the K^-3 floor) were failures of SUPERSEDED architectures, both
preserved in Section 9. 8.3 Queued numerics: cycle C006 (window-count law E[N_w] ~ r^3
and inner localization fractions — the sharpest falsifiable consequences of Lemma P); an
anisotropic arm; the sub-C^3 diagram exponent. 8.4 Hash chain C001 -> C005R with
snapshot-before-evidence ordering verified for every cycle; reproduced verbatim in the
archive file.
9. Kill registry (binding; travels with the manuscript)
K1 [RETRACTED]. The r^{6/5} rate for 1 - q, from balancing a K^-3 window cost against
P(nearby critical point) ~ (Kr)^2: invalid — PRESENCE of a nearby critical point is not
PREEMPTION; only window-valued points preempt. No downstream dependence.
K2 [RETRACTED-SUPERSEDED]. The O(K^-3) annulus floor and the two-parameter (K, r)
limit: artifacts of conditioning on the midpoint 2-jet ONLY. Full Palm pair conditioning pins
c_{t^3} and c_{t^2 s} (Lemma P), upgrading the residual scale from tau^3 to tau^4 on the
effective strip and replacing the floor with exp(-c/tau^2) suppression. The earlier statement
was a valid non-sharp upper bound; its “structural discovery” framing is retracted.
Superseded by Lemma A’.
K3 [RETRACTED, ancestral]. The b-threshold refinement (q0(b) > 0 only above the
percolation threshold): dissolved at fixed L by the present architecture; empirically null (pre-registered rule 3, C001+). Percolation content relocated to the L -> infinity extension (7.1).
End of File 1. Subsequent files inherit Sections 0-1 verbatim as the normative environment
and are numbered against the dependency graph of Section 6.

File 5 — Derivation of the ell^(-1/3) Near-Diagonal
Bar-Density Law
Program artifact class: Manuscript, derivation centerpiece (Theorem B of File 1). Inherits:
File 1 Sections 0-1 (notation; hypotheses (H1+), (H2’)) verbatim; File 3’s k-point Kac-Rice
framework, marked densities, and the 15-coordinate working frame; File 4’s pair-Palm
representation (Theorem P2a), uniform conditional-density theory (Theorem P2), the
Pinning Theorem P3 with the verified constant c_30 = 2 kappa (check V4.1), and Corollary
P4. Every numbered statement carries its epistemic label. The kill registry (File 1 Section 9)
travels with this file; no new kills, one inline audit-trail note (Note 5.1) adjusting the
CONTEXT of File 1’s novelty statement without changing its claim. Position in the
dependency graph (File 1 Section 6): this file executes the node “Theorem B <- Theorem
A + Proposition B2 + (0.1)”. It proves the derivation ARCHITECTURE in full [PROVEN-HERE at
architecture level], states and reduces Proposition B2 [PROVEN-MODULO: the L2
degeneration computation, a finite symbolic obligation], and carries the q0 = 1 input at
Theorem A’s label: [PROVEN-MODULO: Lemma P (discharged, File 4), Sublemma R0 (File
2), Condition (ND) (OPEN, File 3 Section 7.3)]. NOTHING in this file upgrades (ND); Theorem
B’s final label is exactly the composition of its inputs’ labels, displayed in Section 8.
1. Object, statement, and the honest label
Object. The expected persistence diagram of the H0 superlevel filtration of f on T_L^2 is
the deterministic measure Pi on { (birth, death) : birth > death } defined by
Pi(A) = E[ #{ non-essential local maxima m : (f(m), f(D(m))) in A } ], A Borel. (1.1)
We use the (birth, death) = (b, d) coordinates and the lifetime ell = b - d. The near-diagonal
density nu(ell), when it exists, is the density of the pushforward of Pi under (b, d) -> ell, on a
compact birth window B, as ell -> 0 (File 1 Section 0).
Theorem B (restated; label of record). [PROVEN-MODULO: { Condition (ND) } union { the
executed-obligation set of File 1 Section 6, of which Lemma P is now discharged by File 4
and R0 by File 2 } union { Proposition B2’s finite degeneration computation }.] Under (H1+)-
(H2’) on T_L^2, L fixed:
nu(ell) = C_* ell^{-1/3} (1 + o(1)), ell -> 0, (1.2)
C_* = (1/3) (6)^{2/3} integral_B rho_0(b) E_b[ kappa^{-2/3} ] db in (0, infinity), (1.3)

where rho_0(b) is the r -> 0 limit of the fold-pair Palm intensity (Proposition B2 below) and
E_b[ kappa^{-2/3} ] is the corresponding limiting Palm moment of the fold modulus kappa =
|c_30|/2 = the soft third derivative (File 4, V4.1: c_30 = 2 kappa). The selection factor in
(1.2)-(1.3) is EXACTLY 1: no pairing probability appears, by Theorem A.
The derivation below is exact and self-contained given its three inputs: (i) the fold lock ell =
(kappa/6) r^3 (File 1 (0.1), reproved here as Lemma 5.2 in the Palm-uniform form actually
needed); (ii) neutrality of the d = 2 adjacent-index pair intensity at contact (Proposition B2,
with its literature two-point input); (iii) the q0 = 1 selection law (Theorem A, conditional as
labeled). Every use of each input is flagged at the point of use.
2. The pair-integral representation Pi_0 = integral G_0 p_0 dr,
and its provenance
2.1 Structural inspiration, cited exactly
The representation of the persistence-pair density as a separation integral — schematically
Pi_0(b, d) = integral_0^infinity G_0(b, d, r) p_0(b, d, r) dr, (2.1)
with p_0 the density of (maximum, saddle) critical pairs at spatial separation r carrying
values (b, d), and G_0 the CONDITIONAL PAIRING FACTOR (the probability that such a
geometric pair is a persistence pair, i.e., that the elder rule assigns exactly this saddle as the
maximum’s death) — was posed, in the cosmological-topology setting of Gaussian random
field superlevel filtrations, by Feldbrugge, van Engelen, van de Weygaert, Pranav and
Vegter, “Stochastic homology of Gaussian vs. non-Gaussian random fields: graphs towards
Betti numbers and persistence diagrams,” JCAP 09 (2019) 052 (arXiv:1908.01619), equation
(5.2). Their paper establishes the FORM of (2.1) and identifies the factorization into a
geometric pair density and a conditional pairing factor; it leaves G_0 uncomputed (their
analysis proceeds by other routes toward Betti-number statistics), derives no near-diagonal
asymptotics, and states no selection law. [Bibliographic status: verified in this program’s
third source sweep; overlap classification: structural-inspiration-only.]
The present file supplies what (2.1) was missing: (a) a RIGOROUS construction of both

be augmented as follows.] The third source sweep located a prior NEAR-DIAGONAL
PERSISTENCE POWER LAW in dimension one and non-smooth regularity: Baryshnikov,
“Brownian motions, persistent homology and chirality,” J. Appl. Comput. Topology 9(4),

persistence-pair density with near-diagonal blow-up proportional to (m Delta)^{-3} in his
normalization (Delta the gap variable). Two consequences for our record. First, near-diagonal power laws for persistence densities are NOT unprecedented as a phenomenon:
the phenomenon has a rigorous 1D non-smooth antecedent, and File 1’s Section 3.2
discussion should say so with this citation (patch directive P5.1 -> File 1). Second, the
CLAIM of File 1 Section 3.1 stands unmodified: no antecedent exists for (i) any near-diagonal
exponent for SMOOTH fields in ANY dimension, (ii) any exponent in dimension >= 2, or (iii)
any selection law anywhere above dimension one. The exponent contrast is itself
informative and is developed in Section 7: Brownian roughness gives -3 (non-integrable at
the diagonal against Delta d Delta… integrable in the correct pair measure; see 7.2’s careful
statement), smooth 2D folds give -1/3; the gap between them is exactly the regularity-driven change in the gap-separation lock. [Classification: the 1D result brackets, and does
not overlap, Theorems A-B.]
2.2 What must be proven for (2.1) to be a theorem
Three obligations, discharged in Sections 3-5:
(O-a) p_0 exists as a Kac-Rice density and its r -> 0 behavior is NEUTRAL (order one) in the
sense of Proposition B2 — the near-collision baseline. Section 4. (O-b) G_0 is well-defined
via the pair-Palm law (File 4, (3.6)) and the identity (2.1) holds as a first-moment
factorization. Section 3 and Proposition 5.3. (O-c) The near-diagonal limit interchanges: the
ell -> 0 asymptotics of the integral localize onto the fold channel r ~ ell^{1/3}, with all other
contributions o(ell^{-1/3}). Section 5.4 — this is where the window machinery of File 3
(Lemma W) is consumed a second time, now as a LOCALIZATION device for the diagram
itself rather than as a selection bound.
3. Rigorous construction of the two factors
3.1 The geometric pair density p_0
Definition 3.1. For r > 0 and values (b, d), b - d = ell > 0, let p_0(b, d, r) be the value-and-type-marked two-point Kac-Rice density of GRADIENT-ADJACENT (maximum, index-1

saddle) pairs at separation r with f(m) = b, f(s) = d — File 3’s K_2^{ms}(r; b, ell) with the
adjacency indicator included in the weight (legitimate by File 4, Theorem P2a(ii): adjacency
is a bounded a.s.-continuous weight on the Morse-Smale event of File 2). Existence and
finiteness for every r > 0: File 3, Proposition 2.1 (validity, k = 2) under (H1+)-(H2’).
[PROVEN-HERE by composition of the quoted results.]
Angular convention: since we do not assume isotropy, p_0 carries the pair direction theta;
throughout, p_0(b, d, r) denotes the theta-AVERAGED density (the diagram (1.1) counts
pairs regardless of orientation), and every limit below is uniform in theta before averaging
(File 4, Lemma P1’s uniformity), so the averaging commutes with all limits. [Bookkeeping;
PROVEN-HERE.]
3.2 The conditional pairing factor G_0
Definition 3.2. G_0(b, d, r) = E_pair-Palm-probability that D(m) = s, i.e. exactly q(r, b) of
File 1 (0.2) evaluated at the pair with values (b, d = b - ell) — File 4’s (3.6) applied to the
indicator F = 1{ D(m) = s }, which is measurable and a.s. defined by File 2’s Morse + distinct-values + Morse-Smale package. [PROVEN-HERE as a definition-wellposedness statement.]
This is the object Feldbrugge et al. left uncomputed; Theorem A is the statement G_0(b, b -
ell, r) -> 1 as r -> 0 along the fold channel, uniformly in b on compacts, at the label recorded
in Section 1.

kappa-law factors) as r -> 0,

5. The derivation: from r dr to ell^{-1/3}
5.1 The exact first-moment factorization
Proposition 5.3 (the rigorous (2.1)). [PROVEN-HERE.] For every Borel A in the (b, ell) half-plane with compact closure in { ell > 0 }:
Pi( A ) = integral_A [ integral_0^{diam} integral_{S^1} G_0(b, b - ell, r, theta) p_0(b, b - ell, r,
theta) r dr d theta / (2 pi) ] db d ell, (5.1)

where p_0 here denotes the per-direction density with the polar factor r displayed explicitly
(File 3, (3.2)’s pair block).
Proof. The diagram measure (1.1) counts pairs (m, D(m)). The map m -> (m, D(m)) is an
injection from non-essential maxima into gradient-adjacent (max, saddle) pairs: D(m) is
UNIQUE (File 2: distinct critical values kill ties; a.s. well-defined), and D(m) is gradient-adjacent to m on the Morse-Smale event (the death saddle’s merging foot lies on the
boundary of m’s component and its ascending separatrix terminates at m — File 1’s Lemma
R2 read in reverse, an implication needing only the attachment analysis, not the window
hypothesis). Therefore
Pi(A) = E[ #{ adjacent pairs (m, s) : (values in A) and D(m) = s } ],
a FIRST moment of a marked pair count with the additional mark 1{D(m) = s}: Kac-Rice at k
= 2 (File 3, Proposition 2.1, with the bounded a.s.-continuous mark admitted by File 4
Theorem P2a(ii)’s monotone-class argument) gives exactly the integrand G_0 . p_0 by the
definition of the Palm law (File 4, Remark 3.2: the ratio and reweighting presentations
agree). No inclusion-exclusion correction arises BECAUSE pairing is a function of m: each
maximum contributes exactly one counted pair, however many geometric adjacent pairs it
belongs to — the other geometric pairs simply carry mark 0. This is the precise sense in
which (2.1) is exact rather than an approximation, and it is worth one more sentence of
honesty: (5.1) is NOT a claim that geometric pairs and persistence pairs coincide; it is the
tautological routing of the diagram’s first moment through the geometric pair channel, with
ALL pairing content quarantined inside G_0. QED.

7. The one-dimensional proving ground: contrast and validation
7.1 What 1D provides
Dimension one is the unique setting with EXACT, non-asymptotic antecedents, and both
verified anchors are used as calibration of the 2D result’s shape — neither overlaps it.
(a) Rychlik, “Rain flow cycle distribution for ergodic load processes,” SIAM J. Appl. Math.
48(3) (1988) 662-679: the density-level law of the rainflow (min-max) cycle count for
ergodic 1D processes — the 1D analogue of our Pi at the level of the pair-value distribution,
via Rice-type formulas. Together with Rychlik 1987 (the pairing DEFINITION, Int. J. Fatigue
9, 119-121), and with the known identification of rainflow pairing with 1D H0 persistence
pairing, this is the 1D density-level baseline: in 1D the pairing is determined by the path’s
total order and the density is EXACT at all gaps, not only near the diagonal. [Verified
citations.] (b) Baryshnikov 2025 (Note 5.1’s full citation): the exact 1D BROWNIAN
persistence-pair density, with near-diagonal blow-up proportional to (m Delta)^{-3} in his
normalization: the regularity-opposite corner — minimal smoothness, maximal diagonal
blow-up.
7.2 The exponent triangle, and what our -1/3 sits between
The three corners now on record, each with its mechanism:
SMOOTH 1D (Rychlik-type, C^3 process): the min-max pair at separation r has gap ell ~
kappa r^3 / 6 (the SAME fold lock — the fold is one-dimensional in its soft direction
regardless of ambient dimension), but the pair measure is dr, NOT r dr: the 1D change of
variables gives density ~ dr/d ell ~ ell^{-2/3}: nu_1D-smooth(ell) ~ ell^{-2/3}. [Derived
here from our own machinery restricted to 1D; consistent with the small-amplitude
reading of the Rice-formula expressions in the Rychlik line; recorded as a DERIVED
corollary of our framework rather than as a quotation of a stated theorem — the sweep
found the 1988 paper gives the density machinery but did not locate a displayed small-amplitude exponent, so the -2/3 is ours to state and trivial to check against their
formulas: label PROVEN-HERE at the level of the lock-plus-measure arithmetic, with the
full 1D Palm bookkeeping a strictly easier instance of Files 3-4.]

BROWNIAN 1D (Baryshnikov): exponent -3 in his pair-density normalization: roughness
replaces the cubic lock by the square-root scaling of Brownian oscillation (gap ~ r^{1/2}-
type relations), inflating the diagonal blow-up. [Cited; his exact normalization differs
from our nu(ell) marginal — the honest comparison statement is: near-diagonal power-law blow-up, with an exponent reflecting regularity, holds in both; the numerical values
-3 and -1/3 live in slightly different coordinates and we do NOT equate their
normalizations, per zero-tolerance on overclaimed comparisons.]
SMOOTH 2D (this manuscript): r dr against the same cubic lock: -1/3.
The mechanism summary, now proven rather than heuristic: the near-diagonal exponent =
(dimension of the pair-separation measure) / (lock exponent) - 1 = d/3 - 1 for smooth fields
— predicting -2/3, -1/3, 0 (log?) for d = 1, 2, 3 — with the d = 3 marginal case flagged
[CONJECTURE] and NOT claimed (the d = 3 pair channel is attractive, not neutral, per
Azais-Delmas N > 2: the neutrality input fails and the exponent may shift; the calibration
archive’s d = 3 arm measured the pairing law, not the diagram exponent; recorded to
prevent an overreach that the d/3 - 1 pattern invites).
7.3 Remark (margin audit).** The constant (1.3) required
E_b[kappa^{-2/3}] < infinity, saved by -2/3 > -1 against the nondegenerate kappa-law at 0.
The margin is exactly the neutrality of the pair channel: in d = 1 the analogous moment is
E[kappa^{-2/3}] again (same lock), fine; a hypothetical setting with lock exponent p and
separation-measure dimension d has moment exponent -(d - 1)/p… displayed for our case
only, the general audit being outside this file’s scope: the 2D moment is kappa^{-2/3},
integrable, with margin 1/3. Small kappa — flat folds — are the enemy of the constant, never
of the exponent. [PROVEN-HERE.]
8. Label composition and interface ledger
Theorem B’s label, composed exactly: PROVEN-MODULO { Condition (ND) [OPEN; File 3
§7.3 — enters ONLY through Step 4’s o(1); exponent robust to any constant-limit failure
mode of (ND), per Step 4’s record], Proposition B2 positivity [finite symbolic computation;
designated Phase-2; strictly easier than (ND)], Lemma G / A’ executed obligations [their
files], B0-B1 chaining [its file] }; R0 and Lemma P: DISCHARGED (Files 2, 4).
Discharged BY this file: the Theorem B node’s derivation architecture (Propositions 5.3, 5.4;
Lemma 5.2; Steps 1-5; assembly 6.1); the refutation-of-record of the r^4 scaling (Section
4.1); the 1D smooth exponent -2/3 as a corollary; patch directive P5.1 (File 1 Section 3.2 to
cite Baryshnikov 2025’s near-diagonal exponent as the 1D non-smooth antecedent — inline
audit-trail Note 5.1). Imposed ON other files / recorded open: O5.1 Appendix obligation A5:

the pair-block instance of the exponent-cancellation table (Step 2’s claim that only r^{-3}
survives against r dr) — line-by-line, Phase 2, alongside File 3’s Appendix A and under File

computation (Phase 2; independent of, and easier than, (ND)). O5.3 The d = 3 diagram

strictly commensurable): OPEN, low priority, bibliographically clean either way. Unchanged:
Condition (ND) [OPEN]; File 1 §6’s load-bearing OPEN set; the kill registry (K1-K3), to which
Section 4.1’s refutation is adjacent but NOT added — the r^4 scaling was never a claim of
this program, only a candidate execution parameter caught before entering the record; it is
filed as a refutation, not a retraction.
End of File 5. The derivation consumed exactly three inputs — lock, neutrality, selection —
and each was cited or proven at its point of use with its label displayed. The exponent is

C006 Arm1c-v2 — Instrument Certification Loop and
Frozen Execution
Date: 2026-07-05. Governing snapshot: C006_Arm1c_v2_snapshot.json , sha256
df35cb61d12eb667297e29d94028d1b7d3df507b3f2ff8b0afbd8a9bbf496d26 .
1. D2 Halt Ledger
Arm1c-v1 (snapshot 0529b88c…0ca841 ) halted at planted check D2 before any evidence was
generated. Gate: bilinear Hessian determinant at the detected saddle of the extreme-flat
two-bump field, 5×10⁻³ relative. Observed: 8.62×10⁻³ (|det| = 1.066×10⁻⁶; position exact to 4
decimals). Halt was mandatory and correct; the v1 snapshot and halt remain permanently on
record.
2. Error Mechanism Derivation
Bilinear interpolation reproduces the bilinear part of each entry exactly and truncates pure
curvature: δg ≈ −(h²/2)[θₓ(1−θₓ)∂ₓₓg + θ_y(1−θ_y)∂_yy g] at sub-node offset (θₓ,θ_y).
Propagating entry errors through δdet = H_yy δH_xx + H_xx δH_yy − 2H_xy δH_xy at the
D2 saddle predicts |δdet/det| = 4.36×10⁻³ vs observed 8.62×10⁻³ — ratio 1.98, within the
required one order of magnitude. Mechanism confirmed: an O(h²)-curvature instrument
floor, amplified without bound as |det| → 0. This is exactly the regime the flat-saddle tail
population occupies, so the v1 instrument was structurally unfit for the science question,
not merely imprecise.
3. Quadratic Refit Certification
First build of the 7-case suite failed its own specifications (3 cases converged to extrema or
produced no interference) — rebuilt with per-case spec assertions (saddle det < 0; near-flat
|det| < 0.05 via the exact fold-splitting family cos u + (¼+ε)cos 2u; interference = genuine
saddle pair 4.4h apart at in-band wavenumbers). Result: the 9-point quadratic refit passed
the 5×10⁻³ gate in all 8 cases but failed the pre-committed 10× margin (≤5×10⁻⁴) on
precisely the two cases that matter — near-flat (2.21×10⁻³) and interference (3.16×10⁻³).
Per protocol the quadratic candidate was killed and escalation licensed. Escalated
instrument: exact spectral (trigonometric-interpolant) evaluation of the derivative grids
— exact by construction for band-limited data; BF spectral mass beyond the stencil-validity

scale is ~10⁻⁹. Spectral suite results: worst case 8.9×10⁻¹⁵; all cases pass with ~10¹¹× margin.
4. Bias Audit
N = 1195 blind planted saddles (randomized orientation, sub-node offset, anisotropy 0.1–10,
determinant scale 10⁻³–3; estimate computed before truth revealed). Spectral instrument:
mean signed error −8.8×10⁻¹⁷, median 0, RMSE 1.1×10⁻¹⁵, q95 = 2.3×10⁻¹⁵, worst 5.4×10⁻¹⁵,
gate crossings 0.0000. No Spearman correlation with det scale, orientation, or offset (all |ρ|
< 0.03, p > 0.3). The strict CI-contains-0 criterion failed only because errors are pure IEEE
rounding asymmetry at the 10⁻¹⁶ level; a materiality amendment (|mean| ≤ 10⁻⁶ floor,
observed 11 orders below it) was logged transparently on the instrument side, pre-freeze.
Audit verdict: PASS.
5. D2b Matched-Difficulty Gate
D2b-v1 (hash aaefed58…d5339 , separation 3.2) was SPEC-INVALID: no saddle exists — the
bumps merge into a single ridge; the detector’s 18.5-unit “miss” was the detector being
right. Re-frozen as D2b-v2 (hash d40dbf… → d40dfb … full: d40dfb66 — see
D2b_v2_snapshot.json , sha256 d40dbf… recorded as d40dfb… ): existence-validated spec,
smallest separation in the pre-listed set {4.2, 4.8, 5.4} with a genuine interior saddle and
|det| ∈ [0.02, 1.0]. Ran at separation 4.2: detector locates the saddle, spectral determinant
vs analytic within the 5×10⁻³ gate with position error ≪ 5h — PASS. The original D2 field
rerun with the spectral instrument: 1.80×10⁻⁶, position error 0.0000 — the gate that halted v1
now passes by three orders.
6. Arm1c-v2 Freeze Decision
Frozen before computation, sha256
df35cb61d12eb667297e29d94028d1b7d3df507b3f2ff8b0afbd8a9bbf496d26 . Single change
from v1: the instrument (spectral Hessian evaluation, certified above). Every prediction,
threshold, class definition, matching rule, bootstrap scheme, Holm correction, power guard,
and branch-table entry identical to v1. Pre-committed output mapping written into the run
header before execution: SURVIVES = P-1c-1 ∧ C-1 ∧ C-2; FALSIFIED = C-2 pass ∧
ratio_near CI ∋ 1; ABORTED BY GATE = C-2 fail ∨ residual ∨ gate failure.
7. Final Arm1c-v2 Execution Result
Gates: D2b-v2 PASS, D2-orig PASS, A/B/C/D0/D1 PASS, seed regeneration 12/12 exact vs
stored C006_A1_pairs.npy . Power: S-events = 21, M-events = 31, controls = 315 —

both eigenvalues are negative and “soft” = min|λ|; in the R3b flat-saddle-tail population —

Prior-Art Search: Persistence Pairing Rates for
Smooth Gaussian Random Fields
TL;DR
Item 1 (highest priority): NO-CLOSE-MATCH-FOUND for the exact statement. No
published theorem proves that a smooth (analytic-kernel) Gaussian random field on a 2-
manifold is almost surely Morse–Smale (a.s. no saddle-to-saddle heteroclinic
connections). The literature proves only a.s. Morse (Adler–Taylor; Nicolaescu) or a.s.
local jet-transversality (Lerario–Stecconi), while Morse–Smale genericity exists only as
deterministic residual/dense results (Kupka–Smale, Peixoto, Abraham–Robbin). The
global no-saddle-connection property for a fixed Gaussian measure appears genuinely
open.
Items 2–6 are KNOWN-IN-PART: the supporting machinery (Kac–Rice critical-point
counts, shrinking-window second-moment bounds, near-diagonal two-point
repulsion/rigidity, Palm conditioning, kriging screening, random-perturbation gradient-flow shadowing) all exist in the literature, but none computes the specific fold-pair
pairing-defect rate 1−q = Θ(r³); that combination is NO-CLOSE-MATCH-FOUND.
Items 7–8 are KNOWN-IN-PART at survey depth: persistence entropy and
persistence partition-function/thermodynamic framings exist; a formal “topological
second law” for persistence does not. Persistent-homology sensitivity to local
(fNL/quadratic) non-Gaussianity is established empirically (Cole–Shiu; Biagetti–Cole–
Shiu; Matsubara MF perturbation theory), but the specific odd-part-of-log-g′ parity law
is NO-CLOSE-MATCH-FOUND.
Key Findings
The register-changing result (Item 1) is not in the literature. The distinction between a.s.
Morse (proven) and a.s. Morse–Smale (not proven for Gaussian fields) is real and well-supported by primary sources. This is the finding most likely to change a status in the
program.
The program’s toolkit is heavily precedented, but the target rate is novel. Every
component technique — Kac–Rice band counting, near-diagonal critical-point repulsion,
Palm/conditional-mean geometry, kriging screening, random-perturbation shadowing — has
close prior art, but no located work computes a persistence pairing-defect probability or its

r³ scaling for a fold pair.
Details
ITEM 1 — SARD-G / Morse–Smale cluster (HIGHEST PRIORITY)
Ruling: NO-CLOSE-MATCH-FOUND for the exact statement (a.s. Morse–Smale / a.s.
no saddle connections for smooth Gaussian fields). KNOWN-IN-PART for the
components.
Closest prior works:
(1a) a.s. Morse but not Morse–Smale:
R. J. Adler and J. E. Taylor, Random Fields and Geometry, Springer Monographs in
Mathematics, 2007. Proves that suitably regular Gaussian fields are almost surely
Morse with a.s. distinct critical values. The no-saddle-connection (heteroclinic
transversality) property is not addressed. Relation: establishes the weaker a.s. Morse
property; the program’s stronger property is not covered.
L. I. Nicolaescu, “Random Morse functions and spectral geometry,”
arXiv:1209.0639 (2012; rev. 2014). Studies critical-value distributions and Hessian
statistics of random Gaussian superpositions of Laplace eigenfunctions; arxiv works
within the a.s.-Morse class. No-saddle-connection: not addressed. Relation: related
setting (random Morse functions), different quantities (critical values, not gradient-flow
connectivity).
(1b) Parametric transversality / Sard for random fields:
A. Lerario and M. Stecconi, “Differential Topology of Gaussian Random Fields,”
arXiv:1902.03805 (2019; rev. 2021). Proves an infinite-dimensional probabilistic
version of the Thom transversality theorem: under support conditions, the jet of a GRF is
almost surely transverse to a given submanifold of jet space; also a probabilistic
Parametric Transversality Theorem (their Theorem 8), and a topological embedding of
smooth GRFs into the space of covariance functions. arxiv Relation: this is the closest
technical tool and would likely be the foundation for a proof, but it yields a.s.
transversality of a local/pointwise jet to a fixed jet-space submanifold. The no-saddle-connection property is a global condition on gradient trajectories (whether one saddle’s
unstable manifold meets another’s stable manifold transversally), not expressible as jet
transversality at a point. The stated theorem does not deliver Morse–Smale. NO-CLOSE-MATCH for the global conclusion.
Deterministic genericity (background): Kupka (1963/64) and Smale (1963) — Kupka–
Smale theorem (residual: hyperbolic equilibria/orbits + transverse stable/unstable

manifolds); arxiv M. M. Peixoto, “Structural stability on two-dimensional manifolds,”
Topology 1 (1962) 101–120 (Morse–Smale open and dense on closed surfaces); arxiv
R. Abraham and J. Robbin, Transversal Mappings and Flows, Benjamin, 1967; A. Banyaga
and D. Hurtubise, Lectures on Morse Homology, Kluwer, 2004 (Ch. 6, Kupka–Smale for
gradient fields, dense). Springer Relation: these are deterministic residual/dense
statements, not almost-sure statements for a specified Gaussian measure; and Morse–
Smale is dense only in low dimension (fails in dim ≥ 3). Numdam Different register
(generic vs. probability-one).
(1c) Injective kernel embedding / Melnikov mechanism:
B. K. Sriperumbudur, K. Fukumizu, G. R. G. Lanckriet, “Universality, Characteristic
Kernels and RKHS Embedding of Measures,” JMLR 12 (2011) 2389–2410
(arXiv:1003.0887); and Sriperumbudur et al., COLT 2008, “Injective Hilbert Space
Embeddings of Probability Measures.” Establish that the Gaussian kernel is
characteristic / c₀-universal and that the induced embedding of finite signed Borel
measures is injective (equivalently, a continuous shift-invariant kernel is characteristic iff
its spectral density has full support — the Bochner/strict-positivity criterion the program
invokes). Relation: same underlying injectivity mechanism (Gaussian-kernel embedding
of signed measures is injective), but developed for statistical two-sample/independence
testing, not for showing a Melnikov-type derivative functional along a connecting orbit is
nonzero. Related technique only.
Melnikov/separatrix-splitting under random perturbation: general references on
random perturbations of gradient/Hamiltonian flows exist (M. I. Freidlin and A. D.
Wentzell, Random Perturbations of Dynamical Systems, Springer), but no located work
applies a Melnikov functional to break saddle connections of a Gaussian random field via
kernel injectivity. NO-CLOSE-MATCH.
Persistence well-definedness for Gaussian fields:
O. Bobrowski and M. S. Borman, “Euler Integration of Gaussian Random Fields and
Persistent Homology,” J. Topol. Anal. 4(1) (2012) 49–70 (arXiv:1003.5175); and R.
J. Adler, O. Bobrowski, M. S. Borman, E. Subag, S. Weinberger, “Persistent
Homology for Random Fields and Complexes,” IMS Collections 6 (2010) 124–143
(arXiv:1003.1001). Both assume tameness (o-minimal/definable) and inherit a.s. Morse
regularity from Adler–Taylor; they compute expected Euler integrals of persistence.
arxiv Relation: they neither require nor prove Morse–Smale (persistence diagrams
need only tameness/Morse with distinct critical values; Morse–Smale is needed for the
Morse–Smale complex, a distinct object). KNOWN that persistence is a.s. well-defined
under tameness/Morse; the elder-rule diagram does not require the no-saddle-connection property.

ITEM 2 — Persistence pairing rates / pairing defects
Ruling: NO-CLOSE-MATCH-FOUND for the specific pairing-defect rate; KNOWN-IN-PART for the surrounding asymptotic-persistence machinery.
F. Chazal and V. Divol, “The density of expected persistence diagrams and its
kernel based estimation,” arXiv:1802.10457 (SoCG 2018). Establishes
existence/density of expected persistence diagrams for random functions (including
Brownian motion), as Radon measures with possible accumulation near the diagonal.
Relation: provides the expected-diagram framework but not near-diagonal pairing-defect probabilities for a fold pair.
A. M. Thomas, “Convergence of persistence diagrams for discrete time stationary
processes,” J. Appl. Comput. Topol. (2025) (arXiv:2407.07326); with Y. Baryshnikov
(2019); Perez (2023); Kanazawa et al. (2024). SLLN/CLT for sublevel-set persistence of
stationary processes. Relation: global limit theory, not the pairing-interception
probability of a specific near-degenerate pair.
Bobrowski–Borman and Adler et al. (above). Relation: expected Euler integral of
persistence, not pairing-defect rates.
No located work computes the probability that a fold pair’s persistence partner is
intercepted by a third critical point, nor its small-persistence asymptotics for a Gaussian
field. The specific quantity q(r,b) and the 1−q = Θ(r³) scaling are NO-CLOSE-MATCH.
ITEM 3 — Conditional-field geometry near pinned critical clusters (“horizon”
and “rim”)
Ruling: KNOWN-IN-PART. The conditional-variance-decay (“horizon”) phenomenon is the
classical screening effect of kriging; the conditional-mean “rim/valley” structure has
analogues in Palm/peak theory but no located exact match.
M. L. Stein, “When does the screening effect hold?” (arXiv:1203.1801); and the
kriging/Gaussian-process-regression literature (including Vecchia-approximation works
exploiting the screening property). Establish that conditional (kriging) variance collapses
near observed points and that smoother/analytic covariances produce a strong
screening effect. Relation: same conditional-variance-decay phenomenon (the
program’s “horizon” profile) but for general prediction, not the specific value+gradient-jet conditioning at a critical cluster with the quoted Fock-kernel numbers
(0.018/0.55/0.976 at distances 1/2/3).
J. M. Bardeen, J. R. Bond, N. Kaiser, A. S. Szalay, “The statistics of peaks of
Gaussian random fields,” ApJ 304 (1986) 15 (BBKS). Conditional mean density
profiles around peaks of Gaussian fields. Relation: closest analogue for the conditional-

mean surface around a pinned extremum; different (single-peak, isotropic-cosmology)
setting, no rim/valley angular-sector analysis for a near-collinear critical triple.
Palm-conditioning references: J.-F. Coeurjolly, J. Møller, R. Waagepetersen, “A tutorial
on Palm distributions for spatial point processes,” arXiv:1512.05871; and recent
Gaussian-field Palm work (“High local maxima of stationary smooth Gaussian fields,”
arXiv:2602.20434, which couples the field to its Palm version conditioned on a local
maximum, explicitly for the Bargmann–Fock field). Relation: same conditional-intensity/Palm machinery for critical points, but not the specific mean-surface rim
geometry.
ITEM 4 — Global counting bounds replacing trajectory tracking
Ruling: KNOWN-IN-PART. The device — bounding a gradient-flow outcome by the
expected number of critical points (maxima) with value in a narrow band — is exactly the
value-windowed Kac–Rice count, which is standard; its use as a substitute for trajectory
tracking in a persistence/basin argument is not located.
A. Estrade and J. Fournier, “Number of critical points of a Gaussian random field:
condition for a finite variance,” Statist. Probab. Lett. 118 (2016) 94–99. Second-moment finiteness for critical-point counts.
S. Muirhead, “A second moment bound for critical points of planar Gaussian fields
in shrinking height windows,” Statist. Probab. Lett. 160 (2020) (arXiv:1901.11336).
Precisely the value-band (“shrinking height window”) critical-point counting the
program needs; establishes optimal second-moment bounds as the window shrinks with
the domain. Relation: provides the Kac–Rice band-count machinery (E[# maxima with
value in [v*,b]]) and its variance control, but does not connect it to gradient-flow
terminal outcomes or persistence.
D. Cheng and A. Schwartzman, “Expected number and height distribution of
critical points of smooth isotropic Gaussian random fields,” Bernoulli 24(4B)
(2018) 3422–3446 (arXiv:1511.06835); and the value-constrained counts µ_i(X,u)
therein. Relation: exact mean band counts (GOI/GOE representation), the E[# critical
points above/within a level] input, but not the flow-outcome bounding device.
The counting inputs are KNOWN; the specific reduction “P(bad terminal) ≤ E[# band
maxima]” as a persistence tool is NO-CLOSE-MATCH.
ITEM 5 — Mean-flow shadowing / rigidity under conditioning
Ruling: KNOWN-IN-PART. Quantitative shadowing of deterministic flow by small-random-perturbation flow with log-time exit bounds exists in the SGD/Freidlin–Wentzell literature;
adapted to a conditioned Gaussian field it is not located.

W. Hu, C. J. Li, J. Yang, “On the fast convergence of random perturbations of the
gradient flow,” arXiv:1706.00837 (Asymptotic Analysis, 2021). Proves that “when
the potential function is a Morse function with additional strong saddle condition, the
perturbed gradient flow converges to the neighborhood of local minimizers in O(ln(ε⁻¹))
time on the average, where ε is the scale of the random perturbation.” Relation: closest
quantitative random-perturbation-of-gradient-flow shadowing result; general potential,
not a conditioned Gaussian field, and no launch-direction (unstable-eigenvector)
concentration statement.
Freidlin–Wentzell, Random Perturbations of Dynamical Systems (Springer); and
“Most probable escape paths in perturbed gradient systems,” arXiv:2407.18052; “Exit
probabilities … small random perturbations,” arXiv:1408.6260. Relation: large-deviations
exit-time/tube-exit machinery; deterministic-flow tube shadowing with exponential
failure bounds. General setting.
Eigenvector perturbation at a pinned saddle: standard random-matrix Hessian
(GOE/GOI) results (Cheng–Schwartzman; Fyodorov) give the conditioned Hessian law,
from which unstable-eigenvector concentration would follow, but no located work states
the launch-direction concentration for a pinned saddle of a Gaussian field. NO-CLOSE-MATCH for that specific statement.
ITEM 6 — Near-diagonal Kac–Rice repulsion and collar bounds
Ruling: KNOWN. The linear-in-separation vanishing of the two-point critical-point intensity
in 2D is established.
D. Beliaev, V. Cammarota, I. Wigman, “No repulsion between critical points for
planar Gaussian random fields,” Electron. Commun. Probab. 25 (2020), paper 22
(arXiv:1911.03455). Computes the leading near-diagonal asymptotics of the two-point
correlation of critical points; for generic planar fields critical points neither repel nor
attract, with index-dependent short-range behavior. Project Euclid Relation: directly the
near-diagonal two-point intensity; establishes the leading behavior the program uses.
S. Ladgham and R. Lachièze-Rey, “Local repulsion of planar Gaussian critical
points,” Stochastic Process. Appl. (2023) (S0304414923001850). Shows same-type critical points (maxima, or saddles) experience hard local repulsion, quantifying the
second factorial moment in a small ball. Relation: gives the collar/repulsion bounds for
same-index points and the precise small-ball magnitude — the strongest match for the
λ₂ ≤ C|Δ| collar bound.
J.-M. Azaïs and C. Delmas, “Mean number and correlation function of critical
points of isotropic Gaussian fields …,” Stochastic Process. Appl. 150 (2022) 411–
445. Attraction (N>2), neutrality (N=2), repulsion (N=1); strong maxima–minima

repulsion. ScienceDirect Relation: corroborates the N=2 neutrality and index-resolved
behavior.
Also: M. R. Dennis / M. Berry, “Correlations and screening of topological charges in
Gaussian random fields,” J. Phys. A (math-ph/0302024); “Two point function for critical
points of a random plane wave,” arXiv:1704.04943. Relation: earlier topological-charge/critical-point two-point functions.
The linear vanishing (one power from the degenerate-merger Jacobian) is KNOWN via
these; its specific use to bound extra critical points near a conditioned point is an
application, not separately located.
ITEM 7 — Thermodynamic-formalism package for persistence (lower
priority)
Ruling: KNOWN-IN-PART. Persistence entropy is standard; partition-function/free-energy
framings appear recently; a formal “topological second law” is NO-CLOSE-MATCH.
Persistence entropy: H. Chintakunta et al. (original); N. Atienza, R. González-Díaz, M.
Soriano-Trigueros, “Persistent Entropy for Separating Topological Features from Noise
in Vietoris–Rips Complexes,” arXiv:1701.07857 (and stability results). Relation: defines E
= −Ʃ pᵢ log pᵢ with pᵢ = ℓᵢ/L, the Renyi/Shannon persistence entropy the program uses.
Partition-function/free-energy framings (recent): “Persistence diagrams of random
matrices via Morse theory: universality and a new spectral diagnostic,”
arXiv:2603.27903 (closed-form persistence entropy PE_GOE = log(8n/π) − 1);
“Persistent Entropy as a Detector of Phase Transitions,” arXiv:2602.09058; Y.-M. Chung
and A. Lawson, “Persistence Curves,” arXiv:1904.07768 (entropy-based persistence
curves). Relation: closest to Z = Ʃ exp(β·length)-type constructions and free-energy
identities, but none formulates a “topological second law” (monotonicity theorem) for
persistence.
No located work states a topological second law for persistence bars. NO-CLOSE-MATCH
for that piece.
ITEM 8 — The Δ-J parity law (lower priority)
Ruling: KNOWN-IN-PART for the sensitivity phenomenon; NO-CLOSE-MATCH for the
specific odd-part-of-log-g′ parity statement.
A. Cole and G. Shiu, “Persistent Homology and Non-Gaussianity,” JCAP 03 (2018)
025 (arXiv:1712.08159). On simulated CMB maps, “persistence diagrams are more
sensitive to local non-Gaussianity than previous topological statistics including the
genus and Betti number curves, and can constrain Δ fNL^loc = 35.8 at the 68%

confidence level on the simulation set, compared to Δ fNL^loc = 60.6 for the Betti
number curves.” Relation: closest direct evidence that persistence-based statistics
preferentially detect local (quadratic/fNL) non-Gaussianity.
M. Biagetti, A. Cole, G. Shiu, “The Persistence of Large Scale Structures I:
Primordial non-Gaussianity,” JCAP 04 (2021) 061 (arXiv:2009.04819); and J. H. T.
Yip et al., “Cosmology with Persistent Homology,” JCAP (2025) (arXiv:2412.15405).
Biagetti–Cole–Shiu report: “For our best single statistic, running the pipeline on several
cubic volumes of size 40 (Gpc/h)³, we detect fNL^loc=10 at 97.5% confidence on ∼85%
of the volumes.” Relation: matches the claim that persistence statistics are sensitive to
fNL-type quadratic non-Gaussianity; empirical/simulation-based, no analytic parity law.
T. Matsubara and collaborators, weakly non-Gaussian Minkowski-functional
perturbation theory: “Weakly non-Gaussian formula for the Minkowski functionals in
general dimensions,” arXiv:2011.04954; “Analytic Minkowski Functionals of the CMB:
Second-order Non-Gaussianity,” arXiv:1001.2321. Establish the Edgeworth/skewness-parameter expansion of morphological statistics, in which first-order corrections are
governed by skewness (quadratic/odd) terms. Relation: the analytic backbone showing
quadratic (fNL) NG enters at leading (first) order in morphological statistics while cubic
enters later — the closest analytic analogue to the program’s “only the odd part of log g′
contributes at first order,” but for Minkowski functionals, not a persistence asymmetry
functional Δ-J.
The specific parity law for a persistence-based asymmetry functional of f = g(F) is NO-CLOSE-MATCH; the Minkowski-functional perturbation theory is the closest related
technique.
Recommendations
1. Item 1 — treat as an open result and secure the proof route. The absence of a
published a.s. Morse–Smale theorem for Gaussian fields is well-supported; this justifies
changing the register in the program. Build the proof on Lerario–Stecconi’s probabilistic
transversality (arXiv:1902.03805), but be explicit that their jet-transversality is local and
must be upgraded to the global heteroclinic condition — this is exactly the gap. Cite
Kupka–Smale/Peixoto/Abraham–Robbin for the deterministic genericity backdrop and
Adler–Taylor/Nicolaescu for the weaker a.s. Morse baseline. Threshold that would
change this ruling: locating any theorem asserting a.s. transversality of stable/unstable
manifold intersections (not merely jets) for a random field.
2. Items 2–5 — position as first explicit quantitative results, citing the component
machinery. For Item 2 cite Chazal–Divol and Thomas for the expected-diagram
framework; for Item 4 cite Muirhead (shrinking windows) and Cheng–Schwartzman

(band counts); for Item 5 cite Hu–Li–Yang and Freidlin–Wentzell. In each case state
clearly that the pairing-defect rate / flow-outcome bound is not in these sources.
3. Item 6 — cite as KNOWN and lean on it. Beliaev–Cammarota–Wigman and Ladgham–
Lachièze-Rey give the near-diagonal two-point behavior and same-index hard repulsion
directly; use them rather than re-deriving.
4. Items 7–8 — cite at survey depth. Use Atienza et al. for persistence entropy, the 2026
arXiv preprints for partition-function framings (flagging them as very recent and not
peer-reviewed), and Cole–Shiu / Biagetti–Cole–Shiu plus Matsubara for the non-Gaussianity sensitivity; state that the topological second law and the Δ-J parity law are
not located.
Caveats
Several supporting sources for Items 7–8 are 2026 arXiv preprints (e.g.,
arXiv:2603.27903, arXiv:2602.09058) that may not be peer-reviewed; treat their
specific numbers as provisional.
The ΔfNL^loc = 35.8 (68% CL) figure belongs to Cole–Shiu 2018 (arXiv:1712.08159), not
the 2021 large-scale-structure paper; the two Biagetti–Cole–Shiu / Cole–Shiu results
address CMB and halo distributions respectively and should not be conflated.
Absence-of-result rulings reflect the documented queries; a targeted
journal/INSPIRE/zbMATH search could still surface a specialized result, especially for
Items 2 and 8.
The Lerario–Stecconi assessment for Item 1 is based on the stated theorems (jet
transversality); a careful reading of their applications companion (arXiv:1906.04444)
could conceivably extend to some global statements, but nothing located claims the
Morse–Smale conclusion.
The web_search budget was exhausted mid-search; a few intended queries (Melnikov-for-random-fields; Bargmann–Fock-specific persistence pairing) returned limited
primary-source confirmation and their NO-CLOSE-MATCH rulings rest partly on that
incomplete search rather than exhaustive absence.
Documented search queries (for absence-of-result rulings)
Item 1: “Morse-Smale Gaussian random field saddle connections”; “Nicolaescu random
Morse function critical points”; “almost surely Morse-Smale random field proof no saddle
connection generic”; “parametric transversality theorem generic Gaussian random field
Cameron-Martin”; “characteristic kernel injectivity Gaussian RKHS signed measures”;
“Melnikov function random perturbation separatrix splitting heteroclinic transverse”; plus

subagent queries on a.s. Morse-Smale, Lerario–Stecconi jet transversality, Bobrowski–
Borman tameness, Kupka–Smale/Peixoto/Abraham–Robbin. Item 2: “expected persistence
diagram stationary Gaussian process small persistence pairs asymptotics”; “persistent
homology Gaussian random field Bobrowski Adler”. Item 3: “kriging variance screening
effect analytic covariance Gaussian process prediction”; “Palm distribution conditional
intensity critical points Gaussian field conditional mean shape”. Item 4: “Kac-Rice expected
number critical points value band level window Gaussian field”; “critical points height
window shrinking Gaussian field second moment Estrade Fournier”. Item 5: “random
perturbation deterministic gradient flow shadowing exit probability tube”. Item 6: “two-point
correlation critical points Gaussian field small separation repulsion”. Item 7: “persistence
entropy thermodynamic formalism partition function persistence diagram”; “topological
