File 1 — Architectural Overview and Core Theorems
The Elder-Rule Selection Constant and the Near-Diagonal Law
for H0 Persistence of Smooth Gaussian Fields on the Two-Torus
Program artifact class: Manuscript, flagship file (nomenclature-setting). Epistemic status
header (binding on all files): every numbered statement in this manuscript carries exactly
one of the labels [PROVEN-HERE], [PROVEN-MODULO: <named lemmas>], [OPEN],
[CONJECTURE], [RETRACTED-SUPERSEDED]. A statement’s label is part of the statement.
The kill registry (Section 9) travels with the manuscript. Calibration archive: cycles C001–
C005 plus the C005R re-adjudication, with hashed prediction snapshots and observed
updates; hash chain referenced in Section 8.4.
0. Notation and global conventions
Fixed throughout the entire manuscript sequence; subsequent files inherit this section
verbatim.
T_L^2 = R^2 / (L Z)^2, the flat two-torus of side L >= 1, with L FIXED. Points x = (x_1,
x_2); d(x, y) the quotient (flat) metric; Lebesgue measure dx with |T_L^2| = L^2.
f : T_L^2 -> R, a centered Gaussian random field, law P, expectation E. Covariance C(x) =
E[f(y) f(y + x)] (stationarity), C(0) = 1 (unit variance). We do NOT assume isotropy: C(x)
need not depend on |x| alone. See Scope Remark 3.4.
Spectral measure rho on the dual lattice (2 pi / L) Z^2, with C(x) = sum_k rho(k)
e^{i<k,x>}. “Spectral density positive on an open set” refers to the continuum
idealization; the operative torus form is the finite-jet nondegeneracy it implies,
hypothesis (H2’) below.
Spectral moment tensors: Lambda_2 = Cov(grad f) (2x2); Lambda_4, Lambda_6,
Lambda_8 the covariance tensors of the second-, third-, and fourth- derivative
Gaussian vectors at a point. Nondegeneracy of Lambda_{2j} means the full order-j
derivative vector has nondegenerate covariance.
Derivatives: grad f = (f_1, f_2); D^2 f the Hessian with entries f_{ij}; D^3 f the symmetric

third-derivative tensor; for a unit vector v, f_{vvv} = D^3 f[v, v, v].
Crit(f) = { x : grad f(x) = 0 }. Under (H1+)-(H2’), f is a.s. Morse with pairwise distinct
critical values (File 2). Index 0 = local minimum, 1 = saddle, 2 = local maximum.
Superlevel sets: E_t = { x : f(x) >= t }, filtration DESCENDING in t. H0(E_t) = components;
all H0 statements are coefficient-independent.
Elder rule. As t decreases, a component is born at t = f(m) for each local maximum m;
components merge at index-1 critical values. At a merge, the component with the
SMALLER birth value (the younger) dies; its H0 bar is [f(s), f(m)] where s is the merging
saddle. D(m) denotes the death saddle of m; on the torus exactly one component per
realization is essential. Lifetime: ell(m) = f(m) - f(D(m)). dgm(f) = { (f(m), f(D(m))) : m
non-essential local maximum }.
Fold pairs. (m, s) with m a local maximum, s an index-1 saddle, is an r-FOLD PAIR at
height b when d(m, s) = r, f(m) = b, f(s) = b - ell, ell > 0, and s is GRADIENT-ADJACENT
to m: one ascending separatrix of s (maximal integral curve of grad f emanating from s)
terminates at m. The fold normal form (Section 5.1) locks gap to separation: ell = (kappa
/ 6) r^3 (1 + o(1)), r -> 0, (0.1) kappa = |f_{vvv}(x_0)| along the soft direction at the
midpoint x_0 = (m + s)/2. (0.1) is elementary singularity theory, [PROVEN-HERE] (fold-coordinates file); it is link L1 of the program and is verified in-distribution (log-log slope
3.01 in the session-1 archive; 2.883 [2.388, 3.347] under the C005 protocol).
Selection probability. For r > 0 small and b in a compact B, with respect to the Palm
distribution of r-fold pairs at height b (Kac-Rice Palm formalism for critical pairs, File 5
series): q(r, b) = P( D(m) = s | (m, s) an r-fold pair at height b ). (0.2)
Near-diagonal bar density. N(ell_1, ell_2; B) = expected number of H0 bars with lifetime
in [ell_1, ell_2] and birth in B; nu(ell) is the expected bar count density per unit lifetime
as ell -> 0 (birth marginalized over compact B), when it exists.
Asymptotics: a ~ b means a/b -> 1; O, o, Theta standard; constants C, c > 0 may change
line to line and are uniform in b on compacts and in r <= r_0 unless stated otherwise.
u-variable (dimensionless separation, for contact with the calibration archive): u = r
sqrt(lambda_4 / lambda_2) with scalar isotropic moments; in the anisotropic setting the
microscale normalization is direction- dependent and appears only in numerical scope
remarks.
1. Hypotheses
(H1+) f is a centered stationary Gaussian field on T_L^2 with unit variance and C^3 sample

paths; Lambda_2, Lambda_4, Lambda_6 are nondegenerate; and Lambda_8 is finite (sum_k
|k|^8 rho(k) < infinity).
Role of Lambda_8 < infinity: used ONLY for the sharp tau^4 residual scaling in the annulus
estimate (Lemma A’) and hence for the sharp remainder rate in (2.2). If Lambda_8 = infinity
but the field has effective spectral smoothness nu in (3, 4) (spectral tail |k|^{-2(nu+1)}), the
pinned residual scales as tau^{nu + 1/2}, all suppression factors remain super-polynomial,
and Theorems A and B survive with degraded, nu-dependent correction constants. That
degradation is the theoretical counterpart of the kernel-ordered finite-u deficits measured
in calibration cycle C005 (finding F2): mechanism [PROVEN-MODULO: Lemma P general-nu
variant]; the constants themselves [OPEN].
(H2’) The spectral measure has, in the continuum idealization, a density positive on an
open set; operatively we assume the finite-jet nondegeneracy consequence: for every finite
family of derivative functionals { D^{alpha_i} f(y_i) }, |alpha_i| <= 4, at finitely many distinct
points, the joint Gaussian law is nondegenerate, with two-sided quantitative rates at
collision governed by Taylor order (Lemma H, quantitative jet nondegeneracy, [PROVEN-HERE] in File 2 via polynomial determinacy: Var(linear functional minus regression) =
integral |Q(k)|^2 d rho(k) > 0 for nonzero polynomials Q).
Remark 1.1 (economy of hypotheses). Earlier drafts carried a separate hypothesis (H3)
(sixth-order regression nondegeneracy). (H3) is REDUNDANT given (H2’) via Lemma H; it is
demoted to a lemma. The hypothesis set of the entire manuscript is (H1+) and (H2’) only.
[PROVEN-HERE, File 2.]
Remark 1.2 (what is NOT assumed). No isotropy. No covariance positivity (no FKG input;
percolation machinery is unused at fixed L, Section 7.1). No sign or threshold condition on
the height b beyond compactness of its range. The b-uniformity of Theorem A —
contradicting the b-threshold refinement proposed in the program’s ancestral document —
was predicted by the present architecture and confirmed across cycles C001-C005 (q flat in
b across quartiles; pre-registered rule 3 null).
2. The main theorems
Theorem A (elder-rule selection constant; q0 = 1). [PROVEN-MODULO: Lemma P
(Pinning), Lemma I (inner two-scale blow-up nondegeneracy), Sublemma R0 (Morse-Smale
genericity). All remaining ingredients — Reduction Lemma R with Sublemmas R1-R3, far-field Lemma G, annulus Lemma A’, band Lemmas B0-B1 — are proven in this manuscript
sequence, G and A’ carrying finite-dimensional Gaussian-regression obligations executed in
their own files.]

Let f satisfy (H1+) and (H2’) on T_L^2, L fixed, and let B subset R be compact. With q(r, b)
as in (0.2):
 lim_{r -> 0} q(r, b) = 1, uniformly for b in B. (2.1)
The proof yields the quantitative remainder
 1 - q(r, b) <= C(L, B) [ r^3 + r^beta ] + C exp(-c / r^2), (2.2)
where beta > 0 is the exponent of Lemma I (candidate value beta = 4, [CONJECTURE] at the
level of the exact exponent; any beta > 0 suffices for (2.1); beta >= 3 preserves the r^3
remainder). The matching lower bound 1 - q >= c r^3 is [OPEN] (Section 7.2).
Interpretation. The geometric fold partner of a maximum is, asymptotically almost surely,
its homological death partner: geometry determines homology at the diagonal, with
selection constant exactly one. No height threshold, covariance sign condition, or isotropy
enters.
Theorem B (near-diagonal H0 bar-density law). [PROVEN-MODULO: Theorem A’s lemma
set, plus Proposition B2 (pair-intensity nondegeneration, the program’s link L2).]
Under (H1+)-(H2’) on T_L^2, the expected H0 persistence diagram of the superlevel
filtration satisfies
 nu(ell) = C_* ell^{-1/3} (1 + o(1)), ell -> 0, (2.3)
with
 C_* = (1/3) integral_B h(b) J(b) db in (0, infinity), (2.4)
where h is the height density of the participating maxima and J(b) packages the fold-pair
intensity: writing rho_pair(r; b) for the Palm intensity of r-fold pairs at height b, Proposition
B2 asserts rho_pair(r; b) -> rho_0(b) in (0, infinity) as r -> 0 (neutrality at contact of the
adjacent-index channel in dimension 2); the change of variables ell = (kappa/6) r^3 (so that
r dr is proportional to ell^{-1/3} d ell) then yields (2.3)-(2.4) with the kappa-law folded into
J(b). The selection factor in (2.3) is EXACTLY 1 by Theorem A: no selection constant
appears in C_*.
Proposition B2’s two-point input is verified literature: Azais & Delmas, Stochastic Process.
Appl. 150 (2022) 411-445 (attraction for N > 2, NEUTRALITY for N = 2, repulsion for N = 1),
corroborated by Beliaev, Cammarota & Wigman, Electron. Commun. Probab. 25 (2020),
paper 82. The uniform-in-r conditional version required here (convergence of the fold-pair

Palm intensity, not merely the two-point limit) is [PROVEN-MODULO: the L2 degeneration
computation, executed in its own file; its Bargmann-Fock instance is a finite symbolic
computation].
Remark 2.1 (empirical status). In the calibration archive: q measured at 1.000 [0.957,
1.000] in the smallest resolvable separation bin, monotone in r, b-uniform, covariance-sign-indifferent, and dimension-free at matched microscale for u < 1.7 (cluster-robust, Holm-corrected, re-adjudication C005R); the r^3 lock (0.1) verified in-distribution. These are
Reported trend measurements at r/xi >= 0.3. The r -> 0 statements (2.1) and (2.3) are
strictly the theorems’ content, not the measurements’.
3. Novelty statement and prior art
[All citations below were located and setting-classified in the program’s primary-source
verification sweep; zero-tolerance provenance applies.]
3.1 The headline claims are, to the best of a systematic search, new. No published or
preprint result was located that proves a persistence- pairing SELECTION law — identifying
WHICH saddle is the elder-rule death partner of a given maximum, with probability — for
random fields in dimension >= 2. Both claims,
(i) q0 = 1: the geometric fold partner is asymptotically a.s. the homological death partner
(Theorem A), and (ii) the ell^{-1/3} near-diagonal law with unit selection factor (Theorem B),
have no located antecedent for smooth fields in dimension two or higher.
3.2 The 1D contrast (sharpening, not eroding, the novelty). Exact pairing laws DO exist
in one dimension:
Rychlik, I., “A new definition of the rainflow cycle counting method,” Int. J. Fatigue 9
(1987) 119-121: the exact min-max (rainflow) pairing law for 1D processes. Setting: 1D,
exact, non-asymptotic. Classification: morally related; non-overlapping.
Baryshnikov, Y., “Brownian motions, persistent homology and chirality,” J. Appl. Comput.
Topology 9(4), Article 28, 2025; DOI: 10.1007/s41468-025-00224-w (preprint
arXiv:1909.09846): elder-rule persistence laws for Brownian motion. Setting: 1D,
Brownian (non-smooth) regularity. Classification: adjacent — the same homological
pairing object, one dimension down, where the death partner is combinatorially forced
by the total order of the path.
In dimension two the merge structure is mediated by saddle geometry and nothing is
combinatorially forced; the content of Theorem A is precisely that fold geometry forces the
homology asymptotically. This dimensional dichotomy — exact 1D laws versus a newly

proven 2D asymptotic selection law — is the core of the novelty claim.
3.3 What adjacent literature supplies, and what it does not.
Critical-pair correlations at collision: Azais & Delmas (SPA 150, 2022; neutrality in d = 2)
and Ladgham & Lachieze-Rey (SPA 166 (2023) 104221; arXiv:2209.04150; same-index
hard repulsion, minimal repulsion factor 1/(8 sqrt 3)) furnish the two-point inputs used in
Proposition B2 and in Lemma I’s zone analysis. NO located work performs the THREE-point Kac-Rice expansion under two-scale degeneration (pair separation ~ r, third point
at ~ r^2) that Lemma I requires: per the sweep this is a genuine literature gap and the
program’s central open technical object (Section 5.3).
Small bars and universality: the Bobrowski-Skraba universality line (arXiv:2406.05553)
concerns geometric filtrations over point processes, not superlevel filtrations of smooth
fields: morally related only. Persistence-measure frameworks (Chazal-Divol line) provide
the measure-theoretic frame for nu(ell), not a law.
Morse-Smale genericity (our Sublemma R0): an explicit almost-sure no-saddle-connection statement for stationary Gaussian fields was NOT located in the required
form (folklore-gap flag from the sweep). R0 is therefore proven here rather than cited;
the risk is bibliographic, not mathematical.
Palm/Slepian conditioning at critical points: single-point Slepian models are classical
(Lindgren; Azais & Wschebor, Level Sets and Extrema of Random Processes and Fields,
Wiley, 2009). The critical- PAIR version with degenerating-constraint uniformity — and
the observation that pair conditioning PINS the on-axis cubic coefficient (Lemma P) —
was not located anywhere and is claimed as new. Lemma P is simultaneously the
program’s most consequential and most elementary novel ingredient.
3.4 Scope Remark (isotropy and the calibration archive). Theorems A and B are stated
and proved in anisotropic-capable form: hypotheses (H1+) and (H2’) only; the fold chart,
Pinning Lemma, and window machinery are direction-covariant and never invoke isotropy.
However, EVERY numerical artifact in the calibration archive (C001-C005, C005R:
Bargmann-Fock in d = 2, 3; Matern nu = 3.5, 2.5) is isotropic. The anisotropic sector is
analytically supported but numerically untested; an anisotropic calibration arm is queued
(Section 8.3). Inherited stress-table expectation, consistent with the present proof:
anisotropy shifts constants (kappa, mu, directional microscales), never exponents.
4. Architectural overview: the reduction
Design principle: make the topology deterministic and push ALL probability into counting
statements.

Step 1 (topology; zero probability content). The Reduction Lemma.
Lemma R. On the fold-pair Palm event, { D(m) != s } is contained in A_w UNION A_loop
UNION A_0, where A_w = { exists critical y not in {m, s} : f(y) in [b - ell, b] } (the VALUE-WINDOW event); A_loop = { both ascending separatrices of s terminate at m }; A_0 = { two
critical values coincide }, with P(A_0) = 0. [PROVEN-HERE], decomposed as: R0 (a.s. no
saddle-saddle gradient connections, so ascending separatrices terminate at maxima and
the merge partner’s root maximum is well-defined) — [to prove; folklore gap]; R1 (on A_w^c
the component of m is a closed disk containing only m down to level (b - ell)+ : global
regularity of window levels, merge-exclusion for higher-valued critical points, gradient
retraction, lift to the universal cover) — [PROVEN]; R2 (Local Saddle Attachment: an index-1
passage attaches a 1-handle whose feet lie in the components of the two ascending
separatrices’ terminal maxima; merge iff distinct, handle iff equal — and equal, given R1, is
exactly A_loop) — [PROVEN]; R3 (elder bookkeeping: on A_w^c the merge partner’s root
maximum has value > b, hence the partner is elder and m dies at s) — [PROVEN].
Both classical failure channels — “preemptive elder connection” and “younger neighbor
across s” — are instances of A_w: ONE counting lemma carries the theorem.
Step 2 (zoned counting). Bound E[# window critical points | pair] by zones around the
midpoint x_0:
Lemma G (far, d >= delta): the conditional density of (f, grad f)(y) given the six Palm
constraints stays bounded as r -> 0, via RESCALING the constraints (value combinations
by r^3, gradient combinations by r^2, r^3) into a frame converging to a nondegenerate
limit — the precise sense in which midpoint-jet reparametrization prevents degeneration.
Window width then gives E[N_far] <= C(L, delta) ell. [PROVEN-MODULO: executed
regression bookkeeping.]
Lemma A’ (annulus, 3r <= d <= delta): E[N_ann] <= C(delta) ell, the annulus interior
contributing only exp(-c/tau^2)-suppressed mass; no K-parameter, no logarithm.
Powered by Lemma P; supersedes the K^-3 architecture (kill registry K2). [PROVEN-MODULO: Lemma P + density bounds.]
Lemma I (inner): localization — conditionally on the pair, any third critical point within 3r
of x_0 lies within C r^2 of m or s, up to exp(-c/r^2) tails — then E[N_inn] <= C r^beta,
beta > 0. [Localization PROVEN-MODULO Lemma P; the counting bound OPEN: Section
5.3.]
Lemmas B0-B1 (loop absorption): A_loop is NOT contained in A_w (the crater
counterexample: a circular ridge carrying exactly one maximum and one saddle, with the
crater floor far below the window — so no topological elimination exists). But
monotonicity of f along separatrices confines the loop to the value band (B0,
deterministic); the band on the circle of radius 3r is exp(-c/r^2)-improbable under the

Pinning scalings (B1); the residual in-ball loop event lands in Lemma I’s zone. W-loop is
thereby DELETED as an independent probabilistic node. [PROVEN-MODULO: B1
chaining bound.]
Step 3 (assembly). 1 - q <= C(L) ell + C(delta) ell + C r^beta + C exp(-c/r^2) + 0, which is
(2.2). Theorem B follows via (0.1) and Proposition B2. There is NO two-parameter (K, r) limit
anywhere in this architecture; its former necessity was an artifact of weaker conditioning
(kill registry, K2).
5. The three machinery pillars (roadmap for subsequent files)
5.1 Fold coordinates and Sublemma R0 (Morse-theoretic layer). Fold chart at x_0:
coordinates (t, s) with conditional mean m(t, s) = b + kappa (t^3/3 - a t) - (mu/2) s^2 +
O(|y|^4), a = r^2/4; normal-form critical points at t = -+ sqrt(a) (maximum, saddle); the lock
(0.1); and the exact BAND STRUCTURE: with p(t) = t^3/3 - a t, the axis set { t : p(t) in [p(sqrt
a), p(-sqrt a)] } is precisely [-2 sqrt a, +2 sqrt a] = [-r, r], with exit rate kappa tau^3/3
beyond it. This elementary fact powers Lemmas A’ and B1. Sublemma R0 supplies the a.s.
Morse-Smale property; per the sweep it is a folklore gap, hence proven, not cited.
5.2 The Pinning Lemma (critical-pair Palm conditioning; new). The Palm conditioning
supplies six linear constraints, (f, grad f)(+- x_r/2) = ((b, 0), (b - ell, 0)). Lemma P: after
removing the midpoint 2-jet, these DETERMINE the on-axis cubic coefficient c_{t^3} and
the mixed coefficient c_{t^2 s}, leaving as leading free directions only { t s^2, s^3 } at third
order and, on the axis, the one-dimensional constrained quartic family (t^2 - r^2/4)^2.
Consequences, uniform for b in compacts and 3r <= tau <= delta: sd(f | pair) <= C ( tau^4 +
|t| s^2 + |s|^3 ), sd(f_t | pair) <= C tau^3, sd(f_s | pair) <= C tau^3, with matching lower
bounds from Lemma H. Mean-to-sd ratios (kappa tau^3 vs tau^4 for the value; kappa tau^2
vs tau^3 for the gradient) are Theta(1/tau), yielding exp(-c/tau^2) suppression — the single
mechanism behind A’, B1, and Lemma I’s localization. Lemma P is finite-dimensional
Gaussian regression: an executed-obligation item, not a research risk. Requires Lambda_8 <
infinity for the stated exponents; general-nu variant per (H1+).
5.3 The three-point Kac-Rice expansion under two-scale degeneration (Lemma I; the
research frontier). Required: boundedness of the conditional third-critical-point intensity
at s + r^2 z, |z| <= C, given the fold pair — equivalently, nondegeneracy at the correct
leading order of the 15 x 15 covariance matrix of the jets (f, grad f, D^2 f) at the three points
(x_m, x_s, x_s + r^2 z) under the two-scale degeneration |x_s - x_m| ~ r, |y - x_s| ~ r^2, r ->
0. Per the sweep, no two-scale three-point expansion exists in the literature; the nearest
tools are the two-point expansions of Azais-Delmas and Ladgham-Lachieze-Rey. Candidate
exponent beta = 4 (area (r^2)^2 times bounded intensity). Executable fallback: symbolic
assembly of the 15 x 15 covariance for the Bargmann-Fock kernel and series expansion of

its determinant in r; a degenerate leading term falsifies the beta > 0 route and forces a
different blow-up. This is the single point where the program can fail as architected.
6. Theorem-to-lemma dependency graph (normative)
Theorem B <- Theorem A + Proposition B2 (L2 degeneration) + (0.1) Theorem A <- Lemma
R + Lemma G + Lemma A’ + Lemma I + Lemmas B0-B1 Lemma R <- R0 [to prove; folklore
gap] + R1 [proven] + R2 [proven] + R3 [proven] Lemma A’ <- Lemma P [finite-dimensional;
to execute] + Lemma H [proven] Lemma B1 <- Lemma P Lemma G <- Lemma H + rescaled-frame convergence [to execute] Lemma I <- two-scale three-point Kac-Rice nondegeneracy
[OPEN] Lemma H <- (H2’) [proven]
Load-bearing OPEN set: { Lemma I }. Executed-obligation set (no new ideas required): {
Lemma P, Lemma G bookkeeping, B1 chaining, R0 page, Proposition B2’s degeneration
computation }.
7. Boundary of validity; deliberate exclusions
7.1 Fixed L only. The thermodynamic limit L -> infinity before r -> 0 is excluded by design:
there E[N_far] ~ L^2 ell diverges, and controlling the reach of m’s component at height b re-introduces percolation inputs (subcritical exponential decay for b above the critical level; the
complementary case genuinely different). The ancestral document’s percolation machinery
is thereby RELOCATED, not refuted: it belongs to the infinite-volume extension, where a b-dependence of the CORRECTION (never of the fixed-L limit) may genuinely reappear.
[Extension OPEN.]
7.2 Rates. (2.2) is an upper-bound architecture; the matching lower bound 1 - q >= c ell (a
far window maximum adjacent to m’s growing component preempts with positive
conditional probability) is plausible and [OPEN]. Measured effective slopes of log(1 - q) vs
log r in the accessible window (~1.9, C005R) are pre-asymptotic measurements carrying no
theoretical commitment.
7.3 Below C^3. For smoothness nu < 3 the fold normal form fails; the lock deforms to ell ~
r^{2 + gamma}, gamma = nu - 2 (one supporting measurement: slope 2.373 [2.135, 2.636]
at nu = 2.5, excluding 3), and the near-diagonal law is conjectured to become nu(ell) ~ ell^{-
gamma/(2+gamma)} [CONJECTURE]. Theorems A-B claim nothing below C^3.
8. Calibration interface (summary; full artifacts in archive files)

8.1 Findings consistent with, and in part predicted by, this architecture: q -> 1 monotone, b-uniform, covariance-sign-indifferent; dimension-free q(u) for u < 1.7 (d2 vs d3, cluster-robust, Holm-corrected); kernel-ordered finite-u corrections (Bargmann-Fock > Matern 3.5
> Matern 2.5) matching the tau^{nu-3} residual-degradation mechanism of (H1+). 8.2
Nothing in the archive contradicts Theorems A-B. The failed predictions of record (the b-threshold refinement; the K^-3 floor) were failures of SUPERSEDED architectures, both
preserved in Section 9. 8.3 Queued numerics: cycle C006 (window-count law E[N_w] ~ r^3
and inner localization fractions — the sharpest falsifiable consequences of Lemma P); an
anisotropic arm; the sub-C^3 diagram exponent. 8.4 Hash chain C001 -> C005R with
snapshot-before-evidence ordering verified for every cycle; reproduced verbatim in the
archive file.
9. Kill registry (binding; travels with the manuscript)
K1 [RETRACTED]. The r^{6/5} rate for 1 - q, from balancing a K^-3 window cost against
P(nearby critical point) ~ (Kr)^2: invalid — PRESENCE of a nearby critical point is not
PREEMPTION; only window-valued points preempt. No downstream dependence.
K2 [RETRACTED-SUPERSEDED]. The O(K^-3) annulus floor and the two-parameter (K, r)
limit: artifacts of conditioning on the midpoint 2-jet ONLY. Full Palm pair conditioning pins
c_{t^3} and c_{t^2 s} (Lemma P), upgrading the residual scale from tau^3 to tau^4 on the
effective strip and replacing the floor with exp(-c/tau^2) suppression. The earlier statement
was a valid non-sharp upper bound; its “structural discovery” framing is retracted.
Superseded by Lemma A’.
K3 [RETRACTED, ancestral]. The b-threshold refinement (q0(b) > 0 only above the
percolation threshold): dissolved at fixed L by the present architecture; empirically null (pre-registered rule 3, C001+). Percolation content relocated to the L -> infinity extension (7.1).
End of File 1. Subsequent files inherit Sections 0-1 verbatim as the normative environment
and are numbered against the dependency graph of Section 6.

hash bb3d4aa2…; window-lemma-track, from the v2 pass Section 8) and freezing them
separately would double-count scenario weights and split the governance record. This
document merges them into ONE cycle with one scenario assignment.

Arms
ARM 1 — Window-count scaling and localization (the (ND) numerical pre-adjudicator;
runs FIRST because it gates the boss fight). Measurables, per mutual fold pair (M, S) at
separation r on BF d2, n = 512, L = 40: N_w(r) = #{ critical points x != M, S : f(x) in [f(S),
f(M)], dist(x, {M,S}) <= delta = 2 } D_min = dist of nearest such point from {M, S},
conditional on N_w >= 1. Registered predictions: P1 (slope): log-log slope of E[N_w] vs r on r
in [0.45, 0.85] equals 3.0 +/- 0.5 (bootstrap CI rule; per- sub-window slopes reported to
expose pre-asymptotic bias). P2 (localization): >= 70% of window points at distance <= 3r
from the pair; <= 20% in the annulus [3r, delta]. P3 (kernel arm): E[N_w]/ell at matched u is
LARGER for Matern nu = 3.5 (n = 1024) than for BF — the tau^{nu-3} residual mechanism
(File 4, Prop. P5; File 6, Section 6.2(c)). Branch adjudication (pre-committed interpretation,
File 3 Remark 8.1):
P1 pass + P2 pass => pinning architecture CONFIRMED numerically; (ND)’s clean branch

(beta = 4) gains its pre-adjudication; the symbolic computation proceeds as
confirmation.
P2 FAIL by annulus excess (> 20%) => Lemma P’s consequence is numerically falsified;

P1 fail with P2 pass => pre-asymptotic regime flagged; extend the r-window before

1 THE GATE FRAMEWORK — MASTER GATE FILE
1.1 Reconciled standalone specification for proof-carrying reasoning
Version: Master v1.2 (reconciled)
Date: 2026-07-17
Status: current successor specification
Supersedes without overwriting:
• Master v1.0 PDF;
• uploaded Master v1.1 Markdown;
• C095 executable-specification line also named v1.1.
Established machinery: one mandatory SCHEMA preflight, 16 numbered gates, five typed schema profiles,
canonical dependency hashes, and explicit conditional-debt propagation.
Standalone notice. This document contains the complete conceptual and machine-contract speci-fication. It can be implemented without any earlier Q0 file. Earlier versions remain indispensable
provenance and retrodiction evidence, but they are not needed to understand or apply this version.
2 0. Constitutional statement
2.1 0.1 The core rule
Name the restriction; gate the drop; grade the bridge.
A claim is established within a regime. Reusing it outside that regime is a new claim. The reuse is permitted only
when:
1. the restriction is retained; or
2. a first-class bridge node explicitly carries the source regime into the deployment regime; and
3. that bridge is itself graded, evidenced, and admitted by the dependency rules.
The framework therefore operates on three objects at once:
• claims;
• dependency edges;
• bridges, witnesses, and certificates as claims in their own right.
2.2 0.2 What a machine can certify
A proof object is a type. A gate is a typing rule.
Every substantive gate has two layers.
2.2.1 Shell
The shell is mechanically decidable from the declared proof object:
• required fields exist;
3

• domains are contained;
• measures and models match;
• marks appear in the evidence cone;
• a product points to an operation-compatible witness;
• a displayed coefficient recomputes conservatively;
• an edge pins the current canonical hash of its dependency.
2.2.2 Core
The core is the mathematics asserted by those declarations:
• the independence theorem is true;
• the change-of-measure formula is valid;
• the interval proof encloses the real function;
• the failure-region enumeration is complete;
• the cited source actually says what the node claims.
The machine certifies tag consistency and arithmetic-contract consistency. It does not, by itself, certify
tag-to-content fidelity.
That limitation is not a defect to hide. It determines the division of labor:
Gates classify and block structurally invalid reuse. Proofs, recomputation, adversarial
reimplementation, source retrieval, and separated adjudication detect content error.
2.3 0.3 Verdicts
Every applicable gate returns:
• PASS — its shell obligation is discharged;
• FAIL — promotion is blocked;
• PROVISIONAL — the claim remains usable only under a stated warrant cap;
• NOT-APPLICABLE — the operation guarded by that gate is absent.
A gate PASS never means “the theorem is true.” It means:
“The claim is consistent under its declared tags, certificates, and dependency objects, conditional on
those declarations being faithful.”
2.4 0.4 Promotion classes
A graph may be admitted in three different senses:
2.4.1 Archive admission
The graph is structurally valid and hash-consistent. It may contain open, killed, superseded, provisional, or non-promotable claims for provenance.
2.4.2 Candidate admission
The selected roots pass every shell gate, although they may remain explicitly conditional or provisional according
to their grade contract.
2.4.3 Promotion admission
The roots pass every shell gate at their stated warrant. A Proven-Modulo root may promote only as an explic-itly conditional theorem whose complete condition set is displayed. Unconditional promotion requires an empty
condition set.
These states must not be collapsed into one word such as “admitted.”
4

3 1. Lineage reconciliation
Three partially divergent artifacts preceded this version.
3.1 1.1 Master v1.0 PDF
The PDF introduced the restriction-drop framework, 13 gates, and F-1. It overstated the framework as “me-chanically checkable,” treated bridges largely as free-text attestations, placed assumptions, warrants, and terminal
statuses on one ladder, and contained a dangling PROVISIONAL reference.
It is preserved as the origin document, not the current specification.
3.2 1.2 Uploaded Master v1.1 Markdown
The uploaded Markdown made the decisive conceptual repairs:
• shell/core honesty;
• “gates classify; disciplines detect”;
• bridges and witnesses as graded dependency nodes;
• Derived as self-tier dependable;
• content-hash pinning and stale-PASS discipline;
• a second-domain worked example;
• candidate HASH-DRIFT and UNIFORMITY rules.
Those repairs are retained here.
3.3 1.3 C095 executable-specification line
The C095 line separately added machine profiles needed by recorded arithmetic failures:
• SCHEMA preflight;
• establishment and deployment regimes;
• ASSEMBLY;
• DOMAIN-INFIMUM;
• BAND-PROVENANCE;
• certificate objects for common-mode and coverage;
• a second-domain executable contract.
Those additions are integrated here rather than maintained as a competing v1.1.
3.4 1.4 Why v1.2 changes the established count
The uploaded v1.1 correctly refused to mint new gates without retrodiction. Subsequent frozen failures supplied
the evidence:
3.4.1 ASSEMBLY
• an upper display rounded (4.35) downward to (4.3);
• a first-moment coefficient (0.8411) was displayed before applying subunit AO and Bonferroni losses.
3.4.2 UNIFORMITY / DOMAIN-EXTREMUM
• sampled upper rungs were used toward a continuous finite-range claim without between-rung control;
• the sampled Bonferroni threshold exceeded 80 while the full-domain limit was (79.9889203915…).
3.4.3 BAND-PROVENANCE
• an unexplained (±0.02) band entered an upper theorem;
• a randomized orthant diagnostic changed between releases because its algorithmic state was not frozen.
5

These are independent enough, selective over the failure record, and not mechanically discharged by the original
gates. Gates 14–16 are therefore established in v1.2.
4 2. Proof-object schema
Every externally visible claim is an atomic proof object.
4.1 2.1 Identity and provenance
field obligation
claim_id globally unique, stable identifier
statement one atomic assertion
kind statement, assumption, definition, measurement,
bridge, witness, or certificate
source_precedence_id source/supersession lineage
evidence_ids immutable proof, computation, measurement, or source
objects
supersedes claim IDs replaced by this object
alias_of explicit content alias, if any
content_hash canonical SHA-256 of every load-bearing field
status live, open, killed, superseded, or retired
A human label such as C#1 is not a content hash.
4.2 2.2 Logical fields
field obligation
quantifier exact, for-all, exists, asymptotic, typical,
measured-at-rung, or conditional
quantifier_order explicit when two or more quantifiers interact
direction upper, lower, equality, structural, or none
bound_coefficient displayed coefficient for a numerical bound
conditional_on complete finite set of unresolved conditions
closed_core whether the claim asserts an unconditional finished core
4.3 2.3 Epistemic fields
The following are independent axes.
4.3.1 Claim status
• LIVE
• OPEN
• KILLED
• SUPERSEDED
• RETIRED
4.3.2 Assumption role
• NONE
• DEFINITION
• PRIMITIVE-HYPOTHESIS
• POLICY-THRESHOLD
6

4.3.3 Warrant
• PROVEN
• PROVEN-MODULO
• CERTIFIED
• DERIVED
• LITERATURE-SUPPORTED
• MEASURED
• PLAUSIBLE
• CONJECTURE
4.3.4 Reasoning mode
• DEDUCTIVE
• EMPIRICAL
• ANALOGICAL
• HEURISTIC
• NORMATIVE
An assumption role is not a warrant. An open or killed status is not a weak warrant.
4.4 2.4 Restriction fields
Every claim carries both sides of reuse:
• establishment_regime;
• deployment_regime.
A regime is the tuple
(
exact model,
base measure or conditioning law,
parameter domain,
spatial/state-space region,
scale/rung,
conditioning depth,
marks/types,
numerical or deployment mode
)
The parent is checked against the dependency’s establishment regime, not against whatever broad regime the
dependency author later writes into the parent.
4.5 2.5 Evidence marks
• required_marks describe the estimand.
• supplied_marks describe what an evidence node actually controls.
For a non-leaf claim, marks are collected from the evidence/dependency cone. A parent cannot satisfy MARK
merely by copying its own required marks into its own supplied_marks field.
4.6 2.6 Composition fields
Every non-atomic operation declares its operation type:
• PRODUCT
• UNION
• AFFINE-ASSEMBLY
• MONOTONE-TRANSFORM
• INTERVAL-ENCLOSURE
7

• EXACT-IDENTITY
It points to a first-class witness node whose witness type is compatible with that operation.
4.7 2.7 Numerical fields
A numerical proof object may carry:
• measured values with scale, parameter, and evidence tags;
• endpoint certificates;
• an F-2 assembly specification;
• a full-domain extremum certificate;
• an uncertainty-provenance certificate;
• active domain-specific gates.
4.8 2.8 Verification and coverage fields
Agreement-based promotion identifies:
• the instruments;
• shared code/data/preprocessing;
• the error channel under test;
• the disjoint-error argument or external crosscheck.
Coverage assertions identify:
• the possible-failure universe currently registered;
• chart/detector IDs per region;
• an uncovered-mass bound;
• any total-risk target.
5 3. Five typed schema profiles
5.1 F-1 — establishment/deployment regime
A bridge is needed whenever a deployment regime differs from the establishment regime in model, measure, domain,
scale, conditioning depth, region, or marks.
Every bridge node declares:
bridge kind
source regime
target regime
scope domain
transferred marks, where applicable
scope statement
falsifier
A generic “change of measure” label does not bridge arbitrary measures.
5.2 F-2 — assembly specification
Every displayed assembled number records:
canonical expression
named inputs
source ID of each input
monotonicity sign of each input
required terms
8

positive upper residuals
negative lower losses
claim direction
rounding direction
working precision
displayed value
Every required or residual term must be both present and consumed by the expression.
5.3 F-3 — uncertainty provenance
Every load-bearing band records:
kind
side
construction
coverage domain
confidence level, where statistical
sample size
multiplicity scope
seed or algorithmic state
deterministic tolerance
side consumed by the parent theorem
source hash
A forecast is not a theorem band.
5.4 F-4 — common-mode certificate
Every agreement-based promotion records:
instrument IDs
shared code
shared data
shared preprocessing
shared model assumptions
shared numerical libraries
error channel under test
disjoint-error argument
external contradiction test
source hash
A Boolean such as error_independence_arg=true is not a certificate.
5.5 F-5 — reasoning bridge
A load-bearing analogical or heuristic step records:
source domain
target domain
scope
bridge claim ID
proof hash
falsifier
grade cap without the bridge
9

6 4. Canonical hashes and stale-PASS discipline
6.1 4.1 Canonical serialization
The content hash is
SHA256(CanonicalJSON(all load-bearing fields)).
Canonical JSON uses:
• sorted keys;
• deterministic separators;
• normalized enum values;
• deterministic ordering of sets and maps;
• no content_hash field inside the hashed payload.
The payload includes dependency edges and each edge’s pinned target hash.
6.2 4.2 Edge pinning
Every edge stores the canonical content hash of its target at the time the parent was gated.
If the target changes without a supersession event, the parent becomes stale and must be re-gated.
6.3 4.3 Current status of HASH-DRIFT
Hash integrity is mandatory in the SCHEMA/integrity preflight in v1.2.
It remains uncounted as an independent numbered gate until the frozen failure record supplies the two independent
stale-parent incidents demanded by the retrodiction protocol. Implementing an integrity invariant does not require
inflating the numbered gate count.
7 5. Warrant and conditional-debt propagation
7.1 5.1 Primitive hypotheses
A primitive hypothesis does not become true by being labeled primitive.
It may support:
• a Proven-Modulo theorem whose statement displays it as a condition;
• a Derived or Plausible investigation whose condition ledger displays it.
It cannot support an unconditional Proven root.
7.2 5.2 Proven-Modulo
Proven-Modulo grades an implication:
𝐻1, … , 𝐻𝑚 ⟹ 𝐶.
Its condition set is part of the theorem object. Any parent that uses the result non-conditionally must either:
1. discharge all conditions; or
2. become Proven-Modulo and inherit the complete condition union.
Conditions cannot disappear by passing through an intermediate node.
10

7.3 5.3 Derived and Measured
Derived is self-tier dependable:
• Derived-on-Derived is allowed;
• a Derived dependency cannot support a Certified or Proven parent non-conditionally.
A calculation using measured inputs carries the measured weakest link unless a statistical/interval theorem promotes
those inputs.
Independent numerical reproduction normally promotes a result to Certified, not automatically to referee-grade
Proven.
7.4 5.4 Literature-supported claims
A literature-supported theorem may support a high-grade parent only when:
• the cited source supports the exact statement;
• model, measure, marks, and domain match; or
• a graded adaptation bridge is present.
“Published somewhere” is not a universal transfer certificate.
7.5 5.5 Provisional dependencies
A provisional result carries an effective warrant cap. Every non-conditional parent inherits the cap.
A parent cannot evade the cap by reading the dependency’s declared grade while ignoring its gate verdict.
8 6. Composition witnesses
Witnesses are graded nodes.
8.1 6.1 Operation compatibility
8.1.1 PRODUCT
Allowed witnesses:
• independence;
• conditional independence;
• Markov property plus the required transition theorem;
• negative dependence in the needed direction;
• comparison theorem;
• direct joint certificate;
• exact algebra.
8.1.2 UNION
Allowed witnesses:
• union bound;
• direct joint certificate;
• exact algebra.
A union bound requires neither independence nor disjointness.
11

8.1.3 AFFINE-ASSEMBLY
Allowed witnesses:
• monotone assembly;
• outward interval arithmetic;
• exact algebra.
8.1.4 INTERVAL-ENCLOSURE
Allowed witnesses:
• outward interval arithmetic;
• direct joint certificate.
8.1.5 EXACT-IDENTITY
Allowed witness:
• exact algebra.
A union-bound witness cannot license a product.
9 7. Mandatory SCHEMA and integrity preflight
Before Gate 1:
1. parse the exact supported schema version;
2. verify every claim ID is unique;
3. verify every target exists;
4. verify the graph is acyclic;
5. verify kind-specific fields;
6. recompute every content hash;
7. verify every pinned edge hash;
8. verify status/warrant consistency;
9. verify the selected roots exist;
10. reject partial registry loading;
11. reject bundled multi-assertion claims where atomicity is violated;
12. record every refusal rather than silently omitting the claim.
A malformed registry load is all-or-nothing.
10 8. The 16 established gates
11 Gate 1 — DOMAIN
Guards: parameter-range containment.
Shell: every load-bearing dependency explicitly carries every free parent parameter and its establishment domain
contains the complete deployment domain.
Missing domain metadata is a failure for a quantified parent, not a silent skip.
Bridge: a typed domain-transfer node whose target scope contains the parent domain.
12

12 Gate 2 — ENDPOINT
Guards: declared boundaries.
Every finite-range numerical claim carries endpoint certificate IDs. A Boolean written directly into a registry is
shell evidence only; endpoint fidelity still requires an independently executed certificate.
Endpoint PASS is necessary, never sufficient for a uniform claim.
13 Gate 3 — POLARITY
Guards: sidedness and loss propagation.
• upper claims consume upper inputs and add every positive residual;
• lower claims consume lower inputs and apply every subunit multiplicative or subtractive loss;
• a symmetric band is consumed on the unfavorable side.
14 Gate 4 — MEASURE
Guards: base law and conditioning.
A mismatch requires a bridge node whose source measure, target measure, and scope domain exactly match the
edge being bridged.
15 Gate 5 — MARK
Guards: auxiliary types and estimands.
Required marks are collected from evidence dependencies. A parent cannot self-attest its evidence marks. Missing
marks require a typed mark-transfer node that explicitly lists the transferred marks.
16 Gate 6 — COMPOSITION
Guards: the license to combine.
Every non-atomic operation points to an operation-compatible, sufficiently graded witness node.
17 Gate 7 — RUNG
Guards: measured scale and parameter tags.
Every measured value carries:
• scale;
• parameter/rung tags;
• evidence ID.
Cross-scale use requires a typed scale bridge.
18 Gate 8 — PRECEDENCE
Guards: live/dead lineage.
The root itself and every reachable node must be live for a live promoted theorem. Killed, superseded, or retired
roots fail even when they have no descendants.
13

19 Gate 9 — CORE CLOSURE
Guards: finished/open boundary.
A closed core has:
• no Open status;
• no Plausible or Conjecture dependency;
• no explicit conditional debt;
• no provisional gate;
• no open domain-specific active gate.
A conditional theorem may be valid without being a closed core.
20 Gate 10 — MODEL
Guards: exact mathematical or probabilistic model.
A transfer certificate declares the exact source model, target model, and scope. A generic high-grade node cannot
bridge arbitrary model pairs.
21 Gate 11 — COVERAGE
Guards: charted failure space.
The shell checks the registered failure universe. The core remains whether the universe is complete.
A PASS means:
“No gap was found in the currently registered universe.”
It never means:
“No unregistered failure mode exists.”
22 Gate 12 — COMMON-MODE
Guards: shared verification error.
Agreement-based promotion requires a first-class certificate identifying the instruments and the error channel under
test.
• disjoint-error proof or external contradiction test: PASS;
• shared/unknown channel: PROVISIONAL;
• no certificate: PROVISIONAL.
The provisional cap is at most Derived unless a stricter domain policy is declared. It is not “the claim’s current
grade,” because that would preserve an already inflated label.
Meta-validation status: operationally established; the historical retrodiction claims for this gate remain provi-sional until their frozen failure IDs and hashes are supplied.
23 Gate 13 — HEURISTIC-BRIDGE
Guards: analogy-to-derivation transition.
A load-bearing analogy supporting a quantitative or asymptotic claim requires a typed bridge node with scope,
derivation evidence, and a falsifier.
Without it:
• a claim above Plausible fails;
14

• a Plausible/Conjecture claim remains provisional.
Meta-validation status: the same evidence caveat as COMMON-MODE applies.
24 Gate 14 — ASSEMBLY
Guards: arithmetic propagation and conservative display.
PASS requires:
1. the canonical expression evaluates;
2. every input has a source;
3. every named required term is present and used;
4. every positive upper residual is present and used;
5. every negative lower loss is present and used;
6. monotonicity directions are declared;
7. upper values round up;
8. lower values round down;
9. equality displays match exactly or by outward interval.
Canonical retrodiction cases include the (4.3/4.35) upper display and the unpropagated (0.8411) lower coefficient.
25 Gate 15 — UNIFORMITY / DOMAIN-EXTREMUM
Machine alias: DOMAIN-INFIMUM.
Guards: a uniform coefficient or quantifier over the entire parameter domain.
For numerical bounds, accepted certificates include:
• exact analytic extremum;
• monotonicity plus endpoint;
• outward interval or Taylor model;
• exhaustive finite enumeration;
• validated grid plus proved modulus;
• asymptotic limit plus monotonicity and compact remainder.
Sampled rungs are not a uniformity certificate.
For general logical claims, quantifier order is recorded explicitly. The broader non-numerical quantifier-order
profile remains a candidate extension until it obtains its own retrodiction record; the numerical uniformity gate is
established now.
26 Gate 16 — BAND-PROVENANCE
Guards: the construction and interpretation of uncertainty.
A load-bearing band must record all metadata applicable to its type. Randomized numerical algorithms must freeze
their seed or integration state and a deterministic tolerance.
A symmetric band inside an upper theorem is consumed on its upper side; inside a lower theorem, on its lower side.
27 9. Domain-specific active gates
A general kernel may carry named project gates such as:
BR-REP
BR-MARK
H4-PATH
15

U-SHAPE
U-UNCERTAINTY-CAL
TORUS-GLOBAL-PARTITION
UB_G_RESIDUAL_UNIFORM
An active gate is a first-class contract field with status:
• CLOSED
• OPEN
• KILLED
• BLOCKED-EXTERNAL
• NOT-CLAIMED
A load-bearing OPEN or BLOCKED gate blocks promotion unless the parent is explicitly formulated as a condi-tional theorem and the gate is represented as a named condition object.
28 10. Registry semantics
A registry is not merely a dictionary of claims.
It contains:
schema version
root IDs
release metadata
claims in a valid DAG
canonical hashes
edge-pinned hashes
optional admission report
28.1 10.1 Strict loading
Loading must:
1. reject an unsupported schema;
2. reject missing targets;
3. reject cycles;
4. reject content-hash mismatch;
5. reject stale edges;
6. reject invalid status/warrant combinations;
7. reject partial admission;
8. return all errors together where practical.
28.2 10.2 Archive versus theorem registry
A file may be a schema demonstration rather than a mathematical theorem registry. Its metadata must say so.
A toy coefficient, broad placeholder domain, or source-declared “Proven” label cannot be silently identified with a
frozen Q0 theorem.
28.3 10.3 Root verdict
The primary root report separately displays:
shell_valid
conditional_promotable
unconditional_promotable
closable
effective_warrant
16

condition set
provisional gates
failed gates
A root with open conditions must never print a bare “PASS at Proven-Modulo” without displaying those conditions
in the same verdict.
29 11. Operating disciplines
The machine shell presupposes:
• freeze before execute;
• supersede, never overwrite;
• preserve every failure;
• write the ledger after adjudication;
• use adversarial reimplementation;
• separate generation, verification, and adjudication;
• verify external citations in parallel with internal consistency;
• persist every theorem-input seed;
• distinguish diagnostic randomness from theorem-input randomness;
• verify releases in ZIP and true clean-extraction modes;
• maximize the weakest link;
• never promote a gate from a favorable hand-selected test set.
30 12. Retrodiction protocol
A candidate gate qualifies only when:
1. it fires on at least two independent frozen failures;
2. COMMON-MODE analysis shows those failures are not duplicate manifestations of one cause;
3. it is silent on most of the frozen record;
4. no established gate or mandatory preflight already discharges it;
5. the evidence table names IDs, prior catch mechanisms, and artifact hashes.
The survivorship limitation is binding: this protocol sees only failures that were found.
31 13. Candidate extensions
31.1 13.1 HASH-DRIFT as a numbered gate
Hash drift is already a mandatory preflight invariant. It becomes a separately numbered gate only if the failure
ledger supplies two independent cases in which a parent PASS was improperly retained after silent dependency
mutation.
31.2 13.2 General quantifier-order UNIFORMITY
Gate 15 establishes numerical uniformity. A broader gate for logical quantifier swaps such as
∀𝜀 ∃𝛿 ⇏ ∃𝛿 ∀𝜀
remains staged until its own failure evidence clears retrodiction.
17

31.3 13.3 SOURCE-FIDELITY
No gate can decide whether a source really proves its tag from metadata alone. Source fidelity remains an operating
discipline, not a candidate automatic gate, unless a domain supplies machine-checkable proof objects or formal
citations.
32 14. Worked example: conditional pairing bound
Suppose the root claims
𝑃pair-Palm(defect) ≤ 𝐶𝑟3, 0 < 𝑟 ≤ 𝑟0, 𝑏 ∈ 𝐵.
The graph includes:
• inner, far, and boundary support claims;
• a union-bound witness node;
• a typed change-of-measure node for every pinned input;
• a marked-density transfer node;
• a coefficient assembly;
• a full-domain supremum certificate;
• a one-sided uncertainty certificate;
• explicit unresolved conditions.
The root promotes as Proven-Modulo only when:
1. every condition is named in the statement and condition set;
2. all non-conditional support is sufficiently dependable;
3. every bridge is source/target typed;
4. marks are supplied by evidence;
5. the coefficient recomputes conservatively;
6. the full-domain supremum is below the display;
7. uncertainty provenance is complete.
It is unconditional only after the condition set becomes empty.
33 15. Worked example: service latency
Claim:
Median warm-cache request latency is at most 40 ms for every arrival rate up to 2,000 requests/s on
configuration C.
The schema maps:
• model → instance type, operating-system and dependency versions, service configuration;
• measure → warm-cache steady-state workload law;
• domain → arrival rate and payload size;
• rung → milliseconds at p50, not p95;
• marks → request class and cache state;
• composition → end-to-end latency witness;
• band → one-sided simultaneous benchmark uncertainty;
• uniformity → no untested mid-range queue-saturation spike.
Two load generators agreeing is provisional if they share the same clock or warmup path.
This example uses the same gates without weakening them into metaphors.
18

34 16. Adoption checklist
Before promoting a root, answer:
1. SCHEMA — is every required field present?
2. HASH — does canonical SHA-256 recompute?
3. EDGE PINNING — do all dependency hashes match?
4. DOMAIN — does every dependency cover every parent parameter?
5. ENDPOINT — are boundary certificates present and passing?
6. POLARITY — are all sides, residuals, and losses conservative?
7. MEASURE — are conditioning changes typed and graded?
8. MARK — do evidence nodes actually carry every mark?
9. COMPOSITION — is the witness operation-compatible?
10. RUNG — does every measured value carry scale and evidence?
11. PRECEDENCE — is the root or any descendant dead?
12. CORE CLOSURE — are there unresolved debts or gates?
13. MODEL — is every model transfer exact and scoped?
14. COVERAGE — what registered failure region remains uncharted?
15. COMMON-MODE — do checking instruments share the tested error channel?
16. HEURISTIC-BRIDGE — is every load-bearing analogy derived or downgraded?
17. ASSEMBLY — does the displayed number recompute in the conservative direction?
18. UNIFORMITY — is the complete domain certified, not merely sampled?
19. BAND-PROVENANCE — can the band be reconstructed?
20. CONDITIONS — does every unresolved dependency appear in the root statement?
21. WARRANT — does every parent respect dependency ceilings?
22. RELEASE — does the graph pass from a true clean extraction?
35 Appendix A — v1.2 changes
change reason
unified the two v1.1 lineages prevent competing “current” specifications
retained shell/core distinction avoid claiming metadata proves mathematics
retained graded bridge nodes close witness/bridge laundering
split status, warrant, assumptions, reasoning mode remove type confusion
added canonical SHA-256 human labels did not detect content mutation
made domain checking strict absent parameters had been silently skipped
made MARK evidence-cone based parent self-attestation was unsound
typed bridge source and target regimes arbitrary high-grade nodes had bridged arbitrary
mismatches
made witnesses operation-specific union witness could license a product
propagated provisional ceilings provisional dependencies had laundered into Proven
parents
propagated condition sets Proven-Modulo conditions had disappeared through
parents
distinguished archive/candidate/promotion storage had been confused with theorem promotion
added ASSEMBLY two frozen arithmetic-propagation failures
promoted numerical UNIFORMITY two full-domain failures
added BAND-PROVENANCE unexplained band and randomized diagnostic
retained HASH-DRIFT as preflight/candidate integrity is mandatory; gate-count promotion still
awaits retrodiction
added strict registry load v1.2 silently returned partial registries
19

change reason
removed hard-coded output paths executable portability
classified the uploaded Q0 registry as a demo its R0 and coefficient are not canonical Q0 objects
36 Appendix B — claim-language limits
Do not say:
• “a gate PASS proves the theorem”;
• “the kernel checks mathematical truth”;
• “two agreeing implementations certify correctness” without COMMON-MODE;
• “a measured coefficient is scale free”;
• “a theorem is uniform” from sampled rungs;
• “a bridge is proved” because a bridge label exists;
• “the uploaded Q0 registry is the Q0 Rate Program theorem registry”;
• “R0” without disambiguating the canonical Q0 Sard condition from the legacy demo remainder condition.
Say instead:
“The proof object passes the executable shell under the declared tags and certificates. Mathematical
fidelity remains grounded in the cited proofs, computations, measurements, and independent review.”
End of Gate Framework Master v1.2.
20
